children.text: aśeṣacidacidvastuviśeṣiṇe śeṣaśāyine /
children.translated_text: To Him who is distinguished by all sentient and non-sentient entities without exception, who reclines upon <s>Śeṣa</s>,

children.text: nirmalānantakalyāṇanidhaye viṣṇave namaḥ //
children.translated_text: To <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the treasury of stainless, infinite, and auspicious qualities — salutation.

children.text: aśeṣa-cid-acid-vastu-viśeṣiṇe śeṣa-śāyine /
nirmala-ananta-kalyāṇa-nidhaye viṣṇave namaḥ //
paraṃ brahmaivājñaṃ bhramaparigataṃ saṃsarati tatparopādhyālīḍhaṃ vivaśamaśubhasyāspadam iti /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> itself is ignorant, subject to delusion, transmigrates; it is seized by the adventitious conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) of another, helpless, and the abode of impurity — thus,

children.text: śrutinyāyāpetaṃ jagati vitataṃ mohanam idaṃ tamo yenāpāstaṃ sa hi vijayate yāmunamuniḥ //
children.translated_text: This delusion, contrary to scripture and reason, spread throughout the world — this darkness was dispelled by him; indeed, the venerable <s>Yāmunamuni</s> triumphs!

children.text: paraṃ brahma eva ajñaṃ bhrama-parigataṃ saṃsarati tat-para-upādhy-ālīḍhaṃ vivaśama-śubhasyā aspadam iti /
śruti-nyāya-apetaṃ jagati vitataṃ mohanam idaṃ tamo yena apāstaṃ sa hi vijayate yāmuna-muniḥ //

body.text: aśeṣajagaddhitānuśāsanaśrutinikaraśirasi samadhigato 'yam arthaḥ jīvaparamātmayāthātmyajñānapūrvakavarṇāśramadharmetikartavyatākaparamapuruṣacaraṇayugaladhyānārcanapraṇāmādir atyarthapriyas tatprāptiphalaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning ascertained at the summit of the multitude of scriptures that teach what is beneficial to the entire world is this: preceded by the true knowledge of the nature of the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) and <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the duties of <s>varṇa</s> (social class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) as what ought to be performed, and meditation upon, worship of, and prostration before the two feet of the <s>Paramapuruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) — these are supremely dear to Him, and their fruit is the attainment of Him.

children.text: aśeṣa-jagad-dhita-anuśāsana-śruti-nikara-śirasi samadhigato 'yam arthaḥ jīva-parama-ātma-yāthātmya-jñāna-pūrvaka-varṇa-āśrama-dharma-itikartavyatāka-parama-puruṣa-caraṇa-yugala-dhyāna-arcana-praṇāma-ādir atyartha-priyas tat-prāpti-phalaḥ /

body.text:
asya jīvātmano 'nādyavidyāsaṃcitapuṇyapāparūpakarmapravāhahetukabrahmādisuranaratiryaksthāvarātmakacaturvidhadehapraveśakṛtatattadabhimānajanitāvarjanīyabhavabhayavidhvaṃsanāya dehātiriktātmasvarūpatatsvabhāvatadantarayāmiparamātmasvarūpatatsvabhāvatadupāsanatatphalabhūtātmasvarūpāvirbhāvapūrvakānavadhikātiśayānandabrahmānubhavajñāpane pravṛttaṃ hi vedāntavākyajātam, tat tvam asi / ayam ātmā brahma / ya ātmani tiṣṭhann ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ / eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmāpahatapāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ / tam etaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasānāśakena / brahmavid āpnoti param / tam evaṃ vidvān
amṛta iha bhavati nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyata ityādikam /
body.translated_text: For this <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self), whose entry into the fourfold bodies — comprising <s>Brahmā</s> and the gods, humans, animals, and plants — is caused by the flow of <s>karma</s> (action) in the form of merit and demerit accumulated through beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and whose identification with each such body generates the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) that must be avoided — for the destruction of this fear, the body of <s>Vedānta</s> sentences has set forth knowledge of: the essential nature of the self as distinct from the body; its intrinsic character; the essential nature and character of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) who is its inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>); the worship of Him; and the manifestation of the self's true nature as the fruit of that worship, consisting of the experience of <s>Brahman</s> as boundless, unsurpassed bliss — as declared in such texts as: "You are That" (<s>tat tvam asi</s>); "This self is <s>Brahman</s>" (<s>ayam ātmā brahma</s>); "He who dwells in the self, who is within the self, whom the self does not know, whose body the self is, who controls the self from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal" (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>); "This inner self of all beings, free from evil, divine, the one God <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>" (<s>Subāla Upaniṣad</s>); "<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know Him through the study of the <s>Veda</s>, through sacrifice, through charity, through austerity, and through fasting"; "The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the Supreme"; "He who knows thus becomes immortal here; there is no other path for liberation" — and so forth.

children.text:
asya jīva-ātmano 'nādy-avidyā-saṃcita-puṇya-pāpa-rūpa-karma-pravāha-hetuka-brahma-ādi-sura-nara-tiryak-sthāvara-ātmaka-catur-vidha-deha-praveśa-kṛta-tat-tad-abhimāna-janita-avarjanīya-bhava-bhaya-vidhvaṃsanāya deha-atirikta-ātma-svarūpa-tat-sva-bhāva-tad-antarayāmi-parama-ātma-sva-rūpa-tat-sva-bhāva-tad-upāsana-tat-phala-bhūta-ātma-sva-rūpa-āvirbhāva-pūrvaka-anavadhika-atiśaya-ānanda-brahma-anubhava-jñāpane pravṛttaṃ hi vedānta-vākya-jātam, tat tvam asi / ayam ātmā brahma / ya ātmani tiṣṭhann ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātma-antaryāmy amṛtaḥ / eṣa sarva-bhūta-antar-ātma-apahata-pāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ / tam etaṃ veda-anuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasa ānāśakena / brahma-vid āpnoti param / tam evaṃ vidvān
amṛta iha bhavati na anyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyata ity-ādikam /

body.text: jīvātmanaḥ svarūpaṃ devamanuṣyādiprakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣarūpanānāvidhabhedarahitaṃ jñānānandaikaguṇaṃ, tasyaitasya karmakṛtadevādibhede 'padhvaste svarūpabhedo vācām agocaraḥ svasaṃvedyaḥ, jñānasvarūpam ity etāvad eva nirdeśyam / tac ca sarveṣām ātmanāṃ samānam /
body.translated_text: The essential nature of the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) is devoid of the manifold differences such as gods, humans, and the like, which are particular modifications of <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature); its sole attribute is knowledge and bliss (<s>jñānānanda</s>). When the differences such as gods and others, produced by <s>karma</s>, are removed, the essential distinction of its nature is beyond the reach of words, self-luminous and known only to itself; it can be described only thus far — that it is of the nature of knowledge (<s>jñānasvarūpa</s>). And this is the same for all selves.

children.text: jīva-ātmanaḥ sva-rūpaṃ deva-manuṣya-ādi-prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-rūpa-nānā-vidha-bheda-rahitaṃ jñāna-ānanda-eka-guṇaṃ, tasya etasya karma-kṛta-deva-ādi-bhede 'padhvaste sva-rūpa-bhedo vācām agocaraḥ sva-saṃvedyaḥ, jñāna-sva-rūpam ity etāvad eva nirdeśyam / tac ca sarveṣām ātmanāṃ samānam /

body.text: evaṃvidhacidacidātmakaprapañcasyodbhavasthitipralayasaṃsāranirvartanaikahetubhūtaḥ samastaheyapratyanīkānantakalyāṇatayā ca svetarasamastavastuvilakṣaṇasvarūpo 'navadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaḥ sarvātmaparabrahmaparajyotiḥparatattvaparamātmasadādiśabdabhedair nikhilavedāntavedyo bhagavān nārāyaṇaḥ puruṣottama ity antaryāmisvarūpam / asya ca vaibhavapratipādanaparāḥ śrutayaḥ svetarasamastacidacidvastujātāntarātmatayā nikhilaniyamanaṃ tacchaktitadaṃśatadvibhūtitadrūpataccharīratattanuprabhṛtibhiḥ śabdais tatsāmānādhikaraṇyena ca pratipādayanti /
body.translated_text: He who is the sole cause of the origination, sustenance, dissolution, and the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) of the entire universe composed of sentient (<s>cit</s>) and non-sentient (<s>acit</s>) entities; who, by being the opposite of all that is to be rejected and by possessing infinite auspicious qualities, has an essential nature entirely distinct from all other entities; who possesses a multitude of innumerable, boundless, and unsurpassed auspicious qualities; who is known through all the <s>Vedānta</s> texts by the various terms <s>Sarvātman</s> (Self of all), <s>Parabrahman</s> (Supreme <s>Brahman</s>), <s>Parajyotis</s> (Supreme Light), <s>Paratattvam</s> (Supreme Reality), <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), <s>Sat</s>, and others — He is the Blessed Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person): such is the nature of the <s>Antaryāmin</s> (Inner Controller). And the scriptures devoted to establishing His glory set forth that He controls all things by being the inner self of the entire collection of all other sentient and non-sentient entities, and they express this through terms such as His power (<s>śakti</s>), His portion (<s>aṃśa</s>), His manifestation (<s>vibhūti</s>), His form (<s>rūpa</s>), His body (<s>śarīra</s>), His extension (<s>tanu</s>), and others, as well as through co-ordinate predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with those terms.

children.text: evaṃ-vidha-cid-acid-ātmaka-prapañcasya udbhava-sthiti-pralaya-saṃsāra-nirvartana-eka-hetu-bhūtaḥ samasta-heya-pratyanīka-ananta-kalyāṇatayā ca sva-itara-samasta-vastu-vilakṣaṇa-sva-rūpo 'navadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaḥ sarva-ātma-para-brahma-para-jyotiḥ-para-tattva-parama-ātma-sad-ādi-śabda-bhedair nikhila-vedānta-vedyo bhagavān nārāyaṇaḥ puruṣa-uttama ity antaryāmi-sva-rūpam / asya ca vaibhava-pratipādana-parāḥ śrutayaḥ sva-itara-samasta-cid-acid-vastu-jāta-antar-ātmatayā nikhila-niyamanaṃ tac-chakti-tad-aṃśa-tad-vibhūti-tad-rūpa-tac-charīra-tat-tanu-prabhṛtibhiḥ śabdais tat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena ca pratipādayanti /

body.text: tasya vaibhavapratipādanaparāṇām eṣāṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyādīnāṃ vivaraṇe pravṛttāḥ kecana nirviśeṣajñānamātram eva brahma, tac ca nityamuktasvaprakāśasvabhāvam api tat tvam asy ādisāmānādhikaraṇyāvagatajīvāikyaṃ, brahmaivājñaṃ badhyate mucyate ca, nirviśeṣacinmātrātirekeśvareśitavyādyanantavikalparūpaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jaganmithyā, kaścid baddhaḥ, kaścin mukta ity iyam avasthā na vidyate / itaḥ pūrvaṃ kecana muktā ity ayam artho mithyā / ekam eva śarīraṃ jīvavan nirjīvānītarāṇi, taccharīraṃ kim iti na vyavasthitam, ācāryo jñānasyopadeṣṭā mithyā śāstraṃ ca mithyā śāstrapramātā ca mithyā śāstrajanyaṃ jñānaṃ ca mithyā -- etat sarvaṃ mithyābhūtenaiva śāstreṇāvagamyata iti varṇayanti /
body.translated_text: In the course of explaining these co-ordinate predications and similar devices employed by those scriptures devoted to establishing His glory, certain thinkers maintain the following: <s>Brahman</s> is nothing but undifferentiated consciousness (<s>nirviśeṣa-jñāna-mātra</s>); though by nature eternally free and self-luminous, through the co-ordinate predication understood from texts such as "You are That" (<s>tat tvam asi</s>), its identity with the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) is established; <s>Brahman</s> itself, being ignorant, is bound and liberated; the entire world, in the form of infinite manifold appearances such as the Lord, the governed, and the like — all beyond undifferentiated consciousness — is false (<s>mithyā</s>); the states "someone is bound" and "someone is liberated" do not truly exist; the claim that "certain ones were previously liberated" is itself false; only one body is alive while the others are lifeless; why that one body is not fixed is unexplained; the teacher who instructs in knowledge is false, the scripture is false, the one who ascertains scripture is false, and the knowledge born of scripture is also false — all this, they assert, is apprehended through scripture that is itself false.

children.text: tasya vaibhava-pratipādana-parāṇām eṣāṃ sāmānādhikaraṇya-ādīnāṃ vivaraṇe pravṛttāḥ kecana nirviśeṣa-jñāna-mātram eva brahma, tac ca nitya-mukta-sva-prakāśa-sva-bhāvam api tat tvam asy ādi-sāmānādhikaraṇya-avagata-jīva-aikyaṃ, brahma eva ajñaṃ badhyate mucyate ca, nirviśeṣa-cin-mātra-atireka-īśvara-īśitavya-ādy-ananta-vikalpa-rūpaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagan-mithyā, kaścid baddhaḥ, kaścin mukta ity iyam avasthā na vidyate / itaḥ pūrvaṃ kecana muktā ity ayam artho mithyā / ekam eva śarīraṃ jīvavan nirjīvāni itarāṇi, tac-charīraṃ kim iti na vyavasthitam, ācāryo jñānasya upadeṣṭā mithyā śāstraṃ ca mithyā śāstra-pramātā ca mithyā śāstra-janyaṃ jñānaṃ ca mithyā --- etat sarvaṃ mithyā-bhūtena eva śāstreṇa avagamyata iti varṇayanti /

body.text: apare tv apahatapāpmatvādisamastakalyāṇaguṇopetam api brahmaitenaivāikyāvabodhena kenacid upādhiviśeṣeṇa saṃbaddhaṃ badhyate mucyate ca nānāvidhamalarūpapariṇāmāspadaṃ ceti vyavasthitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Others, however, hold that <s>Brahman</s>, though endowed with all auspicious qualities such as being free from evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and the rest, is nevertheless — through this very understanding of identity — connected with some particular adventitious condition (<s>upādhi</s>), and is thus bound and liberated, and is the locus of transformations in the form of manifold impurities.

children.text: apare tv apahata-pāpmatva-ādi-samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-upetam api brahma etena eva aikya-avabodhena kenacid upādhi-viśeṣeṇa saṃbaddhaṃ badhyate mucyate ca nānā-vidha-mala-rūpa-pariṇāma-āspadaṃ ca iti vyavasthitāḥ /

body.text: anye punar aikyāvabodhayāthātmyaṃ varṇayantaḥ svābhāvikaniratiśayāparimitodāraguṇasāgaraṃ brahmaiva suranaratiryaksthāvaranārakisvargyapavargicetaneṣu svabhāvato vilakṣaṇam avilakṣaṇaṃ ca viyadādinānāvidhamalarūpapariṇāmāspadaṃ ceti pratyavatiṣṭhante /
body.translated_text: Still others, while explaining the true meaning of the teaching of identity, maintain that <s>Brahman</s>, which is an ocean of naturally unsurpassed, boundless, and noble qualities, is itself — though inherently distinct from the sentient beings among gods, humans, animals, plants, hell-dwellers, heaven-dwellers, and the liberated — also non-distinct from them, and is the locus of transformations in the form of manifold impurities such as space (<s>vyoman</s>) and the rest.

children.text: anye punar aikya-avabodha-yāthātmyaṃ varṇayantaḥ svābhāvika-niratiśaya-aparimita-udāra-guṇa-sāgaraṃ brahma eva sura-nara-tiryak-sthāvara-nāraki-svargy-apavargi-cetaneṣu sva-bhāvato vilakṣaṇam avilakṣaṇaṃ ca viyad-ādi-nānā-vidha-mala-rūpa-pariṇāma-āspadaṃ ca iti pratyavatiṣṭhante /

body.text: tatra prathamapakṣasya śrutyarthaparyālocanaparā duṣparihārān doṣān udāharanti / prakṛtaparāmarśitacchabdāvagatasvasaṃkalpakṛtajagadudayavibhavavilayādayas tad+aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyetyārabhya sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhā ityādibhiḥ padaiḥ pratipāditās tatsaṃbandhitayā prakaraṇāntaranirdiṣṭāḥ sarvajñatāsarvaśaktitvasarveśvaratvasarvaprakāratvasamābhyadhikanivṛttisatyakāmatvasatyasaṃkalpatvasarvāvabhāsakatvādyanavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇā apahatapāpmetyādyanekavākyāvagatanirastanikhiladoṣatā ca sarve tasmin pakṣe vihanyante /
body.translated_text: Among these, those who scrutinize the meaning of scripture against the first position point out defects that are difficult to overcome: The origination, glory, and dissolution of the universe — brought about by His own will (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), as understood from the word "that" referring to the subject under discussion — established through passages beginning with "It willed: may I become many, may I be born" and continuing through "All these creatures, O <s>Somya</s>, have Being (<s>sat</s>) as their root, Being as their abode, Being as their support"; the host of innumerable, boundless, unsurpassed auspicious qualities — omniscience, omnipotence, supreme lordship, being the ground of all modes, freedom from anything equal or superior, having true desires, having true will, being the illuminator of all — declared in relation to Him, as well as freedom from all defects established by many texts such as "free from evil" (<s>apahatapāpman</s>) and so forth — all these are destroyed in that [Advaita] position.

children.text: tatra prathama-pakṣasya śruty-artha-paryālocana-parā duṣparihārān doṣān udāharanti / prakṛta-parāmarśi-tac-chabda-avagata-sva-saṃkalpa-kṛta-jagad-udaya-vibhava-vilaya-ādayas tad+aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya ity-ārabhya san-mūlāḥ somya imāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sad-āyatanāḥ sat-pratiṣṭhā ity-ādibhiḥ padaiḥ pratipāditās tat-saṃbandhitayā prakaraṇa-antara-nirdiṣṭāḥ sarva-jñatā-sarva-śaktitva-sarva-īśvaratva-sarva-prakāratva-sama-abhyadhika-nivṛtti-satya-kāmatva-satya-saṃkalpatva-sarva-avabhāsakatva-ādy-anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇā apahata-pāpma īty-ādy-aneka-vākya-avagata-nirasta-nikhila-doṣatā ca sarve tasmin pakṣe vihanyante /

body.text: atha syāt -- upakrame 'py ekavijñānena sarvavijñānamukhena kāraṇasyaiva satyatāṃ pratijñāya tasya kāraṇabhūtasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ satyatāṃ vikārajātasyāsatyatāṃ mṛddṛṣṭāntena darśayitvā satyabhūtasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam iti sajātīyavijātīyanikhilabhedanirasanena nirviśeṣataiva pratipāditā / etac chodhakāni prakaraṇāntaragatavākyāny api satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma, niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ nirguṇaṃ, vijñānam ānandam ityādīni sarvaviśeṣapratyanīkaikākāratāṃ bodhayanti / na caikākāratābodhane padānāṃ paryāyatā / ekatve 'pi vastunaḥ sarvaviśeṣapratyanīkatopasthāpanena sarvapadānām arthavattvād iti /
body.translated_text: Now, it might be objected: Even at the outset, having promised that by knowing one thing all things are known — thereby establishing the reality of the cause alone — and having demonstrated by the analogy of clay the reality of <s>Brahman</s> as the cause and the unreality of the class of effects, the text "Being alone, O <s>Somya</s>, was this in the beginning, one only, without a second" (<s>sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam</s>) teaches precisely the attributeless nature (<s>nirviśeṣatā</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, which is the real, by negating all differences — both homogeneous (<s>sajātīya</s>) and heterogeneous (<s>vijātīya</s>). And passages from other contexts that reinforce this — "<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite" (<s>satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma</s>); "without parts, without activity, without qualities" (<s>niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ nirguṇam</s>); "consciousness and bliss" (<s>vijñānam ānandam</s>) and the like — convey a single nature opposed to all distinctions. Nor do these words become mere synonyms in conveying a single nature, for even though the entity is one, each word has its own meaningful content by indicating the negation of all particular distinctions.

children.text: atha syāt --- upakrame 'py eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñāna-mukhena kāraṇasya eva satyatāṃ pratijñāya tasya kāraṇa-bhūtasya eva brahmaṇaḥ satyatāṃ vikāra-jātasya asatyatāṃ mṛd-dṛṣṭāntena darśayitvā satya-bhūtasya eva brahmaṇaḥ sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ekam eva advitīyam iti sajātīya-vijātīya-nikhila-bheda-nirasanena nirviśeṣata aiva pratipāditā / etac chodhakāni prakaraṇa-antara-gata-vākyāny api satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma, niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ nirguṇaṃ, vijñānam ānandam ity-ādīni sarva-viśeṣa-pratyanīka-eka-ākāratāṃ bodhayanti / na ca eka-ākāratā-bodhane padānāṃ paryāyatā / ekatve 'pi vastunaḥ sarva-viśeṣa-pratyanīkatā-upasthāpanena sarva-padānām arthavattvād iti /

body.text: naitad evam / ekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ sarvasya mithyātve sarvasya jñātavyasyābhāvān na setsyati / satyatvamithyātvayor ekatāprasaktir vā / api tv ekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ sarvasya tadātmakatvenaiva satyatve sidhyati /
body.translated_text: This is not so. If everything is false, then since there would be nothing left to be known, knowledge of all through the knowledge of one would not be established. Or else, the identity of reality and falsity would follow. Rather, knowledge of all through the knowledge of one is established only if everything is real by virtue of having That (<s>Brahman</s>) as its essential nature (<s>tadātmakatva</s>).

children.text: na etad evam / eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñānaṃ sarvasya mithyātve sarvasya jñātavyasya abhāvān na setsyati / satyatva-mithyātvayor ekatā-prasaktir vā / api tv eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñānaṃ sarvasya tad-ātmakatvena eva satyatve sidhyati /

body.text:
ayam arthaḥ -- śvetaketuṃ pratyāha stabdho 'sy uta tam ādeśam aprākṣya iti paripūrṇa iva lakṣyase tān ācāryān prati tam apy ādeśaṃ pṛṣṭavān asīti / ādiśyate 'nenety ādeśaḥ / ādeṣaḥ praśāsanam / etasya vā akṣarasya gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhata ity ādibhir aikyarthyāt / tathā ca mānavaṃ vacaḥ -- praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām ityādi / atrāpy ekam eveti jagadupādānatāṃ pratipādyādvitīyapadenādhiṣṭhātaranivāraṇād asyaivādhiṣṭhātṛtvam api pratipādyate /atas taṃ praśāsitāraṃ jagadupādānabhūtam api pṛṣṭavān asi yena śrutena matena vijñātenāśrutam amatam avijñānaṃ śrutaṃ mataṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīty uktaṃ syāt / nikhilajagadudayavibhavavilayādikāraṇabhūtaṃ sarvajñatvasatyakāmatvasatyasaṃkalpatvaparimitodāraguṇagaṇasāgaraṃ
kiṃ brahmāpi tvayā śrutam iti hārdo bhāvaḥ / tasya nikhilakāraṇatayā kāraṇam eva nānāsaṃsthānaviśeṣasaṃsthitaṃ kāryam ity ucyata iti kāraṇabhūtasūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīrakabrahmavijñānena kārrabhūtam akhilaṃ jagad vijñātaṃ bhavatīti hṛdi nidhāya yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavaty amataṃ matam avijñātaṃ vijñātaṃ syād iti putraṃ prati pṛṣṭavān pitā / tad etatsakalasya vastujātasyaikakāraṇatvaṃ pitṛhṛdi nihitam ajānan putraḥ parasparavilakṣaṇeṣu vastuṣv anyasya jñānena tadanyavijñānasyāghaṭamānatāṃ buddhvā paricodayati -- kathaṃ nu bagavaḥ sa ādeśa iti /
body.translated_text: The meaning is as follows: To <s>Śvetaketu</s>, [his father <s>Uddālaka</s>] said, "You seem proud; did you ask for that teaching (<s>ādeśa</s>)?" — that is, "You appear as if fully accomplished; did you ask your teachers about that teaching as well?" That by which something is taught is an <s>ādeśa</s>; <s>ādeśa</s> means sovereign command (<s>praśāsana</s>). This is established by the concordance of meaning with passages such as "Under the command of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and the moon stand held apart" (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>). And likewise the <s>Mānava</s> (Manu's) statement: "the ruler of all" and so forth. Here too, by the word "one only" (<s>ekam eva</s>) the text establishes that [<s>Brahman</s>] is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of the universe, and by the word "without a second" (<s>advitīya</s>), since it negates any other controller, His own controllership (<s>adhiṣṭhātṛtva</s>) is also established. Therefore, [Uddālaka] asked, "Did you inquire about that ruler who is also the material cause of the universe, by hearing, thinking, and knowing whom, what has not been heard becomes heard, what has not been thought becomes thought, what has not been known becomes known?" The inner purport is: "Did you learn about <s>Brahman</s>, who is the cause of the origination, glory, and dissolution of the entire universe, and who is an ocean of boundless, noble qualities such as omniscience, true desire, and true will?" Because He is the cause of everything, the effect — which is nothing but the cause configured in various particular arrangements — is so described; thus, through knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> whose body is the subtle sentient and non-sentient entities that constitute the cause, the entire universe which constitutes the effect becomes known — holding this in his heart, the father asked his son: "By which, what has not been heard becomes heard, what has not been thought becomes thought, what has not been known becomes known." Not knowing this — that the entire collection of entities has a single cause, as held in the father's heart — the son, understanding that when entities are mutually distinct, the knowledge of one cannot yield the knowledge of another, asks with wonder: "How indeed, O venerable sir, can there be such a teaching (<s>ādeśa</s>)?"

children.text:
ayam arthaḥ --- śvetaketuṃ pratyāha stabdho 'sy uta tam ādeśam aprākṣya iti paripūrṇa iva lakṣyase tān ācāryān prati tam apy ādeśaṃ pṛṣṭavān asi iti / ādiśyate 'nena ity ādeśaḥ / ādeṣaḥ praśāsanam / etasya vā akṣarasya gārgi sūryā-candramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhata ity ādibhir aikyarthyāt / tathā ca mānavaṃ vacaḥ --- praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām ity-ādi / atra apy ekam eva iti jagad-upādānatāṃ pratipādya advitīya-padena adhiṣṭhātara-nivāraṇād asya eva adhiṣṭhātṛtvam api pratipādyate /atas taṃ praśāsitāraṃ jagad-upādāna-bhūtam api pṛṣṭavān asi yena śrutena matena vijñātena aśrutam amatam avijñānaṃ śrutaṃ mataṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati ity uktaṃ syāt / nikhila-jagad-udaya-vibhava-vilaya-ādi-kāraṇa-bhūtaṃ sarva-jñatva-satya-kāmatva-satya-saṃkalpatva-parimita-udāra-guṇa-gaṇa-sāgaraṃ
kiṃ brahma api tvayā śrutam iti hārdo bhāvaḥ / tasya nikhila-kāraṇatayā kāraṇam eva nānā-saṃsthāna-viśeṣa-saṃsthitaṃ kāryam ity ucyata iti kāraṇa-bhūta-sūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraka-brahma-vijñānena kārra-bhūtam akhilaṃ jagad vijñātaṃ bhavati iti hṛdi nidhāya yena aśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavaty amataṃ matam avijñātaṃ vijñātaṃ syād iti putraṃ prati pṛṣṭavān pitā / tad etat-sakalasya vastu-jātasya eka-kāraṇatvaṃ pitṛ-hṛdi nihitam ajānan putraḥ paraspara-vilakṣaṇeṣu vastuṣv anyasya jñānena tad-anya-vijñānasya aghaṭamānatāṃ buddhvā paricodayati --- kathaṃ nu bagavaḥ sa ādeśa iti /

body.text: paricoditaḥ punas tad eva hṛdi nihitaṃ jñānānandāmalatvaikasvarūpam aparicchedyamāhātmyaṃ satyasaṃkalpatvamiśrair anavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇair juṣṭam avikārasvarūpaṃ paraṃ brahmaiva nāmarūpavibhāgānarhasūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīraṃ svalīlāyai svasaṃkalpenānantavicitrasthiratrasasvarūpajagatsaṃsthānaṃ svāṃśenāvasthitam iti /
body.translated_text: Being further prompted, [the teacher explains] that same [Brahman] established in the heart — whose essential nature is knowledge, bliss, and purity alone, whose greatness is immeasurable, endowed with an infinite multitude of unsurpassably excellent and innumerable auspicious qualities including the quality of true resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>), whose essential nature is unchanging — that supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself, having as its body the subtle conscious (<s>cit</s>) and non-conscious (<s>acit</s>) entities that are not yet differentiated into name and form, abides through its own portion, for its own sport (<s>līlā</s>), by its own resolve, as the cosmos of infinitely variegated stable and moving forms.

children.text: paricoditaḥ punas tad eva hṛdi nihitaṃ jñāna-ānanda-amalatva-eka-sva-rūpam aparicchedya-māhātmyaṃ satya-saṃkalpatva-miśrair anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇair juṣṭam avikāra-sva-rūpaṃ paraṃ brahma eva nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-anarha-sūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraṃ sva-līlāyai sva-saṃkalpena ananta-vicitra-sthira-trasa-sva-rūpa-jagat-saṃsthānaṃ sva-aṃśena avasthitam iti /

body.text: tajjñānenāsya nikhilasya jñātatāṃ bruvaṃl lokadṛṣṭaṃ kāryakāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ darśayituṃ dṛṣṭāntam āha -- yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syād vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam iti / ekam eva mṛddravyaṃ svaikadeśena nānāvyavahārāspadatvāya ghaṭaśarāvādinānāsaṃsthānāvasthārūpavikārāpannaṃ nānānāmadheyam api mṛttikāsaṃsthānaviśeṣatvān mṛddravyam evettham avasthitaṃ na vastvantaram iti / yathā mṛtpiṇḍavijñānena tatsaṃsthānaviśeṣarūpam ghaṭaśarāvādi sarvaṃ jñātam eva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Declaring that through the knowledge of that [<s>Brahman</s>], everything is known, [the teacher] gives an illustration to show the non-difference of cause and effect as observed in the world: 'Just as, dear one, by one lump of clay all that is made of clay is known — the modification is merely a verbal designation, a name; the reality is only clay.' The one substance, clay, having undergone modifications in the form of various configurations such as pot, plate, and the like — which are the basis for various practical designations — through a portion of itself, even though possessing different names, being merely a particular configuration of clay, is nothing other than the clay substance itself in that state. The meaning is: just as by knowing a lump of clay, all things such as pots, plates, and the like, which are particular configurations of it, are already known.

children.text: taj-jñānena asya nikhilasya jñātatāṃ bruvaṃl loka-dṛṣṭaṃ kārya-kāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ darśayituṃ dṛṣṭāntam āha --- yathā somya ekena mṛt-piṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛn-mayaṃ vijñātaṃ syād vācā ārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāma-dheyaṃ mṛttika īty eva satyam iti / ekam eva mṛd-dravyaṃ sva-eka-deśena nānā-vyavahāra-āspadatvāya ghaṭa-śarāva-ādi-nānā-saṃsthāna-avasthā-rūpa-vikāra-āpannaṃ nānā-nāma-dheyam api mṛttikā-saṃsthāna-viśeṣatvān mṛd-dravyam eva ittham avasthitaṃ na vastv-antaram iti / yathā mṛt-piṇḍa-vijñānena tat-saṃsthāna-viśeṣa-rūpam ghaṭa-śarāva-ādi sarvaṃ jñātam eva bhavati ity-arthaḥ /

body.text: tataḥ kṛtsnasya jagato brahmaikakāraṇatām ajānan putraḥ pṛcchati -- bhagavāṃs tv eva me tad bravītv iti / tataḥ sarvajñaṃ sarvaśakti brahmaiva sarvakāraṇam ity upadiśan sa hovāca sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam iti / atredam iti jagan nirdiṣṭam / agra iti ca sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvakālaḥ / tasmin kāle jagataḥ sadātmakatāṃ sad eveti pratipādya, tatsṛṣṭikāle 'py aviśiṣṭam iti kṛtvaikam eveti sadāpannasya jagatas tadānīm avibhaktanāmarūpatāṃ pratipādya tatpratipādanenaiva sato jagadupādānatvaṃ pratipāditam iti svavyatiriktanimittakāraṇam advitīyapadena pratiṣiddham /
body.translated_text: Then the son, not knowing that <s>Brahman</s> alone is the sole cause of the entire universe, asks: 'May the Blessed One tell me that.' Then, teaching that <s>Brahman</s> itself, omniscient and omnipotent, is the cause of all, he said: 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone, dear one, this was in the beginning — one only, without a second.' Here, by 'this' (<s>idam</s>) the universe is indicated. And 'in the beginning' (<s>agra</s>) refers to the time prior to creation. Establishing that at that time the universe had the nature of Being (<s>sat</s>) by the words 'Being alone,' and teaching that even at the time of creation it was not different, by 'one only' establishing that the universe absorbed into Being at that time had undifferentiated name and form — by that very teaching, the material-cause-hood (<s>upādānatva</s>) of Being with respect to the universe is established, and by the word 'without a second' (<s>advitīya</s>), an efficient cause different from itself is negated.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtsnasya jagato brahma-eka-kāraṇatām ajānan putraḥ pṛcchati --- bhagavāṃs tv eva me tad bravītv iti / tataḥ sarva-jñaṃ sarva-śakti brahma eva sarva-kāraṇam ity upadiśan sa hovāca sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ekam eva advitīyam iti / atra idam iti jagan nirdiṣṭam / agra iti ca sṛṣṭeḥ pūrva-kālaḥ / tasmin kāle jagataḥ sad-ātmakatāṃ sad eva iti pratipādya, tat-sṛṣṭi-kāle 'py aviśiṣṭam iti kṛtva aikam eva iti sad-āpannasya jagatas tadānīm avibhakta-nāma-rūpatāṃ pratipādya tat-pratipādanena eva sato jagad-upādānatvaṃ pratipāditam iti sva-vyatirikta-nimitta-kāraṇam advitīya-padena pratiṣiddham /

body.text:
tam ādeśam prākṣyo yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavatītyādāv eva praśāstitaiva jagadupādānam iti hṛdi nihitam idānīm abhivyaktam / svayam eva jagadupādānaṃ jagannimittaṃ ca sat tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti / tad etacchabdavācyaṃ paraṃ brahma sarvajñaṃ sarvaśakti satyasaṅkalpam avāptasamastakāmam api līlārthaṃ vicitrānantacidacinmiśrajagadrūpeṇāham eva bahu syāṃ tadarthaṃ prajāyeyeti svayam eva saṃkalpya svāṃśaikadeśād eva viyadādibhūtāni sṛṣṭvā punar api saiva sacchabdābhihitā parā devataivam aikṣata hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti / anena jīvenātmaneti - jīvasya brahmātmakatvaṃ pratipādya brahmātmajīvānupraveśād eva kṛtsnasyācidvastunaḥ padārthatvam evaṃbhūtasyaiva sarvasya
vastuno nāmabhāktvam iti ca darśayati / etaduktaṃ bhavati -- jīvātmā tu brahmaṇaḥ śarīratayā prakāratvād brahmātmakaḥ / yasyātmā śarīram iti śrutyantarāt / evaṃbhūtasya jīvasya śarīratayā prakārabhūtāni devamanuṣyādisaṃsthānāni vastūnīti brahmātmakāni tāni sarvāṇi / ato devo manuṣyo rākṣasaḥ paśur mṛgaḥ pakṣī vṛkṣo latā kāṣṭhaṃ śilā tṛṇaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭa ityādayaḥ sarve prakṛtipratyayayogenābhidhāyakatayā prasiddhāḥ śabdā loke tattadvācyatayā pratīyamānatattatsaṃsthānavastumukhena tadabhimānijīvatadantaryāmiparamātmaparyantasaṃghātasyaiva vācakā iti /
body.translated_text: The instruction 'by which the unheard becomes heard' and so forth — [the fact that <s>Brahman</s> is] the material cause of the universe, which was already established in the heart from the very beginning, is now made manifest. Being itself the material cause of the universe and the efficient cause of the universe, that Being willed: 'May I become many, may I be born.' That supreme <s>Brahman</s>, denoted by the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>), omniscient, omnipotent, of true resolve, having attained all desires, yet for the sake of sport (<s>līlā</s>), having itself resolved 'I alone shall become many in the form of a variegated, infinite universe of conscious and non-conscious [entities] mixed together, and for that purpose I shall be born' — from a portion of itself alone it created space (<s>vyom</s>) and the other elements. And furthermore, that same supreme Deity denoted by the word 'Being' willed thus: 'Let me enter into these three divinities as the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) and differentiate name and form.' By 'as this individual self' (<s>anena jīvenātmanā</s>) — teaching that the <s>jīva</s> has <s>Brahman</s> as its self — it shows that through the entry of <s>Brahman</s>-as-self-of-the-<s>jīva</s>, all non-conscious matter attains the status of a real entity, and that all such entities possess names. This is what is stated: the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>), being a mode (<s>prakāra</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> by virtue of being its body, has <s>Brahman</s> as its self — as another <s>śruti</s> states: 'That whose body is the self.' The entities in the forms of gods, humans, and the like, being modes that serve as the body of such a <s>jīva</s>, are all <s>Brahman</s>-natured. Therefore, all words known in the world as denoting [things] through the combination of root and suffix — 'god,' 'human,' '<s>rākṣasa</s>,' 'animal,' 'wild creature,' 'bird,' 'tree,' 'creeper,' 'wood,' 'stone,' 'grass,' 'pot,' 'cloth,' and the like — through the medium of the particular configured entity that each denotes, they are actually denotors of the aggregate extending up to the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) who is the inner controller of the <s>jīva</s> who identifies with that [entity].

children.text:
tam ādeśam prākṣyo yena aśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavati ity-ādāv eva praśāstita aiva jagad-upādānam iti hṛdi nihitam idānīm abhivyaktam / svayam eva jagad-upādānaṃ jagan-nimittaṃ ca sat tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya iti / tad etac-chabda-vācyaṃ paraṃ brahma sarva-jñaṃ sarva-śakti satya-saṅkalpam avāpta-samasta-kāmam api līlā-arthaṃ vicitra-ananta-cid-acin-miśra-jagad-rūpeṇa aham eva bahu syāṃ tad-arthaṃ prajāyeya iti svayam eva saṃkalpya sva-aṃśa-eka-deśād eva viyad-ādi-bhūtāni sṛṣṭvā punar api sa aiva sac-chabda-abhihitā parā devata aivam aikṣata hanta aham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenā atmana ānupraviśya nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi iti / anena jīvenā atmana īti -- jīvasya brahma-ātmakatvaṃ pratipādya brahma-ātma-jīva-anupraveśād eva kṛtsnasya acid-vastunaḥ pada-arthatvam evaṃ-bhūtasya eva sarvasya
vastuno nāma-bhāktvam iti ca darśayati / etad-uktaṃ bhavati --- jīva-ātmā tu brahmaṇaḥ śarīratayā prakāratvād brahma-ātmakaḥ / yasyā atmā śarīram iti śruty-antarāt / evaṃ-bhūtasya jīvasya śarīratayā prakāra-bhūtāni deva-manuṣya-ādi-saṃsthānāni vastūni iti brahma-ātmakāni tāni sarvāṇi / ato devo manuṣyo rākṣasaḥ paśur mṛgaḥ pakṣī vṛkṣo latā kāṣṭhaṃ śilā tṛṇaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭa ity-ādayaḥ sarve prakṛti-pratyaya-yogena abhidhāyakatayā prasiddhāḥ śabdā loke tat-tad-vācyatayā pratīyamāna-tat-tat-saṃsthāna-vastu-mukhena tad-abhimāni-jīva-tad-antaryāmi-parama-ātma-paryanta-saṃghātasya eva vācakā iti /

body.text: evaṃ samastacidacidātmakaprapañcasya sadupādānatāsannimittatāsadādhāratāsanniyamyatāsaccheṣatādi sarvaṃ ca sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhā ityādinā vistareṇa pratipādya kāryakāraṇabhāvādimukhenāitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tatsatyam iti kṛtsnasya jagato brahmātmakatvam eva satyam iti pratipādya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ sa evātmā kṛtsnaṃ jagat tasya śarīraṃ tasmāt tvaṃśabdavācyam api jīvaprakāraṃ brahmaiveti sarvasya brahmātmakatvaṃ pratijñātaṃ tat tvam asīti jīvaviśeṣa upasaṃhṛtam /
body.translated_text: Having thus extensively taught — by passages such as 'all these creatures, dear one, have Being as their root, Being as their abode, Being as their foundation' — that the entire manifest world of conscious and non-conscious [entities] has Being as its material cause, as its efficient cause, as its support, as its controller, and as its subsidiary, and having established through the cause-effect relationship and other means that 'all this has that as its self, that is the reality' — [establishing] that the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the entire universe alone is the truth — and [having taught that] of the entire universe it alone is the self, the entire universe is its body, and therefore even the <s>jīva</s> denoted by the word 'you' (<s>tvam</s>) is nothing but <s>Brahman</s> as possessing the <s>jīva</s> as its mode — the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of everything is declared, and in the individual <s>jīva</s> it is concluded: 'that you are' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>).

children.text: evaṃ samasta-cid-acid-ātmaka-prapañcasya sad-upādānatā-san-nimittatā-sad-ādhāratā-san-niyamyatā-sac-cheṣatā-ādi sarvaṃ ca san-mūlāḥ somya imāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sad-āyatanāḥ sat-pratiṣṭhā ity-ādinā vistareṇa pratipādya kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva-ādi-mukhena aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat-satyam iti kṛtsnasya jagato brahma-ātmakatvam eva satyam iti pratipādya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ sa evā atmā kṛtsnaṃ jagat tasya śarīraṃ tasmāt tvaṃ-śabda-vācyam api jīva-prakāraṃ brahma eva iti sarvasya brahma-ātmakatvaṃ pratijñātaṃ tat tvam asi iti jīva-viśeṣa upasaṃhṛtam /

body.text:
etad uktaṃ bhavati / aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvam iti cetanācetanaprapañcam idaṃ sarvam iti nirdiśya tasya prapañcasyaiṣa ātmeti pratipāditaḥ, prapañcoddeśena brahmātmakatvaṃ patipāditam ityarthaḥ / tad idaṃ brahmātmakatvaṃ kim ātmaśarīrabhāvenota svarūpeṇeti vivecanīyam / svarūpeṇa ced brahmaṇaḥ satyasaṅkalpādyaḥ -- tad aikṣata bahu syaṃ prajāyeyety upakramāvagatā bādhitā bhavanti / śarīrātmabhāvena ca tad ātmakatvaṃ śrutyantarād viśeṣato 'vagatam antaḥpraviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarvātmeti praśāsitṛtvarūpātmatvena sarveṣāṃ janānām antaḥpraviṣṭo 'taḥ sarvātmā sarveṣāṃ janānām ātmā sarvaṃ cāsya śarīram iti viśeṣato jñāyate brahmātmakatvam / ya ātmani tiṣṭhann ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam
antaro yamayati sa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛta iti ca / atrāpy anena jīvenātmanetīdam eva jñāyata iti pūrvam evoktam / ataḥ sarvasya cidacidvastuno brahmaśarīratvāt sarvaprakāraṃ sarvaśabdair brahmaivābhidhīyata iti tat tvam iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena jīvaśarīratayā jīvaprakāraṃ brahmaivābhihitam /
body.translated_text: This is what is stated: by 'all this has that as its self' — having indicated the entire manifest world of conscious and non-conscious [entities] as 'all this' and having taught that this [<s>Brahman</s>] is the self of that manifest world — the <s>Brahman</s>-nature [of all] through the indication of the manifest world is established. Now, this <s>Brahman</s>-nature — is it through the body-self relation or through essential nature? If through essential nature, then <s>Brahman</s>'s [qualities] such as true resolve and the like — understood from the opening 'it willed: may I become many, may I be born' — would be contradicted. But the self-hood through the body-self relation is specifically known from other <s>śruti</s> passages: 'Having entered within, the ruler of beings, the self of all' — as the self in the form of being the ruler of all beings, having entered within, therefore the self of all, the self of all beings, and everything is its body — thus the <s>Brahman</s>-nature is specifically known. Also: 'He who dwells in the self, who is interior to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body is the self, who controls the self from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal one.' Here too, by 'as this individual self' (<s>anena jīvenātmanā</s>), this very [teaching] is known, as was stated earlier. Therefore, since all conscious and non-conscious entities are the body of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> alone is denoted by all words in every way. Thus in 'that you are' (<s>tat tvam</s>), through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), <s>Brahman</s> itself, possessing the <s>jīva</s> as its mode by virtue of being the <s>jīva</s>'s body, is what is denoted.

children.text:
etad uktaṃ bhavati / aitad-ātmyam idaṃ sarvam iti cetana-acetana-prapañcam idaṃ sarvam iti nirdiśya tasya prapañcasya eṣa ātma īti pratipāditaḥ, prapañca-uddeśena brahma-ātmakatvaṃ patipāditam ity-arthaḥ / tad idaṃ brahma-ātmakatvaṃ kim ātma-śarīra-bhāvena uta sva-rūpeṇa iti vivecanīyam / sva-rūpeṇa ced brahmaṇaḥ satya-saṅkalpa-ādyaḥ --- tad aikṣata bahu syaṃ prajāyeya ity upakrama-avagatā bādhitā bhavanti / śarīra-ātma-bhāvena ca tad ātmakatvaṃ śruty-antarād viśeṣato 'vagatam antaḥpraviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarva-ātma īti praśāsitṛtva-rūpa-ātmatvena sarveṣāṃ janānām antaḥpraviṣṭo 'taḥ sarva-ātmā sarveṣāṃ janānām ātmā sarvaṃ ca asya śarīram iti viśeṣato jñāyate brahma-ātmakatvam / ya ātmani tiṣṭhann ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasya atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam
antaro yamayati sa ta ātma-antaryāmy-amṛta iti ca / atra apy anena jīvenā atmana īti idam eva jñāyata iti pūrvam eva uktam / ataḥ sarvasya cid-acid-vastuno brahma-śarīratvāt sarva-prakāraṃ sarva-śabdair brahma eva abhidhīyata iti tat tvam iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena jīva-śarīratayā jīva-prakāraṃ brahma eva abhihitam /

body.text:
evam abhihite saty ayam artho jñāyate -- tvam iti yaḥ pūrvaṃ dehasyādhiṣṭhātṛtayā pratītaḥ sa paramātmaśarīratayā paramātmaprakārabhūtaḥ paramātmaparyantaḥ / atas tvam iti śabdas tvatprakāraviśiṣṭaṃ tvadantaryāmiṇam evācaṣṭa iti / anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti brahmātmakatayaiva jīvasya śarīriṇaḥ svanāmabhāktvāt tat tvam iti sāmānādhikaraṇyapravṛttayor dvayor api padayor brahmaiva vācyam / tatra ca tatpadaṃ jagatkāraṇabhūtaṃ sakalakalyāṇaguṇagaṇākaraṃ nirvadyaṃ nirvikāram ācaṣṭe / tvam iti ca tad eva brahma jīvāntaryāmirūpeṇa saśarīraprakāraviśiṣṭam ācaṣṭe / tad evaṃ pravṛttinimittabhedenaikasmin brahmaṇy eva tat tvam iti dvayoḥ padayor vṛttir uktā / brahmaṇo niravadyaṃ nirvikāraṃ
sakalakalyāṇaguṇagaṇākaratvaṃ jagatkāraṇatvaṃ cābādhitam /
body.translated_text: When it is thus stated, this meaning is known: 'you' — he who was previously understood as the controller of the body — is, by being the body of the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), a mode of the supreme Self, terminating in the supreme Self. Therefore the word 'you' actually denotes your inner controller who is qualified by you as his mode. Since the <s>jīva</s> has <s>Brahman</s> as its self — [as stated] 'having entered as this individual self, I shall differentiate name and form' — the <s>jīva</s>, the embodied one, has its own name by virtue of its <s>Brahman</s>-nature. Therefore, both words in 'that you are' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>), which operate through co-referentiality, denote <s>Brahman</s> alone. Therein, the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) denotes [<s>Brahman</s>] as the cause of the universe, the repository of the entire multitude of auspicious qualities, faultless, and unchanging. The word 'you' (<s>tvam</s>) denotes that same <s>Brahman</s> as qualified by possessing the embodied [<s>jīva</s>] as its mode in the form of the inner controller of the <s>jīva</s>. Thus, the usage of both words 'that' and 'you' is stated with reference to the one <s>Brahman</s> alone through a difference in the grounds of application. <s>Brahman</s>'s being faultless, unchanging, the repository of the entire multitude of auspicious qualities, and the cause of the universe remains uncontradicted.

children.text:
evam abhihite saty ayam artho jñāyate --- tvam iti yaḥ pūrvaṃ dehasya adhiṣṭhātṛtayā pratītaḥ sa parama-ātma-śarīratayā parama-ātma-prakāra-bhūtaḥ parama-ātma-paryantaḥ / atas tvam iti śabdas tvat-prakāra-viśiṣṭaṃ tvad-antaryāmiṇam evā acaṣṭa iti / anena jīvena atmana ānupraviśya nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi iti brahma-ātmakataya aiva jīvasya śarīriṇaḥ sva-nāma-bhāktvāt tat tvam iti sāmānādhikaraṇya-pravṛttayor dvayor api padayor brahma eva vācyam / tatra ca tat-padaṃ jagat-kāraṇa-bhūtaṃ sakala-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-ākaraṃ nirvadyaṃ nirvikāram ācaṣṭe / tvam iti ca tad eva brahma jīva-antaryāmi-rūpeṇa sa-śarīra-prakāra-viśiṣṭam ācaṣṭe / tad evaṃ pravṛtti-nimitta-bhedena ekasmin brahmaṇy eva tat tvam iti dvayoḥ padayor vṛttir uktā / brahmaṇo niravadyaṃ nirvikāraṃ
sakala-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-ākaratvaṃ jagat-kāraṇatvaṃ ca abādhitam /

body.text:
aśrutavedāntāḥ puruṣāḥ padārthāḥ sarve jīvātmanaś ca brahmātmakā iti na paśyati sarvaśabdānāṃ ca kevaleṣu tattatpadārtheṣu vācyaikadeśeṣu vācyaparyavasānaṃ manyante / idānīṃ vedāntavākyaśravaṇena brahmakāryatayā tadantaryāmitayā ca sarvasya brahmātmakatvaṃ sarvaśabdānāṃ tattatprakārasaṃsthitabrahmavācitvaṃ ca jānanti / nanv evaṃ gavādiśabdānāṃ tattatpadārthavācitayā vyutpattir bādhitā syāt / naivaṃ sarve śabdā acijjīvaviśiṣṭasya paramātmano vācakā ity uktam / nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīty atra / tatra laukikāḥ puruṣāḥ śabdaṃ vyāharantaḥ śabdavācye pradhānāṃśasya paramātmanaḥ pratyakṣādyaparicchedyatvād vācyaikadeśabhūte vācyasamāptiṃ manyante / vedāntaśravaṇena ca vyutpattiḥ pūryate / evam eva vaidikāḥ
sarve śabdāḥ paramātmaparyantān svārthān bodhayanti / vaidikā eva sarve śabdā vedādav uddhṛtyoddhṛtya pareṇaiva brahmaṇā sarvapadārthān pūrvavat sṛṣṭvā teṣu paramātmaparyanteṣu pūrvavan nāmatayā prayuktāḥ / tad āha manuḥ --
sarveṣāṃ tu nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthak pṛthak /
vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthaksaṃsthāś ca nirmame //
iti / saṃsthāḥ saṃsthānāni rūpāṇīti yāvat / āha ca bhagavān parāśaraḥ --
nāma rūpaṃ bhūtānāṃ kṛtyānāṃ prapañcanam /
vedaśabdebhya evādau daivādīnāṃ cakāra saḥ //
iti / śrutiś ca -- sūryācandramasau dhātā yathāpūrvam akalpayad iti / sūryādīn pūrvavat parikalpya nāmāni ca pūrvavac cakāra ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Persons who have not heard the <s>Vedānta</s> do not see that all objects and the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) are of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and they consider that all words terminate in only a portion of their referent — the respective particular objects alone. Now, through hearing the <s>Vedānta</s> statements, they know that everything is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, since everything is an effect of <s>Brahman</s> and since <s>Brahman</s> is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of all, and [they know] that all words denote <s>Brahman</s> as qualified by the respective modes. If it be objected that the conventional meaning (<s>vyutpatti</s>) of words like 'cow' etc. as denoting their respective objects would be contradicted — that is not so. It has been stated that all words denote the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) as qualified by non-conscious matter and conscious selves. As stated in [the <s>śruti</s>]: 'Let me differentiate names and forms.' Therein, worldly persons, when uttering a word, consider that the denotation terminates in a portion of the referent — the particular object — because the <s>Paramātman</s>, who is the principal part of the referent, is not apprehensible by perception and other [ordinary means of knowledge]. Through hearing the <s>Vedānta</s>, the conventional understanding is completed. In this way, all Vedic words convey their meanings up to and including the <s>Paramātman</s>. All words are indeed Vedic — having been extracted [by <s>Brahman</s>] at the beginning from the <s>Veda</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself, having created all objects as before, employed [words] as names for those [objects] that extend up to the <s>Paramātman</s>, just as before. Thus says <s>Manu</s>:
'The names and actions of all [beings], separately,
he fashioned at the beginning from the words of the <s>Veda</s>, along with their distinct forms.'
'Forms' means configurations, appearances. And the blessed <s>Parāśara</s> says:
'The names and forms of beings, the elaboration of actions —
he made from the words of the <s>Veda</s> at the beginning, for the divine and other [beings].'
And the <s>śruti</s>: 'The Creator fashioned the sun and the moon as before.' The meaning is: having conceived the sun and other [entities] as before, he made their names as before.

children.text:
aśruta-vedāntāḥ puruṣāḥ pada-arthāḥ sarve jīva-ātmanaś ca brahma-ātmakā iti na paśyati sarva-śabdānāṃ ca kevaleṣu tat-tat-pada-artheṣu vācya-eka-deśeṣu vācya-paryavasānaṃ manyante / idānīṃ vedānta-vākya-śravaṇena brahma-kāryatayā tad-antaryāmitayā ca sarvasya brahma-ātmakatvaṃ sarva-śabdānāṃ tat-tat-prakāra-saṃsthita-brahma-vācitvaṃ ca jānanti / nanv evaṃ gava-ādi-śabdānāṃ tat-tat-pada-artha-vācitayā vyutpattir bādhitā syāt / na evaṃ sarve śabdā acij-jīva-viśiṣṭasya parama-ātmano vācakā ity uktam / nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi ity atra / tatra laukikāḥ puruṣāḥ śabdaṃ vyāharantaḥ śabda-vācye pradhāna-aṃśasya parama-ātmanaḥ pratyakṣa-ādy-aparicchedyatvād vācya-eka-deśa-bhūte vācya-samāptiṃ manyante / vedānta-śravaṇena ca vyutpattiḥ pūryate / evam eva vaidikāḥ
sarve śabdāḥ parama-ātma-paryantān sva-arthān bodhayanti / vaidikā eva sarve śabdā veda-ādav uddhṛtya uddhṛtya pareṇa eva brahmaṇā sarva-pada-arthān pūrvavat sṛṣṭvā teṣu parama-ātma-paryanteṣu pūrvavan nāmatayā prayuktāḥ / tad āha manuḥ ---
sarveṣāṃ tu nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthak pṛthak /
veda-śabdebhya evā adau pṛthak-saṃsthāś ca nirmame //
iti / saṃsthāḥ saṃsthānāni rūpāṇi iti yāvat / āha ca bhagavān parāśaraḥ ---
nāma rūpaṃ bhūtānāṃ kṛtyānāṃ prapañcanam /
veda-śabdebhya evā adau daiva-ādīnāṃ cakāra saḥ //
iti / śrutiś ca --- sūryā-candra-masau dhātā yathā-pūrvam akalpayad iti / sūrya-ādīn pūrvavat parikalpya nāmāni ca pūrvavac cakāra ity-arthaḥ /

body.text: evaṃ jagadbrahmaṇor ananyatvaṃ prapañcitam / tenaikena jñātena sarvasya jñātato 'papāditā bhavati / sarvasya brahmakāryatvapratipādanena tadātmakatayaiva satyatvaṃ nānyatheti tat satyam ityuktam / yathā dṛṣṭānte sarvasya mṛdvikārasya mṛdātmanaiva satyatvam /
body.translated_text: Thus the non-difference (<s>ananyatva</s>) of the world and <s>Brahman</s> has been elaborated. Thereby, the claim that by knowing one, all is known, is established. Through the teaching that everything is an effect of <s>Brahman</s>, its reality is established precisely as being of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> and not otherwise — hence 'that is the Real' (<s>tat satyam</s>) is stated. Just as in the illustration, all modifications of clay have their reality only as being of the nature of clay.

children.text: evaṃ jagad-brahmaṇor ananyatvaṃ prapañcitam / tena ekena jñātena sarvasya jñātato 'papāditā bhavati / sarvasya brahma-kāryatva-pratipādanena tad-ātmakataya aiva satyatvaṃ na anyatha īti tat satyam ity-uktam / yathā dṛṣṭānte sarvasya mṛd-vikārasya mṛd-ātmana aiva satyatvam /

body.text: śodhakavākyāny api niravadyaṃ sarvakalyāṇaguṇākaraṃ paraṃ brahma bodhayanti / sarvapratyanīkākāratābodhane 'pi tattatpratyanīkākāratāyāṃ bhedasyāvarjanīyatvān na nirviśeṣavastusiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: The purificatory statements (<s>śodhakavākya</s>) too reveal the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> as faultless and the repository of all auspicious qualities. Even when they teach that [<s>Brahman</s>] is of a nature opposed to all [defects], since difference in each [statement about] the opposed nature is unavoidable, the establishment of a reality without attributes (<s>nirviśeṣa</s>) does not follow.

children.text: śodhaka-vākyāny api niravadyaṃ sarva-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ākaraṃ paraṃ brahma bodhayanti / sarva-pratyanīka-ākāratā-bodhane 'pi tat-tat-pratyanīka-ākāratāyāṃ bhedasya avarjanīyatvān na nirviśeṣa-vastu-siddhiḥ /

body.text:
nanu ca jñānamātraṃ brahmeti pratipādite nirviśeṣajñānamātraṃ brahmeti niścīyate / naivaṃ / svarūpanirūpaṇadharmaśabdā hi dharmamukhena svarūpam api pratipādayanti / gavādiśabdavat / tad āha sūtrakāraḥ -- tadguṇasāratvāt tadvyapadeśaḥ prājñavat / yāvad ātmabhāvitatvāc ca na doṣa iti / jñānena dharmeṇa svarūpam api nirūpitaṃ na jñānamātraṃ brahmeti / katham idam avagamyata iti ced yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavid ityādijñātṛtvaśruteḥ parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca / vijñātāram are kena vijānīyād ityādiśrutiśatasamadhigatam idam / jñānasya dharmamātratvād dharmamātrasyaikasya vastutvapratipādanānupapatteś ca / ataḥ satyajñānādipadāni svārthabhūtajñānādiviśiṣṭam eva brahma pratipādayanti / tat tvam iti dvayor
api padayoḥ svārthaprahāṇena nirviśeṣavastusvarūpopasthāpanaparatve mukhyārthaparityāgaś ca /
body.translated_text: If it be said that when <s>Brahman</s> is taught as 'mere knowledge,' it is determined that <s>Brahman</s> is mere attributeless knowledge — that is not so. For words that are attributes defining the essential nature (<s>svarūpanirūpaṇadharma</s>) convey the essential nature as well, through the attribute — just like words such as 'cow.' Thus says the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>): 'Because that [knowledge] is the essence of its qualities, it is so designated — like the intelligent [self]. And there is no fault because it [knowledge] is inherent in the nature of the self.' Knowledge is an attribute through which the essential nature is also defined — it is not [the case] that <s>Brahman</s> is mere knowledge. How is this understood? From <s>śrutis</s> declaring knower-hood such as 'He who is omniscient, who knows all,' and 'His supreme power is heard to be of various kinds — inherent knowledge, strength, and action,' and from hundreds of <s>śrutis</s> such as 'By what should one know the knower?' Because knowledge is merely an attribute, and because it is untenable that a single mere attribute constitutes a real entity. Therefore, words like '<s>satya</s>' (reality), '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge), etc. convey <s>Brahman</s> as qualified by knowledge and other [attributes] that constitute its essential nature. If both words in '<s>tat tvam</s>' (That thou [art]) are taken as aimed at presenting the mere essential nature devoid of attributes, by abandoning their own primary meanings, there would be abandonment of the primary meaning.

children.text:
nanu ca jñāna-mātraṃ brahma iti pratipādite nirviśeṣa-jñāna-mātraṃ brahma iti niścīyate / na evaṃ / sva-rūpa-nirūpaṇa-dharma-śabdā hi dharma-mukhena sva-rūpam api pratipādayanti / gava-ādi-śabdavat / tad āha sūtra-kāraḥ --- tad-guṇa-sāratvāt tad-vyapadeśaḥ prājñavat / yāvad ātma-bhāvitatvāc ca na doṣa iti / jñānena dharmeṇa sva-rūpam api nirūpitaṃ na jñāna-mātraṃ brahma iti / katham idam avagamyata iti ced yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vid ity-ādi-jñātṛtva-śruteḥ parāsya śaktir vividha aiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca / vijñātāram are kena vijānīyād ity-ādi-śruti-śata-samadhigatam idam / jñānasya dharma-mātratvād dharma-mātrasya ekasya vastutva-pratipādana-anupapatteś ca / ataḥ satya-jñāna-ādi-padāni sva-artha-bhūta-jñāna-ādi-viśiṣṭam eva brahma pratipādayanti / tat tvam iti dvayor
api padayoḥ sva-artha-prahāṇena nirviśeṣa-vastu-sva-rūpa-upasthāpana-paratve mukhya-artha-parityāgaś ca /

body.text:
nanv aikye tātparyaniścayān na lakṣaṇādoṣaḥ / so 'yaṃ devadatta itivat / yathā so 'yam ity atra sa iti śabdena deśāntarakālāntarasaṃbandhī puruṣaḥ pratīyata ayam iti ca saṃnihitadeśavartamānakālasaṃbandhī, tayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyenāikyaṃ pratīyate / tatraikasya yugapadviruddhadeśakālasaṃbandhitayā pratītir na ghaṭata iti dvayor padayoḥ svarūpamātropasthāpanaparatvaṃ svarūpasya cāikyaṃ pratipadyata iti cen naitad evam / so 'yaṃ devadatta ity atrāpi lakṣaṇāgandho na vidyate / virodhābhāvāt / ekasya bhūtavartamānakriyādvayasaṃbaṃdho na viruddhaḥ / deśāntarasthitir bhūtvā saṃnihitadeśasthitir vartate / ato bhūtavartamānakriyādvayasaṃbandhitayāikyapratipādanam aviruddham / deśadvayavirodhaś ca kālabhedena parihṛtaḥ / lakṣaṇāyām api na dvayor api padayor
lakṣaṇāsamāśrayaṇam / etenaiva lakṣitena virodhaparihārāt / lakṣaṇābhāva evoktaḥ / deśāntarasaṃbandhitayā bhūtasyaivānyadeśasaṃbandhitayā vartamānatvāvirodhāt /
body.translated_text: If it be said that since the purport is established as identity, there is no fault of secondary meaning — like 'This is that <s>Devadatta</s>': Just as in 'This is that [<s>Devadatta</s>],' by the word 'that' a person associated with another place and another time is cognized, and by the word 'this' one associated with the proximate place and the present time [is cognized], and through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) their identity is cognized — therein, since the cognition of one individual as being simultaneously related to contradictory places and times does not hold, the two words are taken as aimed at presenting the mere essential nature, and the identity of the essential natures is understood — if this be said, that is not so. Even in 'This is that <s>Devadatta</s>,' there is not the slightest trace of secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), because there is no contradiction. The relation of a single individual to both past and present actions is not contradictory. Having been situated in another place [in the past], he is now situated in the proximate place. Therefore, the teaching of identity through the relation to both past and present actions is not contradictory. And the contradiction of two places is resolved by the difference in time. Even if secondary meaning were applied, it would not be resorted to for both words — because the contradiction is resolved by this very indicated [meaning]. The absence of secondary meaning has thus been stated — because there is no contradiction between being past with relation to another place and being present with relation to another place.

children.text:
nanv aikye tātparya-niścayān na lakṣaṇā-doṣaḥ / so 'yaṃ deva-datta itivat / yathā so 'yam ity atra sa iti śabdena deśa-antara-kāla-antara-saṃbandhī puruṣaḥ pratīyata ayam iti ca saṃnihita-deśa-vartamāna-kāla-saṃbandhī, tayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena aikyaṃ pratīyate / tatra ekasya yugapad-viruddha-deśa-kāla-saṃbandhitayā pratītir na ghaṭata iti dvayor padayoḥ sva-rūpa-mātra-upasthāpana-paratvaṃ sva-rūpasya ca aikyaṃ pratipadyata iti cen na etad evam / so 'yaṃ deva-datta ity atra api lakṣaṇā-gandho na vidyate / virodha-abhāvāt / ekasya bhūta-vartamāna-kriyā-dvaya-saṃbaṃdho na viruddhaḥ / deśa-antara-sthitir bhūtvā saṃnihita-deśa-sthitir vartate / ato bhūta-vartamāna-kriyā-dvaya-saṃbandhitaya āikya-pratipādanam aviruddham / deśa-dvaya-virodhaś ca kāla-bhedena parihṛtaḥ / lakṣaṇāyām api na dvayor api padayor
lakṣaṇā-samāśrayaṇam / etena eva lakṣitena virodha-parihārāt / lakṣaṇā-abhāva eva uktaḥ / deśa-antara-saṃbandhitayā bhūtasya eva anya-deśa-saṃbandhitayā vartamānatva-avirodhāt /

body.text: evam atrāpi jagatkāraṇabūtasyaiva parasya brahmaṇo jīvāntaryāmitayā jīvātmatvam aviruddham iti pratipāditam / yathā bhūtayor eva hi dvayor aikyaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīyate / tatparityāgena svarūpamātrāikyaṃ na sāmānādhikaraṇyārthaḥ -- bhinnapravṛttinimittānāṃ śabdānām ekasminn arthe vṛttiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyam iti hi tadvidaḥ / tathābhūtayor aikyam upapāditam asmābhiḥ / upakramavirodhyupasaṃhārapadena vākyatātparyaniścayaś ca na ghaṭate / upakrame hi tad aikṣata bahu syām ityādinā satyasaṃkalpatvaṃ jagadekakāraṇatvam apy uktam / tadvirodhi cāvidyāśrayatvādi brahmaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Likewise here too, it is taught that there is no contradiction in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is the cause of the world, being the self of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) by virtue of being the inner controller of the <s>jīva</s>. Just as the identity of two existing [entities] is cognized through co-referentiality — abandoning that [co-referentiality] and [positing] identity of mere essential natures is not the meaning of co-referentiality. For those who know say: 'The occurrence of words with different grounds of application in a single referent is co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>).' The identity of [two] such [entities] has been established by us. And the determination of the purport of the sentence through a concluding statement that contradicts the introductory statement does not hold. For in the introduction, 'It willed: may I become many' — by this, the nature of having true will (<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>) and being the sole cause of the world has been stated. And attributing to <s>Brahman</s> [properties like] being the locus of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) would contradict that.

children.text: evam atra api jagat-kāraṇa-būtasya eva parasya brahmaṇo jīva-antaryāmitayā jīva-ātmatvam aviruddham iti pratipāditam / yathā bhūtayor eva hi dvayor aikyaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīyate / tat-parityāgena sva-rūpa-mātra-aikyaṃ na sāmānādhikaraṇya-arthaḥ --- bhinna-pravṛtti-nimittānāṃ śabdānām ekasminn arthe vṛttiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyam iti hi tad-vidaḥ / tathā-bhūtayor aikyam upapāditam asmābhiḥ / upakrama-virodhy-upasaṃhāra-padena vākya-tātparya-niścayaś ca na ghaṭate / upakrame hi tad aikṣata bahu syām ity-ādinā satya-saṃkalpatvaṃ jagad-eka-kāraṇatvam apy uktam / tad-virodhi ca avidyā-āśrayatva-ādi brahmaṇaḥ /

body.text: api cārthabhedatatsaṃsargaviśeṣabodhanakṛtapadavākyasya svarūpatālabdhapramāṇabhāvasya śabdasya nirviśeṣavastubodhanāsāmarthān na nirviśeṣavastuni śabdaḥ pramāṇam / nirviśeṣa ityādiśabdās tu kenacid viśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭatayāvagatasya vastuno vastvantaragataviśeṣaniṣedhaparatayā bodhakāḥ / itarathā teṣam apy anavabodhakatvam eva / prakṛtipratyayarūpeṇa padasyaivānekaviśeṣagarbhatvād anekapadārthasaṃsargabodhakatvāc ca vākyasya /
body.translated_text: Moreover, since a word — which is a sentence or a component word that functions by conveying differences of meaning and their specific connections, and whose status as a means of knowledge is obtained only through [conveying] essential nature [with attributes] — is incapable of conveying an attributeless reality (<s>nirviśeṣavastu</s>), the word is not a valid means of knowledge regarding an attributeless reality. Words like '<s>nirviśeṣa</s>' (without attributes) etc. function by negating the attributes of other things with respect to a reality that has already been cognized as qualified by some attribute — not by conveying an attributeless thing itself. Otherwise, they too would convey nothing at all — because a word in the form of a root and suffix inherently contains multiple qualifications, and because a sentence conveys the connection of multiple word-meanings.

children.text: api ca artha-bheda-tat-saṃsarga-viśeṣa-bodhana-kṛta-pada-vākyasya sva-rūpatā-ālabdha-pramāṇa-bhāvasya śabdasya nirviśeṣa-vastu-bodhana-asāmarthān na nirviśeṣa-vastuni śabdaḥ pramāṇam / nirviśeṣa ity-ādi-śabdās tu kenacid viśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭataya āvagatasya vastuno vastv-antara-gata-viśeṣa-niṣedha-paratayā bodhakāḥ / itarathā teṣam apy anavabodhakatvam eva / prakṛti-pratyaya-rūpeṇa padasya eva aneka-viśeṣa-garbhatvād aneka-pada-artha-saṃsarga-bodhakatvāc ca vākyasya /

body.text: atha syāt -- nāsmābhir nirviśeṣe svayaṃprakāśe vastuni śabdaḥ pramāṇam ity ucyate / svataḥsiddhasya pramāṇānapekṣatvāt / sarvaiḥ śabdais taduparāgaviśeṣā jñātṛtvādayaḥ sarve nirasyante / sarveṣu viśeṣeṣu nivṛtteṣu vastumātram anavacchinnaṃ svayaṃprakāśaṃ svata evāvatiṣṭhata iti / naitad evam / kena śabdena tadvastu nirdiśya tadgataviśeṣā nirasyante / jñaptimātraśabdeneti cen na / so 'pi saviśeṣam eva vastvavalambate / prakṛtipratyayarūpeṇa viśeṣagarbhatvāt / jñā avabodhana iti sakarmakaḥ sakartṛkaḥ kriyāviśeṣaḥ kriyāntaravyāvartakasvabhāvaviśeṣaś ca prakṛtyāvagamyate / pratyayena ca liṅgasaṃkhyādayaḥ / svataḥsiddhāv apy etatsvabhāvaviśeṣavirahe siddhir eva na syāt / anyasādhanasvabhāvatayā hi jñapteḥ svataḥsiddhir ucyate /
body.translated_text: Now if one were to say: 'We do not claim that a word is the means of knowledge for an attributeless, self-luminous reality, since what is self-established does not require a means of knowledge. By all words, particular superimpositions upon it — such as knower-hood — are negated. When all attributes are removed, the mere reality, unlimited and self-luminous, remains by itself' — that is not so. By what word is that reality indicated so that the attributes belonging to it may be negated? If [one says] 'by the word <s>jñapti</s> (cognition) alone' — no, for even that word apprehends a reality with attributes, because it inherently contains qualifications in the form of root and suffix. By the root '<s>jñā</s>' (to know), a specific action that is transitive and has an agent, and a specific nature that distinguishes it from other actions, is conveyed. And by the suffix, gender, number, etc. [are conveyed]. Even if [the reality] is self-established, without these specific attributes, there would be no establishment at all. For the self-establishment of cognition is said to be of the nature of being a means for [establishing] something else.

children.text: atha syāt --- na asmābhir nirviśeṣe svayaṃ-prakāśe vastuni śabdaḥ pramāṇam ity ucyate / svataḥsiddhasya pramāṇa-anapekṣatvāt / sarvaiḥ śabdais tad-uparāga-viśeṣā jñātṛtva-ādayaḥ sarve nirasyante / sarveṣu viśeṣeṣu nivṛtteṣu vastu-mātram anavacchinnaṃ svayaṃ-prakāśaṃ svata eva avatiṣṭhata iti / na etad evam / kena śabdena tad-vastu nirdiśya tad-gata-viśeṣā nirasyante / jñapti-mātra-śabdena iti cen na / so 'pi saviśeṣam eva vastv-avalambate / prakṛti-pratyaya-rūpeṇa viśeṣa-garbhatvāt / jñā avabodhana iti sa-karmakaḥ sa-kartṛkaḥ kriyā-viśeṣaḥ kriyā-antara-vyāvartaka-sva-bhāva-viśeṣaś ca prakṛtya āvagamyate / pratyayena ca liṅga-saṃkhyā-ādayaḥ / svataḥ-siddhāv apy etat-sva-bhāva-viśeṣa-virahe siddhir eva na syāt / anya-sādhana-sva-bhāvatayā hi jñapteḥ svataḥ-siddhir ucyate /

body.text: brahmasvarūpaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sarvadā svayam eva prakāśate cen na tasminn anyadharmādhyāsaḥ saṃbhavati / na hi rajjusvarūpe 'vabhāsamāne sarpatvādir adhyasyate / ata eva hi bhavadbhir ācchādikāvidyābhyupagamyate / tataś ca śāstrīyanivartakajñānasya brahmaṇi tirohitāṃśo viṣayaḥ / anyathā tasya nivartakatvaṃ ca na syāt / adhiṣṭhānātirekirajjutvaprakāśanena hi sarpatvaṃ bādhyate / ekaś ced viśeṣo jñānamātre vastuni śabdenābhidhīyate sa ca brahmaviśeṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti sarvaśrutipratipāditasarvaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaṃ brahma bhavati /
body.translated_text: If the entire essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> is always self-luminous, then the superimposition of the attributes of other things upon it would not be possible. For when the essential nature of a rope is manifest, serpent-hood and the like are not superimposed upon it. It is precisely for this reason that you [Advaitins] postulate a concealing <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Consequently, the object of the scripture-born removing knowledge is the aspect of <s>Brahman</s> that is concealed. Otherwise, that [knowledge] would have no removing function. For it is by revealing the rope-ness that transcends the substratum that serpent-hood is sublated. If even one attribute is predicated of the reality that is 'mere knowledge' by a word, and if that becomes an attribute of <s>Brahman</s>, then <s>Brahman</s> is qualified by all the attributes taught by all the <s>śrutis</s>.

children.text: brahma-sva-rūpaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sarvadā svayam eva prakāśate cen na tasminn anya-dharma-adhyāsaḥ saṃbhavati / na hi rajju-sva-rūpe 'vabhāsamāne sarpatva-ādir adhyasyate / ata eva hi bhavadbhir ācchādika-avidya ābhyupagamyate / tataś ca śāstrīya-nivartaka-jñānasya brahmaṇi tirohita-aṃśo viṣayaḥ / anyathā tasya nivartakatvaṃ ca na syāt / adhiṣṭhāna-atireki-rajjutva-prakāśanena hi sarpatvaṃ bādhyate / ekaś ced viśeṣo jñāna-mātre vastuni śabdena abhidhīyate sa ca brahma-viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavati iti sarva-śruti-pratipādita-sarva-viśeṣaṇa-viśiṣṭaṃ brahma bhavati /

body.text:
ataḥ prāmāṇikānāṃ na kenāpi pramāṇena nirviśeṣavastusiddhiḥ / nirvikalpakapratyakṣe 'pi saviśeṣam eva vastu pratīyate / anyathā savikalpake so 'yam iti pūrvāvagataprakāraviśiṣṭapratyayānupapatteḥ / vastusaṃsthānaviśeṣarūpatvād gotvāder nirvikalpatadaśāyām api sasaṃsthānam eva vastv ittham iti pratīyate / dvitīyādipratyayeṣu tasya saṃsthānaviśeṣasyānekavastuniṣṭhatāmātraṃ pratīyate / saṃsthānarūpaprakārākhyasya padārthasyānekavastuniṣṭhatayānekavastuviśeṣaṇatvaṃ dvitīyādipratyayāvagamyam iti dvitīyādipratyayāḥ savikalpakā ity ucyante / ata evaikasya padārthasya bhinnābhinnatvarūpeṇa dvyātmakatvaṃ viruddhaṃ pratyuktam / saṃsthānasya saṃsthāninaḥ prakāratayā padārthāntaratvam / prakāratvād eva pṛthaksiddhyanarhatvaṃ pṛthaganupalambhaś
ceti na dvyātmakatvasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, for those who follow valid means of knowledge, the existence of a <s>nirviśeṣa</s> (qualificationless) reality is not established by any <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). Even in <s>nirvikalpaka pratyakṣa</s> (indeterminate perception), only a qualified (<s>saviśeṣa</s>) object is cognized; otherwise, in <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate perception), the cognition of the form 'this is that same thing,' which apprehends an object as qualified by a mode previously cognized, would be impossible. Since <s>gotva</s> (cowness) and such universals are of the nature of a particular configuration of the object, even in the indeterminate stage, the object is cognized as possessing a configuration, in this particular manner. In the second and subsequent cognitions, what is cognized is merely the fact that this particular configuration belongs to many objects. That the entity called a mode (<s>prakāra</s>), which is of the nature of a configuration, qualifies many objects by virtue of its belonging to many objects — this is what is understood from the second and subsequent cognitions; hence those subsequent cognitions are called <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate). For this very reason, the objection that a single entity has a contradictory dual nature — being both identical with and different from [its substrate] — is answered: the configuration is a distinct entity from the configured thing by virtue of being its mode (<s>prakāra</s>). Because it is a mode, it does not merit independent establishment, and it is never perceived independently — hence the alleged dual nature is not established.

children.text:
ataḥ prāmāṇikānāṃ na kena api pramāṇena nirviśeṣa-vastu-siddhiḥ / nirvikalpaka-pratyakṣe 'pi saviśeṣam eva vastu pratīyate / anyathā savikalpake so 'yam iti pūrva-avagata-prakāra-viśiṣṭa-pratyaya-anupapatteḥ / vastu-saṃsthāna-viśeṣa-rūpatvād gotva-āder nirvikalpata-daśāyām api sasaṃsthānam eva vastv ittham iti pratīyate / dvitīya-ādi-pratyayeṣu tasya saṃsthāna-viśeṣasya aneka-vastu-niṣṭhatā-mātraṃ pratīyate / saṃsthāna-rūpa-prakāra-ākhyasya pada-arthasya aneka-vastu-niṣṭhataya āneka-vastu-viśeṣaṇatvaṃ dvitīya-ādi-pratyaya-avagamyam iti dvitīya-ādi-pratyayāḥ savikalpakā ity ucyante / ata eva ekasya pada-arthasya bhinna-abhinnatva-rūpeṇa dvy-ātmakatvaṃ viruddhaṃ pratyuktam / saṃsthānasya saṃsthāninaḥ prakāratayā pada-artha-antaratvam / prakāratvād eva pṛthak-siddhy-anarhatvaṃ pṛthag-anupalambhaś
ca iti na dvy-ātmakatva-siddhiḥ /

body.text:
api ca nirviśeṣavastvādinā svayaṃprakāśe vastuni taduparāgaviśeṣāḥ sarvaiḥ śabdair nirasyanta iti vadatā ke te śabdā niṣedhakā iti vaktavyam / vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam iti vikāranāmadheyayor vācārambhaṇamātratvāt / yat tatra kāraṇatayopalakṣyate vastumātraṃ tad eva satyam anyad asatyam itīyaṃ śrutir vadatīti cen naitad upapadyate / ekasmin vijñāte sarvaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti pratijñāte 'nyajñānenānyajñānāsaṃbhavaṃ manvānasyaikam eva vastu vikārādyavasthāviśeṣeṇa pāramārthikenaiva nāmarūpam avasthitaṃ cet tatraikasmin vijñāte tasmād vilakṣaṇasaṃsthānāntaram api tad eveti tatra dṛṣṭānto 'yaṃ nidarśitaḥ / nātra kasyacid viśeṣasya niṣedhakaḥ ko 'pi śabdo dṛśyate / vācārambhaṇam iti vācā vyavahāreṇārabhyata
ity ārambhaṇam / piṇḍarūpeṇāvasthitāyāḥ mṛttikāyā nāma vānyadvyavahāraś cānyaḥ / ghaṭaśarāvādirūpeṇāvasthitāyās tasyā eva mṛttikāyā anyāni nāmadheyāni vyavahārāś cānyaddaśāḥ / tathāpi sarvatra mṛttikādravyam ekam eva nānāsaṃsthānanānānāmadheyābhyāṃ nānāvyavahāreṇa cārabhyata ityetad eva satyam ity anenānyajñānenānyajñānasaṃbhavo nidarśitaḥ / nātra kiṃcid vastu niṣidhyata iti pūrvam evāyam arthaḥ prapañcitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, one who advocates a <s>nirviśeṣa</s> (qualificationless) reality and claims that all words negate the various superimpositions upon a self-luminous reality must specify: which are these words that effect such negation? If it is argued that by the text '<s>vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam, mṛttikety eva satyam</s>' ('the modification is a mere verbal designation; clay alone is real' — <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.1.4), since modification and name are mere verbal designations, whatever is identified there as the cause is reality as such and nothing else, and this is what the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) teaches — this is untenable. When it is promised that 'by knowing one thing, everything becomes known,' and one considers that the knowledge of one thing could not yield knowledge of another, then if one single substance exists in its real modifications and states with real name and form, the illustration is given to show that upon knowing that one thing in one state, the same thing in another state — even though of a different configuration — is also known. No word negating any qualification whatsoever is seen here. '<s>Vācārambhaṇam</s>' means: it is commenced (<s>ārabhyate</s>) by speech, i.e., by verbal usage. When clay is in the state of a lump, it has one name and one set of usages; when that very same clay is in the state of a pot, saucer, and so on, it has other names and other usages corresponding to those different states. Even so, the clay substance is one throughout — it is commenced upon, i.e., referred to, by diverse configurations, diverse names, and diverse usages — this alone is the truth. By this, it is demonstrated how the knowledge of one thing yields the knowledge of another. Nothing whatsoever is negated here — this meaning has already been elaborated previously.

children.text:
api ca nirviśeṣa-vastv-ādinā svayaṃprakāśe vastuni tad-uparāga-viśeṣāḥ sarvaiḥ śabdair nirasyanta iti vadatā ke te śabdā niṣedhakā iti vaktavyam / vācā ārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāma-dheyaṃ mṛttika īty eva satyam iti vikāra-nāma-dheyayor vācā ārambhaṇa-mātratvāt / yat tatra kāraṇataya ūpalakṣyate vastu-mātraṃ tad eva satyam anyad asatyam iti iyaṃ śrutir vadati iti cen na etad upapadyate / ekasmin vijñāte sarvaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati iti pratijñāte 'nya-jñānena anya-jñāna-asaṃbhavaṃ manvānasya ekam eva vastu vikāra-ādy-avasthā-viśeṣeṇa pāramārthikena eva nāma-rūpam avasthitaṃ cet tatra ekasmin vijñāte tasmād vilakṣaṇa-saṃsthāna-antaram api tad eva iti tatra dṛṣṭānto 'yaṃ nidarśitaḥ / na atra kasyacid viśeṣasya niṣedhakaḥ ko 'pi śabdo dṛśyate / vācā ārambhaṇam iti vācā vyavahāreṇā arabhyata
ity ārambhaṇam / piṇḍa-rūpeṇa avasthitāyāḥ mṛttikāyā nāma va ānyad-vyavahāraś ca anyaḥ / ghaṭa-śarāva-ādi-rūpeṇa avasthitāyās tasyā eva mṛttikāyā anyāni nāma-dheyāni vyavahārāś ca anyad-daśāḥ / tatha āpi sarvatra mṛttikā-dravyam ekam eva nānā-saṃsthāna-nānā-nāma-dheyābhyāṃ nānā-vyavahāreṇa cā arabhyata ity-etad eva satyam ity anena anya-jñānena anya-jñāna-saṃbhavo nidarśitaḥ / na atra kiṃcid vastu niṣidhyata iti pūrvam eva ayam arthaḥ prapañcitaḥ /

body.text: api ca yenāśrutaṃ śrutam ityādinā brahmavyatiriktasya sarvasya mithyātvaṃ pratijñātaṃ ced yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍenetyādidṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhyavikalaḥ syāt / rajjusarpādivan mṛttikāvikārasya ghaṭaśarāvāder asatyatvaṃ śvetaketoḥ śuśrūṣoḥ pramāṇāntareṇa yuktyā cāsiddham ity etad api siṣādhayiṣitam iti cet / yatheti dṛṣṭāntayopādānaṃ na ghaṭate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if it is claimed that the promise 'by which what was unheard becomes heard' and so forth establishes the falsity (<s>mithyātva</s>) of everything other than <s>Brahman</s>, then the illustration 'just as, dear one, by one lump of clay' and so forth would be deficient with respect to what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>). If it is argued that the falsity of the modifications of clay such as pots and saucers — like the falsity of a rope-snake — is something not established for <s>Śvetaketu</s>, who was eager to learn, through any other <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) or reasoning, and that this too is what was intended to be taught, then the use of the word '<s>yathā</s>' ('just as') to introduce an illustration is not appropriate.

children.text: api ca yena aśrutaṃ śrutam ity-ādinā brahma-vyatiriktasya sarvasya mithyātvaṃ pratijñātaṃ ced yathā somya ekena mṛt-piṇḍena ity-ādi-dṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhya-vikalaḥ syāt / rajju-sarpa-ādivan mṛttikā-vikārasya ghaṭa-śarāva-āder asatyatvaṃ śvetaketoḥ śuśrūṣoḥ pramāṇa-antareṇa yuktyā ca asiddham ity etad api siṣādhayiṣitam iti cet / yatha īti dṛṣṭāntaya ūpādānaṃ na ghaṭate /

body.text:
sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam evādvitīyam ity atra sad evaikam evety avadhāraṇadvayenādvitīyam ity anena ca sanmātrātirekisajātīyavijātīyāḥ sarve viśeṣā niṣiddhā iti pratīyata iti cenn etad evam / kāryakāraṇabhāvāvasthādvayāvasthitasyaikasya vastuna ekāvasthāvasthitasya jñānenāvasthāntarāvasthitasyāpi vastvaikyena jñātatāṃ dṛṣṭāntena darśayitvā śvetaketor aprajñātaṃ sarvasya brahmakāraṇatvaṃ ca vaktuṃ sad eva somyedam ity ārabdham / idam agre sad evāsīd iti / agra iti kālaviśeṣaḥ / idaṃśabdavācyasya prapañcasya sadāpattirūpāṃ kriyāṃ sadravyatāṃ ca vadati / ekam eveti cāsya nānānāmarūpavikāraprahāṇam / etasmin pratipādite 'sya jagataḥ sadupādānatā pratipāditā bhavati / anyatropādānakāraṇasya svavyatiriktādhiṣṭhātrapekṣādarśane
'pi sarvavilakṣaṇatvād asya sarvajñasya brahmaṇaḥ sarvaśaktiyogo na viruddha ity advitīyapadam adhiṣṭhātrantaraṃ nivārayati / sarvaśaktiyuktatvād eva brahmaṇaḥ / kāścana śrutayaḥ prathamam upādānakāraṇatvaṃ pratipādya nimittakāraṇam api tad eveti pratipādayanti / yatheyaṃ śrutiḥ / anyāś ca śrutayo brahmaṇo nimittakāraṇatvam anujñāyāsyaivopādānatādi katham iti paricodya, sarvaśaktiyuktatvād upādānakāraṇaṃ taditarāśeṣopakaraṇaṃ ca brahmaiveti pariharanti -- kiṃsvid vanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭakṣurmaṇīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchated utdyad adhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni dhārayan / brahma vanaṃ brahma sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣur manīṣiṇo manasā vibravīmi vaḥ brahmādhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni
/ dhārayann iti sāmānyato dṛṣṭena virodham āśaṅkya brahmaṇaḥ sarvavilakṣaṇatvena parihāra uktaḥ / ataḥ sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ity atrāpy agra ityādyanekaviśeṣā brahmaṇo pratipāditāḥ / bhavadabhimataviśeṣaniṣedhavācī ko 'pi śabdo na dṛśyate / praty uta jagadbrahmaṇoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvajñāpanāyāgra iti kālaviśeṣasadbhāvaḥ / āsīd iti kriyāviśeṣo, jagadupādānatā jagannimittatā ca, nimittopādānayor bhedanirasanena tasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ sarvaśaktiyogaś cety aprajñātaḥ sahasraśo viśeṣā eva pratipāditāḥ /
body.translated_text: '<s>Sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam</s>' ('Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning, one only, without a second' — <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.1) — if it is claimed that the two emphatic particles in '<s>sad eva</s>' ('Being alone') and '<s>ekam eva</s>' ('one only'), together with '<s>advitīyam</s>' ('without a second'), negate all qualifications — whether of the same kind or of a different kind — beyond mere Being, this is not so. The passage '<s>sad eva somyedam</s>' is commenced in order to demonstrate through an illustration that a single substance existing in two states — the state of cause and the state of effect — when known in one state, is known by virtue of its substantial identity even in the other state, and to teach <s>Śvetaketu</s> the previously unknown truth that <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of everything. '<s>Idam agre sad evāsīt</s>' means: this [universe] was in the beginning Being alone. '<s>Agre</s>' specifies a particular time. The word '<s>idam</s>' (this) declares that the manifold universe attains the state of <s>Sat</s> (Being) — it states both the activity of becoming <s>Sat</s> and the substantial identity with <s>Sat</s>. '<s>Ekam eva</s>' indicates the dissolution of its manifold names, forms, and modifications. When this is established, it follows that this world has <s>Sat</s> as its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>).
