Although in other cases a material cause is not seen to require a controller distinct from itself, because this all-knowing <s>Brahman</s> is utterly unlike everything else, the possession of all powers is not contradictory — hence the word '<s>advitīya</s>' (without a second) excludes any other controller. It is precisely because <s>Brahman</s> possesses all powers. Certain <s>śrutis</s> (scriptures), having first taught the material causality [of <s>Brahman</s>], then teach that it is also the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) — as does this very <s>śruti</s>. Other <s>śrutis</s>, having granted <s>Brahman</s>'s efficient causality, raise the objection 'how can it also be the material cause?' and resolve it by stating that because <s>Brahman</s> possesses all powers, it is both the material cause and every other auxiliary cause — '<s>Kiṃ svid vanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ</s>' ('What was the forest, what was the tree from which they fashioned heaven and earth?') '<s>manīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchated u tad yad adhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni dhārayan</s>' ('O wise ones, inquire with your minds into that which stood sustaining the worlds') — '<s>Brahma vanaṃ brahma sa vṛkṣa āsīd</s>' ('Brahman was the forest, Brahman was the tree') '<s>yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ</s>' ('from which they fashioned heaven and earth') '<s>manīṣiṇo manasā vibravīmi vaḥ</s>' ('O wise ones, I declare to you with the mind') '<s>brahmādhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni dhārayan</s>' ('Brahman stood sustaining the worlds') — here, having anticipated the objection based on ordinary experience, the resolution is given through the utter uniqueness of <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, in '<s>sad eva somyedam agra āsīt</s>' as well, numerous qualifications of <s>Brahman</s> are taught, beginning with '<s>agre</s>' and so on. No word negating the qualifications that you [Advaitins] wish to deny is seen anywhere. On the contrary, for the purpose of revealing the cause-effect relationship between the world and <s>Brahman</s>, the existence of a particular time [is stated by] '<s>agre</s>'; a particular activity [by] '<s>āsīt</s>'; material causality with respect to the world and efficient causality with respect to the world [are stated]; by the negation of any difference between the efficient and material cause, the possession of all powers by that very <s>Brahman</s> [is stated] — thus thousands of previously unknown qualifications are actually taught.

children.text:
sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ekam eva advitīyam eva advitīyam ity atra sad eva ekam eva ity avadhāraṇa-dvayena advitīyam ity anena ca san-mātra-atireki-sajātīya-vijātīyāḥ sarve viśeṣā niṣiddhā iti pratīyata iti cenn etad evam / kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva-avasthā-dvaya-avasthitasya ekasya vastuna eka-avasthā-avasthitasya jñānena avasthā-antara-avasthitasya api vastv-aikyena jñātatāṃ dṛṣṭāntena darśayitvā śvetaketor aprajñātaṃ sarvasya brahma-kāraṇatvaṃ ca vaktuṃ sad eva somya idam ity ārabdham / idam agre sad evā asīd iti / agra iti kāla-viśeṣaḥ / idaṃ-śabda-vācyasya prapañcasya sad-āpatti-rūpāṃ kriyāṃ sadravyatāṃ ca vadati / ekam eva iti ca asya nānā-nāma-rūpa-vikāra-prahāṇam / etasmin pratipādite 'sya jagataḥ sad-upādānatā pratipāditā bhavati / anyatra upādāna-kāraṇasya sva-vyatirikta-adhiṣṭhātr-apekṣā-darśane
'pi sarva-vilakṣaṇatvād asya sarva-jñasya brahmaṇaḥ sarva-śakti-yogo na viruddha ity advitīya-padam adhiṣṭhātr-antaraṃ nivārayati / sarva-śakti-yuktatvād eva brahmaṇaḥ / kāścana śrutayaḥ prathamam upādāna-kāraṇatvaṃ pratipādya nimitta-kāraṇam api tad eva iti pratipādayanti / yatha īyaṃ śrutiḥ / anyāś ca śrutayo brahmaṇo nimitta-kāraṇatvam anujñāya asya eva upādānatā-ādi katham iti paricodya, sarva-śakti-yuktatvād upādāna-kāraṇaṃ tad-itara-aśeṣa-upakaraṇaṃ ca brahma eva iti pariharanti --- kiṃsvid vanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvā-pṛthivī niṣṭakṣur-maṇīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchated utdyad adhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni dhārayan / brahma vanaṃ brahma sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvā-pṛthivī niṣṭatakṣur manīṣiṇo manasā vibravīmi vaḥ brahma-adhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni
/ dhārayann iti sāmānyato dṛṣṭena virodham āśaṅkya brahmaṇaḥ sarva-vilakṣaṇatvena parihāra uktaḥ / ataḥ sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ity atra apy agra ity-ādy-aneka-viśeṣā brahmaṇo pratipāditāḥ / bhavad-abhimata-viśeṣa-niṣedha-vācī ko 'pi śabdo na dṛśyate / praty uta jagad-brahmaṇoḥ kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva-jñāpanāya agra iti kāla-viśeṣa-sad-bhāvaḥ / āsīd iti kriyā-viśeṣo, jagad-upādānatā jagan-nimittatā ca, nimitta-upādānayor bheda-nirasanena tasya eva brahmaṇaḥ sarva-śakti-yogaś ca ity aprajñātaḥ sahasraśo viśeṣā eva pratipāditāḥ /

body.text: yato vāstavakāryakāraṇabhāvādivijñāne pravṛttam ata evāsad evedam agra āsīd ityārabhyāsatkāryavādaniṣedhaś ca kriyate -- kutas tu khalu somyaivaṃ syād iti / prāgasata utpattir ahetuketyarthaḥ / tad evopapādayati -- katham asataḥ saj jāyeteti / asata utpannam asadātmakam eva bhavatītyarthaḥ / yathā mṛd utpannaṃ ghaṭādikaṃ mṛdātmakam / sata utpattir nāma vyavahāraviśeṣahetubhūto 'vasthāviśeṣayogaḥ /
body.translated_text: Since [the <s>śruti</s>] has undertaken to teach the real cause-effect relationship and such matters, beginning with '<s>asad evedam agra āsīt</s>' ('Non-being alone was this in the beginning'), a refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine of the non-pre-existence of the effect) is also carried out — '<s>kutas tu khalu somyaivaṃ syāt</s>' ('But how indeed, dear one, could it be so?'). The meaning is: the origination of being from non-being is without cause. This is then substantiated: '<s>katham asataḥ saj jāyeta</s>' ('How could being be born from non-being?'). The meaning is: what is produced from non-being would itself be of the nature of non-being. Just as what is produced from clay — pots and such — is of the nature of clay. The origination from <s>Sat</s> (Being) is [nothing but] the attainment of a particular state that serves as the basis for a particular mode of practical usage.

children.text: yato vāstava-kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva-ādi-vijñāne pravṛttam ata eva asad eva idam agra āsīd ity-ārabhya asat-kārya-vāda-niṣedhaś ca kriyate --- kutas tu khalu somya evaṃ syād iti / prāg-asata utpattir ahetuka īty-arthaḥ / tad eva upapādayati --- katham asataḥ saj jāyeta iti / asata utpannam asad-ātmakam eva bhavati ity-arthaḥ / yathā mṛd utpannaṃ ghaṭa-ādikaṃ mṛd-ātmakam / sata utpattir nāma vyavahāra-viśeṣa-hetu-bhūto 'vasthā-viśeṣa-yogaḥ /

body.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati / ekam eva kāraṇabhūtaṃ dravyam avasthāntarayogena kāryam ity ucyata ity ekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ pratipipādayiṣitam / tad asatkāryavāde na setsyati / tathā hi nimittasamavāyyasamavāyiprabhṛtiḥ kāraṇair avayavyākhyaṃ kāryaṃ dravyāntaram evotpadyata iti kāraṇabhūtād vastunaḥ kāryasya vastvantaratvān na tajjñānenāsya jñātatā katham api saṃbhavatīti / katham avayavi dravyāntaraṃ nirasyata iti cet / kāraṇagatāvasthāntarayogasya dravyāntarotpattivādinaḥ saṃpratipannasyaivaikatvanāmāntarāder upapādakatvād dravyāntarādarśanāc ceti kāraṇam evāvasthāntarāpannaṃ kāryam ity ucyata ity uktam /
body.translated_text: What is stated amounts to this: one and the same substance in the state of being the cause is called the effect when it attains another state — thus the teaching that by knowing one thing everything is known was intended to be established. This cannot be accomplished on the theory of <s>asatkāryavāda</s> (non-pre-existence of effect). For on that view, an effect called the composite whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is produced as an entirely different substance by causes such as the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>), the inherent cause (<s>samavāyin</s>), the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyin</s>), and so forth; since the effect is a substance entirely different from the substance that is the cause, the knowledge of the latter could not in any way yield the knowledge of the former. If it is asked how the composite whole as a distinct substance is refuted — [the answer is:] because no distinct substance is observed beyond the attainment of another state by the cause, the cause itself in a different state is what is called the effect — this has already been stated.

children.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati / ekam eva kāraṇa-bhūtaṃ dravyam avasthā-antara-yogena kāryam ity ucyata ity eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñānaṃ pratipipādayiṣitam / tad asat-kārya-vāde na setsyati / tathā hi nimitta-samavāyy-asamavāyi-prabhṛtiḥ kāraṇair avayavy-ākhyaṃ kāryaṃ dravya-antaram eva utpadyata iti kāraṇa-bhūtād vastunaḥ kāryasya vastv-antaratvān na taj-jñānena asya jñātatā katham api saṃbhavati iti / katham avayavi dravya-antaraṃ nirasyata iti cet / kāraṇa-gata-avasthā-antara-yogasya dravya-antara-utpatti-vādinaḥ saṃpratipannasya eva ekatva-nāma-antara-āder upapādakatvād dravya-antara-adarśanāc ca iti kāraṇam eva avasthā-antara-āpannaṃ kāryam ity ucyata ity uktam /

body.text: nanu niradhiṣṭhānabhramāsaṃbhavajñāpanāyāsatkāryavādanirāsaḥ kriyate / tathā hy ekaṃ cidrūpaṃ satyam evāvidyāc chāditaṃ jagadrūpeṇa vivartata ity avidyāśrayatvāya mūlakāraṇaṃ satyam ity abhyupagantavyam ity asatkāryavādanirāsaḥ / naitad evam / ekavijñānena sarvavijñānapratijñādṛṣṭāntamukhena satkāryavādasyaiva prasaktatvād ity uktam / bhavatpakṣe niradhiṣṭhānabhramāsaṃbhavasya durupapādatvāc ca / yasya hi cetanagatadoṣaḥ pāramārthiko doṣāśrayatvaṃ ca pāramārthikaṃ tasya pāramārthikadoṣeṇa yuktasyāpāramārthikagandharvanagarādidarśanam upapannaṃ, yasya tu doṣaś cāpāramārthiko doṣāśrayatvaṃ cāpāramārthikaṃ tasyāpāramārthikenāpy āśrayeṇa tad upapannam iti bhavatpakṣe na niradhiṣṭhānabhramāsaṃbhavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, if it is objected that the refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s> (non-pre-existence of the effect) is undertaken to demonstrate the impossibility of error without a substrate (<s>niradhiṣṭhāna-bhrama</s>), [as follows:] one reality of the nature of pure consciousness, though real, is concealed by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and appears transformed (<s>vivartate</s>) in the form of the world; to serve as the substrate of <s>avidyā</s>, the root cause must be accepted as real — this is the purpose of refuting <s>asatkāryavāda</s> — this is not so. [Why?] Because, as already stated, through the promise that by knowing one thing everything is known, and through the illustration, it is the doctrine of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (pre-existence of the effect) alone that is contextually relevant. And because on your [Advaitin's] position, the impossibility of error without a substrate is itself difficult to establish. For one in whom the defect belonging to a conscious being is real, and whose being a substrate of defect is also real — for such a one, the perception of unreal things like a mirage-city, caused by a real defect, is intelligible. But for one in whom both the defect and the being-a-substrate-of-defect are unreal — even with an unreal substrate, that [error] would [equally] be intelligible [on your own logic]. Therefore, on your position, there is no [proof of the] impossibility of error without a substrate.

children.text: nanu niradhiṣṭhāna-bhrama-asaṃbhava-jñāpanāya asat-kārya-vāda-nirāsaḥ kriyate / tathā hy ekaṃ cid-rūpaṃ satyam eva avidyāc chāditaṃ jagad-rūpeṇa vivartata ity avidyā-āśrayatvāya mūla-kāraṇaṃ satyam ity abhyupagantavyam ity asat-kārya-vāda-nirāsaḥ / na etad evam / eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñāna-pratijñā-dṛṣṭānta-mukhena sat-kārya-vādasya eva prasaktatvād ity uktam / bhavat-pakṣe niradhiṣṭhāna-bhrama-asaṃbhavasya durupapādatvāc ca / yasya hi cetana-gata-doṣaḥ pāramārthiko doṣa-āśrayatvaṃ ca pāramārthikaṃ tasya pāramārthika-doṣeṇa yuktasya apāramārthika-gandharva-nagara-ādi-darśanam upapannaṃ, yasya tu doṣaś ca apāramārthiko doṣa-āśrayatvaṃ ca apāramārthikaṃ tasya apāramārthikena apy āśrayeṇa tad upapannam iti bhavat-pakṣe na niradhiṣṭhāna-bhrama-asaṃbhavaḥ /

body.text: śodhakeṣv api satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma, ānando brahmetyādiṣu vākyeṣu sāmānyādhikaraṇyavyutpattisiddhānekaguṇaviśiṣṭaikārthāvabodhanam aviruddham iti sarvaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ brahmābhidhīyata iti pūrvam evoktam /
body.translated_text: Even in the purificatory [texts], in statements such as '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' (<s>satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma</s>) and '<s>Brahman</s> is bliss' (<s>ānando brahma</s>), the comprehension of a single entity qualified by multiple attributes, established through the grammatical principle of coordination (<s>sāmānyādhikaraṇya</s>), is not contradicted — and therefore it has been stated earlier that <s>Brahman</s> is described as qualified by all attributes.

children.text: śodhakeṣv api satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma, ānando brahma ity-ādiṣu vākyeṣu sāmānyādhikaraṇya-vyutpatti-siddha-aneka-guṇa-viśiṣṭa-eka-artha-avabodhanam aviruddham iti sarva-guṇa-viśiṣṭaṃ brahma abhidhīyata iti pūrvam eva uktam /

body.text: athāta ādeśo neti netīti bahudhā niṣedho dṛṣyata iti cet / kim atra niṣidhyata iti vaktavyam / dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe mūrtaṃ caivāmūrtaṃ ceti mūrtāmūrtātmakaḥ prapañcaḥ sarvo 'pi niṣidhyata iti cen naivam / brahmaṇo rūpatayāprajñātaṃ sarvaṃ rūpatayopadiśya punar tad eva niṣeddhum ayuktam / prakṣālanād dhi paṅkasya dūrād asparśanaṃ varam iti nyāyāt / kas tarhi niṣedhavākyārthaḥ / sūtrakāraḥ svayam eva vadati -- prakṛtaitāvattvaṃ hi pratiṣedhati tato bravīti ca bhūya iti / uttaratra atha nāmadheyaṃ saty asya satyaṃ prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣām eṣa satyam iti satyādiguṇagaṇasya pratipāditatvāt pūrvaprakṛtaitāvanmātraṃ na bhavati brahmeti, brahmaṇa etāvanmātratā pratiṣidhyata iti sūtrārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, if [the objector says]: 'Here the instruction <s>neti neti</s> (not this, not this) shows manifold negation' — it must be stated what is being negated here. [The text says:] 'There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s>: the formed and the formless' (<s>dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe mūrtaṃ caivāmūrtaṃ ca</s>). If [one says] that the entire phenomenal world consisting of the formed and formless is negated — it is not so. Having taught everything as being the form of <s>Brahman</s>, to negate that very thing would be improper. For by the maxim, 'Rather than washing off mud, it is better not to touch it from afar.' What then is the meaning of the negation statement? The <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>) himself says: 'It negates the limitation (<s>etāvattva</s>) of what has been stated, and then says more' (<s>prakṛtaitāvattvaṃ hi pratiṣedhati tato bravīti ca bhūyaḥ</s>). Further on, [the text states:] 'Now the name: He is the truth of truth; the vital airs are truth, and He is their truth' (<s>atha nāmadheyaṃ saty asya satyaṃ prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣām eṣa satyam</s>). Since a host of attributes beginning with truth has been taught, <s>Brahman</s> is not merely the limited entity previously stated — the meaning of the <s>Sūtra</s> is that what is negated is the limitation (<s>etāvanmātratā</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: atha ata ādeśo na iti na iti iti bahudhā niṣedho dṛṣyata iti cet / kim atra niṣidhyata iti vaktavyam / dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe mūrtaṃ ca eva amūrtaṃ ca iti mūrta-amūrta-ātmakaḥ prapañcaḥ sarvo 'pi niṣidhyata iti cen na evam / brahmaṇo rūpataya āprajñātaṃ sarvaṃ rūpataya ūpadiśya punar tad eva niṣeddhum ayuktam / prakṣālanād dhi paṅkasya dūrād asparśanaṃ varam iti nyāyāt / kas tarhi niṣedha-vākya-arthaḥ / sūtra-kāraḥ svayam eva vadati --- prakṛta-etāvattvaṃ hi pratiṣedhati tato bravīti ca bhūya iti / uttaratra atha nāma-dheyaṃ saty asya satyaṃ prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣām eṣa satyam iti satya-ādi-guṇa-gaṇasya pratipāditatvāt pūrva-prakṛta-etāvan-mātraṃ na bhavati brahma iti, brahmaṇa etāvan-mātratā pratiṣidhyata iti sūtra-arthaḥ /

body.text: neha nānāsti kiṃcanetyādinā nānātvapratiṣedha eva dṛṣyata iti cet / atrāpy uttaratra sarvasya vaśī sarvasyeśana iti satyasaṅkalpatvasarveśvaratvapratipādanāc cetanavastuśarīra īśvara iti sarvaprakārasaṃsthitaḥ sa eka eveti tatpratyanīkābrahmātmakanānātvaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ na bhavadabhimatam / sarvāsv evaṃprakārāsu śrutiṣv iyam eva sthitir iti na kvacid api brahmaṇaḥ saviśeṣatvaniṣedhakavācī ko 'pi śabdo dṛśyate /
body.translated_text: If [the objector says]: 'By the statement "There is no plurality here whatsoever" (<s>neha nānāsti kiṃcana</s>), a negation of plurality itself is seen' — here too, further on [the text states]: 'The controller of all, the lord of all' (<s>sarvasya vaśī sarvasyeśānaḥ</s>). Since true resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>) and lordship over all (<s>sarveśvaratva</s>) are taught, He alone abides in every mode as the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) having all conscious entities as His body. What is negated is the plurality that is opposed to this and consists of non-<s>Brahman</s> entities — not the [plurality] maintained by you [Advaitins]. In all such <s>śruti</s> texts this alone is the settled view; nowhere is any word seen that negates the qualified nature (<s>saviśeṣatva</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: na iha nāna āsti kiṃcana ity-ādinā nānātva-pratiṣedha eva dṛṣyata iti cet / atra apy uttaratra sarvasya vaśī sarvasyā iśana iti satya-saṅkalpatva-sarva-īśvaratva-pratipādanāc cetana-vastu-śarīra īśvara iti sarva-prakāra-saṃsthitaḥ sa eka eva iti tat-pratyanīkā-brahma-ātmaka-nānātvaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ na bhavad-abhimatam / sarvāsv evaṃ-prakārāsu śrutiṣv iyam eva sthitir iti na kvacid api brahmaṇaḥ saviśeṣatva-niṣedhaka-vācī ko 'pi śabdo dṛśyate /

body.text: api ca nirviśeṣajñānamātraṃ brahma tac cāchādikāvidyātirohitasvarūpaṃ svagatanānātvaṃ paśyatīty ayam artho na ghaṭate / tirodhānaṃ nāma prakāśanivāraṇam / svarūpātirekiprakāśadharmānabhyupagamena prakāśasyaiva svarūpatvāt svarūpanāśa eva syāt / prakāśaparyāyaṃ jñānaṃ nityaṃ sa ca prakāśo 'vidyātirohita iti bāliśabhāṣitam idam / avidyayā prakāśatirohita iti prakāśotpattipratibandho vidyamānasya vināśo vā / prakāśasyānutpādyatvād vināśa eva syāt / prakāśo nityo nirvikāras tiṣṭhatīti cet / satyām apy avidyāyāṃ brahmaṇi na kiṃcit tirohitam iti nānātvaṃ paśyatīti bhavatām ayaṃ vyavahāraḥ satsv anirvacanīya eva /
body.translated_text: Moreover, [the position] that <s>Brahman</s> is mere attributeless consciousness (<s>nirviśeṣajñānamātra</s>), and that its nature, concealed by the covering ignorance (<s>āchādikāvidyā</s>), sees internal plurality (<s>svagatanānātva</s>) — this meaning is untenable. Concealment means the obstruction of illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>). Since you do not accept illumination as an attribute distinct from the essence, and since illumination is itself the essence, [concealment] would amount to the destruction of the essence itself. Knowledge being synonymous with illumination, and that illumination is eternal — to say that this [eternal] illumination is concealed by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is childish speech. [To say] that illumination is concealed by <s>avidyā</s> means either obstruction of the arising of illumination or destruction of what already exists. Since illumination is not something produced, it would amount to destruction only. If [one says]: 'Illumination abides as eternal and unchanging' — then even when <s>avidyā</s> exists, nothing is concealed in <s>Brahman</s>; and your assertion that it 'sees plurality' is itself truly inexplicable.

children.text: api ca nirviśeṣa-jñāna-mātraṃ brahma tac cā achādika-avidyā-tirohita-sva-rūpaṃ sva-gata-nānātvaṃ paśyati ity ayam artho na ghaṭate / tirodhānaṃ nāma prakāśa-nivāraṇam / sva-rūpa-atireki-prakāśa-dharma-anabhyupagamena prakāśasya eva sva-rūpatvāt sva-rūpa-nāśa eva syāt / prakāśa-paryāyaṃ jñānaṃ nityaṃ sa ca prakāśo 'vidyā-tirohita iti bāliśa-bhāṣitam idam / avidyayā prakāśa-tirohita iti prakāśa utpatti-pratibandho vidyamānasya vināśo vā / prakāśasya anutpādyatvād vināśa eva syāt / prakāśo nityo nirvikāras tiṣṭhati iti cet / satyām apy avidyāyāṃ brahmaṇi na kiṃcit tirohitam iti nānātvaṃ paśyati iti bhavatām ayaṃ vyavahāraḥ satsv anirvacanīya eva /

body.text: nanu ca bhavato 'pi vijñānasvarūpa ātmābhyupagantavyaḥ / sa ca svayaṃprakāśaḥ / tasya ca devādisvarūpātmābhimāne svarūpaprakāśatirodhānam avaśyam āśrayaṇīyam / svarūpaprakāśe sati svātmany ākārāntarādhyāsāyogāt / ato bhavataś cāyaṃ samāno doṣaḥ / kiṃ cāsmākam ekasminn evātmani bhavadudīritaṃ durghaṭatvam bhavatām ātmānantyābhyupagamāt sarveṣv ayaṃ doṣaḥ pariharaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: But you too must accept that the self (<s>ātman</s>) is consciousness in nature (<s>vijñānasvarūpa</s>). And it is self-luminous (<s>svayaṃprakāśa</s>). And when it wrongly identifies itself with the forms of gods and such, concealment of its self-luminous nature must necessarily be accepted by you. For when there is self-illumination, superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) of other forms upon the self would be impossible. Therefore this same defect applies to you as well. Moreover, the difficulty you raise applies to just one self in our case; but since you accept an infinity of selves, you must resolve this defect in all of them.

children.text: nanu ca bhavato 'pi vijñāna-sva-rūpa ātma-abhyupagantavyaḥ / sa ca svayaṃ-prakāśaḥ / tasya ca deva-ādi-sva-rūpa-ātma-abhimāne sva-rūpa-prakāśa-tirodhānam avaśyam āśrayaṇīyam / sva-rūpa-prakāśe sati sva-ātmany ākāra-antara-adhyāsa-ayogāt / ato bhavataś ca ayaṃ samāno doṣaḥ / kiṃ ca asmākam ekasminn evā atmani bhavad-udīritaṃ durghaṭatvam bhavatām ātma-anantya-abhyupagamāt sarveṣv ayaṃ doṣaḥ pariharaṇīyaḥ /

body.text:
atrocyate -- svabhāvato malapratyanīkānantajñānānandaikasvarūpaṃ svābhāvikānavadhikātiśayāparimitodāraguṇasāgaraṃ nimeṣakāṣṭhākalāmuhūrtādiparārdhaparyantāparimitavyavacchedasvarūpasarvotpattisthitivināśādisarvapariṇāmanimittabhūtakālakṛtapariṇāmāspaṣṭānantamahāvibhūti svalīlāparikarasvāṃśabhūtānantabaddhamuktanānāvidhacetanatadbhogyabhūtānantavicitrapariṇāmaśakticetanetaravastujātāntaryāmitvakṛtasarvaśaktiśarīratvasarvaprakarśāvasthānāvasthitaṃ paraṃ brahmaiva vedyaṃ,
tatsākṣātkārakṣamabhagavaddvaipāyanaparāśaravālmīkimanuyājñavalkyagautamāpastambaprabhṛtimunigaṇapraṇītavidhyarthavādamantrasvarūpavedamūletihāsapurāṇadharmaśāstropabhṛṃhitaparamārthabhūtānādinidhanāvicchinnapāṭhasaṃpradāyargyajuḥsāmātharvarūpānantaśākhaṃ vedaṃ cābhyupagacchatām asmākaṃ kiṃ na setsyati / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā dvaipāyanena mahābhārate --
yo mām ajam anādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram /
dvāv imau puraṣau loke kṣaraś cākṣara eva ca /
kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate //
uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ /
yo lokatrayam āviśya vibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ //
kālaṃ ca pacate tatra na kālas tatra vai prabhūḥ /
ete vai nirayās tāta sthānasya paramātmanaḥ //
avyaktādiviśeṣāntaṃ pariṇāmarddhisaṃyuktam /
krīḍā harer idaṃ sarvaṃ kṣaram ity avadhāryatām //
kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api cāpyayaḥ /
kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ carācaram //
iti / kṛṣṇasya hi kṛta iti kṛṣṇasya śeṣabhūtaṃ sarvam ityarthaḥ /
bhagavatā parāśareṇāpy uktam --
śuddhe mahāvibhūtyākhye pare brahmaṇi śabdyate /
maitreya bhagavacchabdaḥ sarvakāraṇakāraṇe //
jñānaśaktibalāiśvaryavīryatejāṃsy aśeṣataḥ /
bhagavacchabdavācyāni vinā heyair guṇādibhiḥ //
evam eṣa mahāśabdo maitreya bhagavān iti /
paramabrahmabhūtasya vāsudevasya nānyagaḥ //
tatra pūjyapadārthoktiparibhāṣāsamanvitaḥ /
śabdo 'yaṃ nopacāreṇa tv anyatra hy upacārataḥ //
evaṃprakāram amalaṃ satyaṃ vyāpakam akṣayam /
samastaheyarahitaṃ viṣṇvākhyaṃ paramaṃ padam //
kalāmuhūrtādimayaś ca kālo na yadvibhūteḥ pariṇāmahetuḥ //
krīḍato bālakasyeva ceṣṭās tasya niśāmaya //
ityādi / manunāpi --
praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām /
ityuktam / yājñavalkyenāpi --
kṣetrasyeśvarajñānād viśuddhiḥ paramā matā /
iti / āpastambenāpi -- pūḥ prāṇinaḥ sarva eva guhāśayasyeti / sarve prāṇino guhāśayas paramātmanaḥ pūḥ -- puraṃ śarīram ityarthaḥ / prāṇina iti sajīvātmabhūtasaṃghātaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Here it is replied: The Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be known — whose sole nature is infinite knowledge and bliss, inherently opposed to all impurity; an ocean of innate, unsurpassable, infinitely abundant, noble qualities; whose infinite great sovereign glory (<s>mahāvibhūti</s>) is untouched by the transformations wrought by time — that time whose nature is unlimited division into moments (<s>nimeṣa</s>), instants (<s>kāṣṭhā</s>), fractions (<s>kalā</s>), and <s>muhūrtas</s> up to <s>parārdha</s>, and which is the cause of all transformations such as origination, sustenance, and dissolution; whose accessories to His own play (<s>līlā</s>), being His own portions, are the infinite bound and liberated sentient beings of various kinds, along with the class of non-sentient entities of infinitely varied transformative power that serve as the objects of their experience; who, through being the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of all sentient and non-sentient entities, has all powers as His body, and is established in the state of supreme excellence.
Those of us who accept the <s>Veda</s> — whose authentically transmitted, beginningless and endless, unbroken lineage of recitation comprises the infinite branches of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s>, rooted in the <s>Veda</s> whose nature consists of injunctions, explanatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>), and <s>mantras</s>, composed by the assembly of sages beginning with the Blessed <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Vālmīki</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Āpastamba</s>, who are capable of direct realization of That [<s>Brahman</s>], supplemented by the <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and <s>Dharmaśāstras</s> that are of ultimate truth — what will not be accomplished for us? As stated by the Blessed <s>Dvaipāyana</s> in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:
'He who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great Lord of the worlds' —
'There are two persons in the world: the perishable (<s>kṣara</s>) and the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>); the perishable comprises all beings, while the immutable is called the imperishable.
But the Supreme Person (<s>Uttama Puruṣa</s>) is another, called the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), who, entering the three worlds, sustains them — the imperishable Lord' —
'He cooks [transforms] time there; time is not lord over Him' —
'These are indeed the abodes, dear son, of the Supreme Self' —
'From the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) down to the particulars (<s>viśeṣa</s>), endowed with evolving prosperity — all this is the play (<s>krīḍā</s>) of <s>Hari</s>; let it be understood as the perishable' —
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the origin and dissolution of the worlds; for the sake of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has this universe of moving and non-moving things come into being.' '<s>Kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte</s>' means that everything exists as subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>) to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
The Blessed <s>Parāśara</s> also stated:
'O <s>Maitreya</s>, the word "Bhagavān" is predicated of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is pure, called the Great Sovereignty (<s>mahāvibhūti</s>), and is the cause of all causes' —
'Knowledge, power, strength, lordship, vigor, and splendor — without exception, these are what the word "Bhagavān" denotes, excluding all defects and [unworthy] qualities' —
'Thus this great word "Bhagavān," O <s>Maitreya</s>, belongs to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and to none other' —
'Therein, endowed with the conventional meaning of denoting objects worthy of worship, this word is used literally [for <s>Vāsudeva</s>]; for others, however, it is used figuratively' —
'Of such nature is the Supreme Abode called <s>Viṣṇu</s>: pure, true, all-pervading, imperishable, free from all defects' —
'And time, consisting of moments, <s>muhūrtas</s>, and the like, is not the cause of transformation of His sovereignty' —
'Behold the activities of Him as if of a child at play.'
And so forth. <s>Manu</s> also stated: 'The ruler of all, subtler than the subtlest.' <s>Yājñavalkya</s> also stated: 'Supreme purification is considered to come from knowledge of the Lord of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>).' <s>Āpastamba</s> also stated: 'All living beings are the city (<s>pūḥ</s>) of Him who dwells in the cave [of the heart].' All living beings are the city — that is, the body — of the Supreme Self who dwells in the cave of the heart. By 'living beings' (<s>prāṇinaḥ</s>) is meant the aggregate of embodied souls.

atra ucyate --- svabhāvato mala-pratyanīka-ananta-jñāna-ānanda-eka-svarūpaṃ svābhāvika-anavadhika-atiśaya-aparimita-udāra-guṇa-sāgaraṃ nimeṣa-kāṣṭhā-kalā-muhūrta-ādi-para-ardha-paryanta-aparimita-vyavaccheda-sva-rūpa-sarva-utpatti-sthiti-vināśa-ādi-sarva-pariṇāma-nimitta-bhūta-kāla-kṛta-pariṇāma-aspaṣṭa-ananta-mahā-vibhūti sva-līlā-parikara-sva-aṃśa-bhūta-ananta-baddha-mukta-nānā-vidha-cetana-tad-bhogya-bhūta-ananta-vicitra-pariṇāma-śakti-cetana-itara-vastu-jāta-antaryāmitva-kṛta-sarva-śakti-śarīratva-sarva-prakarśa-avasthāna-avasthitaṃ paraṃ brahma eva vedyaṃ,
tat-sākṣātkāra-kṣama-bhagavad-dvaipāyana-parāśara-vālmīki-manu-yājñavalkya-gautama-āpastamba-prabhṛti-muni-gaṇa-praṇīta-vidhy-artha-vāda-mantra-sva-rūpa-veda-mūla-itihāsa-purāṇa-dharma-śāstra-upabhṛṃhita-parama-artha-bhūta-anādi-nidhana-avicchinna-pāṭha-saṃpradāya-rg-yajuḥ-sāma-atharva-rūpa-ananta-śākhaṃ vedaṃ ca abhyupagacchatām asmākaṃ kiṃ na setsyati / yatha ūktaṃ bhagavatā dvaipāyanena mahābhārate ---
yo mām ajam anādiṃ ca vetti loka-mahā-īśvaram /
dvāv imau puraṣau loke kṣaraś ca akṣara eva ca /
kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭa-stho 'kṣara ucyate //
uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ parama-ātma īty udāhṛtaḥ /
yo loka-trayam āviśya vibhartya-vyaya īśvaraḥ //
kālaṃ ca pacate tatra na kālas tatra vai prabhūḥ /
ete vai nirayās tāta sthānasya parama-ātmanaḥ //
avyakta-ādi-viśeṣa-antaṃ pariṇāma-rddhi-saṃyuktam /
krīḍā harer idaṃ sarvaṃ kṣaram ity avadhāryatām //
kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api ca apyayaḥ /
kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ cara acaram //
iti / kṛṣṇasya hi kṛta iti kṛṣṇasya śeṣa-bhūtaṃ sarvam ity-arthaḥ /
bhagavatā parāśareṇa apy uktam ---
śuddhe mahā-vibhūty-ākhye pare brahmaṇi śabdyate /
maitreya bhagavac-chabdaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇe //
jñāna-śakti-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-tejāṃsy aśeṣataḥ /
bhagavac-chabda-vācyāni vinā heyair guṇa-ādibhiḥ //
evam eṣa mahā-śabdo maitreya bhagavān iti /
parama-brahma-bhūtasya vāsudevasya na anya-gaḥ //
tatra pūjya-pada-artha-ukti-paribhāṣā-samanvitaḥ /
śabdo 'yaṃ na upacāreṇa tv anyatra hy upacārataḥ //
evaṃ-prakāram amalaṃ satyaṃ vyāpakam akṣayam /
samasta-heya-rahitaṃ viṣṇv-ākhyaṃ paramaṃ padam //
kalā-muhūrta-ādi-mayaś ca kālo na yad-vibhūteḥ pariṇāma-hetuḥ //
krīḍato bālakasya iva ceṣṭās tasya niśāmaya //
ity-ādi / manuna āpi ---
praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām /
ity-uktam / yājñavalkyena api ---
kṣetrasyā iśvara-jñānād viśuddhiḥ paramā matā /
iti / āpastambena api --- pūḥ prāṇinaḥ sarva eva guha-āśayasya iti / sarve prāṇino guha-āśayas parama-ātmanaḥ pūḥ --- puraṃ śarīram ity-arthaḥ / prāṇina iti sa-jīva-ātma-bhūta-saṃghātaḥ /

body.text:
nanu ca kim anenāḍambareṇa / codyaṃ tu na parihṛtam / ucyate / evam abhyupagacchatām asmākam ātmadharmabhūtasya caitanyasya svābhāvikasyāpi karmaṇā pāramārthikaṃ saṃkocaṃ vikāsaṃ ca bruvatāṃ sarvam idaṃ parihṛtam / bhavas tu prakāśa eva svarūpam iti prakāśo na dharmabhūtas tasya saṃkocavikāsau vā nābyupagamyete / prakāśaprasārānutpattim eva tirodhānabhūtāḥ karmādayaḥ kurvanti / avidyā cet tirodhānaṃ tirodhānabhūtatayāvidyayā svarūpabhūtaprakāśanāśa iti pūrvam evoktam / asmākaṃ tv avidyārūpeṇa karmaṇā svarūpanityadharmabhūtaprakāśaḥ saṃkucitaḥ / tena devādisvarūpātmābhimāno bhavatīti viśeṣaḥ / yathoktam --
avidyā karmasaṃjñānyā tṛtīyā śaktir iṣyate //
yathā kṣetraśaktiḥ sā veṣṭitā nṛpa sarvagā /
saṃsāratāpān akhilān avāpnoty atisaṃtatān //
tayā tirohitatvāc ca śaktiḥ kṣetrajñasaṃjñitā /
sarvabhūteṣu bhūpāle tāratamyena vartate //
iti / kṣetrajñānāṃ svadharmabhūtasya jñānasya karmasaṃjñāvidyayā saṃkocaṃ vikāsaṃ ca darśayati /
body.translated_text:
But what is the point of this display? The objection has not been answered. It is answered: For us who accept this view — who hold that consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), being an attribute (<s>dharma</s>) of the self (<s>ātman</s>), though innate, undergoes real contraction and expansion through <s>karma</s> — for us, all of this is resolved. But according to you [Advaitins], illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>) is the very essence; illumination is not an attribute, and neither contraction nor expansion of it is accepted. [If you say] that <s>karma</s> and the like, being of the nature of concealment, merely prevent the manifestation of illumination — if <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the concealment, then through <s>avidyā</s>, which is of the nature of concealment, there is destruction of illumination which is the essence itself — this has been stated already. In our view, however, illumination, which is an eternal attribute of the essence, is contracted by <s>karma</s> taking the form of <s>avidyā</s>. Through that, false identification with the forms of gods and such arises — this is the distinction. As it has been stated:
'The third power is accepted, called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), also known as <s>karma</s>' —
'That field-power (<s>kṣetraśakti</s>), O king, enveloped and all-pervading, obtains all the continuous afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>' —
'And because it is concealed by that [<s>avidyā</s>], the power called the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) exists in all beings in varying degrees, O king.'
This shows the contraction and expansion of knowledge — which is an inherent attribute (<s>svadharma</s>) of the field-knowers — through <s>avidyā</s> called <s>karma</s>.

children.text:
nanu ca kim anena aḍambareṇa / codyaṃ tu na parihṛtam / ucyate / evam abhyupagacchatām asmākam ātma-dharma-bhūtasya caitanyasya svābhāvikasya api karmaṇā pāramārthikaṃ saṃkocaṃ vikāsaṃ ca bruvatāṃ sarvam idaṃ parihṛtam / bhavas tu prakāśa eva sva-rūpam iti prakāśo na dharma-bhūtas tasya saṃkoca-vikāsau vā na abyupagamyete / prakāśa-prasāra-anutpattim eva tirodhāna-bhūtāḥ karma-ādayaḥ kurvanti / avidyā cet tirodhānaṃ tirodhāna-bhūtataya āvidyayā sva-rūpa-bhūta-prakāśa-nāśa iti pūrvam eva uktam / asmākaṃ tv avidyā-rūpeṇa karmaṇā sva-rūpa-nitya-dharma-bhūta-prakāśaḥ saṃkucitaḥ / tena deva-ādi-sva-rūpa-ātma-abhimāno bhavati iti viśeṣaḥ / yatha ūktam ---
avidyā karma-saṃjñānyā tṛtīyā śaktir iṣyate //
yathā kṣetra-śaktiḥ sā veṣṭitā nṛpa sarva-gā /
saṃsāra-tāpān akhilān avāpnoty atisaṃtatān //
tayā tirohitatvāc ca śaktiḥ kṣetra-jña-saṃjñitā /
sarva-bhūteṣu bhū-pāle tāratamyena vartate //
iti / kṣetra-jñānāṃ sva-dharma-bhūtasya jñānasya karma-saṃjñā-avidyayā saṃkocaṃ vikāsaṃ ca darśayati /

body.text: api cācchādikāvidyā śrutibhiś cāikyopadeśabalāc ca brahmasvarūpatirodhānaheyadoṣarūpāśrīyate tasyāś ca mithyārūpatvena prapañcavatsvadarśanamūladoṣāpekṣatvāt / na sā mithyā darśanamūladoṣaḥ syād iti brahmaiva mithyādarśanamūlaṃ syāt / tasyāś cānāditve 'pi mithyārūpatvād eva brahmadṛśyatvenaivānāditvāt taddarśanamūlaparamārthadoṣānabhyupagamāc ca brahmaiva taddarśanamūlaṃ syāt / tasya nityatvād anirmokṣa eva /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the covering <s>avidyā</s> is posited — on the basis of the <s>śruti</s> texts and the force of the teaching of unity (<s>aikya</s>) — as a defect of the nature of what is to be rejected (<s>heya</s>), capable of concealing the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. And since it is of the nature of falsity (<s>mithyā</s>), like the phenomenal world, it depends on a root defect that is the cause of its own [false] perception. That [<s>avidyā</s>] cannot itself be the false root defect of perception — and so <s>Brahman</s> itself would have to be the root of false perception. Even if <s>avidyā</s> is beginningless, precisely because it is of the nature of falsity, its beginninglessness consists only in being perceived by <s>Brahman</s> [from beginningless time]; and since no ultimate defect as the root of that perception is accepted, <s>Brahman</s> itself would have to be the root of that perception. And since <s>Brahman</s> is eternal, there would be no liberation whatsoever.

children.text: api ca acchādika-avidyā śrutibhiś ca aikya-upadeśa-balāc ca brahma-sva-rūpa-tirodhāna-heya-doṣa-rūpa-āśrīyate tasyāś ca mithyā-rūpatvena prapañcavat-sva-darśana-mūla-doṣa-apekṣatvāt / na sā mithyā darśana-mūla-doṣaḥ syād iti brahma eva mithyā-darśana-mūlaṃ syāt / tasyāś ca anāditve 'pi mithyā-rūpatvād eva brahma-dṛśyatvena eva anāditvāt tad-darśana-mūla-parama-artha-doṣa-anabhyupagamāc ca brahma eva tad-darśana-mūlaṃ syāt / tasya nityatvād anirmokṣa eva /

body.text:
ata evedam api nirastam -- ekam eva śarīraṃ jīvavat, nirjīvānītarāṇi śarīrāṇi svapnadṛṣṭanānāvidhānantaśarīrāṇāṃ yathā nirjīvatvam / tatra svapne draṣṭuḥ śarīram ekam eva jīvavat / tasya svapnavelāyāṃ dṛśyabhūtanānāvidhaśarīrāṇāṃ nirjīvatvam eva / anenaikenaiva parikalpitatvāj jīvā mithyābhūtā iti brahmaṇā svasvarūpavyatiriktasya jīvabhāvasya sarvaśarīrāṇāṃ ca kalpitatvād ekasminn api śarīre śarīravaj jīvabhāvasya ca mithyārūpatvāt sarvāṇi śarīrāṇi mithyārūpāṇi, tatra jīvabhāvaś ca mithyārūpa ity ekasya śarīrasya tatra jīvabhāvasya ca na kaścid viśeṣaḥ / asmākaṃ tu svapne draṣṭuḥ svaśarīrasya tasminn ātmasadbhāvasya ca prabodhavelāyām abādhitatvān anyeṣāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ tadgatajīvānāṃ ca bādhitatvāt
te sarve mithyābhūtāḥ svaśarīram ekaṃ tasmiñ jīvabhāvaś ca paramārtha iti viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, this [argument] too is refuted: that only one body is animate like the <s>jīva</s>, while other bodies are inanimate — just as the innumerable bodies of various kinds seen in a dream are inanimate. In that case, in a dream, only the dreamer's body is animate; the various bodies that are objects of perception during the dream state are indeed inanimate. [The Advaitin argues:] since [everything] is imagined by this one [<s>Brahman</s>] alone, the <s>jīvas</s> are unreal; since the state of being a <s>jīva</s> distinct from <s>Brahman</s>'s own nature, and all bodies, are imagined [by <s>Brahman</s>], the <s>jīva</s>-state even in one body is of an illusory nature, and therefore all bodies are of an illusory nature, and the <s>jīva</s>-state therein is also of an illusory nature — so there is no distinction of the one body and the <s>jīva</s>-state therein [from others]. But for us, since in a dream the dreamer's own body and the existence of the self therein are not sublated upon waking, while other bodies and the <s>jīvas</s> therein are sublated, all those [dream-objects] are unreal, whereas the one's own body and the <s>jīva</s>-state therein are ultimately real — this is the distinction.

children.text:
ata eva idam api nirastam --- ekam eva śarīraṃ jīvavat, nirjīvāni itarāṇi śarīrāṇi svapna-dṛṣṭa-nānā-vidha-ananta-śarīrāṇāṃ yathā nirjīvatvam / tatra svapne draṣṭuḥ śarīram ekam eva jīvavat / tasya svapna-velāyāṃ dṛśya-bhūta-nānā-vidha-śarīrāṇāṃ nirjīvatvam eva / anena ekena eva parikalpitatvāj jīvā mithyā-bhūtā iti brahmaṇā sva-sva-rūpa-vyatiriktasya jīva-bhāvasya sarva-śarīrāṇāṃ ca kalpitatvād ekasminn api śarīre śarīravaj jīva-bhāvasya ca mithyā-rūpatvāt sarvāṇi śarīrāṇi mithyā-rūpāṇi, tatra jīva-bhāvaś ca mithyā-rūpa ity ekasya śarīrasya tatra jīva-bhāvasya ca na kaścid viśeṣaḥ / asmākaṃ tu svapne draṣṭuḥ sva-śarīrasya tasminn ātma-sad-bhāvasya ca prabodha-velāyām abādhitatvān anyeṣāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ tad-gata-jīvānāṃ ca bādhitatvāt
te sarve mithyā-bhūtāḥ sva-śarīram ekaṃ tasmiñ jīva-bhāvaś ca parama-artha iti viśeṣaḥ /

body.text: api ca kena vā vidyānivṛttiḥ sā kīdṛśīti vivecanīyam / aikyajñānaṃ nivartakaṃ nivṛttiś cānirvacanīyapratyanīkākāreti cet / anirvacanīyapratyanīkaṃ nirvacanīyaṃ tac ca sad vāsad vā dvirūpaṃ vā koṭyantaraṃ na vidyate / brahmavyatirekeṇaitadabhyupagame punar avidyā na nivṛttā syāt / brahmaiva cen nivṛttis tatprāg apy aviśiṣṭam iti vedāntajñānāt pūrvam eva nivṛttiḥ syāt / aikyajñānaṃ nivartakaṃ tadabhāvāt saṃsāra iti bhavaddarśanaṃ vihanyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, by what [means] is <s>avidyā</s> removed, and of what nature is that [removal]? If [one says:] 'the knowledge of unity is the remover, and the removal is of a nature opposed to the indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>)' — that which is opposed to the indescribable must be describable, and that is either existent or non-existent, or of both natures — no other alternative exists. If this [removal] is accepted as other than <s>Brahman</s>, then <s>avidyā</s> would not be removed. And if the removal is <s>Brahman</s> itself, then since it was no different even before [the arising of knowledge], the removal would have occurred before Vedāntic knowledge itself. [Thus] your view that the knowledge of unity is the remover and that <s>saṃsāra</s> exists due to its absence is defeated.

children.text: api ca kena vā vidyā-nivṛttiḥ sā kīdṛśi īti vivecanīyam / aikya-jñānaṃ nivartakaṃ nivṛttiś ca anirvacanīya-pratyanīka-ākāra īti cet / anirvacanīya-pratyanīkaṃ nirvacanīyaṃ tac ca sad va āsad vā dvi-rūpaṃ vā koṭy-antaraṃ na vidyate / brahma-vyatirekeṇa etad-abhyupagame punar avidyā na nivṛttā syāt / brahma eva cen nivṛttis tat-prāg apy aviśiṣṭam iti vedānta-jñānāt pūrvam eva nivṛttiḥ syāt / aikya-jñānaṃ nivartakaṃ tad-abhāvāt saṃsāra iti bhavad-darśanaṃ vihanyate /

body.text: kiñ ca nivartakajñānasyāpy avidyārūparvāt tannivartanaṃ keneti vaktavyam / nivartakajñānaṃ svetarasamastabhedaṃ nivartya kṣaṇikatvād eva svayam eva vinaśyati dāvānalaviṣanāśanaviṣāntaravad iti cen na / nivartakajñānasya brahmavyatiriktatvena tatsvarūpatadutpattivināśānāṃ mithyārūpatvāt tadvināśarūpā vidyā tiṣṭhaty eveti tadvināśadarśanasya nivartakaṃ vaktacyam eva / dāvāgnyādīnām api pūrvāvasthāvirodhipariṇāmaparaṃparāvarjanīyaiva /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, since the removing knowledge itself is also of the nature of <s>avidyā</s>, one must say by what it is removed. If [one says:] 'the removing knowledge, having removed all differences other than itself, perishes of its own accord due to its momentariness — like a forest fire or a poison that destroys another poison' — no. Since the removing knowledge is other than <s>Brahman</s>, its own nature, its arising, and its destruction are all of an illusory nature. Therefore, the <s>vidyā</s> in the form of the destruction of that [knowledge] persists — and one must state what removes the perception of its destruction. Even with forest fires and the like, an inevitable succession of transformations contrary to the prior state must be accepted.

children.text: kiñ ca nivartaka-jñānasya apy avidyā-rūparvāt tan-nivartanaṃ kena iti vaktavyam / nivartaka-jñānaṃ sva itara-samasta-bhedaṃ nivartya kṣaṇikatvād eva svayam eva vinaśyati dāva-anala-viṣa-nāśana-viṣa-antaravad iti cen na / nivartaka-jñānasya brahma-vyatiriktatvena tat-sva-rūpa-tad-utpatti-vināśānāṃ mithyā-rūpatvāt tad-vināśa-rūpā vidyā tiṣṭhaty eva iti tad-vināśa-darśanasya nivartakaṃ vaktacyam eva / dāva-agny-ādīnām api pūrva-avasthā-virodhi-pariṇāma-paraṃpara-avarjanīya aiva /

body.text:
api ca cinmātrabrahmavyatiriktakṛtsnaniṣedhaviṣayajñānasya ko 'yaṃ jñātā / adhyāsarūpa iti cen na / tasya niṣedhatayā nivartakajñānakarmatvāt tatkartṛtvānupapatteḥ / brahmasvarūpa eveti cen na / brahmaṇo nivartakajñānaṃ prati jñātṛtvaṃ kiṃ svarūpam utādhyastam / adhyastaṃ ced ayam adhyāsas tanmūlavidyāntaraṃ ca nivartakajñānaviṣayatayā tiṣṭhaty eva / tannivartakāntarābhyupagame tasyāpi trirūpatayānavasthaiva / sarvasya hi jñānasya trirūpakatvavirahe jñānatvam eva hīyate / kasyacit kaṃcanārthaviśeṣaṃ prati siddhirūpatvāt / jñānasya trirūpatvavirahe bhavatāṃ svarūpabhūtajñānavan nivartakajñānam apy anivartakaṃ syāt / brahmasvarūpasyaiva jñātṛtvābhyupagame 'smadīya eva pakṣaḥ parigṛhītaḥ syāt / nivartakajñānasvarūpajñātṛtvaṃ ca svanivartyāntargatam
iti vacanaṃ bhūtalavyatiriktaṃ kṛtsnaṃ chinnaṃ devadattenety asyām eva chedanakriyāyām asyāś chedanakriyāyāś chettṛtvasya ca chedyāntarbhāvavacanavad upahāsyam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, who is this knower of the knowledge whose object is the negation of everything other than <s>Brahman</s>, which is pure consciousness? If [one says:] 'one in the form of superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>)' — no, because that [superimposed knower] is the object of negation and hence the object of the removing knowledge, and therefore cannot be the agent of that [knowledge]. If [one says:] 'the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> itself' — no. Is <s>Brahman</s>'s knower-hood with respect to the removing knowledge its own nature or superimposed? If superimposed, this superimposition and the <s>avidyā</s> that is its root persist as the object of the removing knowledge. If one accepts another remover for that, then because that too has three aspects [knower, knowledge, known], there is an infinite regress. For all knowledge, in the absence of the threefold nature, loses its very character as knowledge — since some [cognition] has the nature of being established with respect to some particular object. In the absence of the threefold nature of knowledge, your removing knowledge too, like the knowledge that is [<s>Brahman</s>'s] own nature, would be non-removing. If one accepts that <s>Brahman</s>'s own essential nature itself is the knower, then our very position would be adopted. And the statement that the knower-hood belonging to the essential nature of the removing knowledge is included within what is to be removed by it — is as laughable as saying 'everything other than a clod of earth has been cut by <s>Devadatta</s>' and including the cutting action itself and the cutter-hood [of <s>Devadatta</s>] within what is cut.

children.text:
api ca cin-mātra-brahma-vyatirikta-kṛtsna-niṣedha-viṣaya-jñānasya ko 'yaṃ jñātā / adhyāsa-rūpa iti cen na / tasya niṣedhatayā nivartaka-jñāna-karmatvāt tat-kartṛtva-anupapatteḥ / brahma-sva-rūpa eva iti cen na / brahmaṇo nivartaka-jñānaṃ prati jñātṛtvaṃ kiṃ sva-rūpam uta adhyastam / adhyastaṃ ced ayam adhyāsas tan-mūla-vidyā-antaraṃ ca nivartaka-jñāna-viṣayatayā tiṣṭhaty eva / tan-nivartaka-antara-abhyupagame tasya api tri-rūpataya ānavastha aiva / sarvasya hi jñānasya tri-rūpakatva-virahe jñānatvam eva hīyate / kasyacit kaṃcana artha-viśeṣaṃ prati siddhi-rūpatvāt / jñānasya tri-rūpatva-virahe bhavatāṃ sva-rūpa-bhūta-jñānavan nivartaka-jñānam apy anivartakaṃ syāt / brahma-sva-rūpasya eva jñātṛtva-abhyupagame 'smadīya eva pakṣaḥ parigṛhītaḥ syāt / nivartaka-jñāna-sva-rūpa-jñātṛtvaṃ ca sva-nivartya-antargatam
iti vacanaṃ bhūtala-vyatiriktaṃ kṛtsnaṃ chinnaṃ deva-dattena ity asyām eva chedana-kriyāyām asyāś chedana-kriyāyāś chettṛtvasya ca chedya-antarbhāva-vacanavad upahāsyam /

body.text:
api ca nikhilabhedanivartakam idam aikyajñānaṃ kena jātam iti vimarśanīyam / śrutyaiveti cen na / tasyā brahmavyatiriktāyā avidyāparikalpitatvāt prapañcabādhakajñānasyotpādakatvaṃ na saṃbhavati / tathā hi duṣṭakāraṇajātam api rajjusarpajñānaṃ na duṣṭakāraṇajanyena rajjur iyaṃ na sarpa iti jñānena bādhyate / rajjusarpajñānabhaye vartamāne kenacidbhrāntena puruṣeṇa rajjur iyaṃ na sarpa ityukte 'py ayaṃ bhrānta iti jñāte sati tadvacanaṃ rajjusarpajñānasya bādhakaṃ na bhavati bhayaṃ ca na nivartate / prayojakajñānavataḥ śravaṇavelāyām eva hi brahmavyatiriktatvena śruter api bhrāntimūlatvaṃ jñātam iti / nivartakajñānasya jñātus tatsāmagrībhūtaśāstrasya ca brahmavyatiriktatayā yadi bādhyatvam ucyate hanta tarhi prapañcanivṛtter mithyātvam āpatatīti prapañcasya satyatā syāt /
svapnadṛṣṭapuruṣavākyāvagatapitrādimaraṇasya mithyātvena pitrādisatyatāvat / kiñca tat tvam asy ādivākyaṃ na prapañcasya bādhakam / bhrāntimūlatvād bhrāntaprayuktarajjusarpabādhakavākyavat /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, one should examine: by what was this knowledge of unity, which removes all difference, produced? If [one says:] 'by scripture (<s>śruti</s>) itself' — no, because scripture, being other than <s>Brahman</s>, is imagined by <s>avidyā</s>, and hence it cannot produce knowledge that sublates the manifest world. For consider: even the cognition of a rope-snake, though produced by a defective cause, is not sublated by the cognition 'this is a rope, not a snake' produced by [another] defective cause. When the fear arising from the cognition of a rope-snake is present, and some deluded person says 'this is a rope, not a snake,' when it is known that he is deluded, his statement does not sublate the cognition of the rope-snake, and the fear is not removed. For at the very time of hearing, the scripture's being rooted in error is known — since it is other than <s>Brahman</s> — to one who possesses motivating knowledge. If the sublatable character of the removing knowledge, of its knower, and of the scripture that is part of its assemblage of conditions is asserted on the ground of their being other than <s>Brahman</s> — well then, the removal of the manifest world would itself be illusory, and hence the manifest world would be real!
Just as the illusoriness of the death of one's father learned from the words of a person seen in a dream [entails] the reality of the father. Moreover, the sentence 'that you are' and the like does not sublate the manifest world — because, being rooted in error, it is like the statement sublating a rope-snake uttered by a deluded person.

children.text:
api ca nikhila-bheda-nivartakam idam aikya-jñānaṃ kena jātam iti vimarśanīyam / śrutya aiva iti cen na / tasyā brahma-vyatiriktāyā avidyā-parikalpitatvāt prapañca-bādhaka-jñānasya utpādakatvaṃ na saṃbhavati / tathā hi duṣṭa-kāraṇa-jātam api rajju-sarpa-jñānaṃ na duṣṭa-kāraṇa-janyena rajjur iyaṃ na sarpa iti jñānena bādhyate / rajju-sarpa-jñāna-bhaye vartamāne kena-cid-bhrāntena puruṣeṇa rajjur iyaṃ na sarpa ity-ukte 'py ayaṃ bhrānta iti jñāte sati tad-vacanaṃ rajju-sarpa-jñānasya bādhakaṃ na bhavati bhayaṃ ca na nivartate / prayojaka-jñānavataḥ śravaṇa-velāyām eva hi brahma-vyatiriktatvena śruter api bhrānti-mūlatvaṃ jñātam iti / nivartaka-jñānasya jñātus tat-sāmagrī-bhūta-śāstrasya ca brahma-vyatiriktatayā yadi bādhyatvam ucyate hanta tarhi prapañca-nivṛtter mithyātvam āpatati iti prapañcasya satyatā syāt /
svapna-dṛṣṭa-puruṣa-vākya-avagata-pitr-ādi-maraṇasya mithyātvena pitr-ādi-satyatāvat / kiñca tat tvam asy ādi-vākyaṃ na prapañcasya bādhakam / bhrānti-mūlatvād bhrānta-prayukta-rajju-sarpa-bādhaka-vākyavat /

body.text: nanu ca svapne kasmiṃścid bhaye vartamāne svapnadaśāyām evāyaṃ svapna iti jñāte sati pūrvabhayanivṛttir dṛṣṭā / tadvad atrāpi saṃbhavatīti / naivam / svapnavelāyām eva so 'pi svapna iti jñāte sati punarbhayānivṛttir eva dṛṣṭeti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: But surely, when during a dream some fear is present, and within the dream state itself it is known 'this is a dream,' the cessation of the prior fear is observed! Likewise, it should be possible here too. Not so. When within the dream state itself it is known 'that too is a dream,' the non-cessation of fear is equally observed — so there is no distinction.

children.text: nanu ca svapne kasmiṃścid bhaye vartamāne svapna-daśāyām eva ayaṃ svapna iti jñāte sati pūrva-bhaya-nivṛttir dṛṣṭā / tadvad atra api saṃbhavati iti / na evam / svapna-velāyām eva so 'pi svapna iti jñāte sati punar-bhaya-anivṛttir eva dṛṣṭa īti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ /

body.text: śravaṇavelāyām eva so'pi svapna iti jñātam evetyuktam / yad api cedam uktaṃ bhrāntiparikalpitatvena mithyārūpam api śāstram advitīyaṃ brahmeti bodhayati tasya sato brahmaṇo viṣayasya paścāt tanabādhādarśanād brahma susthitam eveti / tad ayuktam / śūnyam eva tat tvam iti vākyena tasyāpi bādhitatvāt / idaṃ bhrāntimūlavākyam iti cet / sad advitīyaṃ brahmeti vākyam api bhrāntimūlam iti tvayaivoktam / paścāt tanabādhādarśanaṃ tu sarvaśūnyavākyasyaiveti viśeṣaḥ / sarvaśūnyavādino brahmavyatiriktavastumithyātvavādinaś ca svapakṣasādhanapramāṇapāramārthyānabyupagamenābhiyuktair vādānadhikāra eva pratipāditaḥ / adhikāro 'nabhyupāyatvān na vāde śūnyavādinaḥ / iti /
body.translated_text: It was already stated that at the very time of hearing, 'that too is a dream' is known. As for what was said — 'though of an illusory nature as imagined by error, scripture teaches that <s>Brahman</s> is one without a second, and since subsequently no sublation of that existent <s>Brahman</s> as its object is observed, <s>Brahman</s> stands well-established' — that is untenable, because even that [<s>Brahman</s>] is sublated by the sentence 'everything is void' as 'that is you.' If [one says:] 'that is a statement rooted in error' — you yourself have stated that the statement '<s>Brahman</s> is one without a second' is also rooted in error. The subsequent non-observation of sublation pertains to the statement of universal voidness alone — this is the distinction. Competent [philosophers] have demonstrated that the proponents of universal voidness (<s>sarvaśūnyavādin</s>) and the proponents of the unreality of everything other than <s>Brahman</s>, by not accepting the ultimate validity of the means of proof for their own positions, are in fact disqualified from debate: 'The voidist has no right to debate, because he does not accept [any valid] means.'

children.text: śravaṇa-velāyām eva so'pi svapna iti jñātam eva ity-uktam / yad api ca idam uktaṃ bhrānti-parikalpitatvena mithyā-rūpam api śāstram advitīyaṃ brahma iti bodhayati tasya sato brahmaṇo viṣayasya paścāt tan-abādha-adarśanād brahma susthitam eva iti / tad ayuktam / śūnyam eva tat tvam iti vākyena tasya api bādhitatvāt / idaṃ bhrānti-mūla-vākyam iti cet / sad advitīyaṃ brahma iti vākyam api bhrānti-mūlam iti tvaya aiva uktam / paścāt tan-abādha-adarśanaṃ tu sarva-śūnya-vākyasya eva iti viśeṣaḥ / sarva-śūnya-vādino brahma-vyatirikta-vastu-mithyātva-vādinaś ca sva-pakṣa-sādhana-pramāṇa-pāramārthya-anabyupagamena abhiyuktair vāda-anadhikāra eva pratipāditaḥ / adhikāro 'nabhyupāyatvān na vāde śūnya-vādinaḥ / iti /

body.text: api ca pratyakṣadṛṣṭasya prapañcasya mithyātvaṃ kena pramāṇena sādhyate / pratyakṣasya doṣamūlatvenānyathāsiddhisaṃbhavān nirdoṣaṃ śāstram ananyathāsiddhaṃ pratyakṣasya bādhakam iti cet / kena doṣeṇa jātaṃ pratyakṣam anantabhedaviṣayam iti vaktavyam / anādibhedavāsanākhyadoṣajātaṃ pratyakṣam iti cet / hanta tarhy anenaiva doṣeṇa jātaṃ śāstram apīty ekadoṣamūlatvāc chāstrapratyakṣayor na bādhyabādhakabhāvasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, by what means of valid knowledge is the unreality of the manifest world, which is perceived by direct perception, established? If [one says:] 'since perception is produced from a defect and hence can be otherwise accounted for, scripture, which is flawless and cannot be otherwise accounted for, sublates perception' — one must state by what defect the perception whose object is infinite distinctions is produced. If [one says:] 'perception is produced by the defect called beginningless habitual impressions of difference' — well then, scripture too is produced by that very defect, and since both scripture and perception have the same defective root, the sublater-sublated relation between scripture and perception is not established.

children.text: api ca pratyakṣa-dṛṣṭasya prapañcasya mithyātvaṃ kena pramāṇena sādhyate / pratyakṣasya doṣa-mūlatvena anyathā-siddhi-saṃbhavān nirdoṣaṃ śāstram ananyathā-siddhaṃ pratyakṣasya bādhakam iti cet / kena doṣeṇa jātaṃ pratyakṣam ananta-bheda-viṣayam iti vaktavyam / anādi-bheda-vāsanā-ākhya-doṣa-jātaṃ pratyakṣam iti cet / hanta tarhy anena eva doṣeṇa jātaṃ śāstram api ity eka-doṣa-mūlatvāc chāstra-pratyakṣayor na bādhya-bādhaka-bhāva-siddhiḥ /

body.text: ākāśavāyvādibhūtatadārabdhaśabdasparśādiyuktamanuṣyatvādisaṃsthānasaṃsthitapadārthagrāhi pratyakṣam / śāstraṃ tu pratyakṣādyaparicchedyasarvāntarātmatvasatyatvādyanantaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭabrahmasvarūpatadupāsanādyārādhanaprakāratatprāptipūrvakatatprasādalabhyaphalaviśeṣatadaniṣṭakaraṇamūlanigrahaviśeṣaviṣayam iti na śātrapratyakṣayor virodhaḥ / anādinidhanāvicchinnapāṭasaṃpradāyatādyanekaguṇaviśiṣṭasya śāstrasya balīyastvaṃ vadatā pratyakṣapāramārthyam avaśyam abhyupagantavyam ity alam anena śrutiśatavitativātavegaparāhatakudṛṣṭiduṣṭayuktijālatūlanirasanenety uparamyate /
body.translated_text: Perception apprehends entities configured in the forms of humanity and the like, which are composed of elements such as space, wind, and the like, and endowed with their products — sound, touch, and the like. Scripture, on the other hand, has for its subject matter the nature of <s>Brahman</s> qualified by infinite attributes such as being the inner self of all, truth, and the like — which are beyond the grasp of perception and other [ordinary means] — as well as the modes of worship and propitiation of that [<s>Brahman</s>], the attainment thereof, the particular fruits obtainable through its grace, and the particular punishments resulting from what displeases it. Therefore there is no contradiction between scripture and perception. By one who asserts the greater strength of scripture — qualified by many excellences such as its unbroken lineage of textual tradition without beginning or end — the ultimate reality of perception must necessarily be accepted. Enough of this refutation of the cobweb of corrupt reasoning generated by wrong views, blown away by the storm-force gale of hundreds of <s>śrutis</s> — here we rest.

children.text: ākāśa-vāyv-ādi-bhūta-tad-ārabdha-śabda-sparśa-ādi-yukta-manuṣyatva-ādi-saṃsthāna-saṃsthita-pada-artha-grāhi pratyakṣam / śāstraṃ tu pratyakṣa-ādy-aparicchedya-sarva-antara-ātmatva-satyatva-ādy-ananta-viśeṣaṇa-viśiṣṭa-brahma-sva-rūpa-tad-upāsana-ādy-ārādhana-prakāra-tat-prāpti-pūrvaka-tat-prasāda-labhya-phala-viśeṣa-tad-aniṣṭa-karaṇa-mūla-nigraha-viśeṣa-viṣayam iti na śātra-pratyakṣayor virodhaḥ / anādi-nidhana-avicchinna-pāṭa-saṃpradāyatā-ādy-aneka-guṇa-viśiṣṭasya śāstrasya balīyastvaṃ vadatā pratyakṣa-pāramārthyam avaśyam abhyupagantavyam ity alam anena śruti-śata-vitati-vāta-vega-parāhata-kudṛṣṭi-duṣṭa-yukti-jāla-tūla-nirasanena ity uparamyate /

body.text: dvitīye tu pakṣa upādhibrahmavyatiriktavastvantarānabhyupagamād brahmaṇy evopādhisaṃsargād aupādhikāḥ sarve doṣā brahmaṇy eva bhaveyuḥ / tataś cāpahatapāpmatvādinirdoṣatvaśrutayaḥ sarve vihanyante /
body.translated_text: In the second view, however, since no entity other than <s>Brahman</s> [qualified by] limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) is accepted, all defects that are <s>upādhi</s>-based would belong to <s>Brahman</s> itself due to the contact with <s>upādhis</s> in <s>Brahman</s> alone. Consequently, all <s>śruti</s> passages declaring [<s>Brahman</s>'s] freedom from evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and flawlessness would be contradicted.

children.text: dvitīye tu pakṣa upādhi-brahma-vyatirikta-vastv-antara-anabhyupagamād brahmaṇy eva upādhi-saṃsargād aupādhikāḥ sarve doṣā brahmaṇy eva bhaveyuḥ / tataś ca apahata-pāpmatva-ādi-nirdoṣatva-śrutayaḥ sarve vihanyante /

body.text:
yathā ghaṭākāśādeḥ paricchinnatayā mahākāśād vailakṣaṇyaṃ parasparabhedaś ca dṛśyate -- tatrasthā guṇā vā doṣā vānavacchinne mahākāśe na saṃbadhyante evam upādhikṛtabhedavyavasthitajīvagatā doṣā anupahite pare brahmaṇi na saṃbadhyanta iti cet / naitad upapadyate / niravayavasyākāśasyānavacchedyasya ghaṭādibhiś chedāsaṃbhavāt tenaivākāśena ghaṭādayaḥ saṃyuktā iti brahmaṇo 'py acchedyatvād brahmaivopādhisaṃyuktaṃ syāt / ghaṭasaṃyuktākāśapradeśo 'nyasmād ākāśapradeśād bhidyata ic cet / ākāśasyaikasyaiva pradeśabhedena ghaṭādisaṃyogād ghaṭādau gacchati tasya ca pradeśabhedasyāniyama iti tadvad brahmaṇy eva pradeśabhedāniyamenopādhisaṃsargād upādhau gacchati saṃyuktaviyuktabrahmapradeśabhedāc ca brahmaṇy evopādhisaṃsargaḥ
kṣaṇe kṣaṇe bandhamokṣau syātām iti santaḥ parihasanti /
body.translated_text:
If [it be said]: just as the space enclosed in a pot (<s>ghaṭākāśa</s>) is seen to differ from the great space (<s>mahākāśa</s>) by being delimited, and to differ from other [enclosed spaces] — and the qualities or defects of things situated therein do not pertain to the undelimited great space — so too, the defects belonging to <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) whose differentiation is established through limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) do not pertain to the unaffected Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — that is not tenable. Because <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is without parts and cannot be divided, it is impossible for it to be cut by pots and the like. It is that very same space that is conjoined with the pots, etc. Therefore, since <s>Brahman</s> too is indivisible, <s>Brahman</s> itself would be conjoined with the limiting adjuncts. If [one says]: the region of space conjoined with the pot differs from another region of space — [we reply]: since the one and same space, through the difference of regions, is conjoined with pots and the like, when the pot moves, that [space-region] moves with it; and since there is no fixity of such regional differences, similarly in <s>Brahman</s> itself, through the unfixed association with limiting adjuncts through regional differences, the limiting adjunct moves; and from the difference of <s>Brahman</s>-regions that are conjoined and disjoined,
bondage and liberation would occur at every moment in <s>Brahman</s> itself — thus the wise ridicule [this view].

children.text:
yathā ghaṭa-ākāśa-ādeḥ paricchinnatayā mahā-ākāśād vailakṣaṇyaṃ paraspara-bhedaś ca dṛśyate --- tatra-sthā guṇā vā doṣā va ānavacchinne mahā-ākāśe na saṃbadhyante evam upādhi-kṛta-bheda-vyavasthita-jīva-gatā doṣā anupahite pare brahmaṇi na saṃbadhyanta iti cet / na etad upapadyate / niravayavasyā akāśasya anavacchedyasya ghaṭa-ādibhiś chedā-saṃbhavāt tena evā akāśena ghaṭa-ādayaḥ saṃyuktā iti brahmaṇo 'py acchedyatvād brahma eva upādhi-saṃyuktaṃ syāt / ghaṭa-saṃyukta-ākāśa-pradeśo 'nyasmād ākāśa-pradeśād bhidyata ic cet / ākāśasya ekasya eva pradeśa-bhedena ghaṭa-ādi-saṃyogād ghaṭa-ādau gacchati tasya ca pradeśa-bhedasya aniyama iti tadvad brahmaṇy eva pradeśa-bheda-aniyamena upādhi-saṃsargād upādhau gacchati saṃyukta-viyukta-brahma-pradeśa-bhedāc ca brahmaṇy eva upādhi-saṃsargaḥ
kṣaṇe kṣaṇe bandha-mokṣau syātām iti santaḥ parihasanti /

body.text: niravayavasyaivākāśasya śrotrendriyatve 'pīndriyavyavasthāvad brahmaṇy api vyavasthopapadyata iti cet / na vāyuviśeṣasaṃskṛtakarṇapradeśasaṃyuktasyaivākāśapradeśasyendriyatvāt tasya ca pradeśāntarābhede 'pīndriyavyavasthopapadyate / ākāśasya tu sarveṣāṃ śarīreṣu gacchat svaniyamena sarvapradeśasaṃyoga iti brahmaṇy upādhisaṃyogapradeśāniyama eva /
body.translated_text: If [it be said]: just as even the partless space, which is the organ of hearing, has a determinate organ-arrangement, so too there can be a determinate arrangement in <s>Brahman</s> — [we reply]: No, because only the region of space conjoined with the ear-cavity, which has been specially modified by a particular type of air, serves as the sense organ. Even though that [organ-region] is not different from other regions, the determinate arrangement of the organ is tenable. But since space, moving into all bodies, is conjoined with all regions by its own rule, in <s>Brahman</s> too there is precisely an unfixed association of limiting-adjunct regions.

children.text: niravayavasya evā akāśasya śrotra-indriyatve 'pi indriya-vyavasthāvad brahmaṇy api vyavastha ūpapadyata iti cet / na vāyu-viśeṣa-saṃskṛta-karṇa-pradeśa-saṃyuktasya evā akāśa-pradeśasya indriyatvāt tasya ca pradeśa-antara-abhede 'pi indriya-vyavastha ūpapadyate / ākāśasya tu sarveṣāṃ śarīreṣu gacchat sva-niyamena sarva-pradeśa-saṃyoga iti brahmaṇy upādhi-saṃyoga-pradeśa-aniyama eva /

body.text:
ākāśasya svarūpeṇaiva śrotrendriyatvam abhyupagamyāpīndriyavyavasthokatā / paramārthatas tv ākāśo na śrotrendriyam / vaikārikād ahaṃkārād ekādaśendriyāṇi jāyanta iti hi vaidikāḥ / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa --
taijasānīndriyāṇy āhur devā vaikārikā daśa /
ekādaśaṃ manaś cātra devā vaikārikāḥ smṛtāḥ // iti /
ayam arthaḥ / vaikārikas taijaso bhūtādir iti trividho 'haṃkāraḥ / sa ca kramāt sāttviko rājasas tāmasaś ca / tatra tāmasād bhūtāder ākāśādīni bhūtāni jāyanta iti sṛṣṭikramam uktvā taijasād rājasād ahaṃkārād ekadaśendriyāṇi jāyanta iti paramatam upanyasya sāttvikāhaṃkārād vaikārikānīndriyāṇi jāyanta iti svamatam ucyate -- devā vaikārikāḥ smṛtā iti / devā indriyāṇi / evam indriyāṇām āhaṃkārikāṇāṃ bhūtaiś cāpy āyanaṃ mahābhārata ucyate / bhautikatve 'pīndriyāṇām ākāśādibhūtavikāratvād evākāśādibhūtapariṇāmaviśeṣā vyavasthitā eva śarīravat puruṣāṇām indriyāṇi bhavantīti brahmaṇy acchedye niravayave nirvikāre tv aniyamenānantaheyopādhisaṃsargadoṣo duṣparihara eveti śraddadhānānām evāyam pakṣa iti śāstravido
na bahu manyante / svarūpapariṇāmābhyupagamād avikāratvaśrutir bādhyate / niravadyatā ca brahmaṇaḥ śaktipariṇāma iti cet / keyaṃ śaktir ucyate / kiṃ brahmapariṇāmarūpā / uta brahmaṇo 'nanyā kāpīti / ubhayapakṣe 'pi svarūpapariṇāmo 'varjanīya eva /
body.translated_text:
Even if the hearing-organ-hood of space in its own essential nature is accepted, the determinate organ-arrangement has been explained. But in ultimate reality, space is not the organ of hearing. For the Vedic [texts state]: 'From the transformative (<s>vaikārika</s>) ego, the eleven sense organs are born.' As stated by the blessed <s>Parāśara</s>:
'The sense organs are said to be of the <s>taijasa</s> (luminous) [type]; the ten gods are of the <s>vaikārika</s> (transformative) [type].
The eleventh, <s>manas</s> (mind), is also here; the gods are remembered as <s>vaikārika</s>.'
The meaning is this: the ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) is threefold — <s>vaikārika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>bhūtādi</s> (elemental). And these are respectively <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s>. Therein, having stated the order of creation — that from the <s>tāmasa bhūtādi</s>, the elements beginning with space are born — and having presented the opposing view that from the <s>rājasa taijasa ahaṃkāra</s> the eleven sense organs are born, his own view is stated — that from the <s>sāttvika ahaṃkāra</s>, the sense organs of the <s>vaikārika</s> type are born: 'the gods are remembered as <s>vaikārika</s>.' 'Gods' means sense organs. Thus, although the sense organs are products of the ego (<s>āhaṃkārika</s>), their being seated in the elements is also stated in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>. Even if the sense organs are elemental (<s>bhautika</s>), since they are modifications of elements beginning with space, specific transformations of elements beginning with space are determinately established as sense organs of persons, just like bodies. But in <s>Brahman</s>, which is indivisible, partless, and changeless, the defect of unfixed association with infinite reprehensible limiting adjuncts is inescapable — those who know the scriptures
do not esteem this position, [recognizing it as] only for the credulous. If the transformation of <s>Brahman's</s> own nature is accepted, the <s>śruti</s> declaring its changelessness is contradicted. If [one says]: <s>Brahman</s> is faultless because the transformation is of its power (<s>śakti</s>) — what is this power? Is it a transformation of <s>Brahman</s> itself? Or is it something not different from <s>Brahman</s>? In either case, the transformation of the essential nature is unavoidable.

children.text:
ākāśasya sva-rūpeṇa eva śrotra-indriyatvam abhyupagamya api indriya-vyavastha ūkatā / parama-arthatas tv ākāśo na śrotra-indriyam / vaikārikād ahaṃ-kārād ekādaśa-indriyāṇi jāyanta iti hi vaidikāḥ / yatha ūktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa ---
taijasāni indriyāṇy āhur devā vaikārikā daśa /
ekādaśaṃ manaś ca atra devā vaikārikāḥ smṛtāḥ // iti /
ayam arthaḥ / vaikārikas taijaso bhūta-ādir iti tri-vidho 'haṃkāraḥ / sa ca kramāt sāttviko rājasas tāmasaś ca / tatra tāmasād bhūta-āder ākāśa-ādīni bhūtāni jāyanta iti sṛṣṭi-kramam uktvā taijasād rājasād ahaṃkārād ekadaśa-indriyāṇi jāyanta iti para-matam upanyasya sāttvika-ahaṃkārād vaikārikāni indriyāṇi jāyanta iti sva-matam ucyate --- devā vaikārikāḥ smṛtā iti / devā indriyāṇi / evam indriyāṇām āhaṃkārikāṇāṃ bhūtaiś ca apy āyanaṃ mahā-bhārata ucyate / bhautikatve 'pi indriyāṇām ākāśa-ādi-bhūta-vikāratvād evā akāśa-ādi-bhūta-pariṇāma-viśeṣā vyavasthitā eva śarīravat puruṣāṇām indriyāṇi bhavanti iti brahmaṇy acchedye niravayave nirvikāre tv aniyamena ananta-heya-upādhi-saṃsarga-doṣo duṣparihara eva iti śraddadhānānām eva ayam pakṣa iti śāstra-vido
na bahu manyante / sva-rūpa-pariṇāma-abhyupagamād avikāratva-śrutir bādhyate / niravadyatā ca brahmaṇaḥ śakti-pariṇāma iti cet / ka īyaṃ śaktir ucyate / kiṃ brahma-pariṇāma-rūpā / uta brahmaṇo 'nanyā ka āpi iti / ubhaya-pakṣe 'pi sva-rūpa-pariṇāmo 'varjanīya eva /

body.text: tṛtīye 'pi pakṣe jīvabrahmaṇor bhedavad abhedasya cābhyupagamāt tasya ca tadbhāvāt saubharibhedavac ca svāvatārabhedavac ca sarvasyeśvarabhedatāt sarve jīvagatā doṣās tasyaiva syuḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati / īśvaraḥ svarūpeṇaiva suranaratiryaksthāvarādibhedenāvasthita iti hi tadātmakatvavarṇanaṃ kriyate / tathā saty ekamṛtpiṇḍārabdhaghaṭaśarāvādigatāny udakāharaṇādīni sarvakāryāṇi yathā tasyaiva bhavanti, evaṃ sarvajīvagatasukhaduḥkhādi sarvam īśvaragatam eva syāt /
body.translated_text: Even in the third position [<s>bhedābheda</s>, difference-and-non-difference], since both difference and non-difference of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s> are accepted, and since [they maintain] the state of being that [<s>Brahman</s>], and since — like the divisions of <s>Saubhari</s> and like the divisions of one's own <s>avatāras</s> — all [beings] are divisions of <s>Īśvara</s>, all the defects belonging to <s>jīvas</s> would belong to Him alone. What is being stated is this: it is described that <s>Īśvara</s> is situated by his very own nature in the divisions of gods, humans, animals, plants, etc. — for that is how his being their very self is described. That being so, just as all functions such as fetching water etc. belonging to pots, plates, etc. fashioned from a single lump of clay are [functions] of that very [clay], so too all the pleasure, suffering, etc. belonging to all <s>jīvas</s> would be attributable to <s>Īśvara</s> alone.

children.text: tṛtīye 'pi pakṣe jīva-brahmaṇor bhedavad abhedasya ca abhyupagamāt tasya ca tad-bhāvāt saubhari-bhedavac ca sva-avatāra-bhedavac ca sarvasyā iśvara-bhedatāt sarve jīva-gatā doṣās tasya eva syuḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati / īśvaraḥ sva-rūpeṇa eva sura-nara-tiryak-sthāvara-ādi-bhedena avasthita iti hi tad-ātmakatva-varṇanaṃ kriyate / tathā saty eka-mṛt-piṇḍa-ārabdha-ghaṭa-śarāva-ādi-gatāny udaka-āharaṇa-ādīni sarva-kāryāṇi yathā tasya eva bhavanti, evaṃ sarva-jīva-gata-sukha-duḥkha-ādi sarvam īśvara-gatam eva syāt /

body.text:
ghaṭaśarāvādisaṃsthānānupayuktamṛddravyaṃ yathā kāryāntarānvitam evam eva surapaśumanujādijīvatvānupayukteśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ satyasaṃkalpatvādikalyāṇaguṇākara iti cet satyaṃ sa eveśvara ekenāṃśena kalyāṇaguṇagaṇākaraḥ sa evānyenāṃśena heyaguṇākara ity uktam / dvayor aṃśayor īśvarāviśeṣāt / dvav aṃśau vyavasthitav iti cet / kas tena lābhaḥ / ekasyaivānekāṃśena nityaduḥkhitvād aṃśāntareṇa sukhitvam api neśvaratvāya kalpate / yathā devadattasyaikasmin haste candanapaṅkānulepakeyūrakaṭakāṅgulīyālaṃkāras tasyaivānyasmin haste mudgarābhighātaḥ kālānalajvālānupraveśaś ca tadvad eveśvarasya syād iti brahmājñānapakṣād api pāpīyān ayaṃ bhedābhedapakṣaḥ / aparimitaduḥkhasya pāramārthikatvāt
saṃsāriṇām anantatvena dustaratvāc ca /
body.translated_text:
If [one says]: just as the clay substance, which is unfit for the configurations of pots, plates, etc., is associated with other effects — so too <s>Īśvara</s>, unfit for being the selves of gods, animals, humans, etc., is omniscient, a repository of auspicious qualities such as true resolve, etc. — [we reply]: True, that same <s>Īśvara</s>, by one portion, is the repository of a multitude of auspicious qualities, and that same [<s>Īśvara</s>], by another portion, is the repository of reprehensible qualities — thus it has been stated. Because there is no difference between the two portions as being <s>Īśvara</s>. If [one says]: the two portions are determinately established — what is the gain from that? Since one and the same [being] is eternally suffering through one portion, being happy through another portion does not constitute <s>Īśvara</s>-hood. Just as <s>Devadatta</s> on one hand has his hand anointed with sandalwood paste and adorned with bracelets, armlets, and rings, and on his other hand suffers the blow of a mace and the entry of the flames of the fire of time — so it would be for <s>Īśvara</s>. Thus this <s>bhedābheda</s> (difference-and-non-difference) position is even worse than the <s>Brahman</s>-as-locus-of-ignorance position — because the unlimited suffering [of souls] is ultimately real,
and because <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), being endless for the worldly beings, is impossible to cross.

children.text:
ghaṭa-śarāva-ādi-saṃsthāna-anupayukta-mṛd-dravyaṃ yathā kārya-antara-anvitam evam eva sura-paśu-manuja-ādi-jīvatva-anupayukta-īśvaraḥ sarva-jñaḥ satya-saṃkalpatva-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ākara iti cet satyaṃ sa evā iśvara ekena aṃśena kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-ākaraḥ sa eva anyena aṃśena heya-guṇa-ākara ity uktam / dvayor aṃśayor īśvara-aviśeṣāt / dvav aṃśau vyavasthitav iti cet / kas tena lābhaḥ / ekasya eva aneka-aṃśena nitya-duḥkhitvād aṃśa-antareṇa sukhitvam api nā iśvaratvāya kalpate / yathā deva-dattasya ekasmin haste candana-paṅka-anulepa-keyūra-kaṭaka-aṅgulīya-alaṃkāras tasya eva anyasmin haste mudgara-abhighātaḥ kāla-anala-jvāla-anupraveśaś ca tadvad evā iśvarasya syād iti brahma-ajñāna-pakṣād api pāpīyān ayaṃ bheda-abheda-pakṣaḥ / aparimita-duḥkhasya pāramārthikatvāt
saṃsāriṇām anantatvena dustaratvāc ca /

body.text: tasmād vilakṣaṇo 'yaṃ jīvāṃśa iti cet / āgato 'si tarhi madīyaṃ panthānam / īśvarasya svarūpeṇa tādātmyavarṇane syād ayaṃ doṣaḥ / ātmaśarīrabhāvena tu tādātmyapratipādane na kaścid doṣaḥ / praty uta nikhilabhuvananiyamanādir mahān ayaṃ guṇagaṇaḥ pratipādito bhavati / sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca mukhyavṛttam /
body.translated_text: If [one says]: therefore, this <s>jīva</s>-portion is distinct — then you have come to my path! If the identity with <s>Īśvara</s> in terms of essential nature is described, there would be this fault. But when the identity is taught through the body-self relation (<s>ātmaśarīrabhāva</s>), there is no fault at all. On the contrary, a great host of qualities — the governance of the entire universe, etc. — is established. And the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is in the primary sense.

children.text: tasmād vilakṣaṇo 'yaṃ jīva-aṃśa iti cet / āgato 'si tarhi madīyaṃ panthānam / īśvarasya sva-rūpeṇa tādātmya-varṇane syād ayaṃ doṣaḥ / ātma-śarīra-bhāvena tu tādātmya-pratipādane na kaścid doṣaḥ / praty uta nikhila-bhuvana-niyamana-ādir mahān ayaṃ guṇa-gaṇaḥ pratipādito bhavati / sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca mukhya-vṛttam /

body.text: api caikasya vastuno bhinnābhinnatvaṃ viruddhatvān na saṃbhavatītyuktam / ghaṭasya paṭād bhinnatve sati tasya tasminn abhāvaḥ / abhinnatve sati tasya ca bhāva iti / ekasmin kāle caikasmin deśe caikasya hi padārthasya yugapatsadbhāvo 'sadbhāvaś ca viruddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, it has been stated that the simultaneous difference and non-difference of one and the same entity is not possible due to contradiction. When a pot is different from a cloth, there is the absence of the pot in that [cloth]. When it is non-different, there is the presence of that [pot] in that [cloth]. For one entity, the simultaneous real presence and absence in one place at one time is contradictory.

children.text: api ca ekasya vastuno bhinna-abhinnatvaṃ viruddhatvān na saṃbhavati ity-uktam / ghaṭasya paṭād bhinnatve sati tasya tasminn abhāvaḥ / abhinnatve sati tasya ca bhāva iti / ekasmin kāle ca ekasmin deśe ca ekasya hi pada-arthasya yugapat-sad-bhāvo 'sad-bhāvaś ca viruddhaḥ /

body.text: jātyātmanā bhāvo vyaktyātmanā cābhāva iti cet / jāter muṇḍena cābhāve sati khaṇḍe muṇḍasyāpi sadbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / khaṇḍena ca jāter abhinnatve sadbhāvo bhinnatve cāsadbhāvaḥ aśve mahiśatvasyaiveti virodho duṣparihara eva / jātyāder vastusaṃsthānatayā vastunaḥ prakāratvāt prakāraprakāriṇoś ca padārthāntaratvaṃ prakārasya pṛthaksiddhyanarhatvaṃ pṛthaganupalambhaś ca tasya ca saṃsthānasya cānekavastuṣu prakāratayāvasthitaś cetyādi pūrvam uktam /
body.translated_text: If [one says]: there is presence qua the universal (<s>jāti</s>) and absence qua the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) — [we reply]: if the universal is absent from a bald head, then there would be the unwanted consequence that a broken [pot] too would have presence. And if the universal is non-different from the broken [pot], it would be present; if different, it would be absent — so the presence of buffalo-hood in a horse [would follow], and the contradiction is inescapable. Since universals and the like, being configurations of a real entity, are modes (<s>prakāra</s>) of the entity — and a mode and its possessor are not separate categories, and the mode is not capable of independent existence and is not independently apprehended, and that configuration is situated as a mode in multiple entities — all this was stated earlier.

children.text: jāty-ātmanā bhāvo vyakty-ātmanā ca abhāva iti cet / jāter muṇḍena ca abhāve sati khaṇḍe muṇḍasya api sad-bhāva-prasaṅgaḥ / khaṇḍena ca jāter abhinnatve sad-bhāvo bhinnatve ca asad-bhāvaḥ aśve mahiśatvasya eva iti virodho duṣparihara eva / jāty-āder vastu-saṃsthānatayā vastunaḥ prakāratvāt prakāra-prakāriṇoś ca pada-artha-antaratvaṃ prakārasya pṛthak-siddhy-anarhatvaṃ pṛthag-anupalambhaś ca tasya ca saṃsthānasya ca aneka-vastuṣu prakārataya āvasthitaś ca ity-ādi pūrvam uktam /

body.text: so 'yam iti buddhiḥ prakārāikyād ayam api daṇḍīti buddhimat / ayam ca jātyādiprakāro vastuno bheda ity ucyate / tadyoga eva vastuno bhinnam iti vyavahārahetur ityarthaḥ / sa ca vastuno bhedavyavahārahetuḥ svasya ca saṃvedanavat / yathā saṃvedanaṃ vastuno vyavahārahetuḥ svasya vyavahārahetuś ca bhavati /
body.translated_text: The cognition 'this is that [same person]' is due to the identity of the mode, just like the cognition 'this [person] too has a staff.' And this mode of universals etc. is called the 'difference' (<s>bheda</s>) of the entity. The presence of that [mode] alone is the basis for the practical usage '<s>bhinna</s>' (different) with respect to the entity — that is the meaning. And that basis for the practical usage of difference with respect to the entity is also [the basis] for its own cognition — just as cognition is the basis for the practical usage of the entity and also the basis for its own practical usage.

children.text: so 'yam iti buddhiḥ prakāra-aikyād ayam api daṇḍi īti buddhimat / ayam ca jāty-ādi-prakāro vastuno bheda ity ucyate / tad-yoga eva vastuno bhinnam iti vyavahāra-hetur ity-arthaḥ / sa ca vastuno bheda-vyavahāra-hetuḥ svasya ca saṃvedanavat / yathā saṃvedanaṃ vastuno vyavahāra-hetuḥ svasya vyavahāra-hetuś ca bhavati /

body.text: ata eva sanmātragrāhi pratyakṣaṃ na bhedagrāhītyādivādā nirastāḥ / jātyādisaṃsthānasaṃsthitasyaiva vastunaḥ pratyakṣeṇa gṛhītatvāt tasyaiva saṃsthānarūpajātyādeḥ pratiyogyapekṣayā bhedavyavahārahetutvāc ca / svarūpapariṇāmadoṣaś ca pūrvam evoktaḥ /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the claims that 'perception apprehends mere being and does not apprehend difference' etc. are refuted — because the entity is apprehended by perception only as situated in the configuration of universals and the like, and because that very [universal] which is of the nature of a configuration is the basis for the practical usage of difference in relation to its counterpositive. And the fault of transformation of essential nature has already been stated earlier.

children.text: ata eva san-mātra-grāhi pratyakṣaṃ na bheda-grāhi ity-ādi-vādā nirastāḥ / jāty-ādi-saṃsthāna-saṃsthitasya eva vastunaḥ pratyakṣeṇa gṛhītatvāt tasya eva saṃsthāna-rūpa-jāty-ādeḥ pratiyogy-apekṣayā bheda-vyavahāra-hetutvāc ca / sva-rūpa-pariṇāma-doṣaś ca pūrvam eva uktaḥ /

body.text:
yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ / ya ātmani tiṣṭhann ātmano 'ntaro ya ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ / yaḥ pṛthivīm antare saṃcaran yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaṃ pṛthivī na vedetyādi -- yo 'kṣaram antare saṃcaran yasyākṣaraṃ śarīraṃ akṣaraṃ na veda -- yo mṛtyum antare saṃcaran yasya mṛtyuḥ śarīraṃ yaṃ mṛtyur na veda -- eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmāpahatapāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ / dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte / tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśīti / antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ
