sarvātmā / tatsṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviśat / tadanupraviśya sac ca tyac cānṛtaṃ ca satyam abhavat / anena jīvenātmanetyādi / pṛthagātmānaṃ preritāraṃ matvā jaṣṭas tatas tenāmṛtatvam eti / bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā sarvaṃ proktaṃ trividhaṃ brahma, etat / nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān / pradhānakṣetrajñapatir guṇeśaḥ / jñājñau dvav ajav īśānīśav ityādiśrutiśatais tadupabṛṃhaṇaiḥ --
jagat sarvaṃ śarīraṃ te sthairyaṃ te vasudhātalam //
yat kiṃcit sṛjyate yena sattvajātena vai dvija /
tasya sṛjyasya saṃbhūtau tatsarvaṃ vai hares tanuḥ //
aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ //
sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi saṃniviṣṭo
mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca //
ityādivedavidagresaravālmīkiparāśaradvaipāyanavacobhiś ca parasya brahmaṇaḥ sarvasyātmatvāvagamāc cidacidātmakasya vastunas taccharīratvāvagamāc ca śarīrasya śarīriṇaṃ prati prakāratayaiva padārthatvāc śarīraśarīriṇoś ca dharmabhede 'pi tayor asaṃkarāt sarvaśarīraṃ brahmeti brahmaṇo vaibhavaṃ pratipādayadbhiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyādibhir mukhyavṛttaiḥ sarvacetanācetanaprakāraṃ brahmaivābhidhīyate / sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ hi dvayoḥ padayoḥ prakāradvayamukhenaikārthaniṣṭhatvaṃ / tasya caitasmin pakṣe mukhyatā / tathā hi tat tvam iti sāmānādhikaraṇye tad ityanena jagatkāraṇaṃ sarvakalyāṇaguṇagaṇākaraṃ niravadyaṃ brahmocyate / tvam iti ca cetanasāmānādhikaraṇyavṛttena jīvāntaryānirūpi taccharīraṃ tadātmatayāvasthitaṃ tatprakāraṃ
brahmocyate / itareṣu pakṣeṣu sāmānādhikaraṇyahānir brahmaṇaḥ sadeṣatā ca syāt /
body.translated_text: He who, standing in the earth, is interior to the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who controls the earth from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal one. He who, standing in the <s>ātman</s> (individual self), is interior to the <s>ātman</s>, whom the <s>ātman</s> does not know, whose body the <s>ātman</s> is, who controls the <s>ātman</s> from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal one. He who moves within the earth, whose body the earth is, whom the earth does not know — and so on — He who moves within the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), whose body the imperishable is, whom the imperishable does not know — He who moves within death, whose body death is, whom death does not know — this is the inner self of all beings, free from evil, divine, the one God <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. "Two birds, companions joined together, cling to the same tree. Of these two, one eats the sweet fruit, while the other, not eating, merely looks on." "Having entered within, He is the ruler of all beings, the self of all." "Having created that, He Himself entered into it. Having entered into it, He became both the real and the unreal, both the true and the untrue." "By this living self" — and so on. "Knowing the individual self and the impeller as distinct, delighted by Him, one attains immortality thereby." "Knowing the enjoyer, the object of enjoyment, and the impeller — all this threefold has been declared to be <s>Brahman</s>." "The eternal among eternals, the conscious among the conscious, the one among many who fulfills desires." "The lord of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field), the master of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)." "The two, the knowing and the unknowing, the lord and the non-lord, both unborn" — by hundreds of such <s>śruti</s> passages, and by their corroborating texts from <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>: "The entire universe is Your body; the surface of the earth is Your steadfastness." "Whatever is created by whatever class of beings, O twice-born, all that at the time of its origination is the body of <s>Hari</s>." "I am the self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, dwelling in the hearts of all beings." "And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and the removal of doubt." By these words of <s>Vālmīki</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, and <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, who are the foremost among those versed in the <s>Vedas</s> — since the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is understood to be the self of all, and since the entire reality consisting of conscious and non-conscious entities is understood to be His body, and since a body exists as a <s>prakāra</s> (mode/attribute) of the embodied self, and since despite the difference of properties between body and embodied self there is no confusion between them — <s>Brahman</s> whose body is everything, through <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-ordinate predication) and other expressions used in their primary sense, it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is denoted as having all conscious and non-conscious entities as Its modes. For <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> means the two terms referring to a single entity through two different modes of characterization. And in this interpretation, this usage is primary (non-metaphorical). Thus, in the <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> of "<s>tat tvam</s>" (That thou art), by the word "<s>tat</s>" (That), <s>Brahman</s> is denoted as the cause of the universe, the mine of all auspicious qualities, and free from all imperfection. By the word "<s>tvam</s>" (thou), used in co-ordinate predication with the conscious self, <s>Brahman</s> is denoted as characterized by the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) as Its inner controller, whose body the <s>jīva</s> is, who subsists as the self of the <s>jīva</s>, and who has the <s>jīva</s> as Its mode. In the other interpretations, <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> would be abandoned, and <s>Brahman</s> would be subject to defects.

children.text:
yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati eṣa ta ātma-antaryāmy-amṛtaḥ / ya ātmani tiṣṭhann ātmano 'ntaro ya ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati eṣa ta ātma-antaryāmy-amṛtaḥ / yaḥ pṛthivīm antare saṃcaran yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaṃ pṛthivī na veda ity-ādi --- yo 'kṣaram antare saṃcaran yasya akṣaraṃ śarīraṃ akṣaraṃ na veda --- yo mṛtyum antare saṃcaran yasya mṛtyuḥ śarīraṃ yaṃ mṛtyur na veda --- eṣa sarva-bhūta-antara-ātma-apahata-pāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ / dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣa-sva-jāte / tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśi iti / antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ
sarva-ātmā / tat-sṛṣṭvā tad eva anuprāviśat / tad-anupraviśya sac ca tyac ca anṛtaṃ ca satyam abhavat / anena jīvenā atmana īty-ādi / pṛthag-ātmānaṃ preritāraṃ matvā jaṣṭas tatas tena amṛtatvam eti / bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā sarvaṃ proktaṃ tri-vidhaṃ brahma, etat / nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān / pradhāna-kṣetra-jña-patir guṇa-īśaḥ / jña-ajñau dvav ajav īśa-anīśav ity-ādi-śruti-śatais tad-upabṛṃhaṇaiḥ ---
jagat sarvaṃ śarīraṃ te sthairyaṃ te vasudhā-talam //
yat kiṃcit sṛjyate yena sattva-jātena vai dvi-ja /
tasya sṛjyasya saṃbhūtau tat-sarvaṃ vai hares tanuḥ //
aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ //
sarvasya ca ahaṃ hṛdi saṃniviṣṭo
mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca //
ity-ādi-veda-vid-agre-sara-vālmīki-parāśara-dvaipāyana-vacobhiś ca parasya brahmaṇaḥ sarvasyā atmatva-avagamāc cid-acid-ātmakasya vastunas tac-charīratva-avagamāc ca śarīrasya śarīriṇaṃ prati prakārataya aiva pada-arthatvāc śarīra-śarīriṇoś ca dharma-bhede 'pi tayor asaṃkarāt sarva-śarīraṃ brahma iti brahmaṇo vaibhavaṃ pratipādayadbhiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇya-ādibhir mukhya-vṛttaiḥ sarva-cetana-acetana-prakāraṃ brahma eva abhidhīyate / sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ hi dvayoḥ padayoḥ prakāra-dvaya-mukhena eka-artha-niṣṭhatvaṃ / tasya ca etasmin pakṣe mukhyatā / tathā hi tat tvam iti sāmānādhikaraṇye tad ity-anena jagat-kāraṇaṃ sarva-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-ākaraṃ niravadyaṃ brahma ucyate / tvam iti ca cetana-sāmānādhikaraṇya-vṛttena jīva-antaryāni-rūpi tac-charīraṃ tad-ātmataya āvasthitaṃ tat-prakāraṃ
brahma ucyate / itareṣu pakṣeṣu sāmānādhikaraṇya-hānir brahmaṇaḥ sa-deṣatā ca syāt /

body.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati / brahmaivam avasthitam ity atraivaṃśabdārthabhūtaprakāratayaiva vicitracetanācetanātmakaprapañcasya sthūlasya sūkṣmasya ca sadbhāvaḥ / tathā ca bahu syāṃ prajāyeyety ayam arthaḥ saṃpanno bhavati / tasyaiveśvarasya kāryatayā kāraṇatayā ca nānāsaṃsthānasaṃsthitasya saṃsthānatayā cidacidvastujātam avasthitam iti /
body.translated_text: What has been stated amounts to this: the variegated world of conscious and non-conscious entities, whether in its gross or subtle state, exists only as the mode that constitutes the meaning of the word "<s>evam</s>" (thus) in the statement "<s>Brahman</s> exists thus." Accordingly, the text "May I become many, may I be born forth" yields this meaning: the entire reality consisting of conscious and non-conscious entities exists as the <s>saṃsthāna</s> (configuration/form) of that very <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord) who subsists in various configurations as both effect and cause.

children.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati / brahma evam avasthitam ity atra evaṃ-śabda-artha-bhūta-prakārataya aiva vicitra-cetana-acetana-ātmaka-prapañcasya sthūlasya sūkṣmasya ca sad-bhāvaḥ / tathā ca bahu syāṃ prajāyeya ity ayam arthaḥ saṃpanno bhavati / tasya evā iśvarasya kāryatayā kāraṇatayā ca nānā-saṃsthāna-saṃsthitasya saṃsthānatayā cid-acid-vastu-jātam avasthitam iti /

body.text:
nanu ca saṃsthānarūpeṇa prakāratayaivaṃśabdārthatvam jātiguṇayor eva dṛṣṭaṃ na dravyasya / svatantrasiddhiyogyasya padārthasyaivaṃśabdārthatayeśvarasya prakāramātratvam ayuktaṃ / ucyate -- dravyasyāpi daṇḍakuṇḍalāder dravyāntaraprakāratvaṃ dṛṣṭam eva / nanu ca daṇḍādeḥ svatantrasya dravyāntaraprakāratve matvarthīyapratyayo dṛṣṭaḥ / yathā daṇḍī kuṇḍalīti / ato gotvāditulyatayā cetanācetanasya dravyabhūtasya vastuna īśvaraprakāratayā sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ na yujyate / atrocyate -- gaur aśvo manuṣyo deva iti bhūtasaṃghātarūpāṇāṃ dravyāṇām eva devadatto manuṣyo jātaḥ puṇyaviśeṣeṇa yajñadatto gaurjātaḥ pāpena, anyaś cetanaḥ puṇyātirekeṇa devo jāta ityādidevādiśarīrāṇāṃ cetanaprakāratayā
lokadevayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ dṛṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Objection: It is observed that only <s>jāti</s> (universals) and <s>guṇa</s> (qualities) serve as modes in the sense of being the referent of the word "thus" (<s>evaṃśabdārthatva</s>), not <s>dravya</s> (substances). It is improper that a substance capable of independent existence should be reduced to a mere mode of <s>Īśvara</s> as the referent of the word "thus." Reply: It is indeed observed that even substances such as a staff or earrings serve as modes of other substances. Counter-objection: When an independently existing substance like a staff becomes a mode of another substance, we observe the possessive suffix (<s>matvarthīya</s>), as in "one who has a staff" (<s>daṇḍī</s>), "one who has earrings" (<s>kuṇḍalī</s>). Therefore, it is not proper to present a conscious or non-conscious substance as a mode of <s>Īśvara</s> through <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-ordinate predication) in the same way as universals like cow-ness. To this we reply: In expressions like "cow," "horse," "man," "god" — these are themselves substances in the form of aggregates of elements. And it is observed that co-ordinate predication between the person and the divine is used when a conscious being serves as the mode of such bodies — as in "<s>Devadatta</s> was born a man," "<s>Yajñadatta</s> was born a cow due to sin," "another conscious being was born a god due to extraordinary merit" — here the bodies of gods and others are presented through <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> with the conscious self as their mode.

children.text:
nanu ca saṃsthāna-rūpeṇa prakārataya aivaṃ-śabda-arthatvam jāti-guṇayor eva dṛṣṭaṃ na dravyasya / sva-tantra-siddhi-yogyasya pada-arthasya evaṃ-śabda-arthatayā īśvarasya prakāra-mātratvam ayuktaṃ / ucyate --- dravyasya api daṇḍa-kuṇḍala-āder dravya-antara-prakāratvaṃ dṛṣṭam eva / nanu ca daṇḍa-ādeḥ sva-tantrasya dravya-antara-prakāratve matv-arthīya-pratyayo dṛṣṭaḥ / yathā daṇḍī kuṇḍali īti / ato gotva-ādi-tulyatayā cetana-acetanasya dravya-bhūtasya vastuna īśvara-prakāratayā sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ na yujyate / atra ucyate --- gaur aśvo manuṣyo deva iti bhūta-saṃghāta-rūpāṇāṃ dravyāṇām eva deva-datto manuṣyo jātaḥ puṇya-viśeṣeṇa yajña-datto gaur-jātaḥ pāpena, anyaś cetanaḥ puṇya-atirekeṇa devo jāta ity-ādi-deva-ādi-śarīrāṇāṃ cetana-prakāratayā
loka-devayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ dṛṣṭam /

body.text: ayam arthaḥ -- jātir vā guṇo vā dravyaṃ vā na tatrādaraḥ / kaṃcana dravyaviśeṣaṃ prati viśeṣaṇatayaiva yasya sadbhāvas tasya tadapṛthaksiddhes tatprakāratayā tatsāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ yuktam / yasya punar dravyasya pṛthaksiddhasyaiva kadācitkvaciddravyāntaraprakāratvam iṣyate tatra matvarthīyapratyaya iti viśeṣaḥ / evam eva sthāvarajaṅgamātmakasya sarvasya vastuna īśvaraśarīratvena tatprakāratayaiva svarūpasadbhāva iti / tatprakārīśvara eva tattacchabdenābhidhīyata iti tatsāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ yuktaṃ / tad evaitat sarvaṃ pūrvam eva nāmarūpavyākaraṇaśrutivivaraṇe prapañcitam /
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: whether it be a universal, a quality, or a substance — that does not matter. Whatever exists as a qualifier of a particular substance, since it is inseparable from it (<s>apṛthaksiddhi</s>), it is proper to present it through <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-ordinate predication) as a mode of that substance. However, when a substance that has independent existence occasionally becomes a mode of another substance, the possessive suffix (<s>matvarthīya</s>) is used — that is the distinction. In exactly this way, since all reality comprising the moving and the non-moving exists as the body of <s>Īśvara</s>, its very existence is as His mode. <s>Īśvara</s> who has these as His modes is Himself denoted by the words designating those entities, and hence it is proper to present this through <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>. All this has already been elaborated earlier in the exposition of the <s>śruti</s> passages on the differentiation of names and forms (<s>nāmarūpavyākaraṇa</s>).

children.text: ayam arthaḥ --- jātir vā guṇo vā dravyaṃ vā na tatra-ādaraḥ / kaṃcana dravya-viśeṣaṃ prati viśeṣaṇataya aiva yasya sad-bhāvas tasya tad-apṛthak-siddhes tat-prakāratayā tat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ yuktam / yasya punar dravyasya pṛthak-siddhasya eva kadācit-kvacid-dravya-antara-prakāratvam iṣyate tatra matv-arthīya-pratyaya iti viśeṣaḥ / evam eva sthāvara-jaṅgama-ātmakasya sarvasya vastuna īśvara-śarīratvena tat-prakārataya aiva sva-rūpa-sad-bhāva iti / tat-prakāri-īśvara eva tat-tac-chabdena abhidhīyata iti tat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratipādanaṃ yuktaṃ / tad eva etat sarvaṃ pūrvam eva nāma-rūpa-vyākaraṇa-śruti-vivaraṇe prapañcitam /

body.text: ataḥ prakṛtipuruṣamahadahaṃkāratanmātrabhūtendriyatadārabdhacaturdaśabhuvanātmakabrahmāṇḍatadantarvartidevatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvarādisarvaprakārasaṃsthānasaṃsthitaṃ kāryam api sarvaṃ brahmaiveti kāraṇabhūtabrahmavijñānād eva sarvaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīty ekavijñānena sarvavijñānam upapannataram / tad evaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvādimukhena kṛtsnasya cidacidvastunaḥ parabrahmaprakāratayā tadātmakatvam uktam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the entire effect — consisting of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal matter), <s>Puruṣa</s> (individual souls), <s>Mahat</s> (cosmic intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), gross elements, sense organs, the fourteen worlds constituting the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) originating from these, and all the gods, animals, humans, plants, and other beings of every kind within it — all this is nothing but <s>Brahman</s>. Hence, through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> who is the cause, everything becomes known; thus the promise that "through one cognition all is cognized" is most well established. In this way, through the relation of cause and effect and other such means, it has been stated that the entire reality of conscious and non-conscious entities, being modes of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>tadātmaka</s>).

children.text: ataḥ prakṛti-puruṣa-mahad-ahaṃkāra-tanmātra-bhūta-indriya-tad-ārabdha-catur-daśa-bhuvana-ātmaka-brahma-aṇḍa-tad-antarvarti-deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-ādi-sarva-prakāra-saṃsthāna-saṃsthitaṃ kāryam api sarvaṃ brahma eva iti kāraṇa-bhūta-brahma-vijñānād eva sarvaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati ity eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñānam upapannataram / tad evaṃ kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva-ādi-mukhena kṛtsnasya cid-acid-vastunaḥ para-brahma-prakāratayā tad-ātmakatvam uktam /

body.text: nanu ca parasya brahmaṇaḥ svarūpeṇa pariṇāmāspadatvaṃ nirvikāratvaniravadyatvaśrutivyākopaprasañgena nivāritam / prakṛtiś ca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhād ity ekavijñānena sarvavijñānapratijñānamṛttatkāryadṛṣṭāntābhyāṃ paramapuruṣasya jagadupādānakāraṇatvaṃ ca pratipāditam / upādānakāraṇatvaṃ ca pariṇāmāspadatvam eva / katham idam upapadyate /
body.translated_text: Objection: It has been precluded that the supreme <s>Brahman</s> undergoes transformation in Its own essential nature, since that would conflict with the <s>śruti</s> passages declaring Its immutability and freedom from imperfection. And by the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>Prakṛti</s> too, on account of there being no conflict with the proposition and the illustration" — through the proposition that by knowing one thing everything is known and the illustration of clay and its products — it has been established that the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) is the <s>upādāna-kāraṇa</s> (material cause) of the universe. But being a material cause means being the substratum of transformation. How can both these be reconciled?

children.text: nanu ca parasya brahmaṇaḥ sva-rūpeṇa pariṇāma-āspadatvaṃ nirvikāratva-niravadyatva-śruti-vyākopa-prasañgena nivāritam / prakṛtiś ca pratijñā-dṛṣṭānta-anuparodhād ity eka-vijñānena sarva-vijñāna-pratijñāna-mṛt-tat-kārya-dṛṣṭāntābhyāṃ parama-puruṣasya jagad-upādāna-kāraṇatvaṃ ca pratipāditam / upādāna-kāraṇatvaṃ ca pariṇāma-āspadatvam eva / katham idam upapadyate /

body.text: atrocyate -- sajīvasya prapañcasyāviśeṣeṇa kāraṇatvam uktam / tatreśvarasya jīvarūpapariṇāmābhyupagamena nātmā śruter nityatvāc ca tābhya iti virudhyate / vaiṣamyanairghṛṇyaparihāraś ca jīvanam anāditvābhyupagamena tatkarmanimittatayā pratipāditaḥ -- vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvān na karmavibhāgād iti cen na -- anāditvād upapadyate cāpy upalabhyate cetyakṛtābhyāgamakṛtavipraṇāśaprasaṅgaś cānityatve 'bhihitaḥ /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: It has been stated that He is the cause of the world together with <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), without distinction. In that context, by accepting that <s>Īśvara</s> transforms in the form of <s>jīvas</s>, the <s>sūtras</s> "the self is not (produced), because <s>śruti</s> says so" and "because of eternality, from those very (texts)" are not contradicted. And the resolution of the objections of inequality and cruelty has been presented by accepting the beginninglessness of <s>jīvas</s>, showing that these are occasioned by their own <s>karma</s> — as in the <s>sūtras</s>: "Inequality and cruelty — not so, because of dependence (on <s>karma</s>). If it be said that this is not possible because there is no distinction of <s>karma</s> (before creation) — no, because it is beginningless. And it is established and also observed." And the absurd consequences of attaining what has not been earned and losing what has been earned, in the case of non-eternality (of <s>karma</s>), have also been stated.

children.text: atra ucyate --- sajīvasya prapañcasya aviśeṣeṇa kāraṇatvam uktam / tatrā iśvarasya jīva-rūpa-pariṇāma-abhyupagamena nā atmā śruter nityatvāc ca tābhya iti virudhyate / vaiṣamya-nairghṛṇya-parihāraś ca jīvanam anāditva-abhyupagamena tat-karma-nimittatayā pratipāditaḥ --- vaiṣamya-nairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvān na karma-vibhāgād iti cen na --- anāditvād upapadyate ca apy upalabhyate ca ity-akṛta-abhyāgama-kṛta-vipraṇāśa-prasaṅgaś ca anityatve 'bhihitaḥ /

body.text:
tathā prakṛter apy anāditā śrutibhiḥ pratipaditā --
ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahnīṃ prajāṃ janayantīṃ sarūpām /
ajo hy eko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahāty enāṃ bhuktabhogām ajo 'nyaḥ //
iti prakṛtipuruṣayor ajatvaṃ darśayati / asmān māyī sṛjate viśvam etat tasmiṃś cānyo māyayā saṃniruddhaḥ -- māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu maheśvaram iti prakṛtir eva svarūpeṇa vikārāspadam iti ca darśayati / gaur anādyantavatī sā janitrī bhūtabhāvinīti ca / smṛtiś ca bhavati --
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhy anādī ubhav api /
vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś caiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān //
bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca /
ahaṃkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā //
apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām /
jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat //
prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ /
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram //
ityādikā /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the beginninglessness of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal matter) too has been established by <s>śruti</s> passages: "The one unborn, red, white, and black, producing many offspring of the same form — one unborn male delights in her and stays close; another unborn male abandons her after enjoying her pleasures." This shows the unborn nature of both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. "From us the <s>Māyin</s> (wielder of <s>Māyā</s>) projects this entire universe, and in it the other is confined by <s>Māyā</s>" — "Know <s>Māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the <s>Māyin</s> to be the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>)" — this shows that it is <s>Prakṛti</s> alone that is the substratum of transformation in its own nature. And: "The cow (<s>Prakṛti</s>) is without beginning or end; she is the genetrix, the source of what has been and what will be." And the <s>smṛti</s> also says: "Know both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> to be beginningless; know the modifications and the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) to be born of <s>Prakṛti</s>." "Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego-sense — this is My <s>Prakṛti</s> divided eightfold." "This is the lower; but know My other, higher <s>Prakṛti</s>, O mighty-armed one, which has become the <s>jīvas</s> (living beings) and by which this world is sustained." "Resting upon My own <s>Prakṛti</s>, I send forth again and again; under My supervision, <s>Prakṛti</s> gives birth to all that moves and does not move" — and so forth.

children.text:
tathā prakṛter apy anāditā śrutibhiḥ pratipaditā ---
ajām ekāṃ lohita-śukla-kṛṣṇāṃ bahnīṃ prajāṃ janayantīṃ sarūpām /
ajo hy eko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahāty enāṃ bhukta-bhogām ajo 'nyaḥ //
iti prakṛti-puruṣayor ajatvaṃ darśayati / asmān māyī sṛjate viśvam etat tasmiṃś ca anyo māyayā saṃniruddhaḥ --- māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu mahā-īśvaram iti prakṛtir eva sva-rūpeṇa vikāra-āspadam iti ca darśayati / gaur anādy-antavatī sā janitrī bhūta-bhāvini īti ca / smṛtiś ca bhavati ---
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ ca eva viddhy anādī ubhav api /
vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś ca eva viddhi prakṛti-saṃbhavān //
bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca /
ahaṃkāra iti iyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā //
apara īyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām /
jīva-bhūtāṃ mahā-bāho yaya īdaṃ dhāryate jagat //
prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ /
maya ādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacara-acaram //
ity-ādikā /

body.text:
evaṃ ca prakṛter apīśvaraśarīratvāt prakṛtiśabdo 'pi tadātmabhūtasyeśvarasya tatprakārasaṃsthitasya vācakaḥ / puruṣaśabdo 'pi tadātmabhūtasyeśvarasya puruṣaprakārasaṃsthitasya vācakaḥ / atas tadvikārāṇām api tatheśvara evātmā / tad āha --
vyaktaṃ viṣṇus tathāvyaktaṃ puruṣaḥ kāla eva ca /
sā eva kṣobhako brahman kṣobhyaś ca parameśvaraḥ //
iti / ataḥ prakṛtiprakārasaṃsthite paramātmani prakārabhūtaprakṛtyaṃse vikāraḥ prakāryaṃse cāvikāraḥ / evam eva jīvaprakārasaṃsthite paramātmani ca prakārabhūtajīvāṃśe sarve cāpuruṣārthāḥ prakāryaṃśo niyantā niravadyaḥ sarvakalyāṇaguṇākaraḥ satyasaṃkalpa eva /
body.translated_text:
And thus, since <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial matter) is also the body of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the word '<s>prakṛti</s>' too denotes <s>Īśvara</s> who is the self of that [<s>prakṛti</s>] and who is characterized by having <s>prakṛti</s> as his mode. The word '<s>puruṣa</s>' (person/soul) too denotes <s>Īśvara</s> who is the self of that [<s>puruṣa</s>] and who is characterized by having <s>puruṣa</s> as his mode. Therefore, <s>Īśvara</s> alone is the self of their modifications as well. As it is stated:
'The manifest is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and likewise the unmanifest; the <s>Puruṣa</s> and time as well —
He alone, O <s>Brahman</s>, is the agitator and the agitated, the supreme Lord.'
Therefore, in the supreme Self characterized by having <s>prakṛti</s> as its mode, there is modification in the <s>prakṛti</s>-portion that is the mode, and non-modification in the possessor-of-modes. Likewise, in the supreme Self characterized by having the <s>jīva</s> as its mode, all misfortunes belong to the <s>jīva</s>-portion that is the mode, while the possessor-of-modes [i.e., <s>Paramātman</s>] is the controller, faultless, the repository of all auspicious qualities, and of true resolve alone.

children.text:
evaṃ ca prakṛter apī iśvara-śarīratvāt prakṛti-śabdo 'pi tad-ātma-bhūtasyā iśvarasya tat-prakāra-saṃsthitasya vācakaḥ / puruṣa-śabdo 'pi tad-ātma-bhūtasyā iśvarasya puruṣa-prakāra-saṃsthitasya vācakaḥ / atas tad-vikārāṇām api tathā īśvara evā atmā / tad āha ---
vyaktaṃ viṣṇus tatha āvyaktaṃ puruṣaḥ kāla eva ca /
sā eva kṣobhako brahman kṣobhyaś ca parama-īśvaraḥ //
iti / ataḥ prakṛti-prakāra-saṃsthite parama-ātmani prakāra-bhūta-prakṛty-aṃse vikāraḥ prakāry-aṃse ca avikāraḥ / evam eva jīva-prakāra-saṃsthite parama-ātmani ca prakāra-bhūta-jīva-aṃśe sarve ca apuruṣa-arthāḥ prakāry-aṃśo niyantā niravadyaḥ sarva-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ākaraḥ satya-saṃkalpa eva /

body.text:
tathā ca sati kāraṇāvastha īśvara eveti tadupādānakajagatkāryāvastho 'pi sa eveti kāryakāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ sarvaśrutyavirodhaś ca bhavati / tad evaṃ nāmarūpavibhāgānarhasūkṣmadaśāpannaprakṛtipuruṣaśarīraṃ brahma kāraṇāvasthaṃ, jagatas tadāpattir eva ca pralayaḥ / nāmarūpavibhāgavibhaktasthūlacidacidvastuśarīraṃ brahma kāryatvaṃ, brahmaṇas tathāvidhasthūlabhāva eva jagataḥ sṛṣṭir ity ucyate / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa --
pradhānapuṃsor ajayoḥ kāraṇaṃ kāryabhūtayoḥ / iti /
body.translated_text:
And this being the case, <s>Īśvara</s> alone is in the causal state, and hence [<s>Īśvara</s>] in the effect-state as the universe produced from that [cause] is also he alone — thus the non-difference of cause and effect and the non-contradiction of all <s>śruti</s> passages are established. Thus, <s>Brahman</s> having as its body <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> in their subtle state — unfit for the differentiation of name and form — is the causal state; the absorption of the universe into that [state] is what is called dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>). <s>Brahman</s> having as its body the gross conscious and non-conscious entities differentiated by the differentiation of name and form is the effect-state; the becoming of <s>Brahman</s> into such a gross state is what is called creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>). As stated by the blessed <s>Parāśara</s>:
'The cause of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, which are unborn, is that which becomes the effect.'

children.text:
tathā ca sati kāraṇa-avastha īśvara eva iti tad-upādānaka-jagat-kārya-avastho 'pi sa eva iti kārya-kāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ sarva-śruty-avirodhaś ca bhavati / tad evaṃ nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-anarha-sūkṣma-daśā-āpanna-prakṛti-puruṣa-śarīraṃ brahma kāraṇa-avasthaṃ, jagatas tad-āpattir eva ca pralayaḥ / nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-vibhakta-sthūla-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraṃ brahma kāryatvaṃ, brahmaṇas tathā-vidha-sthūla-bhāva eva jagataḥ sṛṣṭir ity ucyate / yatha ūktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa ---
pradhāna-puṃsor ajayoḥ kāraṇaṃ kārya-bhūtayoḥ / iti /

body.text: tasmād īśvaraprakārabhūtasarvāvasthaprakṛtipuruṣavācinaḥ śabdās tatprakāraviśiṣṭatayāvasthite paramātmani mukhyatayā vartante / jīvātmavācidevamanuṣyaśabdavat / yathā devamanuṣyādiśabdā devamanuṣyādiprakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣāṇāṃ jīvātmaprakāratayaiva padārthatvāt prakāriṇi jīvātmani mukhyatayā vartante / tasmāt sarvasya cidacidvastunaḥ paramātmaśarīratayā tatprakāratvāt paramātmani mukhyatayā vartante sarve vācakāḥ śabdāḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the words denoting <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> in all their states — which are modes of <s>Īśvara</s> — primarily apply to the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) who is characterized by having those as his modes. Just as the words 'god' and 'human' that denote the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>). Just as the words 'god,' 'human,' and the like primarily apply to the individual self, since the particular modifications of <s>prakṛti</s> [in the form of] gods, humans, and the like have their entity-hood only as modes of the <s>jīvātman</s> — and hence apply primarily to the <s>jīvātman</s> as the possessor of those modes. Therefore, since all conscious and non-conscious entities are modes of the supreme Self by virtue of being his body, all denotative words primarily apply to the supreme Self.

children.text: tasmād īśvara-prakāra-bhūta-sarva-avastha-prakṛti-puruṣa-vācinaḥ śabdās tat-prakāra-viśiṣṭataya āvasthite parama-ātmani mukhyatayā vartante / jīva-ātma-vāci-deva-manuṣya-śabdavat / yathā deva-manuṣya-ādi-śabdā deva-manuṣya-ādi-prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣāṇāṃ jīva-ātma-prakārataya aiva pada-arthatvāt prakāriṇi jīva-ātmani mukhyatayā vartante / tasmāt sarvasya cid-acid-vastunaḥ parama-ātma-śarīratayā tat-prakāratvāt parama-ātmani mukhyatayā vartante sarve vācakāḥ śabdāḥ /

body.text: ayam eva cātmaśarīrabhāvaḥ pṛthaksiddhyanarhādhārādheyabhāvo niyantṛniyāmyabhāvaḥ śeṣaśeṣibhāvaś ca / sarvātmanādhāratayā niyantṛtayā śeṣitayā ca -- āpnotīty ātmā sarvātmanādheyatayā niyāmyatayā śeṣatayā ca -- apṛthaksiddhaṃ prakārabhūtam ity ākāraḥ śarīram iti cocyate / evam eva hi jīvātmanaḥ svaśarīrasaṃbandhaḥ / evam eva paramātmanaḥ sarvaśarīratvena sarvaśabdavācyatvam /
body.translated_text: And this very body-self relation is [also] the relation of support and supported that cannot be established separately, the relation of controller and controlled, and the relation of subsidiary (<s>śeṣa</s>) and principal (<s>śeṣin</s>). As the support, controller, and principal of all — '<s>ātman</s>' [is so called] because it pervades all. As the supported, controlled, and subsidiary of all — that which, as a mode, cannot be established apart [from the possessor of modes] is called a form (<s>ākāra</s>), a body (<s>śarīra</s>). This is precisely the relation of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) to its own body. And it is precisely thus that the supreme Self, by being the self of all bodies, is denotable by all words.

children.text: ayam eva cā atma-śarīra-bhāvaḥ pṛthak-siddhy-anarha-ādhāra-ādheya-bhāvo niyantṛ-niyāmya-bhāvaḥ śeṣa-śeṣi-bhāvaś ca / sarva-ātmanā ādhāratayā niyantṛtayā śeṣitayā ca --- āpnoti ity ātmā sarva-ātmanā ādheyatayā niyāmyatayā śeṣatayā ca --- apṛthak-siddhaṃ prakāra-bhūtam ity ākāraḥ śarīram iti ca ucyate / evam eva hi jīva-ātmanaḥ sva-śarīra-saṃbandhaḥ / evam eva parama-ātmanaḥ sarva-śarīratvena sarva-śabda-vācyatvam /

body.text:
tad āha śrutigaṇaḥ -- sarve vedā yatpadam āmananti sarve vedā yatraikaṃ bhavantīti / tasyaikasya vācyatvād ekārthavācino bhavantītyarthaḥ / eko devo bahudhā niviṣṭaḥ, sahaiva santaṃ na vijānanti devā ityādi / devā indriyāṇi / devamanuṣyādīnām antaryāmitayātmatvena niviśya sahaiva santaṃ teṣām indriyāṇi manaḥparyantāni na vijānantītyarthaḥ / tathā ca paurāṇikāni vacāṃsi --
natāḥ sma sarvavacasāṃ pratiṣṭhā yatra śaśvatī /
vācye hi vacasaḥ pratiṣṭhā /
kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇāṃ pūrvaṃ vacasāṃ vācyam uttamam /
vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ /
ityādīni sarvāṇi hi vacāṃsi saśarīrātmaviśiṣṭam antaryāmiṇam evācakṣate / hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti hi śrutiḥ / tathā ca mānavaṃ vacaḥ --
praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām
rukmābhaṃ svapnadhīgamyaṃ vidyāt taṃ puruṣaṃ param //
antaḥ praviśyāntaryāmitayā sarveṣāṃ praśāsitāraṃ niyantāram -- aṇīyāṃsa ātmānaḥ kṛtsnasyācetanasya vyāpakatayā sūkṣmabhūtās te teṣām api vyāpakatvāt tebhyo 'pi sūkṣmatara ityarthaḥ -- rukmābhaḥ ādityavarṇaḥ -- svapnakalpabuddhiprāpyaḥ, viśadatamapratyakṣatāpannānudhyānaikalabhya ityarthaḥ /
enam eke vadanty agniṃ māruto 'nye prajāpatim /
indram eke pare pramāṇam apare brahma śāśvatam //
iti / eke -- vedā ityarthaḥ / uktarītyā parasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ sarvasya praśāsitṛtvena sarvāntarātmatayā praviśyāvasthitatvād agnyādayaḥ śabdā api śāśvatabrahmaśabdavat tasyaiva vācakā bhavantītyarthaḥ / tathā ca smṛtyantaram --
ye yajanti pitQn devān brāhmaṇān sahutāśanān /
sarvabhūtāntarātmānaṃ viṣṇum eva yajanti te //
iti / pitṛdevabrāhmaṇahutāśanādiśabdās tanmukhena tadantarātmabhūtasya viṣṇor eva vācakā ityuktaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text:
As the assemblage of <s>śrutis</s> declares: 'All the <s>Vedas</s> proclaim that abode; all the <s>Vedas</s> become one therein.' The meaning is: because that one [<s>Brahman</s>] alone is the denotatum, they become denoters of one meaning. 'The one God, entered in many ways' — 'though present together, the <s>devas</s> do not know him' and so forth. '<s>Devas</s>' means the senses. Having entered as the self through being the inner controller of gods, humans, and the like, though present together [with them], their senses including the mind do not know him — this is the meaning. Likewise the <s>Purāṇic</s> statements:
'We bow to that in which the eternal foundation of all words [abides].'
For the foundation of a word is its denotatum.
'The cause of effects, the supreme denotatum of words.'
'And by all the <s>Vedas</s> I alone am to be known.'
All these words denote the inner controller who is the self, qualified by the embodied [<s>jīva</s>]. For the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Let me enter these three divinities as the individual self and differentiate name and form.' And the statement of <s>Manu</s>:
'The ruler of all, subtler than the subtlest,
golden in hue, to be known through dream-like meditation —
know that supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>.'
Having entered within as the inner controller, the ruler and governor of all — the selves (<s>ātmans</s>) are subtle by pervading the entire non-conscious [realm]; he, being the pervader of even those, is subtler than the subtle — this is the meaning. 'Golden in hue' means having the color of the sun. 'To be known through dream-like meditation' means attainable only through meditation that has reached the state of the most vivid direct perception — this is the meaning.
'Some call him <s>Agni</s>, others <s>Vāyu</s>, others <s>Prajāpati</s>,
some <s>Indra</s>, others the means of valid knowledge, others the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.'
'Some' means the <s>Vedas</s>. Because the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone, in the manner stated, abides having entered as the inner self and ruler of all, the words '<s>Agni</s>' and the like, just like the word 'eternal <s>Brahman</s>,' denote that [<s>Brahman</s>] alone — this is the meaning. Likewise another <s>smṛti</s>:
'Those who worship the ancestors, gods, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and the sacrificial fire
worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, who is the inner self of all beings.'
The words 'ancestors,' 'gods,' '<s>brāhmaṇas</s>,' 'sacrificial fire,' and the like denote, through those [entities], <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who is their inner self — this is what is stated.

children.text:
tad āha śruti-gaṇaḥ --- sarve vedā yat-padam āmananti sarve vedā yatra ekaṃ bhavanti iti / tasya ekasya vācyatvād eka-artha-vācino bhavanti ity-arthaḥ / eko devo bahudhā niviṣṭaḥ, saha eva santaṃ na vijānanti devā ity-ādi / devā indriyāṇi / deva-manuṣya-ādīnām antaryāmitayā ātmatvena niviśya saha eva santaṃ teṣām indriyāṇi manaḥ-paryantāni na vijānanti ity-arthaḥ / tathā ca paurāṇikāni vacāṃsi ---
natāḥ sma sarva-vacasāṃ pratiṣṭhā yatra śaśvatī /
vācye hi vacasaḥ pratiṣṭhā /
kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇāṃ pūrvaṃ vacasāṃ vācyam uttamam /
vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ /
ity-ādīni sarvāṇi hi vacāṃsi sa-śarīra-ātma-viśiṣṭam antaryāmiṇam evā acakṣate / hanta aham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenā atma-anupraviśya nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi iti hi śrutiḥ / tathā ca mānavaṃ vacaḥ ---
praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām
rukma-abhaṃ svapna-dhī-gamyaṃ vidyāt taṃ puruṣaṃ param //
antaḥ praviśya antaryāmitayā sarveṣāṃ praśāsitāraṃ niyantāram --- aṇīyāṃsa ātmānaḥ kṛtsnasya acetanasya vyāpakatayā sūkṣma-bhūtās te teṣām api vyāpakatvāt tebhyo 'pi sūkṣmatara ity-arthaḥ --- rukma-abhaḥ āditya-varṇaḥ --- svapna-kalpa-buddhi-prāpyaḥ, viśadatama-pratyakṣatā-āpanna-anudhyāna-eka-labhya ity-arthaḥ /
enam eke vadanty agniṃ māruto 'nye prajāpatim /
indram eke pare pramāṇam apare brahma śāśvatam //
iti / eke --- vedā ity-arthaḥ / ukta-rītyā parasya eva brahmaṇaḥ sarvasya praśāsitṛtvena sarva-antara-ātmatayā praviśya avasthitatvād agny-ādayaḥ śabdā api śāśvata-brahma-śabdavat tasya eva vācakā bhavanti ity-arthaḥ / tathā ca smṛty-antaram ---
ye yajanti pitQn devān brāhmaṇān sahuta-āśanān /
sarva-bhūta-antara-ātmānaṃ viṣṇum eva yajanti te //
iti / pitṛ-deva-brāhmaṇa-huta-āśana-ādi-śabdās tan-mukhena tad-antara-ātma-bhūtasya viṣṇor eva vācakā ity-uktaṃ bhavati /

body.text:
atredaṃ sarvaśāstrahṛdayam -- jīvātmānaḥ svayam asaṃkucitāparicchinnanirmalajñānasvarūpāḥ santaḥ karmarūpāvidyāveṣṭitās tattatkarmānurūpajñānasaṃkocam āpannāḥ, brahmādistambaparyantavividhavicitradeheṣu praviśṭās tattaddehocitalabdhajñānaprasarās tattaddehātmābhimāninas taducitakarmāṇi kurvāṇās tadanuguṇasukhaduḥkhopabhogarūpasaṃsārapravāhaṃ pratipadyante / eteṣāṃ saṃsāramocanaṃ bhagavatprapattim antareṇa nopapadyata iti tadarthaḥ prathamam eṣāṃ devādibhedarahitajñānaikākāratayā sarveṣāṃ sāmyaṃ pratipādya, tasyāpi svarūpasya bhagavaccheṣataikarasatayā bhagavadātmakatām api pratipādya, bhagavatsvarūpaṃ ca heyapratyanīlakalyāṇaikatānatayā sakaletaravisajātīyam anavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇāśrayaṃ
svasaṃkalpapravṛttasamastacidacidvastujātatayā sarvasyātmabhūtaṃ pratipādya, tadupāsana sāṅgaṃ tatprāpakaṃ pratipadayanti śāstrāṇīti /
body.translated_text: Here is the heart of all scripture: the individual selves (<s>jīvātmans</s>), being by nature of unconditioned, unlimited, and pure consciousness, yet enwrapped by <s>avidyā</s> in the form of <s>karma</s>, having undergone a contraction of consciousness corresponding to their respective <s>karmas</s>, having entered into various and variegated bodies ranging from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, having acquired the spread of consciousness appropriate to each body, identifying themselves with each body, performing actions appropriate thereto — they enter into the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s> in the form of the experience of pleasure and pain corresponding to those [actions]. The liberation of these [beings] from <s>saṃsāra</s> is impossible without taking refuge in the Blessed Lord (<s>bhagavatprapatti</s>) — for this purpose, first establishing the equality of all [selves] by virtue of their having the single form of knowledge, devoid of distinctions such as god and the like; then establishing the <s>Brahman</s>-nature [of the self] also by its essential nature consisting entirely of being a subsidiary of the Lord; and establishing the Lord's own nature as being entirely of a kind opposed to all that is to be rejected, of a class completely different from everything else, the repository of an infinite multitude of unsurpassably excellent and innumerable auspicious qualities, the self of all by virtue of the entire host of conscious and non-conscious entities proceeding from his own resolve — the scriptures teach the worship of him, together with its limbs, as the means of attaining him.

children.text:
atra idaṃ sarva-śāstra-hṛdayam --- jīva-ātmānaḥ svayam asaṃkucita-aparicchinna-nirmala-jñāna-sva-rūpāḥ santaḥ karma-rūpa-avidyā-veṣṭitās tat-tat-karma-anurūpa-jñāna-saṃkocam āpannāḥ, brahma-ādi-stamba-paryanta-vividha-vicitra-deheṣu praviśṭās tat-tad-deha-ucita-labdha-jñāna-prasarās tat-tad-deha-ātma-abhimāninas tad-ucita-karmāṇi kurvāṇās tad-anuguṇa-sukha-duḥkha-upabhoga-rūpa-saṃsāra-pravāhaṃ pratipadyante / eteṣāṃ saṃsāra-mocanaṃ bhagavat-prapattim antareṇa na upapadyata iti tad-arthaḥ prathamam eṣāṃ deva-ādi-bheda-rahita-jñāna-eka-ākāratayā sarveṣāṃ sāmyaṃ pratipādya, tasya api sva-rūpasya bhagavac-cheṣatā-eka-rasatayā bhagavad-ātmakatām api pratipādya, bhagavat-sva-rūpaṃ ca heya-pratyanīla-kalyāṇa-eka-tānatayā sakala-itara-visajātīyam anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-āśrayaṃ
sva-saṃkalpa-pravṛtta-samasta-cid-acid-vastu-jātatayā sarvasyā atma-bhūtaṃ pratipādya, tad-upāsana sāṅgaṃ tat-prāpakaṃ pratipadayanti śāstrāṇi iti /

body.text:
yathoktam --
nirvāṇamaya evāyam ātmā jñānamayo 'malaḥ /
duḥkhājñānamalā dharmā prakṛtes te na cātmanaḥ /
iti prakṛtisaṃsargakṛtakarmamūlatvān nātmadvarūpaprayuktā dharmā ityarthaḥ / prāptāprāptavivekena prakṛter eva dharmā ityuktam /
vidyāvinayasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini /
śuni caiva śvapāke ca pāṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ /
iti / devatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvararūpaprakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasyātmanaḥ svarūpavivecanī buddhir eṣāṃ te paṇḍitāḥ / tattat prakṛtiviśeṣaviyuktātmayāthātmyajñānavantas tatra tatrātyantaviṣamākāre vartamānam ātmānaṃ samānākāraṃ paśyantīti samadarśina ity uktam / tad idam āha --
ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ /
nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ //
iti / nirdoṣaṃ -- devādiprakṛtiviśeṣasaṃsargarūpadoṣarahitaṃ svarūpeṇāvasthitaṃ sarvam ātmavastu nirvāṇarūpajñānaikākāratayā samam ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
As stated:
'This self is indeed of the nature of liberation, of the nature of knowledge, pure.
The attributes of suffering, ignorance, and impurity belong to <s>prakṛti</s> and not to the self.'
The meaning is: the attributes are not due to the self's own nature, because they are rooted in <s>karma</s> produced by contact with <s>prakṛti</s>. By discriminating what properly belongs [to the self] from what does not, it is said that the attributes belong to <s>prakṛti</s> alone.
'The wise are those who see equally
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant,
a dog, and an outcaste.'
The wisdom that discriminates the true nature of the self, which is connected with <s>prakṛti</s> in the forms of gods, animals, humans, and plants — those who possess this are the wise (<s>paṇḍitas</s>). Those who know the true nature of the self disjoined from each particular modification of <s>prakṛti</s> see the self, though existing in extremely unequal forms, as of a uniform nature — hence they are called 'those who see equally.' This is then stated:
'Even here, creation is conquered by those whose mind is established in equality.
For <s>Brahman</s> is flawless and equal; therefore they are established in <s>Brahman</s>.'
'Flawless' means free from the defect of contact with particular modifications of <s>prakṛti</s> such as those of gods and the like; all self-substance, established in its own nature, is equal by virtue of having the single form of <s>nirvāṇa</s>-nature knowledge — this is the meaning.

children.text:
yatha ūktam ---
nirvāṇa-maya eva ayam ātmā jñāna-mayo 'malaḥ /
duḥkha-ajñāna-malā dharmā prakṛtes te na cā atmanaḥ /
iti prakṛti-saṃsarga-kṛta-karma-mūlatvān nā atma-dva-rūpa-prayuktā dharmā ity-arthaḥ / prāpta-aprāpta-vivekena prakṛter eva dharmā ity-uktam /
vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini /
śuni ca eva śva-pāke ca pāṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ /
iti / deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-rūpa-prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasyā atmanaḥ sva-rūpa-vivecanī buddhir eṣāṃ te paṇḍitāḥ / tat-tat- prakṛti-viśeṣa-viyukta-ātma-yāthātmya-jñānavantas tatra tatra atyanta-viṣama-ākāre vartamānam ātmānaṃ samāna-ākāraṃ paśyanti iti sama-darśina ity uktam / tad idam āha ---
iha eva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ /
nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ //
iti / nirdoṣaṃ --- deva-ādi-prakṛti-viśeṣa-saṃsarga-rūpa-doṣa-rahitaṃ sva-rūpeṇa avasthitaṃ sarvam ātma-vastu nirvāṇa-rūpa-jñāna-eka-ākāratayā samam ity-arthaḥ /

body.text: tasyaivaṃbhūtasyātmano bhagavaccheṣataikarasatā tanniyāmyatā tadekādhāratā ca taccharīratattanuprabhṛtibhiḥ śabdais tatsamānādhikaraṇyena ca śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇeṣu pratipādyata iti pūrvam evoktam /
body.translated_text: That the self of such a nature has its essence consisting entirely of being the subsidiary of the Lord (<s>bhagavaccheṣatā</s>), of being controlled by him, and of having him alone as its support — and that this is taught in <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>itihāsa</s>, and <s>purāṇas</s> by words such as 'body,' 'self,' and so forth in co-referentiality with [the Lord] — this was already stated earlier.

children.text: tasya evaṃ-bhūtasyā atmano bhagavac-cheṣatā-eka-rasatā tan-niyāmyatā tad-eka-ādhāratā ca tac-charīra-tat-tanu-prabhṛtibhiḥ śabdais tat-samāna-adhikaraṇyena ca śruti-smṛti-itihāsa-purāṇeṣu pratipādyata iti pūrvam eva uktam /

body.text:
daivī hy eṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā /
mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te //
iti tasyātmanaḥ karmakṛtavicitraguṇamayaprakṛtisaṃsargarūpāt saṃsārān mokṣo bhagavatprapattim antareṇa nopapadayata ityuktaṃ bhavati / nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyata ityādiśrutibhiś ca /
mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyaktamūrtinā /
matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣu avasthitaḥ //
na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram //
iti sarvaśaktiyogāt svāiśvaryavaicitryam uktam / tad āha --
viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat /
iti -- anantavicitramahāścaryarūpaṃ jagan mamāyutāṃśenātmatayā praviśya sarvaṃ matsaṃkalpena viṣṭabhyānena rūpeṇānantamahāvibhūtiparimitodāraguṇasāgaro niratiśayāścaryabhūtaḥ sthito 'ham ityarthaḥ / tad idam āha --
ekatve sati nānātvaṃ nānātve sati caikatā /
acintyaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ kutas tadveditum arhati //
iti / praśāsitṛtvenaika eva sanvicitracidacidvastuṣv antarātmatayā praviśya tattadrūpeṇa vicitraprakāro vicitrakarma kārayan nānārūpāṃ bhajate / evaṃ svalpāṃśena tu sarvāścaryaṃ nānārūpaṃ jagattadantarātmatayā praviśya viṣṭabhya nānātvenāvasthito 'pi sann anavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaḥ sarveśvaraḥ parabrahmabhūtaḥ puruṣottamo nārāyaṇo niratiśayāścaryabhūto nīlatoyadasaṃkāśaḥ puṇḍarīkadalāmalāyatekṣaṇaḥ sahasrāṃśusahasrakiraṇaḥ parame vyomni yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyomaṃs tadakṣare parame vyomann ityādiśrutisiddha eka evātiṣṭhate /
body.translated_text:
'For this divine <s>māyā</s> of Mine, constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, is difficult to cross;
but those who take refuge in Me alone cross beyond this <s>māyā</s>.'
Thus it is stated that liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> — which is of the nature of contact with <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial matter) constituted of the varied <s>guṇas</s> produced by that self's <s>karma</s> — is not possible without taking refuge in the Blessed Lord. And by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'There is no other path for attainment.'
'By Me, in My unmanifest form, this entire universe is pervaded;
all beings abide in Me, but I do not abide in them.
Nor do beings abide in Me — behold My divine <s>yoga</s>!'
Thus, through the conjunction of all powers, the magnificence of His sovereign lordship is stated. He then says:
'Having pervaded this entire universe, I stand by a single portion.'
The meaning is: having entered the universe — of infinite, wondrous, and marvelous form — as the Self through a ten-thousandth portion of Myself, having pervaded everything by My will, in this form, being an ocean of generous qualities delimited by infinite and great splendor, I stand as one of unsurpassable wonder. This is expressed thus:
'There being oneness, there is multiplicity; there being multiplicity, there is oneness;
the form of <s>Brahman</s> is inconceivable — who indeed is able to know it?'
Being one as the ruler, having entered the diverse conscious and non-conscious entities as their inner Self, assuming diverse forms through each of those forms, causing diverse actions to be performed, He takes on manifold forms. Thus, having entered and pervaded with a mere fraction the entire universe of wondrous manifold forms as their inner Self, though abiding in multiplicity, the Lord of all, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — possessing hosts of innumerable auspicious qualities of unsurpassable excellence, of unsurpassable wonder, resembling a dark rain-cloud, with eyes vast and pure like lotus petals, with a thousand rays and a thousand beams — He alone abides in the supreme heaven, as established by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'He who knows that which is deposited in the cave, in the supreme heaven,' 'in that imperishable, in the supreme heaven.'

children.text:
daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā /
mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te //
iti tasyā atmanaḥ karma-kṛta-vicitra-guṇa-maya-prakṛti-saṃsarga-rūpāt saṃsārān mokṣo bhagavat-prapattim antareṇa na upapadayata ity-uktaṃ bhavati / na anyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyata ity-ādi-śrutibhiś ca /
mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā /
mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na ca ahaṃ teṣu avasthitaḥ //
na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram //
iti sarva-śakti-yogāt sva aiśvarya-vaicitryam uktam / tad āha ---
viṣṭabhya aham idaṃ kṛtsnam eka-aṃśena sthito jagat /
iti --- ananta-vicitra-mahā-āścarya-rūpaṃ jagan mama ayuta-aṃśenā atmatayā praviśya sarvaṃ mat-saṃkalpena viṣṭabhya anena rūpeṇa ananta-mahā-vibhūti-parimita-udāra-guṇa-sāgaro niratiśaya-āścarya-bhūtaḥ sthito 'ham ity-arthaḥ / tad idam āha ---
ekatve sati nānātvaṃ nānātve sati ca ekatā /
acintyaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ kutas tad-veditum arhati //
iti / praśāsitṛtvena eka eva san-vicitra-cid-acid-vastuṣv antara-ātmatayā praviśya tat-tad-rūpeṇa vicitra-prakāro vicitra-karma kārayan nānā-rūpāṃ bhajate / evaṃ sv-alpa-aṃśena tu sarva-āścaryaṃ nānā-rūpaṃ jagat-tad-antara-ātmatayā praviśya viṣṭabhya nānātvena avasthito 'pi sann anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaḥ sarva-īśvaraḥ para-brahma-bhūtaḥ puruṣa-uttamo nārāyaṇo niratiśaya-āścarya-bhūto nīla-toya-da-saṃkāśaḥ puṇḍarīka-dala-amala-āyata-īkṣaṇaḥ sahasra-aṃśu-sahasra-kiraṇaḥ parame vyomni yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyomaṃs tad-akṣare parame vyomann ity-ādi-śruti-siddha eka eva atiṣṭhate /

body.text:
brahmavyatiriktasya kasyacid api vastuna ekasvabhāvasyaikakāryaśaktiyuktasyaikarūpasya rūpāntarayogaḥ svabhāvāntarayogaḥ śaktyantarayogaś ca na ghaṭate / tasyaitasya parabrahmaṇaḥ sarvavastuvijātīyatayā sarvasvabhāvatvaṃ sarvaśaktiyogaś cety ekasyaiva vicitrānantarūpatā ca punar apy anantāparimitāścaryayogenaikarūpatā ca na viruddheti vastumātrasāmyād virodhacintā na yuktetyarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ --
śaktayaḥ sarvabhāvānām acintyajñānagocarāḥ /
yato 'to brahmaṇas tās tu sargādyā bhāvaśaktayaḥ //
bhavanti tapasāṃ śreṣṭa pāvakasya yathoṣṇatā //iti /
etad uktaṃ bhavati -- sarveṣām agnijalādīnāṃ bhāvānām ekasminn api bhāve dṛṣṭaiva śaktis tadvijātīyabhāvāntare 'pīti na cintayituṃ yuktā jalādāv adṛṣṭāpi tadvijātīyapāvake bhāsvaratvoṣṇatādiśaktir yathā dṛśyate, evam eva sarvavastuvisajātīye brahmaṇi sarvasāmyaṃ nānumātuṃ yuktam iti / ato vicitrānantaśaktiyuktaṃ brahmaivetyarthaḥ tad āha --
jagad etan mahāścaryaṃ rūpaṃ yasya mahātmanaḥ /
tenāścaryavareṇāhaṃ bhavatā kṛṣṇa saṃgataḥ //
iti /
body.translated_text:
For any entity other than <s>Brahman</s>, which has a single nature, a single capacity for producing effects, and a single form — the conjunction with another form, another nature, or another power is not possible. But for this Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, because of being different in kind from all entities, the possession of all natures, the conjunction with all powers — and thus the diverse and infinite multiplicity of forms of this one [<s>Brahman</s>], and yet again the oneness through conjunction with infinite and unlimited wonder — are not contradictory. The meaning is that from mere similarity with [ordinary] entities, reasoning about contradiction is not appropriate. As stated:
'The powers of all entities are in the domain of inconceivable knowledge;
therefore, those powers of <s>Brahman</s> — creation and so forth — the powers of existence,
arise, O best of ascetics, just as heat [arises] from fire.'
What is being said is this: of all entities such as fire, water, etc., any power seen in even one entity — one should not reason that it cannot exist in another entity of a different kind. Just as the power of luminosity, heat, etc., unseen in water and the like, is nevertheless seen in fire, which is of a different kind — so too, in <s>Brahman</s>, which is of a kind different from all entities, complete similarity [of powers] should not be inferred. Therefore, the meaning is that <s>Brahman</s> alone is endowed with diverse and infinite powers. He then says:
'This wondrous universe is the form of that great-souled One;
by that most wondrous One — by You, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — I am joined.'

children.text:
brahma-vyatiriktasya kasyacid api vastuna eka-sva-bhāvasya eka-kārya-śakti-yuktasya eka-rūpasya rūpa-antara-yogaḥ sva-bhāva-antara-yogaḥ śakty-antara-yogaś ca na ghaṭate / tasya etasya para-brahmaṇaḥ sarva-vastu-vijātīyatayā sarva-sva-bhāvatvaṃ sarva-śakti-yogaś ca ity ekasya eva vicitra-ananta-rūpatā ca punar apy ananta-aparimita-āścarya-yogena eka-rūpatā ca na viruddha īti vastu-mātra-sāmyād virodha-cintā na yukta īty-arthaḥ / yatha ūktaṃ ---
śaktayaḥ sarva-bhāvānām acintya-jñāna-gocarāḥ /
yato 'to brahmaṇas tās tu sarga-ādyā bhāva-śaktayaḥ //
bhavanti tapasāṃ śreṣṭa pāvakasya yatha ūṣṇatā //iti /
etad uktaṃ bhavati --- sarveṣām agni-jala-ādīnāṃ bhāvānām ekasminn api bhāve dṛṣṭa aiva śaktis tad-vijātīya-bhāva-antare 'pi iti na cintayituṃ yuktā jala-ādāv adṛṣṭa āpi tad-vijātīya-pāvake bhāsvaratva-uṣṇatā-ādi-śaktir yathā dṛśyate, evam eva sarva-vastu-visajātīye brahmaṇi sarva-sāmyaṃ na anumātuṃ yuktam iti / ato vicitra-ananta-śakti-yuktaṃ brahma eva ity-arthaḥ tad āha ---
jagad etan mahā-āścaryaṃ rūpaṃ yasya mahā-ātmanaḥ /
tenā aścarya-vareṇa ahaṃ bhavatā kṛṣṇa saṃgataḥ //
iti /

body.text:
tad etan nānāvidhānantaśrutinikaraśiṣṭaparigṛhītatadvyākhyānapariśramād avadhāritam / tathā hi -- pramāṇāntarāparidṛṣṭāparimitapariṇāmān ekatattvaniyatakramaviśiṣṭau sṛṣṭipralayau brahmaṇo 'nekavidhāḥ śrutayo vadanti -- niravadyaṃ nirañjanaṃ vijñānam ānandaṃ nirvikāraṃ niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntaṃ nirguṇam ity ādikāḥ nirguṇaṃ jñānasvarūpaṃ brahmeti kāścana śrutayo 'bhidadhati / neha nānāsti kiṃcana -- mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati --yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaivābhūt -- tat kena kaṃ paśyet tat kena kaṃ vijātīyād ityādikā nānātvaniṣedhavādinyaḥ santi kāścana śrutayaḥ / yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit -- yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ --sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vicitya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadan yad āste
-- sarve nimeṣā jajñire vidyutaḥ puruṣādadhi -- apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijaghatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpa iti sarvasmiñ jagati heyatayāvagataṃ sarvaguṇaṃ pratiṣidhya niratiśayakalyāṇaguṇānantyaṃ sarvajñatā sarvaśaktiyogaṃ sarvanāmarūpavyākaraṇaṃ sarvasyāvadhāratāṃ ca kāścana śrutayo bruvate / sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma tajjalān iti -- aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ -- ekaḥ san bahudhā vicāra ityādikā brahmasṛṣṭaṃ jagan nānākāraṃ pratipādya tadaikyaṃ ca pratipādayanti kāścana / pṛthagātmānaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā -- bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā -- prajāpatir akāmayata prajāḥ sṛjeyeti -- patiṃ viśvasyātmeśvaraṃ -- śvāstaṃ śivam acyutaṃ -- tam īśvarāṇāṃ paraṃ maheśvaraṃ taṃ devatānāṃ paraṃ ca
daivataṃ -- sarvasya vaśī sarvasyeśāna ityādikā brahmaṇaḥ sarvasmād anyatvaṃ sarvasyeśitavyam īśvaratvaṃ ca brahmaṇaḥ sarvasya śeṣatāṃ patitvaṃ ceśvarasya kāścana / antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarvātmā -- eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ -- yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ -- yasyāpaḥ śarīraṃ -- yasya tejaḥ śarīram ityādi yasyāvyaktaṃ śarīraṃ -- yasyākṣaraṃ śarīraṃ - yasya mṛtyuḥ śarīraṃ --yasyātmā śarīram iti brahmavyatiriktasya sarvasya vastuno brahmaṇaś ca śarīrātmabhāvaṃ darśayanti kāścaneti /
body.translated_text: This has been ascertained from the diverse and innumerable collections of <s>śrutis</s> and from the efforts of the explanations accepted by the learned. Thus: various <s>śrutis</s> declare creation and dissolution — which involve unlimited transformations unseen by other means of knowledge, and which belong to a single reality in a fixed sequence — of <s>Brahman</s>. Some <s>śrutis</s> declare that <s>Brahman</s> is of the nature of knowledge and without attributes, such as: 'Faultless, untainted, knowledge, bliss, changeless, without parts, without action, tranquil, without qualities.' Some <s>śrutis</s> are statements negating plurality: 'There is no plurality here whatsoever' — 'Death after death he attains, who sees as if there is plurality here' — 'When for him everything has become the Self alone' — 'By what would one see whom? By what would one know what is of a different kind?' Some <s>śrutis</s> declare the infinity of unsurpassable auspicious qualities — negating all qualities understood as defective and reprehensible in the entire world — omniscience, conjunction with all powers, the differentiation of all names and forms, and the governance of all: 'He who is omniscient, who knows all' — 'whose austerity is made of knowledge' — 'the wise one, having fashioned all forms, creating names, declares them' — 'all flashings were born from the lightning, from the <s>Puruṣa</s>' — 'free from evil, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are true, whose resolves are true.' Some <s>śrutis</s>, having established the world of diverse forms as created by <s>Brahman</s>, also establish its identity with [<s>Brahman</s>]: 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>, from which it is born, into which it dissolves, and in which it breathes' — 'This all has that as its Self' — 'Being one, He variously entered.' Some [<s>śrutis</s> declare] the otherness of <s>Brahman</s> from everything, its being the ruler of all that is to be ruled, and its lordship, as well as the subordination and belongingness of everything to <s>Īśvara</s>: 'Knowing the individual self and the impeller as distinct' — 'Knowing the enjoyer, the object of enjoyment, and the impeller' — '<s>Prajāpati</s> desired: may I create beings' — 'The lord of the universe, the self-ruler' — 'the auspicious, the unchanging, the imperishable' — 'Him, the supreme great lord of lords, Him, the supreme deity of deities' — 'the ruler of all, the lord of all.' Some [<s>śrutis</s>] show the body-self relation between everything other than <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Brahman</s>: 'Having entered within, the ruler of people, the Self of all' — 'This is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal' — 'whose body is the earth' — 'whose body is the waters' — 'whose body is light' — and so on up to 'whose body is the unmanifest' — 'whose body is the imperishable' — 'whose body is death' — 'whose body is the Self.'
