atyalpam etat -
vedavitpravaraproktavākyanyāyopabṛṃhitāḥ /
vedāḥ sāṅgā hariṃ prāhur jagajjanmādikāraṇaṃ //
janmādyasya yataḥ -- yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante, yena jātāni jīvanti, yat prayanty abhisaṃviśanti, tad vijijñānasva tad brahmeti jagajjanmādikāraṇaṃ brahmety avagamyate / tac ca jagatsṛṣṭipralayaprakaraṇeṣv avagantavyam / sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam iti jagadupādānatājagannimittatājagadantaryāmitādimukhena paramakāraṇaṃ sacchabdena praitpāditaṃ brahmety avagatam / ayam evārthaḥ -- brahma vā idam ekam evāgra āsīd iti śākhāntare brahmaśabdena pratipaditaḥ / anena sacchabdenābhihitaṃ brahmety avagatam / ayam evārthas tathā śākhāntara ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīn nānyat kiṃcana miṣad iti sadbrahmaśabdābhyām ātmaivābhihita ity avagamyate / tathā ca śākhāntara eko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīn na brahma neśāno neme dyāvapṛthivī na nakṣatrāṇīti
sadbrahmātmādiparamakāraṇavādibhiḥ śabdair nārāyaṇa evābhidhīyata iti niścīyate /
body.translated_text:
This is a very small [objection] —
'The <s>Vedas</s>, with their subsidiary sciences, supported by the statements and reasoning proclaimed by the foremost knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, declare <s>Hari</s> to be the cause of the world's origin and the rest.'
'From whom is the origin and the rest of this [universe]' — 'From which these beings are born, by which once born they live, into which they enter upon departing — seek to know That, That is <s>Brahman</s>' — thus it is understood that <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world's origin and the rest. And that is to be understood in the contexts dealing with the creation and dissolution of the world. 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone, dear one, was this in the beginning, one only without a second' — through the aspects of being the material cause of the world, the efficient cause of the world, the inner controller of the world, and so forth, it is understood that the Supreme Cause denoted by the word '<s>sat</s>' (Being) is <s>Brahman</s>. This same meaning is expressed in another <s>Vedic</s> branch by the word '<s>Brahman</s>': '<s>Brahman</s> alone was this in the beginning, one only.' Thus it is understood that what is denoted by the word '<s>sat</s>' is <s>Brahman</s>. This same meaning is expressed in yet another branch: 'The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) alone was this in the beginning, one only; nothing else whatsoever stirred' — thus it is understood that what is denoted by the words '<s>sat</s>' and '<s>Brahman</s>' is the <s>Ātman</s> itself. And likewise in another branch: 'Only <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> existed; there was no <s>Brahmā</s>, no <s>Īśāna</s>, no heaven and earth, no stars' —
Thus it is determined that by the words '<s>sat</s>', '<s>Brahman</s>', '<s>Ātman</s>', and other terms denoting the Supreme Cause, it is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone who is referred to.

children.text:
atyalpam etat --
veda-vit-pravara-prokta-vākya-nyāya-upabṛṃhitāḥ /
vedāḥ sa-aṅgā hariṃ prāhur jagaj-janma-ādi-kāraṇaṃ //
janma-ādy-asya yataḥ --- yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante, yena jātāni jīvanti, yat prayanty abhisaṃviśanti, tad vijijñānasva tad brahma iti jagaj-janma-ādi-kāraṇaṃ brahma ity avagamyate / tac ca jagat-sṛṣṭi-pralaya-prakaraṇeṣv avagantavyam / sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ekam eva advitīyam iti jagad-upādānatā-jagan-nimittatā-jagad-antaryāmitā-adi-mukhena parama-kāraṇaṃ sac-chabdena praitpāditaṃ brahma ity avagatam / ayam eva arthaḥ --- brahma vā idam ekam eva agra āsīd iti śākhā-antare brahma-śabdena pratipaditaḥ / anena sac-chabdena abhihitaṃ brahma ity avagatam / ayam eva arthas tathā śākhā-antara ātmā vā idam eka eva agra āsīn na anyat kiṃcana miṣad iti sad-brahma-śabdābhyām ātma eva abhihita ity avagamyate / tathā ca śākhā-antara eko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīn na brahma nā iśāno na ime dyāva-pṛthivī na nakṣatrāṇi iti
sad-brahma-ātma-ādi-parama-kāraṇa-vādibhiḥ śabdair nārāyaṇa eva abhidhīyata iti niścīyate /

body.text: yam antaḥ samudre kavayo vayantītyādi -- nainam ūrdhvaṃ na tiryañcaṃ na madhye parijagrabhat / na tasyeśe kaścana tasya nāma mahadyaśaḥ // na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam, hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya evaṃ vidur amṛtās te bhavantīti sarvasmāt paratvam asya pratipādya, na tasyeśe kaścaneti tasmāt paraṃ kim api na vidyata iti ca pratiṣidhya, adbhyaḥ sambhūto hiraṇyagarbha ityaṣṭāv iti tenaikavākyatāṃ gamayati / tac ca mahāpuruṣaprakaraṇaṃ hrīś ca te lakṣmīś ca patnyāv iti ca nārāyaṇa eveti dyotayati /
body.translated_text: 'Whom the sages weave within the ocean' and so forth — 'Neither above, nor across, nor in the middle did they grasp him. There is none who rules over him; his name is great glory.' 'His form does not stand within sight; no one sees him with the eye. Those who know him thus through the heart, with wisdom, with the mind that is devoted — they become immortal.' Having thus established his supremacy over all, and having negated by 'there is none who rules over him' that there is anything whatsoever beyond him, [the text] 'from the waters was born <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>' and 'eight' are shown to form a single connected statement with the former. And the section on the <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>, by '<s>Hrī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s> are his consorts,' reveals that this is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone.

children.text: yam antaḥ samudre kavayo vayanti ity-ādi --- na enam ūrdhvaṃ na tiryañcaṃ na madhye parijagrabhat / na tasyā iśe kaścana tasya nāma mahad-yaśaḥ // na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścana enam, hṛdā manīṣā manasa ābhikḷpto ya evaṃ vidur amṛtās te bhavanti iti sarvasmāt paratvam asya pratipādya, na tasyā iśe kaścana iti tasmāt paraṃ kim api na vidyata iti ca pratiṣidhya, adbhyaḥ sambhūto hiraṇya-garbha ity-aṣṭāv iti tena eka-vākyatāṃ gamayati / tac ca mahā-puruṣa-prakaraṇaṃ hrīś ca te lakṣmīś ca patnyāv iti ca nārāyaṇa eva iti dyotayati /

body.text: ayam artho nārāyaṇānuvāke prapañcitaḥ / sahasraśīrṣaṃ devam ityārabhya sa brahma sa śivaḥ sendraḥ so 'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ svarāḍ iti / sarvaśākhāsu paratattvapratipādanaparān akṣaraśivaśaṃbhuparabrahmaparajyotiḥparatattvaparāyaṇaparamātmādisarvaśabdāṃs tattadguṇayogena nārāyaṇa eva prayujya tadvyatiriktasya samastasya tadādhāratāṃ tanniyāmyatāṃ taccheṣatām tadātmakatāṃ ca pratipādya brahmaśivayor apīndrādisamānākāratayā tadvibhūtitvaṃ ca pratipāditam / idaṃ ca vākyaṃ kevalaparatattvapratipādanaikaparam anyat kiṃcid apy atra na vidhīyate /
body.translated_text: This meaning is elaborated in the <s>Nārāyaṇānuvāka</s>. Beginning with 'the God of a thousand heads' and up to 'He is <s>Brahmā</s>, he is <s>Śiva</s>, he is <s>Indra</s>, he is the imperishable, the supreme, the self-ruler.' In all the branches [of the <s>Veda</s>], all words such as '<s>Akṣara</s>,' '<s>Śiva</s>,' '<s>Śaṃbhu</s>,' 'supreme <s>Brahman</s>,' 'supreme light,' 'supreme reality,' 'supreme refuge,' '<s>Paramātman</s>,' and so forth — which are devoted to teaching the supreme reality — are applied to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone by virtue of the connection with each respective quality. And having taught that everything other than him has him as its support, is controlled by him, is his subsidiary, and has him as its self, the <s>vibhūti</s>-status (glorious manifestation) of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śiva</s> too, on the same level as <s>Indra</s> and the rest, is established. And this statement is solely devoted to teaching the supreme reality alone — nothing else whatsoever is enjoined herein.

children.text: ayam artho nārāyaṇa-anuvāke prapañcitaḥ / sahasra-śīrṣaṃ devam ity-ārabhya sa brahma sa śivaḥ sa indraḥ so 'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ sva-rāḍ iti / sarva-śākhāsu para-tattva-pratipādana-parān akṣara-śiva-śaṃbhu-para-brahma-para-jyotiḥ-para-tattva-para-āyaṇa-parama-ātma-ādi-sarva-śabdāṃs tat-tad-guṇa-yogena nārāyaṇa eva prayujya tad-vyatiriktasya samastasya tad-ādhāratāṃ tan-niyāmyatāṃ tac-cheṣatām tad-ātmakatāṃ ca pratipādya brahma-śivayor api indra-ādi-samāna-ākāratayā tad-vibhūtitvaṃ ca pratipāditam / idaṃ ca vākyaṃ kevala-para-tattva-pratipādana-eka-param anyat kiṃcid apy atra na vidhīyate /

body.text: asmin vākye pratipāditasya sarvasmāt paratvenāvasthitasya brahmaṇo vākyāntareṣu brahmavid āpnoti param ityādiṣūpāsanādi vidhīyate / ataḥ prāṇaṃ manasi saha karaṇair ityādi vākyaṃ sarvakāraṇe paramātmani karaṇaprāṇādi sarvaṃ vikārajātam upasaṃhṛtya tam eva paramātmānaṃ sarvasyeśānaṃ dhyāyīteti parabrahmabhūtanārāyaṇasyaiva dhyānaṃ vidadhāti /
body.translated_text: Of <s>Brahman</s> established as supreme over all, as taught in this statement, worship and the like is enjoined in other statements such as 'the knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme.' Therefore, the statement 'the <s>prāṇa</s> [is to be merged] in the mind, together with the sense-faculties' and so forth enjoins the meditation upon the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) who is the cause of all — having withdrawn all modifications such as sense-faculties, vital breath, and the rest into the supreme Self, the lord of all, one should meditate on that very supreme Self — thus it prescribes meditation upon <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone, who is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: asmin vākye pratipāditasya sarvasmāt paratvena avasthitasya brahmaṇo vākya-antareṣu brahma-vid āpnoti param ity-ādiṣu upāsana-ādi vidhīyate / ataḥ prāṇaṃ manasi saha karaṇair ity-ādi vākyaṃ sarva-kāraṇe parama-ātmani karaṇa-prāṇa-ādi sarvaṃ vikāra-jātam upasaṃhṛtya tam eva parama-ātmānaṃ sarvasyā iśānaṃ dhyāyīta iti para-brahma-bhūta-nārāyaṇasya eva dhyānaṃ vidadhāti /

body.text: patiṃ viśvasyeti na tasyeśe kaścaneti ca tasyaiva sarvasyeśānatā pratipāditā / ata eva sarvāiśvaryasaṃpannaḥ sarveśvaraḥ śaṃbhurākāśamadhye dhyeya iti nārāyaṇasyaiva paramakāraṇasya śaṃbhuśabdavācyasya dhyānaṃ vidhīyate / kaś ca dhyeya ityārabhya kāraṇaṃ tu dhyeya iti kāryasyādhyeyatāpūrvakakāraṇaikadhyeyatāparatvād vākyasya / tasyaiva nārāyaṇasya paramakāraṇatā śaṃbhuśabdavācyatā ca paramakāraṇapratipādanaikapare nārāyaṇānuvāka eva pratipanneti tadvirodhyarthāntaraparikalpanaṃ kāraṇasyaiva dhyeyatvena vidhivākye na yujyate /
body.translated_text: By 'the lord of the universe' and 'there is none who rules over him,' the lordship over all is taught as belonging to him alone. For this very reason, the meditation prescribed as 'the Lord of all powers, the Lord of all, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, is to be meditated upon in the midst of space' prescribes the meditation of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone, the supreme cause, who is denoted by the word '<s>Śaṃbhu</s>.' Beginning with 'who is to be meditated upon?' and concluding 'the cause alone is to be meditated upon' — since the statement aims solely at prescribing meditation on the cause alone, preceded by the non-meditability of the effect. The supreme causality and the denotation by the word '<s>Śaṃbhu</s>' of that same <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> are understood from the <s>Nārāyaṇānuvāka</s> alone, which is devoted solely to teaching the supreme cause. Therefore, the fabrication of a different meaning contradicting it is not tenable in a prescriptive statement about meditation on the cause alone.

children.text: patiṃ viśvasya iti na tasyā iśe kaścana iti ca tasya eva sarvasyā iśānatā pratipāditā / ata eva sarva-aiśvarya-saṃpannaḥ sarva-īśvaraḥ śaṃbhura-ākāśa-madhye dhyeya iti nārāyaṇasya eva parama-kāraṇasya śaṃbhu-śabda-vācyasya dhyānaṃ vidhīyate / kaś ca dhyeya ity-ārabhya kāraṇaṃ tu dhyeya iti kāryasya adhyeyatā-pūrvaka-kāraṇa-eka-dhyeyatā-paratvād vākyasya / tasya eva nārāyaṇasya parama-kāraṇatā śaṃbhu-śabda-vācyatā ca parama-kāraṇa-pratipādana-eka-pare nārāyaṇa-anuvāka eva pratipanna īti tad-virodhy-artha-antara-parikalpanaṃ kāraṇasya eva dhyeyatvena vidhi-vākye na yujyate /

body.text: yad api tato yaduttaram ity atra puruṣād anyasya parataratvaṃ pratīyata ityabhyadhāyi tad api yasmāt paraṃ nāparam asti kiṃcid yasmān nāṇīyo na jyāyo 'sti kaścit-- yasmād aparaṃ -- yasmād anyat kiṃcid api paraṃ nāsti kenāpi prakāreṇa puruṣavyatiriktasya paratvaṃ nāstītyarthaḥ / aṇīyastvaṃ -- sūkṣmatvam / jyāyastvaṃ -- sarveśvaratvam / sarvavyāpitvāt sarveśvaratvād asyaitadvyatirikitasya kasyāpy aṇīyastvaṃ jyāyastvaṃ ca nāstītyarthaḥ / yasmān nāṇīyo na jyāyo 'sti kaścid iti puruṣād anyasya kasyāpi jyāyastvaṃ niṣiddham iti tasmād anyasya paratvaṃ na yujyata iti pratyuktam /
body.translated_text: As for what was asserted — that in 'that which is beyond that,' the supremacy of something other than the <s>Puruṣa</s> is understood — that too [is refuted]: 'from which there is nothing higher nor lower, from which there is nothing subtler nor greater' — 'from which there is nothing other' means that there is nothing whatsoever that is in any way supreme beyond the <s>Puruṣa</s> — this is the meaning. 'Subtlety' means pervasiveness. 'Greatness' means lordship over all. Due to his all-pervasiveness and lordship over all, nothing other than him possesses either subtlety or greatness — this is the meaning. Since by 'from which there is nothing subtler nor greater' the greatness of anything other than the <s>Puruṣa</s> is negated, the supremacy of anything other is not tenable — thus the [objection] is answered.

children.text: yad api tato yad-uttaram ity atra puruṣād anyasya parataratvaṃ pratīyata ity-abhyadhāyi tad api yasmāt paraṃ na aparam asti kiṃcid yasmān na aṇīyo na jyāyo 'sti kaścit--- yasmād aparaṃ --- yasmād anyat kiṃcid api paraṃ na asti kena api prakāreṇa puruṣa-vyatiriktasya paratvaṃ na asti ity-arthaḥ / aṇīyastvaṃ --- sūkṣmatvam / jyāyastvaṃ --- sarva-īśvaratvam / sarva-vyāpitvāt sarva-īśvaratvād asya etad-vyatirikitasya kasya apy aṇīyastvaṃ jyāyastvaṃ ca na asti ity-arthaḥ / yasmān na aṇīyo na jyāyo 'sti kaścid iti puruṣād anyasya kasya api jyāyastvaṃ niṣiddham iti tasmād anyasya paratvaṃ na yujyata iti pratyuktam /

body.text:
kas tarhy asya vākyasyārthaḥ / asya prakaraṇasyopakrame tam eva viditvātimṛtyum eti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāyāiti puruṣavedanasyāmṛtatvahetutāṃ tadvyatiriktasyāpathatāṃ ca pratijñāya yasmāt paraṃ nāparam asti kiṃcit tenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa sarvam ity etad antena sarvasmāt paratvaṃ pratipāditam / yataḥ puruṣatattvam evottarataraṃ tato yaduttarataraṃ puruṣatattvaṃ tad evārūpam anāmayaṃ ya etadvidur amṛtās te bhavanti, athetare duḥkham evāpiyantīti puruṣavedanasyāmṛtatvahetutvaṃ taditarasyāpathatvaṃ pratijñātaṃ sahetukam upasaṃhṛtam / anyathopakramagatapratijñābhyāṃ virudhyate / puruṣasyaiva śuddhiguṇayogena śivaśabdābhiprāyatvaṃ śāśvataṃ śivam acyutam ityādinā jñātam eva / puruṣa eva śivaśabdābhidheya ityanantaram eva vadati -- mahān
prabhur vai puruṣaḥ sattvasyaiṣa pravartaka iti / uktenaiva nyāyena na san na cāsac chiva eva kevala ityādi sarvaṃ neyam /
body.translated_text: What then is the meaning of this statement? At the opening of this section, having declared 'by knowing him alone one transcends death; there is no other path for going' — [thus declaring] that the knowledge of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause of immortality and that [any path] other than that is a non-path — by the passage ending with 'from which there is nothing higher nor lower, all this is filled by <s>Puruṣa</s>,' the supremacy over all is established. Since the <s>Puruṣa</s> reality alone is the highest, 'that which is the highest is the <s>Puruṣa</s> reality itself — it is formless, without affliction; those who know this become immortal; others indeed go only to suffering' — thus the declared proposition that knowledge of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause of immortality and that the alternative is a non-path is concluded together with its reason. Otherwise it would contradict the propositions stated in the opening. That the <s>Puruṣa</s> himself is intended by the word '<s>Śiva</s>' through the connection with qualities of purity is already known from passages like 'eternal, auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), imperishable (<s>acyuta</s>).' That the <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is denoted by the word '<s>Śiva</s>' is stated immediately after: 'Great indeed is the Lord, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the activator of <s>sattva</s>.' By the reasoning already stated, passages like 'neither existent nor non-existent, <s>Śiva</s> alone, the absolute' and so forth are all to be interpreted [as referring to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>].

children.text:
kas tarhy asya vākyasya arthaḥ / asya prakaraṇasya upakrame tam eva viditva ātimṛtyum eti na anyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya aiti puruṣa-vedanasya amṛtatva-hetutāṃ tad-vyatiriktasya apathatāṃ ca pratijñāya yasmāt paraṃ na aparam asti kiṃcit tena idaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa sarvam ity etad antena sarvasmāt paratvaṃ pratipāditam / yataḥ puruṣa-tattvam eva uttarataraṃ tato yad-uttarataraṃ puruṣa-tattvaṃ tad eva arūpam anāmayaṃ ya etad-vidur amṛtās te bhavanti, atha itare duḥkham eva apiyanti iti puruṣa-vedanasya amṛtatva-hetutvaṃ tad-itarasya apathatvaṃ pratijñātaṃ sahetukam upasaṃhṛtam / anyatha ūpakrama-gata-pratijñābhyāṃ virudhyate / puruṣasya eva śuddhi-guṇa-yogena śiva-śabda-abhiprāyatvaṃ śāśvataṃ śivam acyutam ity-ādinā jñātam eva / puruṣa eva śiva-śabda-abhidheya ity-anantaram eva vadati --- mahān
prabhur vai puruṣaḥ sattvasya eṣa pravartaka iti / uktena eva nyāyena na san na ca asac chiva eva kevala ity-ādi sarvaṃ na iyam /

body.text:
kiṃca na tasyeśe kaścaneti nirastasamābhyadhikasaṃbhāvanasya puruṣasyāṇor aṇīyānityasminn anuvāke vedādyantarūpatayā vedabījabhūtapraṇavasya prakṛtibhūtākāravācyatayā maheśvaratvaṃ pratipādya daharapuṇḍarīkamadhyasthākāśāntarvartitayopāsyatvam uktam / ayam arthaḥ -- sarvasya vedajātasya prakṛtiḥ praṇava uktaḥ / praṇavasya ca prakṛtir akāraḥ / praṇavavikāro vedaḥ svaprakṛtibhūte praṇave līnaḥ / praṇavo 'py akāravikārabhūtaḥ svaprakṛtāv akāre līnaḥ / tasya praṇavaprakṛtibhūtasyākārasya yaḥ paro vācyaḥ sa eva maheśvara iti sarvavācakajātaprakṛtibhūtākāravācyaḥ sarvavācyajātaprakṛtibhūtanārāyaṇo yaḥ sa maheśavara ityarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā --
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā /
mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyatkiṃcid asti dhanaṃjaya //
akṣaraṇām akāro 'smi ----------------- //
iti / a iti brahmeti ca śruteḥ / akāro vai sarvā vāg iti ca / vācakajātasyākāraprakṛtitvaṃ vācyajātasya brahmaprakṛtitvaṃ ca suspaṣṭam / ato brahmaṇo 'kāravācyatāpratipādanād akāravācyo nārāyaṇa eva maheśvara iti siddham /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, regarding the <s>Puruṣa</s> whose equal and superior are negated by 'there is none who rules over him' — 'subtler than the subtle' — in this <s>anuvāka</s>, having taught his great lordship (<s>maheśvaratva</s>) through the form of being the beginning and end of the <s>Veda</s>, that is, through the <s>akāra</s> which is the material cause of <s>praṇava</s>, the seed of the <s>Veda</s>, his being the object of worship as dwelling within the space inside the small lotus [of the heart] is stated. The meaning is this: <s>praṇava</s> is stated as the source (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the entire class of <s>Vedas</s>. And the <s>akāra</s> is the source of <s>praṇava</s>. The <s>Veda</s>, a modification of <s>praṇava</s>, is dissolved in <s>praṇava</s>, its source. <s>Praṇava</s> too, being a modification of <s>akāra</s>, is dissolved in <s>akāra</s>, its source. The supreme denotatum of that <s>akāra</s>, which is the source of <s>praṇava</s> — he alone is <s>Maheśvara</s> (the great Lord). Thus the meaning is: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is the source of the entire class of denotata and who is denoted by <s>akāra</s>, the source of the entire class of denotors — he is <s>Maheśvara</s>. As stated by the Blessed Lord:
'I am the origin and dissolution of the entire universe.
There is nothing whatsoever higher than me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.'
'Among letters I am the <s>akāra</s> —'
And from the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>a</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' And: '<s>akāra</s> is indeed all speech.' The <s>akāra</s>-source-hood of the class of denotors and the <s>Brahman</s>-source-hood of the class of denotata are perfectly clear. Therefore, since <s>Brahman</s>'s being denoted by <s>akāra</s> is established, it is proved that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone, denoted by <s>akāra</s>, is <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text:
kiṃca na tasyā iśe kaścana iti nirasta-sama-abhyadhika-saṃbhāvanasya puruṣasya aṇor aṇīya-anityasminn anuvāke veda-ādy-anta-rūpatayā veda-bīja-bhūta-praṇavasya prakṛti-bhūta-akāra-vācyatayā mahā-īśvaratvaṃ pratipādya dahara-puṇḍarīka-madhya-stha-ākāśa-antarvartitaya ūpāsyatvam uktam / ayam arthaḥ --- sarvasya veda-jātasya prakṛtiḥ praṇava uktaḥ / praṇavasya ca prakṛtir akāraḥ / praṇava-vikāro vedaḥ sva-prakṛti-bhūte praṇave līnaḥ / praṇavo 'py akāra-vikāra-bhūtaḥ sva-prakṛtāv akāre līnaḥ / tasya praṇava-prakṛti-bhūtasya akārasya yaḥ paro vācyaḥ sa eva mahā-īśvara iti sarva-vācaka-jāta-prakṛti-bhūta-akāra-vācyaḥ sarva-vācya-jāta-prakṛti-bhūta-nārāyaṇo yaḥ sa mahā-īśavara ity-arthaḥ / yathā-uktaṃ bhagavatā ---
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā /
mattaḥ parataraṃ na anyat-kiṃcid asti dhanaṃjaya //
akṣaraṇām akāro 'smi -------------------------- //
iti / a iti brahma iti ca śruteḥ / akāro vai sarvā vāg iti ca / vācaka-jātasya akāra-prakṛtitvaṃ vācya-jātasya brahma-prakṛtitvaṃ ca suspaṣṭam / ato brahmaṇo 'kāra-vācyatā-pratipādanād akāra-vācyo nārāyaṇa eva mahā-īśvara iti siddham /

body.text:
tasyaiva sahasraśīrṣaṃ devam iti kevalaparatattvaviśeṣapratipādanapareṇa nārāyaṇānuvākena sarvasmāt paratvaṃ prapañcitam / anenānanyapareṇa pratipāditam eva paratattvam anyapareṣu sarvavākyeṣu kenāpi śabdena pratīyamānaṃ tad evety avagamya iti śāstradṛṣtyā tūpadeśo vāmadevavad iti sūtrakāreṇa nirṇītam / tad etat paraṃ brahma kvacid brahmaśivādiśabdād avagatam iti kevalabrahmaśivayor na paratvaprasaṅgaḥ / asminn ananyapare 'nuvāke tayor indrāditulyatayā tadvibhūtitvapratipādanāt / kvacid ākāśaprāṇādiśabdena paraṃ brahmābhihitam iti bhūtākāśaprāṇāder yathā na paratvam / yat punar idam āśaṅkitam atha yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminn antarākāśas tasmin yad antas tad anveṣṭavyaṃ tad vā va vijijñāsitavyam
ity atrākāśaśabdena jagadupādānakāraṇaṃ pratipādya tadantarvartinaḥ kasyacit tattvaviśeṣasyānveṣṭavyatā pratipādyate / asyākāśasya nāmarūpayor nivoḍhṛtvaśravaṇāt puruṣasūkte puruṣasya nāmarūpayoḥ kartṛtvadarśanāc cākāśaparyāyabhūtāt puruṣād anyasyānveṣṭavyatayopāsyatvaṃ pratīyata ityanadhītavedānām adṛṣṭaśāstrāṇām idaṃ codyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Of that same [<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>], the supremacy over all is elaborated by the <s>Nārāyaṇānuvāka</s>, beginning with 'the God of a thousand heads,' which is solely devoted to teaching the particular supreme reality. Having understood that the supreme reality taught by this [<s>anuvāka</s>] — which has no other purpose — is the same [reality] that is understood in all other statements through whatever word, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>] has determined: 'But through the scriptural perspective, the instruction [applies], like <s>Vāmadeva</s>.' Therefore, this supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is sometimes understood through the words '<s>Brahma</s>,' '<s>Śiva</s>,' and the like — there is no occasion for the supremacy of <s>Brahmā</s> or <s>Śiva</s> by themselves, since in this <s>anuvāka</s>, which has no other purpose, their <s>vibhūti</s>-status on the same level as <s>Indra</s> and the rest is taught. Sometimes the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is denoted by the words 'space,' '<s>prāṇa</s>,' and the like — just as elemental space and <s>prāṇa</s> are not thereby supreme. As for the doubt that was raised — 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s> there is a small lotus dwelling, and within it a small space; what is within that is to be sought, that indeed is to be known' — here, having taught the material cause of the universe by the word 'space,' the seeking of some particular reality dwelling within it is taught. Since one hears of this space's carrying name and form, and since in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> the <s>Puruṣa</s> is seen as the creator of name and form — [the objection that] the object of worship is something other than the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is synonymous with space — this is a doubt of those who have not studied the <s>Veda</s> and have not examined the scriptures.

children.text:
tasya eva sahasra-śīrṣaṃ devam iti kevala-para-tattva-viśeṣa-pratipādana-pareṇa nārāyaṇa-anuvākena sarvasmāt paratvaṃ prapañcitam / anena ananya-pareṇa pratipāditam eva para-tattvam anya-pareṣu sarva-vākyeṣu kena api śabdena pratīyamānaṃ tad eva ity avagamya iti śāstra-dṛṣtyā tu upadeśo vāma-devavad iti sūtra-kāreṇa nirṇītam / tad etat paraṃ brahma kvacid brahma-śiva-ādi-śabdād avagatam iti kevala-brahma-śivayor na paratva-prasaṅgaḥ / asminn ananya-pare 'nuvāke tayor indra-ādi-tulyatayā tad-vibhūtitva-pratipādanāt / kvacid ākāśa-prāṇa-ādi-śabdena paraṃ brahma abhihitam iti bhūta-ākāśa-prāṇa-āder yathā na paratvam / yat punar idam āśaṅkitam atha yad idam asmin brahma-pure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminn antara-ākāśas tasmin yad antas tad anveṣṭavyaṃ tad vā va vijijñāsitavyam
ity atrā akāśa-śabdena jagad-upādāna-kāraṇaṃ pratipādya tad-antarvartinaḥ kasyacit tattva-viśeṣasya anveṣṭavyatā pratipādyate / asyā akāśasya nāma-rūpayor nivoḍhṛtva-śravaṇāt puruṣa-sūkte puruṣasya nāma-rūpayoḥ kartṛtva-darśanāc cā akāśa-paryāya-bhūtāt puruṣād anyasya anveṣṭavyataya ūpāsyatvaṃ pratīyata ity-anadhīta-vedānām adṛṣṭa-śāstrāṇām idaṃ codyaṃ /

body.text: yatas tatra śrutir evāsya parihāram āha / vākyakāraś ca -- daharo 'sminn antarākāśaḥ kiṃ tad atra vidyate yad anveṣṭavyaṃ yad vā va vijijñāsitavyam iti codite yāvān vā ayam ākāśas tāvān eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśa ityādināsyākāśaśabdavācyasya paramapuruṣasyānavadhikamahattvaṃ sakalajagadādhāratvaṃ ca pratipādya tasmin kāmāḥ samāhitā iti kāmaśabdenāpahatapāpmatvādisatyasaṃkalpaparyantaguṇāṣṭakaṃ nihitam iti paramapuruṣavat paramapuruṣaguṇāṣṭakasyāpi pṛthivijijñāsitavyatāpratipādayiṣayā tasmin yad antas tadanveṣṭavyam ityuktam iti śrutyaiva sarvaṃ parihṛtam /
body.translated_text: For therein, the <s>śruti</s> itself states the resolution of this [objection]. And the <s>Vākyakāra</s> (author of the <s>Vākyapadīya</s>) [explains]: when the question is raised — 'In this small space within the heart (<s>dahara</s>), what is there that is to be sought, that is to be inquired into?' — the <s>śruti</s>, beginning with 'As vast as this space is, so vast is this space within the heart,' establishes the unlimited greatness and the nature of being the support of the entire universe of the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>) who is denoted by the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space). Then, by the word '<s>kāma</s>' (desire) in 'In it are deposited the desires,' the eightfold group of qualities ranging from freedom from evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) to true resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>) is deposited [therein]. With the intention of establishing that the eightfold group of qualities of the Supreme Person, like the Supreme Person Himself, is separately worthy of inquiry, it is said 'that which is within it is to be sought' — thus everything is resolved by the <s>śruti</s> itself.

children.text: yatas tatra śrutir eva asya parihāram āha / vākya-kāraś ca --- daharo 'sminn antar-ākāśaḥ kiṃ tad atra vidyate yad anveṣṭavyaṃ yad vā va vijijñāsitavyam iti codite yāvān vā ayam ākāśas tāvān eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśa ity-ādina āsyā akāśa-śabda-vācyasya parama-puruṣasya anavadhika-mahattvaṃ sakala-jagad-ādhāratvaṃ ca pratipādya tasmin kāmāḥ samāhitā iti kāma-śabdena apahata-pāpmatva-ādi-satya-saṃkalpa-paryanta-guṇa-aṣṭakaṃ nihitam iti parama-puruṣavat parama-puruṣa-guṇa-aṣṭakasya api pṛthivi-jijñāsitavyatā-pratipādayiṣayā tasmin yad antas tad-anveṣṭavyam ity-uktam iti śrutya aiva sarvaṃ parihṛtam /

body.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati -- kiṃ tad atra vidyate yad aneṣṭavyam ity asya codyasya tasmin sarvasya jagataḥ sraṣṭṛtvam ādhāratvaṃ niyantṛtvaṃ śeṣitvam apahatapāpmatvādayo guṇāś ca vidyanta iti parihāra iti / tathā ca vākyakāravacanam -- tasmin yad antar iti kāmavyapadeśa iti / kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ / apahatapāpmatvādayo guṇā ityarthaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- yad etad daharākāśaśabdābhidheyaṃ nikhilajagadudayavaibhavalayalīlaṃ paraṃ brahma tasmin yad antar nihitam anavadhikātiśayam apahatapāpmatvādiguṇāṣṭakaṃ tad ubhayam apy anveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyam iti / yathāha -- atha ya ihātmānam anuvidya vrajanty etāṃś ca satyān kāmāṃs teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavantīti /
body.translated_text: What is being said is this: the resolution of the objection 'What is there that is to be sought?' is that therein are found the creatorship of the entire universe, its supportership, its controllership, its mastership, and the qualities such as freedom from evil, etc. And thus the statement of the <s>Vākyakāra</s>: 'That which is within it — this is the designation by the word <s>kāma</s>.' '<s>Kāmas</s>' means 'those that are desired' — that is, the qualities such as freedom from evil, etc. — that is the meaning. What is being said is this: that Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, denoted by the term '<s>daharākāśa</s>' (small space), whose sport is the creation, magnificence, and dissolution of the entire universe — both that [<s>Brahman</s>] and the eightfold group of qualities such as freedom from evil, etc., of unsurpassable excellence deposited within it — both are to be sought, both are to be inquired into. As it says: 'Now, those who, having realized the Self here, depart, and [having realized] these true desires — for them, in all worlds, there is freedom of movement.'

children.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati --- kiṃ tad atra vidyate yad aneṣṭavyam ity asya codyasya tasmin sarvasya jagataḥ sraṣṭṛtvam ādhāratvaṃ niyantṛtvaṃ śeṣitvam apahata-pāpmatva-ādayo guṇāś ca vidyanta iti parihāra iti / tathā ca vākya-kāra-vacanam --- tasmin yad antar iti kāma-vyapadeśa iti / kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ / apahata-pāpmatva-ādayo guṇā ity-arthaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- yad etad dahara-ākāśa-śabda-abhidheyaṃ nikhila-jagad-udaya-vaibhava-laya-līlaṃ paraṃ brahma tasmin yad antar nihitam anavadhika-atiśayam apahata-pāpmatva-ādi-guṇa-aṣṭakaṃ tad ubhayam apy anveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyam iti / yathā āha --- atha ya ihā atmānam anuvidya vrajanty etāṃś ca satyān kāmāṃs teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāma-cāro bhavanti iti /

body.text: yaḥ punaḥ kāraṇasyaiva dhyeyatāpratipādanapare vākye viṣṇor ananyaparavākyapratipāditaparatattvabhūtasya kāryamadhye niveśaḥ sa svakāryabhūtatattvasaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ kurvataḥ svalīlayā jagadupakārāya svecchāvatāra ity avagantavyaḥ / yathā līlayā devasaṃkhyāpūrṇaṃ kurvata upendratvaṃ parasyaiva, yathā ca sūryavaṃśodbhavarājasaṃkhyāpūrṇaṃ kurvataḥ parasyaiva brahmaṇo dāśarathirūpeṇa svecchāvatāraḥ, yathā ca somavaṃśasaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ kurvato bhagavato bhūbhārāvatāraṇāya svecchayā vasudevagṛhe 'vatāraḥ /
body.translated_text: As for the placing of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — who is established as the supreme reality by other, unambiguous statements — among the effects, in a passage whose purport is to establish that the cause alone is to be meditated upon: this should be understood as the voluntary descent (<s>avatāra</s>) of Him who, by His own sport, completes the enumeration of the realities that are His own effects, for the benefit of the world. Just as the becoming <s>Upendra</s> belongs to the Supreme One alone, who by sport completes the number of the gods; just as the voluntary descent of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> Himself in the form of the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, completing the number of kings born in the solar dynasty; and just as the voluntary descent of the Blessed Lord in the house of <s>Vasudeva</s>, completing the number of the lunar dynasty, for the purpose of relieving the burden of the earth.

children.text: yaḥ punaḥ kāraṇasya eva dhyeyatā-pratipādana-pare vākye viṣṇor ananya-para-vākya-pratipādita-para-tattva-bhūtasya kārya-madhye niveśaḥ sa sva-kārya-bhūta-tattva-saṃkhyā-pūraṇaṃ kurvataḥ sva-līlayā jagad-upakārāya sva icchā-avatāra ity avagantavyaḥ / yathā līlayā deva-saṃkhyā-pūrṇaṃ kurvata upendratvaṃ parasya eva, yathā ca sūrya-vaṃśa-udbhava-rāja-saṃkhyā-pūrṇaṃ kurvataḥ parasya eva brahmaṇo dāśa-rathi-rūpeṇa sva-icchā-avatāraḥ, yathā ca soma-vaṃśa-saṃkhyā-pūraṇaṃ kurvato bhagavato bhū-bhāra-avatāraṇāya sva-icchayā vasudeva-gṛhe 'vatāraḥ /

body.text:
sṛṣṭipralayaprakaraṇeṣu nārāyaṇa eva paramakāraṇatayā pratipādyata iti pūrvam evoktam / yat punar atharvaśirasi rudreṇa svasarvāiśvaryaṃ prapañcitaṃ tat so 'ntarād antaraṃ prāviśad iti paramātmapraveśād uktam iti śrutyaiva vyaktam / śāstradṛṣṭyā tūpadeśo vāmadevavad iti sūtrakāreṇaivaṃvādinām arthaḥ pratipāditaḥ / yathoktaṃ prahlādenāpi --
sarvagatvād anantarasya sa evāham avasthitaḥ /
mattaḥ sarvam ahaṃ sarvaṃ mayi sarvaṃ sanātane //
ityādi / atra sarvagatvād anantasyeti hetur uktaḥ / svaśarīrabhūtasya sarvasya cidacidvastuna ātmatvena sarvagaḥ paramātmeti sarve śabdāḥ sarvaśarīraṃ paramātmānam evābhidadhatīty uktam / ato 'ham iti śabdaḥ svātmaprakāraprakāriṇaṃ paramātmānam evācaṣṭe / ata idam ucyate / ātmety eva tu gṛhṇīyāt sarvasya tanniṣpatter ityādināhaṃgrahaṇopāsanaṃ vākyakāreṇa kāryāvasthaḥ kāraṇāvasthaś ca sthūlasūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīraḥ paramātmaiveti sarvasya tanniṣpatter ity uktam / ātmeti tūpagacchanti grāhayanti ceti sūtrakāreṇa ca / mahābhārate ca brahmarudrasaṃvāde brahmā rudraṃ prayāha --
tavāntarātmā mama ca ye cānye dehisaṃjñitāḥ /
iti / rudrasya brahmaṇaś cānyeṣāṃ ca dehināṃ parameśvaro nārāyaṇo 'ntarātmatayāvasthita iti / tathā tatraiva --
viṣṇur ātmā bhagavato bhavasyāmitatejasaḥ /
tasmād dhanurjyāsaṃsparśaṃ sa viṣehe maheśvaraḥ //
iti / tatraiva --
etau dvau vibudhaśreṣṭhau prasādakrodhajau smṛtau /
tadādarśitapanthānau sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakau //
iti / antarātmatayāvasthitanārāyaṇadarśitapathau brahmarudrau sṛṣṭisaṃhārakāryakarāv ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
It has already been stated earlier that in the passages dealing with creation and dissolution, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is established as the supreme cause. As for the fact that in the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>, <s>Rudra</s> elaborates his own complete sovereignty — that is stated because of the entry of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), as [the <s>śruti</s>] says 'He entered within the innermost' — this is made clear by the <s>śruti</s> itself. 'But [this is] instruction from the standpoint of scripture, like <s>Vāmadeva</s>' — by this, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>) has established the meaning of those who speak thus. As stated by <s>Prahlāda</s> too:
'Because of being all-pervading, because of being infinite, He alone — I am established [as Him].
From me is everything; I am everything; in me, the eternal, is everything.'
And so forth. Here the reason is stated: 'because of being all-pervading, because of being infinite.' Since the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) is all-pervading by being the Self of all conscious and non-conscious entities that are His body — therefore all words denote the Supreme Self who is the body of all. Thus it is said. Therefore the word 'I' (<s>aham</s>) denotes the Supreme Self alone, who is qualified by one's own self as a mode. Hence this is stated: 'One should understand [it] as the Self alone, because everything is produced from that' — by this and similar [statements], the <s>Vākyakāra</s> states that the meditation through the apprehension of 'I' [is appropriate because] the Supreme Self alone, having as His body the gross and subtle conscious and non-conscious entities in both the causal and effectual states, [is denoted], because everything is produced from that. And the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> too [says]: 'They understand as the Self, and they make [others] understand [so].' And in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> addresses <s>Rudra</s>:
'The inner Self of you, of me, and of others who are called embodied [beings].'
The meaning is that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Supreme Lord, is established as the inner Self of <s>Rudra</s>, of <s>Brahmā</s>, and of other embodied beings. Likewise, therein:
'<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the Self of the Blessed <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva) of unlimited splendor;
therefore that great lord endured the touch of the bowstring.'
And therein:
'These two, the best of the wise, are said to be born of [His] grace and wrath;
they carry out creation and dissolution, shown the path by Him.'
The meaning is that <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, shown the path by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who is established as their inner Self, are the agents of creation and dissolution.

children.text:
sṛṣṭi-pralaya-prakaraṇeṣu nārāyaṇa eva parama-kāraṇatayā pratipādyata iti pūrvam eva uktam / yat punar atharva-śirasi rudreṇa sva-sarva-aiśvaryaṃ prapañcitaṃ tat so 'ntarād antaraṃ prāviśad iti parama-ātma-praveśād uktam iti śrutya aiva vyaktam / śāstra-dṛṣṭyā tu upadeśo vāmadevavad iti sūtra-kāreṇa evaṃ-vādinām arthaḥ pratipāditaḥ / yatha ūktaṃ prahlādena api ---
sarva-gatvād anantarasya sa eva aham avasthitaḥ /
mattaḥ sarvam ahaṃ sarvaṃ mayi sarvaṃ sanātane //
ity-ādi / atra sarva-gatvād anantasya iti hetur uktaḥ / sva-śarīra-bhūtasya sarvasya cid-acid-vastuna ātmatvena sarva-gaḥ parama-ātma īti sarve śabdāḥ sarva-śarīraṃ parama-ātmānam eva abhidadhati ity uktam / ato 'ham iti śabdaḥ sva-ātma-prakāra-prakāriṇaṃ parama-ātmānam evā acaṣṭe / ata idam ucyate / ātma īty eva tu gṛhṇīyāt sarvasya tan-niṣpatter ity-ādina āhaṃ-grahaṇa-upāsanaṃ vākya-kāreṇa kārya-avasthaḥ kāraṇa-avasthaś ca sthūla-sūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraḥ parama-ātma aiva iti sarvasya tan-niṣpatter ity uktam / ātma īti tu upagacchanti grāhayanti ca iti sūtra-kāreṇa ca / mahā-bhārate ca brahma-rudra-saṃvāde brahmā rudraṃ prayāha ---
tava antara-ātmā mama ca ye ca anye dehi-saṃjñitāḥ /
iti / rudrasya brahmaṇaś ca anyeṣāṃ ca dehināṃ parama-īśvaro nārāyaṇo 'ntara-ātmataya āvasthita iti / tathā tatra eva ---
viṣṇur ātmā bhagavato bhavasya amita-tejasaḥ /
tasmād dhanur-jyā-saṃsparśaṃ sa viṣehe maha-īśvaraḥ //
iti / tatra eva ---
etau dvau vibudha-śreṣṭhau prasāda-krodha-jau smṛtau /
tad-ādarśita-panthānau sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra-kārakau //
iti / antara-ātmataya āvasthita-nārāyaṇa-darśita-pathau brahma-rudrau sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra-kārya-karāv ity-arthaḥ /

body.text: nimittopādānayos tu bhedaṃ vadanto vedabāhyā eva syuḥ / janmādyasya yataḥ -- prakṛtiś ca -- pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhād ityādi vedavitpraṇītasūtravirodhāt / sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam -- tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti -- brahmavanaṃ brahma sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ -- brahmādhyatiṣṭhadbhuvanāni dhārayan -- sarve nimeṣā jajñire vidyutaḥ puruṣādadhi -- na tasyeśe kaścana tasya nāma mahadyaśaḥ -- neha nānāsti kiṃcana -- sarvasya vaśī sarvasyeśānaḥ -- puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyam utāmṛtattvasyeśānaḥ -- nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyata ityādisarvaśrutivirodhāc ca /
body.translated_text: Those who maintain a difference between the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) and the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) would be outside the <s>Veda</s> altogether — because this contradicts the <s>sūtras</s> composed by the knower of the <s>Veda</s>: 'That from which the origin, etc., [of this world proceed]' — 'And the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>)' — 'Because there is no contradiction with the thesis and the illustration.' And because it contradicts all <s>śrutis</s> such as: 'Being alone, dear one, this was in the beginning, one only, without a second' — 'It willed: may I become many, may I be born' — '<s>Brahman</s> was the forest, <s>Brahman</s> was the tree from which heaven and earth were fashioned' — '<s>Brahman</s> stood supporting the worlds' — 'All flashings were born from the lightning, from the <s>Puruṣa</s>' — 'No one is His master; His name is great glory' — 'There is no plurality here whatsoever' — 'The ruler of all, the lord of all' — '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this — what has been and what is to be; and He is the lord of immortality' — 'There is no other path for attainment.'

children.text: nimitta-upādānayos tu bhedaṃ vadanto veda-bāhyā eva syuḥ / janma-ādy-asya yataḥ --- prakṛtiś ca --- pratijñā-dṛṣṭānta-anuparodhād ity-ādi veda-vit-praṇīta-sūtra-virodhāt / sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ekam eva advitīyam --- tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya iti --- brahma-vanaṃ brahma sa vṛkṣa āsīd yato dyāvā-pṛthivī niṣṭa-takṣuḥ --- brahma-adhyatiṣṭhad-bhuvanāni dhārayan --- sarve nimeṣā jajñire vidyutaḥ puruṣa-adadhi --- na tasyā iśe kaścana tasya nāma mahad-yaśaḥ --- na iha nāna āsti kiṃcana --- sarvasya vaśī sarvasyā iśānaḥ --- puruṣa eva idaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyam uta amṛtattvasyā iśānaḥ --- na anyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyata ity-ādi-sarva-śruti-virodhāc ca /

body.text:
itihāsapurāṇeṣu ca sṛṣṭisthitipralayaprakaraṇayor idam eva paratattvam ity avagamyate / yathā mahābhārate --
kutaḥ sṛṣṭam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
pralaye ca kam abhyeti tan to brūhi pitāmaha //
iti pṛṣṭo --
nārāyaṇo jaganmūrtir anantātmā sanātana /
ityādi ca vadati --
ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā mahābhūtāni dhātavaḥ /
jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ cedaṃ jagannārāyaṇodbhavam //
iti ca / prācyodīcyadākṣiṇātyapāścātyasarvaśiṣṭaiḥ sarvadharmasarvatattvavyavasthāyām idam eva paryāptam ity avigānaparigṛhītaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca purāṇaṃ janmādy asya yata iti jagajjanmādikāraṇaṃ brahmety avagamyate / tajjanmādikāraṇaṃ kim iti praśnapūrvakaṃ viṣṇoḥ sakāśād bhūtam ityādinā brahmasvarūpaviśeṣapratipādanaikaparatayā pravṛttam iti sarvasaṃmatam / tathā tatraiva --
prakṛtir yā khyātā vyaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇī /
puruṣaś ca+py ubhāv etau līyete paramātmani //
paramātmā ca sarveṣām ādhāraḥ parameśvaraḥ /
viṣṇunāmā sa vedeṣu vedānteṣu ca gīyate //
iti / sarvavedavedānteṣu sarvaiḥ śabdaiḥ paramakāraṇatayāyam eva gīyata ityarthaḥ / yathā sarvāsu ṣrutiṣu kevalaparabrahmasvarūpaviśeṣapratipādanāyaiva pravṛtto nārāyaṇānuvākas tathedaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca purāṇam --
so 'ham icchāmi dharmajña śrotuṃ tvatto yathā jagat /
babhūva bhūyaś ca yathā mahābhāga bhaviṣyati //
yanmayaṃ ca jagadbrahmany ataś caitaccarācaram /
līnam āsīd yathā yatra layam eṣyati yatra ca //
iti paraṃ brahma kim iti prakramya --
viṣṇoḥ sakāśād udbhūtaṃ jagat tatraiva ca sthitam /
sthitisaṃyamakartāsau jagato 'sya jagac ca saḥ //
paraḥ parāṇāṃ paramaḥ paramātmātmasaṃsthitaḥ /
rūpavarṇādinirdeśaviśeṣaṇavivarjitaḥ //
apakṣayavināśābhyāṃ pariṇāmarddhijanmabhiḥ /
varjitaḥ śakyate vaktuṃ yaḥ sad astīti kevalam //
sarvatrāsau samastaṃ ca vasaty atreti vai yataḥ /
tataḥ sa vāsudeveti vidvadbhiḥ paripaṭhyate //
tadbrahma paraṃ nityam ajam akṣayam avyayam /
ekasvarūpaṃ ca sadā heyābhāvāc ca nirmalam //
tad eva sarvam evaitadvyaktāvyaktasvarūpavat /
tathā puruṣarūpeṇa kālarūpeṇa ca sthitam //
sa sarvabhūtaprakṛtiṃ vikārān guṇādidoṣāṃś ca mune vyatītaḥ /
atītasarvāvaraṇo 'khilātmā tenāstṛtaṃ yad bhuvanāntarāle //
samastakalyāṇaguṇātmako 'sau svaśaktileśoddhṛtabhūtavargaḥ /
icchāgṛhītābhimatorudehaḥ saṃsādhitāśeṣajagaddhito 'sau //
tejobalāiśvaryamahāvabodhasuvīryaśaktyādiguṇaikarāśiḥ /
paraḥ parāṇāṃ sakalā na yatra kleśādayaḥ santi parāvareśe //
sa īśvaro vyaṣṭisamaṣṭirūpo 'vyaktasvarūpaḥ prakaṭasvarūpaḥ /
sarveśvaraḥ sarvadṛksarvavettā samastaśaktiḥ parameśvarākhyaḥ //
saṃjñāyate yena tad astadoṣaṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ nirmalam ekarūpam /
saṃdṛśyate vāpy adhigamyate vā tajjñānam ajñānam ato 'nyad uktam //
iti parabrahmasvarūpaviśeṣanirṇayāyaiva pravṛttam /

children.text:
itihāsa-purāṇeṣu ca sṛṣṭi-sthiti-pralaya-prakaraṇayor idam eva para-tattvam ity avagamyate / yathā mahā-bhārate ---
kutaḥ sṛṣṭam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagat-sthāvara-jaṅgamam /
pralaye ca kam abhyeti tan to brūhi pitāmaha //
iti pṛṣṭo ---
nārāyaṇo jagan-mūrtir ananta-ātmā sanātana /
ity-ādi ca vadati ---
ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā mahā-bhūtāni dhātavaḥ /
jaṅgama-ajaṅgamaṃ ca idaṃ jagan-nārāyaṇa-udbhavam //
iti ca / prācya-udīcya-dākṣiṇātya-pāścātya-sarva-śiṣṭaiḥ sarva-dharma-sarva-tattva-vyavasthāyām idam eva paryāptam ity avigāna-parigṛhītaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca purāṇaṃ janma-ādy asya yata iti jagaj-janma-ādi-kāraṇaṃ brahma ity avagamyate / taj-janma-ādi-kāraṇaṃ kim iti praśna-pūrvakaṃ viṣṇoḥ sakāśād bhūtam ity-ādinā brahma-sva-rūpa-viśeṣa-pratipādana-eka-paratayā pravṛttam iti sarva-saṃmatam / tathā tatra eva ---
prakṛtir yā khyātā vyakta-avyakta-sva-rūpiṇī /
puruṣaś ca+py ubhāv etau līyete parama-ātmani //
parama-ātmā ca sarveṣām ādhāraḥ parama-īśvaraḥ /
viṣṇu-nāmā sa vedeṣu vedānteṣu ca gīyate //
iti / sarva-veda-vedānteṣu sarvaiḥ śabdaiḥ parama-kāraṇataya āyam eva gīyata ity-arthaḥ / yathā sarvāsu ṣrutiṣu kevala-para-brahma-sva-rūpa-viśeṣa-pratipādanāya eva pravṛtto nārāyaṇa-anuvākas tatha īdaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca purāṇam ---
so 'ham icchāmi dharma-jña śrotuṃ tvatto yathā jagat /
babhūva bhūyaś ca yathā mahā-bhāga bhaviṣyati //
yan-mayaṃ ca jagad-brahmany ataś ca etac-cara-acaram /
līnam āsīd yathā yatra layam eṣyati yatra ca //
iti paraṃ brahma kim iti prakramya ---
viṣṇoḥ sakāśād udbhūtaṃ jagat tatra eva ca sthitam /
sthiti-saṃyama-karta āsau jagato 'sya jagac ca saḥ //
paraḥ parāṇāṃ paramaḥ parama-ātma-ātma-saṃsthitaḥ /
rūpa-varṇa-ādi-nirdeśa-viśeṣaṇa-vivarjitaḥ //
apakṣaya-vināśābhyāṃ pariṇāma-rddhi-janmabhiḥ /
varjitaḥ śakyate vaktuṃ yaḥ sad asti iti kevalam //
sarvatra asau samastaṃ ca vasaty atra iti vai yataḥ /
tataḥ sa vāsudeva iti vidvadbhiḥ paripaṭhyate //
tad-brahma paraṃ nityam ajam akṣayam avyayam /
eka-sva-rūpaṃ ca sadā heya-abhāvāc ca nirmalam //
tad eva sarvam eva etad-vyakta-avyakta-sva-rūpavat /
tathā puruṣa-rūpeṇa kāla-rūpeṇa ca sthitam //
sa sarva-bhūta-prakṛtiṃ vikārān guṇa-ādi-doṣāṃś ca mune vyatītaḥ /
atīta-sarva-āvaraṇo 'khila-ātmā tena astṛtaṃ yad bhuvana-antarāle //
samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ātmako 'sau sva-śakti-leśa-uddhṛta-bhūta-vargaḥ /
icchā-gṛhīta-abhimata-uru-dehaḥ saṃsādhita-aśeṣa-jagad-dhito 'sau //
tejo-bala-aiśvarya-mahā-avabodha-suvīrya-śakty-ādi-guṇa-eka-rāśiḥ /
paraḥ parāṇāṃ sakalā na yatra kleśa-ādayaḥ santi para-avara-īśe //
sa īśvaro vyaṣṭi-samaṣṭi-rūpo 'vyakta-sva-rūpaḥ prakaṭa-sva-rūpaḥ /
sarva-īśvaraḥ sarva-dṛk-sarva-vettā samasta-śaktiḥ parama-īśvara-ākhyaḥ //
saṃjñāyate yena tad asta-doṣaṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ nirmalam eka-rūpam /
saṃdṛśyate va āpy adhigamyate vā taj-jñānam ajñānam ato 'nyad uktam //
iti para-brahma-sva-rūpa-viśeṣa-nirṇayāya eva pravṛttam /

body.text: anyāni sarvāṇi purāṇāny etadavirodhena neyāni / anyaparatvaṃ ca tattadārambhaprakārair avagamyate / sarvātmanā viruddhāṃśas tāmasatvād anādaraṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: All other <s>Purāṇas</s> should be interpreted in a manner consistent with this [Viṣṇu Purāṇa]. That they have other primary subjects is understood from the manner of their commencement. Those portions that are entirely contradictory should be disregarded, being of a <s>tāmasa</s> character.

children.text: anyāni sarvāṇi purāṇāny etad-avirodhena neyāni / anya-paratvaṃ ca tat-tad-ārambha-prakārair avagamyate / sarva-ātmanā viruddha-aṃśas tāmasatvād anādaraṇīyaḥ /

body.text:
nanv asminn api --
sṛṣṭisthityantakaraṇīṃ brahmaviṣnuśivātmikāṃ /
sa saṃjñā yāti bhagavān eka janārdanaḥ //
iti trimūrtosāmyaṃ pratīyate / naitad evam / eka eva janārdana iti jana ardanasyaiva brahmaśivādikṛtsnaprapañcatādātmyaṃ vidhīyate / jagac ca sa iti pūrvoktam eva vivṛṇoti -- sraṣṭā sṛjati cātmānaṃ viṣṇuḥ pālyaṃ ca pāti ca /
upasaṃhriyate cānte saṃhartā ca svatyaṃprabhuḥ //
iti ca sraṣṭṛtvenāvasthitaṃ brahmaṇaṃ sṛjyaṃ ca saṃhartāraṃ saṃhāryaṃ ca yugapan nirdiśya sarvasya viṣṇutādātmyopadeśāt sṛjyasaṃhāryabhūtād vastunaḥ sraṣṭṛsaṃhartror janārdanavibhūtitvena viśeṣo dṛśyate / janārdanaviṣṇuśabdayoḥ paryāyatvena brahmaviṣṇuśivātmikām iti vibhūtim / ata eva svecchayā līlārthaṃ vibhūtyantarbhāva ucyate / yathedam anantaram evocyate --
pṛthivyāpas tathā tejo vāyur ākāśa eva ca /
sarvendriyāntaḥkaraṇaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ hi yaj jagat //
sa eva sarvabhūtātmā viśvarūpo yato 'vyayaḥ /
sargādikaṃ tato 'syaiva bhūtastham upakārakam //
sa eva sṛjyaḥ sa ca sarvakartā sa eva pātyatti ca pālyate ca /
brahmādyavasthābhir aśeṣamūrtir viṣṇur variṣṭho varado vareṇyaḥ // iti /
body.translated_text:
Now, even in this [Viṣṇu Purāṇa] —
'He who performs the function of creation, sustenance, and dissolution, assuming the forms of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> — the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s> alone takes those designations' —
the equality of the three forms (<s>trimūrti</s>) appears to be conveyed. This is not so. By saying 'the one <s>Janārdana</s> alone,' the identity of <s>Janārdana</s> alone — who is the agitator of people — with the entire phenomenal world including <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and all else is being taught. It elaborates on what was stated earlier — 'and He is the world itself' — as follows:
'<s>Viṣṇu</s> the creator creates Himself; and He the protector protects what is to be protected; and at the end, the destroyer, the self-sovereign, withdraws [all].'
By simultaneously designating <s>Brahmā</s>, who is established as the creator, as also the created, and the destroyer as also the destroyed, a distinction is shown from the Viṣṇu-identity teaching of everything: <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śiva</s>, being entities that are created and destroyed, differ from <s>Janārdana</s> in being His sovereign manifestations (<s>vibhūtis</s>). Since the words <s>Janārdana</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> are synonymous, [the phrase] 'assuming the forms of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>' refers to [His] <s>vibhūti</s>. For this very reason, it is said that His inclusion within [His own] <s>vibhūti</s> is by His own will, for the sake of play (<s>līlā</s>). As stated immediately after:
'Earth, water, fire, wind, space, all the senses, the inner organ, and the world called <s>Puruṣa</s> —
He alone is the Self of all beings, of universal form, since He is imperishable; therefore the creation and the rest of this [world], being situated within Him, serve Him;
He alone is the created, He is the creator of all; He alone is protected and He is the protector; through the states of <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest, [He is] of all forms — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the most excellent, the bestower of boons, the most worthy.'

sa saṃjñā yāti bhagavān eka jana-ardanaḥ //
iti tri-mūrto-sāmyaṃ pratīyate / na etad evam / eka eva jana-ardana iti jana ardanasya eva brahma-śiva-ādi-kṛtsna-prapañca-tādātmyaṃ vidhīyate / jagac ca sa iti pūrva-uktam eva vivṛṇoti --- sraṣṭā sṛjati cā atmānaṃ viṣṇuḥ pālyaṃ ca pāti ca /

body.text:
atra sāmānādhikaraṇyanirdiṣṭaṃ heyamiśraprapañcatādātmyaṃ niravadyasya nirvikārasya samastakalyāṇaguṇātmakasya brahmaṇaḥ katham upapadyata ity āśaṅkhya sa eva sarvabhūtātmā viśvarūpo yato 'vyaya iti svayam evopapādayati / sa eva sarveśvaraḥ parabrahmabhūto viṣṇur eva sarvaṃ jagad iti pratijñāya sarvabhūtātmā viśvarūpo yato 'vyaya iti hetur uktaḥ / sarvabhūtānām ayam ātmā viśvaśarīro yato 'vyaya ityarthaḥ / vakṣyati ca -- satsarvaṃ vai hares tanur iti /
etad uktaṃ bhavati / asyāvyayasyāpi parasya brahmaṇo viṣṇor viśvaśarīratayā tādātmyaviruddham ity ātmaśarīrayoś ca svabhāvā vyavasthitā eva / evaṃbhūtasya sarveśvarasya viṣṇoḥ prapañcāntarbhūtaniyāmyakoṭiniviṣṭabrahmādidevatiryaṅmanuṣyeṣu tat tat samāśrayaṇīyatvāya svecchāvatāraḥ pūrvoktaḥ / tad etad brahmādīnāṃ bhāvanātrayānvayena karmavaśyatvaṃ bhagavataḥ parabrahmabhūtasya vāsudevasya nikhilajagadupakārāya svecchayā svenaiva rūpeṇa devādiṣv avatāra iti ca ṣaṣṭe 'ṃśe śubhāśrayaprakaraṇe suvyaktam uktam / asya devādirūpeṇāvatāreṣv api na prākṛto deha iti mahābhārate -- na bhūtasaṃghasaṃsthāno deho 'sya paramātmanaḥ / iti pratipāditaḥ / śrutibhiś ca -- ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate -- tasya dhīrāḥ parijānanti
yonim iti / karmavaśyānāṃ brahmādīnām anicchatām api tattatkarmānuguṇaprakṛtipariṇāmarūpabhūtasaṃghasaṃsthānaviśeṣadevādiśarīrapraveśarūpaṃ janmāvarjanīyam / ayaṃ tu sarveśvaraḥ satyasaṃkalpo bhagavān evaṃbhūtaśubhetarajanmākurvann api svecchayā svenaiva niratiśayakalyāṇarūpeṇa devādiṣu jagadupakārāya bahudhā jāyate, tasyaitasya śubhetarajanmākurvato 'pi svakalyāṇaguṇānantyena bahudhā yoniṃ bahuvidhajanma dhīrādhīramatām agresarā jānantītyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Here, objecting how the coordination (expressed through grammatical co-reference) of the defect-mixed phenomenal world as identical with <s>Brahman</s> — who is free from fault, changeless, and whose nature consists of all auspicious qualities — is possible, [the text] itself resolves this: 'He alone is the Self of all beings, of universal form, since He is imperishable.' Having proposed that He alone, the Supreme Lord, who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is the entire world, the reason is stated: 'He is the Self of all beings, of universal form, since He is imperishable.' The meaning is: He is the Self of all beings, having the universe as His body, since He is imperishable. As it will be said later: 'Indeed, all that exists is the body of <s>Hari</s>.'
This is what has been stated: Even though this Supreme <s>Brahman</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> is imperishable, His identity with [the world] through having the universe as His body is not contradicted — the natures of the Self and the body are indeed well-established [as distinct]. For such a Lord of all, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, His voluntary descent (<s>avatāra</s>) into the gods, animals, humans, and other beings — who are included within the phenomenal world as the class of entities controlled [by Him] — including <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods, for the purpose of being worthy of being sought as refuge, has been described earlier. This — that <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods are subject to <s>karma</s> through the triple mode of existence, while the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, incarnates by His own will in His own form among gods and others for the benefit of the entire world — is clearly stated in the sixth book, in the section on the auspicious abode (<s>śubhāśraya</s>). That even in His <s>avatāras</s> in the forms of gods and others, His body is not material (<s>prākṛta</s>) — this is established in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>: 'The body of this Supreme Self is not composed of material elements.' And by the <s>śrutis</s>: 'Though unborn, He is born in many ways — the wise know His source.' For <s>Brahmā</s> and others, who are subject to <s>karma</s>, birth in the form of entry into specific bodies of gods and others — which are particular configurations of material elements that are transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s> corresponding to their respective <s>karmas</s> — is unavoidable even against their will. But this Lord of all, the Blessed One of true resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>), though not undergoing birth of the auspicious-or-otherwise kind, is born in many ways by His own will, in His own unsurpassable auspicious form, among gods and others for the benefit of the world; and the meaning is that those who are the foremost among the wise and discerning know the source — the manifold birth — of Him who does not undergo birth of the ordinary kind, by virtue of the infinity of His own auspicious qualities.

children.text:
atra sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdiṣṭaṃ heya-miśra-prapañca-tādātmyaṃ niravadyasya nirvikārasya samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ātmakasya brahmaṇaḥ katham upapadyata ity āśaṅkhya sa eva sarva-bhūta-ātmā viśva-rūpo yato 'vyaya iti svayam eva upapādayati / sa eva sarva-īśvaraḥ para-brahma-bhūto viṣṇur eva sarvaṃ jagad iti pratijñāya sarva-bhūta-ātmā viśva-rūpo yato 'vyaya iti hetur uktaḥ / sarva-bhūtānām ayam ātmā viśva-śarīro yato 'vyaya ity-arthaḥ / vakṣyati ca --- sat-sarvaṃ vai hares tanur iti /
etad uktaṃ bhavati / asya avyayasya api parasya brahmaṇo viṣṇor viśva-śarīratayā tādātmya-viruddham ity ātma-śarīrayoś ca sva-bhāvā vyavasthitā eva / evaṃ-bhūtasya sarva-īśvarasya viṣṇoḥ prapañca-antarbhūta-niyāmya-koṭi-niviṣṭa-brahma-ādi-deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣyeṣu tat tat samāśrayaṇīyatvāya sva-icchā-avatāraḥ pūrva-uktaḥ / tad etad brahma-ādīnāṃ bhāvanā-traya-anvayena karma-vaśyatvaṃ bhagavataḥ para-brahma-bhūtasya vāsu-devasya nikhila-jagad-upakārāya sva-icchayā svena eva rūpeṇa deva-ādiṣv avatāra iti ca ṣaṣṭe 'ṃśe śubha-āśraya-prakaraṇe suvyaktam uktam / asya deva-ādi-rūpeṇa-avatāreṣv api na prākṛto deha iti mahābhārate --- na bhūta-saṃgha-saṃsthāno deho 'sya parama-ātmanaḥ / iti pratipāditaḥ / śrutibhiś ca --- ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate --- tasya dhīrāḥ parijānanti
yonim iti / karma-vaśyānāṃ brahma-ādīnām anicchatām api tat-tat-karma-anuguṇa-prakṛti-pariṇāma-rūpa-bhūta-saṃgha-saṃsthāna-viśeṣa-deva-ādi-śarīra-praveśa-rūpaṃ janma avarjanīyam / ayaṃ tu sarva-īśvaraḥ satya-saṃkalpo bhagavān evaṃ-bhūta-śubha-itara-janma akurvann api sva-icchayā svena eva niratiśaya-kalyāṇa-rūpeṇa deva-ādiṣu jagad-upakārāya bahudhā jāyate, tasya etasya śubha-itara-janma akurvato 'pi sva-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ānantyena bahudhā yoniṃ bahu-vidha-janma dhīrā-dhīramatām agresarā jānanti ity-arthaḥ /

body.text: tadetannikhilajagannimittopādānabhūtāj janmādy asya yataḥ -- prakṛtiś ca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhādityādisūtraiḥ pratipāditāt parasmād brahmaṇaḥ paramapuruṣād anyasya kasyacit parataratvaṃ paramataḥ setūn mānasaṃbandhabhedavyapadeśebhya ityāśaṅkya sāmānyāt tu -- buddhyarthaḥ pādavat -- sthānaviśeṣāt prakāśādivat -- upapatteś ca -- tathānyapratiṣedhāt -- anena sarvagatatvamāyām ādiśabdādibhya iti sūtrakāraḥ svayam eva nirākaroti /
body.translated_text: Thus, with respect to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Person, who is both the efficient and material cause of the entire world — established by the <s>Sūtras</s> 'From whom is the origin and the rest of this [universe]' and '<s>Prakṛti</s> too, because there would be no contradiction of the proposition, illustration, and the rest' — anticipating the doubt from other doctrines that something else might be higher, [the objection is raised:] 'the barriers, on account of the differences of connection, relation, and designation.' The <s>Sūtrakāra</s> himself refutes this through [the sūtras]: 'But on account of the general [teaching]' — 'For the sake of the intellect, like feet' — 'On account of the specific position, like light and the rest' — 'And because it is logically established' — 'And because of the negation of anything else' — 'By this, omnipresence, appearance — from the word "ādi" and the rest.'

children.text: tad-etan-nikhila-jagan-nimitta-upādāna-bhūtāj janma-ādy asya yataḥ --- prakṛtiś ca pratijñā-dṛṣṭānta-anuparodha-āditya-ādi-sūtraiḥ pratipāditāt parasmād brahmaṇaḥ parama-puruṣād anyasya kasyacit parataratvaṃ para-mataḥ setūn māna-saṃbandha-bheda-vyapadeśebhya ity-āśaṅkya sāmānyāt tu --- buddhy-arthaḥ pādavat --- sthāna-viśeṣāt prakāśa-ādivat --- upapatteś ca --- tatha ānya-pratiṣedhāt --- anena sarva-gatatva-māyām ādi-śabda-ādibhya iti sūtra-kāraḥ svayam eva nirākaroti /

body.text:
mānave ca śāstre --
prādurāsīt tamonudaḥ sisṛkṣur vividhāḥ prajāḥ /
apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryam apāsṛjat //
tasmiñ jajñe svayaṃ brahma
iti brahmaṇo janmaśravaṇāt kṣetrajñatvam evāvagamyate / tathā ca sraṣṭuḥ paramapuruṣasya tadvisṛṣṭasya ca brahmaṇaḥ
ayaṃ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tadvisṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣo loke brahmeti kīrtyate //
iti nāmanirdeśāc ca / tathā ca vaiṣṇave purāṇe hiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ bhāvanātrayānvayād aśuddhatvena śubhāśrayatvānarhatopapādanāt kṣetrajñatvaṃ niścīyate /
body.translated_text:
And in the <s>Mānava Śāstra</s> (Code of <s>Manu</s>):
'The dispeller of darkness manifested, desiring to create the various beings;
He first created the waters, and into them discharged his potency.
In that [water] <s>Brahmā</s> was born of himself.'
From the hearing of <s>Brahmā</s>'s birth, his <s>kṣetrajña</s>-status (status as an embodied soul) alone is understood. And thus, by the designation of names for the creating Supreme Person and for <s>Brahmā</s> who was created by him:
'He is his; those [waters] were formerly [his]; hence he is known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
The <s>Puruṣa</s> created by him is celebrated in the world as <s>Brahmā</s>.'
And in the <s>Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa</s> (Viṣṇu Purāṇa), because it is demonstrated that <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and the others — being connected with the three states of existence (<s>bhāvatraya</s>) — are impure and therefore unfit to be the repository of auspiciousness, their <s>kṣetrajña</s>-status (status as embodied souls) is ascertained.

prādur-āsīt tamonudaḥ sisṛkṣur vividhāḥ prajāḥ /
apa eva sasarjā adau tāsu vīryam apa asṛjat //
tasmiñ jajñe svayaṃ brahma
iti brahmaṇo janma-śravaṇāt kṣetra-jñatvam eva avagamyate / tathā ca sraṣṭuḥ parama-puruṣasya tad-visṛṣṭasya ca brahmaṇaḥ

body.text:
yad api kaiścid uktam -- sarvasya śabdajātasya vidhyarthavādamantrarūpasya
kāryābhidhāyitvenaiva prāmāṇyaṃ varṇanīyam / vyavahārād anyatra śabdasya bodhakatvaśaktyavadhāraṇāsaṃbhavād vyavahārasya ca kāryabuddhimūlatvāt kāryarūpa eva śabdārthaḥ / na pariniṣpanne vastuni śabdaḥ pramāṇam iti / atrocyate / pravartakavākyavyavahāra eva śabdānām arthabodhakatvaśaktyavadhāraṇaṃ kartavyam iti kim iyaṃ rājājñā / siddhavastuṣu śabdasya bodhakatvaśaktigrahaṇam atyantasukaram / tathā hi -- kenacid dhastaceṣṭādināpavarake daṇḍaḥ sthita iti devadattāya jñāpayeti preṣitaḥ kaścit tajjñāpane pravṛtto 'pavarake daṇḍaḥ sthita iti śabdaṃ prayuṅkte / mūkavad dhastaceṣṭām imāṃ jānan pārśvastho 'nyaḥ prāgvyutpanno 'pi tasyārthasya bodhanāyāpavarake daṇḍaḥ sthita ityasya śabdasya prayogadarśanād asyārthasyāyaṃ śabdo
bodhaka iti jānātīti kim atra duṣkaram / tathā bālas tāto 'yam iyaṃ mātāyaṃ mātulo 'yaṃ manuṣyo 'yaṃ mṛgaś candro 'yam ayaṃ ca sarpa iti mātāpitṛprabhṛtibhiḥ śabdaiḥ śanaiḥ śanair aṅgulyā nirdeśane tatra tatra bahuśaḥ śikṣitas tair eva śabdais teṣv artheṣu svātmanaś ca buddhyutpattiṃ dṛṣṭvā teṣv artheṣu teṣāṃ śabdānām aṅgulyā nirdeśapūrvakaḥ prayogaḥ sambandhāntarābhāvāt saṃketayitṛpuruṣājñānāc ca bodhakatvanibandhana iti krameṇa niścitya punar apy asya śabdasyāyam artha iti pūrvavṛddhaiḥ śikṣitaḥ sarvaśabdānām artham avagamya svayam api sarvaṃ vākyajātaṃ prayuṅkte / evam eva sarvapadānāṃ svārthābhidhāyitvaṃ saṃghātaviśeṣaṇāṃ ca yathāvasthitasaṃsargaviśeṣavācitvaṃ ca jānātīti kāryārthaiva
vyuttipattir ityādinirbandho nirbandhanaḥ / ataḥ pariṣpannaḥ vastuni śabdasyabodhakatvaśaktyavadhāraṇāt sarvāṇi vedāntavākyāni sakalajagatkāraṇaṃ sarvakalyāṇaguṇākaramuktalakṣaṇaṃ brahma bodhayanty eva /
body.translated_text: As for what has been stated by some — that the validity of all classes of verbal expression, whether in the form of injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>), explanatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>), or <s>mantras</s>, is to be explained solely through their capacity to denote something to be done (<s>kārya</s>); that outside of practical usage it is impossible to ascertain the denotative capacity of words; and that since practical usage is rooted in the cognition of something to be done, the meaning of words is of the nature of action alone; and that words are not a valid means of knowledge regarding an already established reality — to this we reply: Is it a royal decree that the denotative capacity of words must be ascertained only in the context of injunctive sentences? The ascertainment of the denotative capacity of words regarding established realities is exceedingly easy. For example: someone is sent by another — through gestures of the hand and the like — to inform <s>Devadatta</s> that 'a stick is placed in the closet.' That person, engaged in conveying the information, utters the words 'a stick is placed in the closet.' Another person standing nearby, who already has prior linguistic competence, knowing this gesture as one would a mute person's, upon seeing the use of the words 'a stick is placed in the closet' for conveying that very meaning, understands that 'this word is the denoter of this meaning' — what difficulty is there in this? Similarly, a child, being taught gradually by his mother, father, and others, with pointing of the finger, in various instances and repeatedly, with the words 'this is father,' 'this is mother,' 'this is uncle,' 'this is a man,' 'this is a deer,' 'this is the moon,' 'this is a snake' — observing the arising of cognition in himself through those very words regarding those objects, and ascertaining step by step that the use of those words with finger-pointing toward those objects, in the absence of any other relation and in ignorance of any person who established the convention, must be grounded in the denotative capacity [of the words] — and then, being further taught by elders that 'this word has this meaning,' comprehends the meanings of all words and himself employs all kinds of sentences. In exactly this way, one understands the denotative capacity of all words for their respective meanings and the capacity of particular combinations [of words] to convey particular relations as they actually obtain. Therefore, the insistence that linguistic competence arises only in the context of action is groundless. Hence, since the denotative capacity of words regarding established realities is ascertained, all <s>Vedānta</s> sentences do indeed teach <s>Brahman</s> — the cause of the entire universe, the mine of all auspicious qualities, characterized by liberation (<s>mukta</s>).

children.text:
yad api kaiścid uktam --- sarvasya śabda-jātasya vidhy-artha-vāda-mantra-rūpasya
kārya-abhidhāyitvena eva prāmāṇyaṃ varṇanīyam / vyavahārād anyatra śabdasya bodhakatva-śakty-avadhāraṇa-asaṃbhavād vyavahārasya ca kārya-buddhi-mūlatvāt kārya-rūpa eva śabda-arthaḥ / na pariniṣpanne vastuni śabdaḥ pramāṇam iti / atra ucyate / pravartaka-vākya-vyavahāra eva śabdānām artha-bodhakatva-śakty-avadhāraṇaṃ kartavyam iti kim iyaṃ rāja-ājñā / siddha-vastuṣu śabdasya bodhakatva-śakti-grahaṇam atyanta-sukaram / tathā hi --- kenacid dhasta-ceṣṭā-ādina āpavarake daṇḍaḥ sthita iti deva-dattāya jñāpaya iti preṣitaḥ kaścit taj-jñāpane pravṛtto 'pavarake daṇḍaḥ sthita iti śabdaṃ prayuṅkte / mūkavad dhasta-ceṣṭām imāṃ jānan pārśva-stho 'nyaḥ prāg-vyutpanno 'pi tasya-arthasya bodhanāya-apavarake daṇḍaḥ sthita ity-asya śabdasya prayoga-darśanād asya arthasya ayaṃ śabdo
bodhaka iti jānāti iti kim atra duṣkaram / tathā bālas tāto 'yam iyaṃ māta āyaṃ mātulo 'yaṃ manuṣyo 'yaṃ mṛgaś candro 'yam ayaṃ ca sarpa iti mātā-pitṛ-prabhṛtibhiḥ śabdaiḥ śanaiḥ śanair aṅgulyā nirdeśane tatra tatra bahuśaḥ śikṣitas tair eva śabdais teṣv artheṣu sva-ātmanaś ca buddhy-utpattiṃ dṛṣṭvā teṣv artheṣu teṣāṃ śabdānām aṅgulyā nirdeśa-pūrvakaḥ prayogaḥ sambandha-antara-abhāvāt saṃketayitṛ-puruṣa-ājñānāc ca bodhakatva-nibandhana iti krameṇa niścitya punar apy asya śabdasya ayam artha iti pūrva-vṛddhaiḥ śikṣitaḥ sarva-śabdānām artham avagamya svayam api sarvaṃ vākya-jātaṃ prayuṅkte / evam eva sarva-padānāṃ sva-artha-abhidhāyitvaṃ saṃghāta-viśeṣaṇāṃ ca yathā-avasthita-saṃsarga-viśeṣa-vācitvaṃ ca jānāti iti kārya-artha-eva
vyuttipattir ity-ādi-nirbandho nirbandhanaḥ / ataḥ pariṣpannaḥ vastuni śabdasya-bodhakatva-śakty-avadhāraṇāt sarvāṇi vedānta-vākyāni sakala-jagat-kāraṇaṃ sarva-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ākara-mukta-lakṣaṇaṃ brahma bodhayanty eva /

body.text: api ca kāryārtha eva vyutpattir astu / vedāndavākyāny apy upāsanaviṣayakāryādhikṛtaviśeṣaṇabhūtaphalatvena duḥkhāsaṃbhinnadeśaviśeṣarūpasvargādivad rātrisatrapratiṣṭhānādivad apagoraṇaśatayātanāsādhyasādhanabhāvavac ca karyopayogitayaiva sarvaṃ bodhayanti / tathā+hi -- brahmavid āpnoti param ityatra brahmopāsanaviṣayakāryādhikṛtaviśeṣaṇabhūtaphalatvena brahmaprāptiḥ śrūyate -- paraprāptikāmo brahma vidyād ityatra prāpyatayā pratīyamānaṃ brahmasvarūpaṃ tadviśeṣaṇaṃ ca sarvaṃ kāryopayogitayaiva siddhaṃ bhavati / tadantargatam eva jagatsraṣṭṛtvaṃ saṃhartṛtvam ādhāratvam antarātmatvam ityādy uktam anuktaṃ ca sarvam iti na kiṃcid anupapannam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, let it be granted that linguistic competence arises only in the context of action. Even so, <s>Vedānta</s> sentences teach everything solely through their utility for action — in the same way that the fruit, being a qualifier of the subject qualified by the injunction concerning worship, [is taught] like heaven (<s>svarga</s>) and the like which are specific regions untouched by suffering, like the concluding session of the overnight <s>Soma</s> sacrifice (<s>rātrisattrapratiṣṭhā</s>) and the like, and like the means-end relationship to be accomplished through hundreds of prohibitions and torments. Thus, in 'the knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme,' the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> is heard as the fruit that qualifies the subject qualified by the injunction concerning the worship of <s>Brahman</s>. In 'one who desires the attainment of the supreme should know <s>Brahman</s>,' the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> — apprehended as that which is to be attained — and all its qualifications are established solely through their utility for action. Included within that are the creatorship of the universe, the power of dissolution, the nature of being the support, the nature of being the inner Self, and so forth — both what has been stated and what has not been stated — so nothing whatsoever is untenable.

children.text: api ca kārya-artha eva vyutpattir astu / vedānda-vākyāny apy upāsana-viṣaya-kārya-adhikṛta-viśeṣaṇa-bhūta-phalatvena duḥkha-asaṃbhinna-deśa-viśeṣa-rūpa-svarga-ādivad rātri-satra-pratiṣṭhāna-ādivad apagoraṇa-śata-yātanā-sādhya-sādhana-bhāvavac ca karya-upayogitaya aiva sarvaṃ bodhayanti / tathā+hi --- brahma-vid āpnoti param ity-atra brahma-upāsana-viṣaya-kārya-adhikṛta-viśeṣaṇa-bhūta-phalatvena brahma-prāptiḥ śrūyate --- para-prāpti-kāmo brahma vidyād ity-atra prāpyatayā pratīyamānaṃ brahma-sva-rūpaṃ tad-viśeṣaṇaṃ ca sarvaṃ kārya-upayogitaya aiva siddhaṃ bhavati / tad-antargatam eva jagat-sraṣṭṛtvaṃ saṃhartṛtvam ādhāratvam antarātmatvam ity-ādy uktam anuktaṃ ca sarvam iti na kiṃcid anupapannam /

body.text: evaṃ ca sati mantrārthavādagatā hy aviruddhā apūrvāś cārthāḥ sarve vidhiśeṣatayaiva siddhā bhavanti / yathoktaṃ dramiḍabhāṣye -- ṛṇaṃ hi vai jāyata iti śruter ity upakramya yady apy avadānastutiparaṃ vākyaṃ tathāpi nāsatā stutir upapadyata iti / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- sarvo hy arthavādabhāgo devatārādhanabhūtayāgādeḥ sāṅgasyārādhyadevatāyāś cādṛṣṭarūpān guṇān sahasraśo vadan sahasraśaḥ karmaṇi prāśastyabuddhim utpādayati / teṣām asadbhāve prāśastyabuddhir eva na syād iti karmaṇi prāśastyabuddhyarthaṃ guṇasadbhāvam eva bodhayatīti / anayaiva diśā sarve mantrārthavādāvagatā arthāḥ siddhāḥ /
body.translated_text: This being the case, all meanings derived from <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages) that are non-contradictory and novel are established solely as subsidiary to the injunction. As stated in the <s>Dramiḍa Bhāṣya</s>, beginning with 'for one is born with a debt, according to <s>śruti</s>': 'Even though the sentence is devoted to praising the offering (<s>avadāna</s>), praise through falsehood is not tenable.' What is meant is this: every portion of <s>arthavāda</s>, by stating thousands of unseen qualities of the deity to be propitiated and of the sacrifice together with its auxiliaries that constitutes the propitiation of that deity, generates in thousands of ways an attitude of esteem toward the ritual action. If those [qualities] were non-existent, the attitude of esteem would not arise at all — therefore [the <s>arthavāda</s>] teaches the actual existence of those qualities for the purpose of generating the attitude of esteem toward the ritual action. In exactly this direction, all meanings understood from <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> are established.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati mantra-artha-vāda-gatā hy aviruddhā apūrvāś ca arthāḥ sarve vidhi-śeṣataya aiva siddhā bhavanti / yatha ūktaṃ dramiḍa-bhāṣye --- ṛṇaṃ hi vai jāyata iti śruter ity upakramya yady apy avadāna-stuti-paraṃ vākyaṃ tatha āpi na-asatā stutir upapadyata iti / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- sarvo hy artha-vāda-bhāgo devatā-ārādhana-bhūta-yāga-ādeḥ sāṅgasyā arādhya-devatāyāś ca adṛṣṭa-rūpān guṇān sahasraśo vadan sahasraśaḥ karmaṇi prāśastya-buddhim utpādayati / teṣām asad-bhāve prāśastya-buddhir eva na syād iti karmaṇi prāśastya-buddhy-arthaṃ guṇa-sad-bhāvam eva bodhayati iti / anaya aiva diśā sarve mantra-artha-vāda-avagatā arthāḥ siddhāḥ /

body.text:
api ca kāryavākyārthavādibhiḥ kim idaṃ kāryatvaṃ nāmeti vaktavyam / kṛtibhāvabhāvitā kṛtyuddeśyatā ceti cet / kim idaṃ kṛtyuddeśyatvam / yad adhikṛtya kṛtir vartate tat kṛtyuddeśyatvam iti cet / puruṣavyāpārarūpāyāḥ kṛteḥ ko 'yam adhikāro nāma / yatprāptīcchayā kṛtim utpādayati puruṣaḥ tat kṛtyuddeśyatvam iti ced dhanta tarhīṣṭatvam eva kṛtyuddeśyatvam / athaivaṃ manuṣe iṣṭasyaiva rūpadvayam asti / icchāviṣayatayā sthitiḥ puruṣaprerakatvaṃ ca / tatra prerakatvākāraḥ kṛtyuddeśyatvam iti so 'yaṃ svapakṣābhiniveśakārito vṛthāśramaḥ / tathā hīcchāviṣayatayā pratītasya svaprayatnotpattim antareṇāsiddhir eva prerakatvam / tata eva pravṛtteḥ / icchāyāṃ jātāyām iṣṭasya svaprayatnotpattim antareṇāsiddhiḥ pratīyate cet tataś
cikīrṣā jāyate tataḥ pravartate puruṣa iti tattvavidāṃ prakriyā / tasmād iṣṭasya kṛtyadhīnātmalābhatvātireki kṛtyuddeśyatvaṃ nāma kim pi na dṛṣyate / athocyate -- iṣṭatāhetuś ca puruṣānukūlatā / tatpuruṣānukūlatvaṃ kṛtyuddeśyatvam iti cet / naivam / puruṣānukūlaṃ sukham ity anarthāntaram / tathā puruṣānukūlaṃ duḥkhaparyāyam / ataḥ sukhavyatiriktasya kasyāpi puruṣānukūlatvaṃ na saṃbhavati /
nanu ca duḥkhanivṛtter api sukhavyatiriktāyāḥ puruṣānukūlatā dṛṣṭā / naitat / ātmānukūlaṃ sukham ātmapratikūlaṃ duḥkham iti hi sukhaduḥkhayor vivekaḥ / tatrātmānukūlaṃ sukham iṣṭaṃ bhavati / tatpratikūlaṃ duḥkhaṃ cāniṣṭam / ato duḥkhasaṃyogasyāsahyatayā tannivṛttir apīṣṭā bhavati / tata eveṣṭatāsāmyād anukūlatābhramaḥ / tathā hi -- prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya saṃsāriṇaḥ puruṣasyānukūlasaṃyogaḥ pratikūlasaṃyogaḥ svarūpeṇāvasthitir iti ca tisro 'vasthāḥ / tatra pratikūlasaṃbandhanivṛttiś cānukūlasaṃbandhanivṛttiś ca svarūpeṇāvasthitir eva / tasmāt pratikūlasaṃyoge vartamāne tannivṛttirūpā svarūpeṇāvasthitir apīṣṭā bhavati / tatreṣṭatāsāmyād anukūlatābhramaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, those who maintain that the meaning of sentences is action (<s>kārya</s>) must explain: what exactly is this 'actionability' (<s>kāryatva</s>)? If [they say] it is 'being brought about by effort' and 'being the objective of effort' — then what is this 'being the objective of effort'? If [they say] 'that for the sake of which effort operates is the objective of effort' — then what is this 'being for the sake of' with respect to effort, which is of the nature of a person's activity? If [they say] 'that which a person produces effort desiring to attain — that is being the objective of effort' — well then, 'being the objective of effort' is nothing but desirability (<s>iṣṭatva</s>). Now, in the case of what is desired by a human being, there are two aspects: its status as an object of desire, and its capacity to motivate the person. Of these, if the 'motivating aspect' is [what is meant by] 'being the objective of effort,' then this is a futile labor born of attachment to one's own position. For the 'motivating capacity' of that which is apprehended as an object of desire is nothing but its being unattainable without one's own effort — and it is from that very [recognition] that activity arises. When desire has arisen and the unattainability of the desired [object] without one's own effort is apprehended, then the will to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>) arises, and then the person acts — such is the analysis of those who know reality. Therefore, no 'being the objective of effort' is seen that is anything beyond the desired [object's] dependence on effort for its attainment. Now if it is said: the cause of desirability is agreeableness to the person (<s>puruṣānukūlatā</s>), and that 'agreeableness to the person' is what constitutes 'being the objective of effort' — this is not so. 'That which is agreeable to the person' is pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) — this is not a different thing. Likewise, 'that which is disagreeable to the person' is a synonym of pain (<s>duḥkha</s>). Therefore, agreeableness to the person is not possible for anything other than pleasure.
Now, [one may object:] the cessation of pain too, which is different from pleasure, is seen to be agreeable to the person. Not so. 'That which is agreeable to the self is pleasure; that which is disagreeable to the self is pain' — this indeed is the distinction between pleasure and pain. Of these, pleasure, being agreeable to the self, is desired; and pain, being disagreeable to it, is undesired. Therefore, since the conjunction with pain is unbearable, the cessation of that [pain] too is desired. It is precisely because of this similarity in desirability that there arises the illusion of agreeableness [in the cessation of pain]. For a person in contact with <s>prakṛti</s> and caught in <s>saṃsāra</s>, there are three states: conjunction with what is agreeable, conjunction with what is disagreeable, and abiding in one's own nature. Of these, both the cessation of disagreeable conjunction and the cessation of agreeable conjunction are [forms of] abiding in one's own nature. Therefore, when one is in a state of disagreeable conjunction, abiding in one's own nature in the form of the cessation of that [disagreeable conjunction] is also desired. The illusion of agreeableness there is due to the similarity in desirability.
