body.text:
ataḥ sukharūpatvād anukūlatāyāḥ niyogasyānukūlatāṃ vadantaṃ prāmāṇikāḥ parihasanti / iṣṭasyārthaviśeṣasya nivartakatayaiva hi niyogasya niyogatvaṃ sthiratvam apūrvatvaṃ ca pratīyate / svargakāmo yajetety atra kāryasya kriyātiriktā svargakāmapadasamabhivyāhāreṇa svargasādhanatvaniścayād eva bhavanti / na ca vācyaṃ yajetety atra prathamaṃ niyogaḥ svapradhānatayaiva pratīyate svargakāmapadasamabhivyāhārāt svasiddhaye svargasiddhyanukūlatā ca niyogasyeti / yajeteti hi dhātvarthasya puruṣaprayatnasādhyatā pratīyate / svargakāmapadasamabhivyāhārād eva dhātvarthātirekiṇo niyogatvaṃ sthiratvam apūrvatvaṃ cetyādi / tac ca svargasādhanatvapratītinibandhanam / samabhivyāhṛtasvargakāmapadārthānvayayogyaṃ svargasādhanam eva kāryaṃ liṅādayo 'bhidadhatīti lokavyutpattir
api tiraskṛtā / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- samabhivyahṛtapadāntaravācyārthānvayayogyam evetarapadapratipādyam ityanvitābhidhāyipadasaṃghātarūpavākyaśravaṇasaman antaram eva pratīyate / tac ca svargasādhanarūpam / ataḥ kriyāvad ananyārthatāpi virodhād eva parityakteti / ata eva gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau ghoṣaprativāsayogyārthopasthāpanaparatvaṃ gaṅgāpadasyāśrīyate / prathamaṃ gaṅgāpadena gaṅgārthaḥ smṛta iti gaṅgāpadārthasya peyatvaṃ na vākyārthānvayībhavati / evam atra api yajetetyetāvanmātraśravaṇe kāryam ananyārthaṃ smṛtam iti vākyārthānvayasamaye kāryasyānanyārthatā nāvatiṣṭhate / kāryābhidhāyipadaśravaṇavelāyāṃ prathamaṃ kāryam ananyārthaṃ pratītam ity etad api na saṃgacchate / vyutpattikāle gavānayanādikriyāyā duḥkharūpāyā
iṣṭaviśeṣasādhanatayaiva kāryatāpratīteḥ / ato niyogasya puruṣānukūlatvaṃ sarvalokaviruddhaṃ niyogasya sukharūpapuruṣānukūlatāṃ vadataḥ svānubhavavirodhaś ca / karīryā vṛṣṭikāmo yajeytetyādiṣu siddhe 'pi niyoge vṛṣṭyādisiddhinimittasya vṛṣṭivyatirekeṇa niyogasyānukūlatā nānubhūyate / yady apy asmiñ janmani vṛṣṭyādisiddher aniyamas tathāpy aniyamād eva niyogasiddhir avaśyāśrayaṇīyā / tasminn anukūlatāparyāyasukhānubhūtir na dṛśyate / evam uktarītyā kṛtisādhyeṣṭatvātireki kṛtyuddeśyatvaṃ na dṛśyate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, since <s>anukūlatā</s> (agreeableness) is of the nature of pleasure, the authorities ridicule one who asserts the <s>anukūlatā</s> of <s>niyoga</s> (injunctive obligation). For the <s>niyogatva</s> (nature of being an injunction), permanence, and <s>apūrvatva</s> (transcendental potency) of <s>niyoga</s> are understood only through its being the means of bringing about a desired particular object. In the injunction "<s>svargakāmo yajeta</s>" ("one who desires heaven should sacrifice"), the fact that what is to be done (<s>kārya</s>) is something beyond the mere action, its being a means to heaven, is established precisely through the co-occurrence with the word <s>svargakāma</s> ("desirer of heaven"). Nor should it be said that in "<s>yajeta</s>" ("one should sacrifice"), <s>niyoga</s> is first apprehended as having itself as its own principal purpose, and that through co-occurrence with the word <s>svargakāma</s>, the <s>niyoga</s>'s agreeableness consists in being conducive to the attainment of heaven for the sake of its own fulfillment. For in "<s>yajeta</s>," what is understood is that the meaning of the verbal root is accomplishable through human effort. It is only from the co-occurrence with the word <s>svargakāma</s> that the <s>niyogatva</s>, permanence, <s>apūrvatva</s>, and so forth of something over and above the meaning of the verbal root are understood, and that understanding is grounded in the cognition of its being a means to heaven. The ordinary linguistic convention is also thereby set aside, namely that what the <s>liṅ</s> (optative suffix) and similar forms denote is precisely <s>kārya</s> (what is to be done) as a means to heaven, fit for syntactic connection with the meaning of the co-occurring word <s>svargakāma</s>. What this amounts to is the following: the meaning conveyed by one word is understood as precisely that which is fit for syntactic connection with the meaning expressed by the other co-occurring words — this is apprehended immediately upon hearing the sentence, which is a collection of words each denoting their meanings as already connected (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>, related denotation). And that meaning is of the nature of being a means to heaven. Therefore, just as with action, the notion of self-sufficiency (<s>ananyārthatā</s>, not being for the sake of something else) is also abandoned precisely because of contradiction. For this very reason, in expressions like "a village on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>," the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> is understood as having the purpose of presenting a meaning fit for being a suitable dwelling-place for the village — not that the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> first brings to mind the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> herself, whose drinkability then fails to enter into the sentence-meaning. Similarly here too, when merely hearing "<s>yajeta</s>," even if <s>kārya</s> as self-sufficient is recalled, at the time of determining the sentence-meaning, the self-sufficiency of <s>kārya</s> does not stand. Even the claim that at the moment of hearing the word denoting <s>kārya</s>, <s>kārya</s> is first apprehended as self-sufficient — this too does not hold, because at the time of learning linguistic convention, the <s>kāryatā</s> (obligatoriness) of actions such as fetching cows, which are of the nature of pain, is apprehended only as being a means to a desired particular end. Therefore, the agreeableness of <s>niyoga</s> to the person contradicts all common experience, and one who asserts that <s>niyoga</s> has an agreeableness to the person that is of the nature of pleasure contradicts even one's own experience. In injunctions such as "one desiring rain should perform the <s>karīrī</s> sacrifice (<s>karīryā vṛṣṭikāmo yajeta</s>)," even when the <s>niyoga</s> is established, one does not experience any agreeableness of <s>niyoga</s> apart from rain, which is the cause of the attainment of rain and similar results. Even if the attainment of rain and such results is not fixed in this very lifetime, it is precisely from that unfixedness that the establishment of <s>niyoga</s> follows. For a person who recognizes that the <s>niyoga</s> has yielded an unfixed particular result, with a surplus of reverence produced by the certainty of its being a means to the desired end, having turned away from the experience of sense objects, overwhelmed by an excess of delight, joy, and rapture — he undertakes and performs that very <s>kārya</s>. Thus, even when one is impelled by desire for another's sake in the teaching of <s>kārya</s> as <s>niyoga</s>, the <s>kāryatva</s> of <s>niyoga</s> arises from the understanding that it is for that purpose. And thus, from the understanding of the <s>kāryatā</s> of the <s>karīrī</s> sacrifice as a means to rain for the person qualified by the desire for rain, the <s>niyoga</s> is <s>kārya</s> — this is its <s>kāryatva</s>. There is no agreeableness of <s>niyoga</s> here. On the ground where there is no experience of being a means to rain, the claim that even when <s>niyoga</s> is established, action proceeds from <s>niyoga</s> alone is difficult to sustain. As for the others, those <s>Bhāṭṭas</s> — for them the <s>niyoga</s> is subordinate to another (<s>anyaśeṣatva</s>), being a secondary vital force; the result is desired (<s>kāmya</s>); activity proceeds from desire; and results such as heaven from sacrifices and the like are as prescribed by the <s>Veda</s> — all this stands in accordance with experience.

ataḥ sukha-rūpatvād anukūlatāyāḥ niyogasya anukūlatāṃ vadantaṃ prāmāṇikāḥ parihasanti / iṣṭasya artha-viśeṣasya nivartakataya aiva hi niyogasya niyogatvaṃ sthiratvam apūrvatvaṃ ca pratīyate / svarga-kāmo yajeta ity atra kāryasya kriyā-atiriktā svarga-kāma-pada-samabhivyāhāreṇa svarga-sādhanatva-niścayād eva bhavanti / na ca vācyaṃ yajeta ity atra prathamaṃ niyogaḥ sva-pradhānataya aiva pratīyate svarga-kāma-pada-samabhivyāhārāt sva-siddhaye svarga-siddhy-anukūlatā ca niyogasya iti / yajeta iti hi dhātv-arthasya puruṣa-prayatna-sādhyatā pratīyate / svarga-kāma-pada-samabhivyāhārād eva dhātv-artha-atirekiṇo niyogatvaṃ sthiratvam apūrvatvaṃ ca ity-ādi / tac ca svarga-sādhanatva-pratīti-nibandhanam / samabhivyāhṛta-svarga-kāma-pada-artha-anvaya-yogyaṃ svarga-sādhanam eva kāryaṃ liṅ-ādayo 'bhidadhati iti loka-vyutpattir
api tiraskṛtā / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- samabhivyahṛta-pada-antara-vācya-artha-anvaya-yogyam eva itara-pada-pratipādyam ity-anvita-abhidhāyi-pada-saṃghāta-rūpa-vākya-śravaṇa-saman antaram eva pratīyate / tac ca svarga-sādhana-rūpam / ataḥ kriyāvad ananya-arthata āpi virodhād eva parityakta īti / ata eva gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ity-ādau ghoṣa-prativāsa-yogya-artha-upasthāpana-paratvaṃ gaṅgā-padasyā aśrīyate / prathamaṃ gaṅgā-padena gaṅgā-arthaḥ smṛta iti gaṅgā-pada-arthasya peyatvaṃ na vākya-artha-anvayībhavati / evam atra api yajeta ity-etāvan-mātra-śravaṇe kāryam ananya-arthaṃ smṛtam iti vākya-artha-anvaya-samaye kāryasya ananya-arthatā na avatiṣṭhate / kārya-abhidhāyi-pada-śravaṇa-velāyāṃ prathamaṃ kāryam ananya-arthaṃ pratītam ity etad api na saṃgacchate / vyutpatti-kāle gava-ānayana-ādi-kriyāyā duḥkha-rūpāyā
iṣṭa-viśeṣa-sādhanataya aiva kāryatā-pratīteḥ / ato niyogasya puruṣa-anukūlatvaṃ sarva-loka-viruddhaṃ niyogasya sukha-rūpa-puruṣa-anukūlatāṃ vadataḥ sva-anubhava-virodhaś ca / karīryā vṛṣṭi-kāmo yajeyta ity-ādiṣu siddhe 'pi niyoge vṛṣṭy-ādi-siddhi-nimittasya vṛṣṭi-vyatirekeṇa niyogasya anukūlatā na anubhūyate / yady apy asmiñ janmani vṛṣṭy-ādi-siddher aniyamas tatha āpy aniyamād eva niyoga-siddhir avaśya-āśrayaṇīyā / tasminn anukūlatā-paryāya-sukha-anubhūtir na dṛśyate / evam ukta-rītyā kṛti-sādhya-iṣṭatva-atireki kṛty-uddeśyatvaṃ na dṛśyate /

body.text:
kṛtiṃ prati śeṣitvaṃ kṛtyuddeśyatvam iti cet / kim idaṃ śeṣitvaṃ kiṃ ca śeṣatvam iti vaktavyam / kāryaṃ prati saṃbandhī śeṣaḥ / tatpratisaṃbandhitvaṃ śeṣitvam iti cet / evaṃ tarhi kāryatvam eva śeṣitvam ity uktaṃ bhavati / kāryatvam eva vicāryate / paroddeśapravṛttakṛtivyāptyarhatvam śeṣatvam iti cet / ko 'yaṃ paroddeśo nāmeti / ayam eva hi vicāryate / uddeśyatvaṃ nāmepsitatvasādhyatvam iti cet / kim idam īpsitatvam / kṛtiprayojanatvam iti cet puruṣasya kṛtyārambhaprayojanam eva hi kṛtiprayojanam / sa cecchāviṣayaḥ kṛtyadhīnātmalābha iti pūrvokta eva / ayam eva hi sarvatra śeṣaśeṣibhāvaḥ / paragatātiśayādhānecchopādeyatvam eva yasya svarūpaṃ sa śeṣaḥ paraḥ śeṣī / phalotpattīcchayā yāgādes tatprayatnasya copādeyatvaṃ yāgādisiddhīcchayānyat
sarvam upādeyam /
body.translated_text: If it is said that being the principal (<s>śeṣitva</s>) with respect to action means being the purpose for which action is undertaken — then one must explain: what is this <s>śeṣitva</s> (being the principal) and what is <s>śeṣatva</s> (being subordinate)? Is it the relation of cause and effect, or the relation of master and servant? The relation of cause and effect is not what is intended, because it is of the nature of mutual dependence. Nor is it the relation of master and servant. For that relation consists in one's being useful for producing an <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence) in another. The <s>atiśaya</s> that action produces in a person is the accomplishment of that person's purpose. What <s>atiśaya</s> does <s>niyoga</s> produce in a person? It is certainly not the teaching that it is of the nature of pleasure. Nor is it the teaching that it is a means to pleasure. The proponent of the view that <s>niyoga</s> has an agreeableness of the nature of pleasure would not dispute that <s>niyoga</s> is of the nature of pleasure as the locus of enjoyment. And both the claim that <s>niyoga</s> is a means to a desired end has been refuted by you and by this other [opponent] as well. Now, if it is said that action (<s>kṛti</s>) is for the sacrifice, <s>niyoga</s> is for the action, and the result is for the <s>niyoga</s>, and thus the subordination to both (<s>ubhayaśeṣatva</s>) of <s>niyoga</s> produces an <s>atiśaya</s> in the person — then what is this result? If heaven and such are the result of <s>niyoga</s>, then since heaven and such are desired, <s>niyoga</s> is for the sake of heaven — this is yet another subordination of <s>niyoga</s> to something else, and does not constitute the production of <s>atiśaya</s> in the person.

children.text:
kṛtiṃ prati śeṣitvaṃ kṛty-uddeśyatvam iti cet / kim idaṃ śeṣitvaṃ kiṃ ca śeṣatvam iti vaktavyam / kāryaṃ prati saṃbandhī śeṣaḥ / tat-pratisaṃbandhitvaṃ śeṣitvam iti cet / evaṃ tarhi kāryatvam eva śeṣitvam ity uktaṃ bhavati / kāryatvam eva vicāryate / para-uddeśa-pravṛtta-kṛti-vyāpty-arhatvam śeṣatvam iti cet / ko 'yaṃ para-uddeśo nāma iti / ayam eva hi vicāryate / uddeśyatvaṃ nāmā ipsitatva-sādhyatvam iti cet / kim idam īpsitatvam / kṛti-prayojanatvam iti cet puruṣasya kṛty-ārambha-prayojanam eva hi kṛti-prayojanam / sa ca icchā-viṣayaḥ kṛty-adhīna-ātma-lābha iti pūrva-ukta eva / ayam eva hi sarvatra śeṣa-śeṣi-bhāvaḥ / para-gata-atiśaya-ādhāna-icchā-upādeyatvam eva yasya sva-rūpaṃ sa śeṣaḥ paraḥ śeṣī / phala-utpatti-icchayā yāga-ādes tat-prayatnasya ca upādeyatvaṃ yāga-ādi-siddhi-icchaya ānyat
sarvam upādeyam /

body.text: evaṃ garbhadāsādīnām api puruṣaviśeṣātiśayādhānopādeyatvam eva svarūpam / evam īśvaragatātiśayādhānecchayopādeyatvam eva cetanācetanātmakasya nityasyānityasya ca sarvasya vastunaḥ svarūpam iti sarvam īśvaraśeṣatvam eva sarvasya ceśvaraḥ śeṣīti sarvasya vaśī sarvasyeśānaḥ patiṃ viśvasyetyādyuktam / kṛtisādhyaṃ pradhānaṃ yat tatkāryam abhidhīyata ity ayam arthaḥ śraddadhāneṣv eva śobhate /
body.translated_text: Thus, even for those born as slaves and the like, their essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) is precisely their being valuable for producing an <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence) in a particular person. Similarly, it will be established that the essential nature of the self (<s>ātman</s>) is precisely its being useful for producing an <s>atiśaya</s> in <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). And this is to be understood together with the relationship of the self as owned and God as owner (<s>ātma-svāmi-bhāva</s>).

children.text: evaṃ garbha-dāsa-ādīnām api puruṣa-viśeṣa-atiśaya-ādhāna-upādeyatvam eva sva-rūpam / evam īśvara-gata-atiśaya-ādhāna-icchaya ūpādeyatvam eva cetana-acetana-ātmakasya nityasya anityasya ca sarvasya vastunaḥ sva-rūpam iti sarvam īśvara-śeṣatvam eva sarvasya cā iśvaraḥ śeṣi īti sarvasya vaśī sarvasyā iśānaḥ patiṃ viśvasya ity-ādy-uktam / kṛti-sādhyaṃ pradhānaṃ yat tat-kāryam abhidhīyata ity ayam arthaḥ śraddadhāneṣv eva śobhate /

body.text:
api ca svargakāmo yajetetyādiṣu lakāravācyakartṛviśeṣasamarpaṇaparāṇāṃ svargakāmādipadānāṃ niyojyaviśeṣasamarpaṇaparatvaṃ śabdānuśāsanaviruddhaṃ kenāvagamyate / sādhyasvargaviśiṣṭasya svargasādhane kartṛtvānvayo na ghaṭata iti cet / niyojyatvānvayo 'pi na ghaṭata iti hi svargasādhanatvaniścayaḥ / sa tu śāstrasiddhe kartṛtvānvaye svargasādhanatvaniścayaḥ kriyate / yathā bhoktukāmo devadattagṛhaṃ gacched ityukte bhojanakāmasya devadattagṛhagamane kartṛtvaśravaṇād eva prāgajñātam api bhojanasādhanatvaṃ devadattagṛhagamanasyāvagamyate / evam atrāpi bhavati / na kriyāntaraṃ prati kartṛtayā śrutasya kriyāntare kartṛtvakalpanaṃ yuktam -- yajeteti hi yāgakartṛtayā śrutasya biddhau kartṛtvakalpanaṃ kriyate / buddheḥ kartṛtvakalpanam eva hi
niyojyatvam / yathoktaṃ --
  niyojya sarvakāryaṃ yaḥ svakīyatvena budhyate /
iti / yaṣṭṛtvānuguṇaṃ tadbodhṛtvam iti cet / devadattaḥ paced iti pāke kartṛtayā śrutasya devadattasya pākārthagamanaṃ pākānuguṇam iti gamane kartṛtvakalpanaṃ na yujyate /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, in injunctions such as "<s>svargakāmo yajeta</s>" ("one who desires heaven should sacrifice"), since the words like <s>svargakāma</s> are intended to specify the particular agent denoted by the verbal suffix (<s>lakāra</s>), by the force of their capacity to express the qualification of the person enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>) — this <s>niyoga</s> belongs only to the one who desires heaven. Through its being indicative of a <s>kārya</s> rooted in the person to be enjoined, the <s>niyoga</s> alone possesses the result — this is <s>niyoga-phalatva</s> (the result belonging to the injunction). The sacrifice, on the other hand, is a means to <s>apūrva</s> (transcendental potency). Therefore, the <s>Nirukta</s> explanation that desirability (<s>kāmyatva</s>) pertains to what is enjoined, or alternatively the understanding of <s>kārya</s> — this is the methodology of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, and the arrangement of the ten chapters and so forth has been shown accordingly. All this pertains to the inquiry into eligibility for results in this world. And there it culminates in just this: that results such as heaven are desired objects (<s>kāmya</s>). But here, just as heaven is desired, so too the experience of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is desired by one seeking liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) — this is the higher state of desirability.
Thus, one who with a humbled mind knows this particular mode of reasoning and the supreme lordship of <s>Īśvara</s>,
whose nature is solely characterized by being the principal (<s>śeṣin</s>) of all things without exception,
the teaching is that he devotes himself for the sake of fulfilling His desire.
It is also taught that through sin one becomes greatly sinful, falls into the cycle of offenses, and comes under the power of death — yet He pacifies even that.
Thus it is in the <s>Śvetāśvataropaniṣad</s>.

children.text:
api ca svarga-kāmo yajeta ity-ādiṣu la-kāra-vācya-kartṛ-viśeṣa-samarpaṇa-parāṇāṃ svarga-kāma-ādi-padānāṃ niyojya-viśeṣa-samarpaṇa-paratvaṃ śabda-anuśāsana-viruddhaṃ kena avagamyate / sādhya-svarga-viśiṣṭasya svarga-sādhane kartṛtva-anvayo na ghaṭata iti cet / niyojyatva-anvayo 'pi na ghaṭata iti hi svarga-sādhanatva-niścayaḥ / sa tu śāstra-siddhe kartṛtva-anvaye svarga-sādhanatva-niścayaḥ kriyate / yathā bhoktu-kāmo devadatta-gṛhaṃ gacched ity-ukte bhojana-kāmasya devadatta-gṛha-gamane kartṛtva-śravaṇād eva prāg-ajñātam api bhojana-sādhanatvaṃ devadatta-gṛha-gamanasya avagamyate / evam atra api bhavati / na kriyā-antaraṃ prati kartṛtayā śrutasya kriyā-antare kartṛtva-kalpanaṃ yuktam --- yajeta iti hi yāga-kartṛtayā śrutasya biddhau kartṛtva-kalpanaṃ kriyate / buddheḥ kartṛtva-kalpanam eva hi
niyojyatvam / yathā-uktaṃ ---
  niyojya sarva-kāryaṃ yaḥ svakīyatvena budhyate /
iti / yaṣṭṛtva-anuguṇaṃ tad-bodhṛtvam iti cet / devadattaḥ paced iti pāke kartṛtayā śrutasya devadattasya pāka-artha-gamanaṃ pāka-anuguṇam iti gamane kartṛtva-kalpanaṃ na yujyate /

body.text:
kiṃ ca liṅādiśabdavācyaṃ sthāyirūpaṃ kim ity apūrvam āśrīyate / svargakāmapadasamabhivyāhārānupapatter iti cet / kātrānupapattiḥ / siṣādhayiṣitasvargo hi svargakāmaḥ / tasya svargakāmasya kālāntarabhāvisvargasiddhau kṣaṇabhaṅginī yāgādikriyā na samartheti cet / anāghrātavedasiddhāntānām iyam anupapattiḥ / sarvaiḥ karmabhir ārādhitaḥ parameśvaro bhagavān nārāyaṇas tattadiṣṭaṃ phalaṃ dadātīti vedavido vadanti / yathāhur vedavidagresarā dramiḍācāryāḥ -- phalasaṃbibhatsayā hi karmabhir ātmānaṃ piprīṣanti sa prīto 'laṃ phalāyeti śāstramaryādā iti / phalasaṃbandhecchayā karmabhir yāgadānahomādibhir indriyādidevatāmukhena tattadantaryāmirūpeṇāvasthitam indrādiśabdavācyaṃ paramātmānaṃ bhagavantaṃ vāsudevam ārirādhayiṣanti,
sa hi karmabhir ārādhitas teṣām iṣṭāni phalāni prayacchatītyarthaḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ -- iṣṭāpūrtaṃ bahudhā jātaṃ jāyamānaṃ viśvaṃ bibharti bhuvanasya nābhir iti / iṣṭāpūrtam iti sakalaśrutismṛticoditaṃ karmocyate / tadviśvaṃ bibharti -- indrāgnivaruṇādisarvadevatāsaṃbandhitayā pratīyamānaṃ tattadantarātmatayāvasthitaḥ paramapuruṣaḥ svayam eva bibharti svayam eva svīkaroti / bhuvanasya nābhiḥ -- brahmakṣatrādisarvavarṇapūrṇasya bhuvanasya dhārakaḥ -- tais taiḥ karmabhir ārādhitas tattadiṣṭaphalapradānena bhuvanānāṃ dhāraka iti nābhir ityuktaḥ / agnivāyuprabhṛtidevatāntarātmatayā tattacchabdābhidheyo 'yam evety āha -- tad evāgnis tadvāyus tatsūryas tad u candramā iti / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā --
yo yo yām yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati /
tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmy aham //
sa tasya śraddhayā yuktas tasyārādhanam īhate /
labhate ca tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān iha tān // iti /
yāṃ yāṃ tanum itīndrādidevatāviśeṣās tattadantaryāmitayāvasthitasya bhagavatas tanavaḥ śarīrāṇītyarthaḥ /
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca /
ityādi / prabhur eva ceti sarvaphalānāṃ pradātā cetyarthaḥ / yathā ca
yajñais tvam ijyase nityaṃ sarvadevamayācyuta /
yaiḥ svadharmaparair nātha narair ādādhito bhavān /
te taranty akhilām etāṃ mayām ātmavimuktaye //
iti / setihāsapurāṇeṣu sarveṣv eva vedeṣu sarvāṇi karmāṇi sarveśvarārādhanarūpāṇi, tais taiḥ karmabhir ārādhitaḥ puruṣottamas tattadiṣṭaṃ phalaṃ dadātīti tatra tatra prapañcitam / evam hi sarvaśaktiṃ sarvajñaṃ sarveśvaraṃ bhagavantam indrādidevatāntaryāmirūpeṇa yāgadānahomādivedoditasarvakarmaṇāṃ bhoktāraṃ sarvaphalānāṃ pradātāraṃ ca sarvāḥ śrutayo vadanti / caturhotāro yatra saṃpadaṃ gacchanti devair ityādyāḥ / caturhotāro yajñāḥ, yatra paramātmani deveṣv antaryāmirūpeṇāvasthite, devaiḥ saṃpadaṃ gacchanti -- devaiḥ saṃbandhaṃ gacchanti yajñā ityarthaḥ / antaryāmirūpeṇāvasthitasya paramātmanaḥ śarīratayāvasthitānām indrādīnāṃ yāgādisaṃbandha ity uktaṃ bhavati / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā --
bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram /
iti / tasmād agnyādidevatāntarātmabhūtaparamapuruṣārādhanarūpabhūtāni sarvāṇi karmāṇi, sa eva cābhilaṣitaphalapradāteti kim atrāpūrveṇa vyutpattipathadūravartinā vācyatayābhyupagatena kalpitena vā prayojanam / evaṃ ca sati liṅādeḥ ko 'yam arthaḥ parigṛhīto bhavati / yaja devapūjāyām iti devatārādhanabhūtayāgādeḥ prakṛtyarthasya kartṛvyāpārasādhyatāṃ vyutpattisiddhāṃ liṅādayo 'bhidadhatīti na kiṃcid anupapannam / kartṛvācināṃ pratyayānāṃ prakṛtyarthasya kartṛvyāpārasaṃbandhaprakāro hi vācyaḥ / bhūtavartamānādikam anye vadanti / liṅādayas tu kartṛvyāpārasādhyatāṃ vadanti /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, why is the imperceptible (<s>apūrva</s>) resorted to, when the enduring form denoted by the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) and the like [can explain the injunction]? If [it be said]: because of the impossibility of co-occurrence with the expression '<s>svargakāma</s>' (one who desires heaven) — where is the impossibility? For '<s>svargakāma</s>' means one who wishes to accomplish heaven. If [it be said]: when the heaven that will come into being at a later time is to be accomplished, the momentary sacrificial action and the like are not capable [of producing it] — this impossibility [arises] only for those who have not even smelled the established conclusions of the <s>Veda</s>. The knowers of the <s>Veda</s> say that the Supreme Lord, the Blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, being worshipped through all <s>karmas</s> (ritual actions), grants the desired fruit to each. As the foremost among the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, the <s>Dramiḍācāryas</s> (southern teachers), say: 'Through <s>karmas</s>, desiring connection with the fruit, they seek to please Him; He, being pleased, is sufficient for the fruit — this is the rule of scripture.' With the desire for connection with the fruit, through <s>karmas</s> such as sacrifice, charity, oblation, etc., via the deities of the senses and others, they seek to worship the Supreme Self, the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who is established in the form of the inner controller of each [deity] and who is denoted by the words '<s>Indra</s>' and the like,
for He, being worshipped through <s>karmas</s>, grants them their desired fruits — that is the meaning. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'The <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (Vedic and meritorious works), born in many ways, being born, the universe He sustains — the navel of the world.' '<s>Iṣṭāpūrta</s>' refers to all <s>karmas</s> enjoined by the entire <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. 'That universe He sustains' — the Supreme Person, established as the inner Self of each of the deities <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, etc., through whom [the rituals] are understood as connected, Himself sustains [them], Himself accepts [them]. 'The navel of the world' — the supporter of the world filled with all <s>varṇas</s> (classes) such as <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, etc. — being worshipped through those various <s>karmas</s>, He is called the 'navel' because He is the sustainer of the worlds by granting the desired fruit to each. That He alone is denoted by the respective words by being the inner Self of deities such as <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, etc. is stated: 'That itself is <s>Agni</s>, that is <s>Vāyu</s>, that is <s>Sūrya</s>, that indeed is <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon).' As stated by the Blessed Lord:
'Whatever form a devotee with faith wishes to worship,
I make that very faith of his firm and unwavering.
Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that [deity],
and obtains therefrom the desires that are indeed ordained by Me alone.'
'Whatever form' — the specific deities such as <s>Indra</s> and others are the bodies, the forms, of the Blessed Lord who is established as the inner controller of each — that is the meaning.
'For I am the enjoyer and also the lord of all sacrifices.'
And so forth. 'The lord indeed' means the bestower of all fruits. And as:
'Through sacrifices You are always worshipped, O <s>Acyuta</s>, who contains all gods;
Those men who are devoted to their own <s>dharma</s>, O Lord, by whom You are served,
they cross over this entire <s>māyā</s> for the liberation of the self.'
In the <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and indeed in all the <s>Vedas</s>, all <s>karmas</s> are of the nature of worship of the Lord of all; <s>Puruṣottama</s>, being worshipped through those various <s>karmas</s>, grants the desired fruit to each — this is elaborated in each of those [texts]. For thus all the <s>śrutis</s> declare the Blessed Lord — who is omnipotent, omniscient, the Lord of all — to be the enjoyer of all <s>karmas</s> enjoined by the <s>Veda</s> such as sacrifice, charity, and oblation, through His form as the inner controller of deities such as <s>Indra</s> and others, and to be the bestower of all fruits. 'Where the four types of priests attain fulfillment with the gods,' etc. The four types of sacrificial priests [attain fulfillment] where — in the Supreme Self established in the form of the inner controller of the gods — they attain fulfillment with the gods, that is, they attain connection with the gods through the sacrifices — that is the meaning. What is being said is that the connection of <s>Indra</s> and other [deities], who exist as the body of the Supreme Self established as their inner controller, with sacrifices and the like [is thus established]. As stated by the Blessed Lord:
'The enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all worlds.'
Therefore, all <s>karmas</s> are of the nature of worship of the Supreme Person who is the inner Self of the deities <s>Agni</s> and others, and He alone is the bestower of the desired fruit — so what purpose is served by the <s>apūrva</s>, which stands far from the path of conventional understanding, being accepted as the denotation, or being fabricated? This being the case, what meaning of the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) and the like is accepted? 'To sacrifice' (<s>yaja</s>) means 'for the worship of a deity' — the optative and other [suffixes] denote the accomplishability through the agent's effort of the meaning of the verbal root, namely, sacrifice and the like, which are of the nature of worship of the deity — thus nothing is untenable. For the denotation of the suffixes that denote the agent is the specific mode of connection of the meaning of the root with the agent's effort. Others say [it denotes] past, present, etc. But the optative and the like denote accomplishability through the agent's effort.

children.text:
kiṃ ca liṅ-ādi-śabda-vācyaṃ sthāyi-rūpaṃ kim ity apūrvam āśrīyate / svarga-kāma-pada-samabhivyāhāra-anupapatter iti cet / ka ātra anupapattiḥ / siṣādhayiṣita-svargo hi svarga-kāmaḥ / tasya svarga-kāmasya kāla-antara-bhāvi-svarga-siddhau kṣaṇa-bhaṅginī yāga-ādi-kriyā na samartha īti cet / anāghrāta-veda-siddhāntānām iyam anupapattiḥ / sarvaiḥ karmabhir ārādhitaḥ parama-īśvaro bhagavān nārāyaṇas tat-tad-iṣṭaṃ phalaṃ dadāti iti veda-vido vadanti / yathā āhur veda-vid-agresarā dramiḍa-ācāryāḥ --- phala-saṃbibhatsayā hi karmabhir ātmānaṃ piprīṣanti sa prīto 'laṃ phalāya iti śāstra-maryādā iti / phala-saṃbandha-icchayā karmabhir yāga-dāna-homa-ādibhir indriya-ādi-devatā-mukhena tat-tad-antaryāmi-rūpeṇa avasthitam indra-ādi-śabda-vācyaṃ parama-ātmānaṃ bhagavantaṃ vāsudevam ārirādhayiṣanti,
sa hi karmabhir ārādhitas teṣām iṣṭāni phalāni prayacchati ity-arthaḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ --- iṣṭa-apūrtaṃ bahudhā jātaṃ jāyamānaṃ viśvaṃ bibharti bhuvanasya nābhir iti / iṣṭa-apūrtam iti sakala-śruti-smṛti-coditaṃ karma ucyate / tad-viśvaṃ bibharti --- indra-agni-varuṇa-ādi-sarva-devatā-saṃbandhitayā pratīyamānaṃ tat-tad-antara-ātmataya āvasthitaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ svayam eva bibharti svayam eva svī-karoti / bhuvanasya nābhiḥ --- brahma-kṣatra-ādi-sarva-varṇa-pūrṇasya bhuvanasya dhārakaḥ --- tais taiḥ karmabhir ārādhitas tat-tad-iṣṭa-phala-pradānena bhuvanānāṃ dhāraka iti nābhir ity-uktaḥ / agni-vāyu-prabhṛti-devatā-antara-ātmatayā tat-tac-chabda-abhidheyo 'yam eva ity āha --- tad eva agnis tad-vāyus tat-sūryas tad u candra-mā iti / yathā-uktaṃ bhagavatā ---
yo yo yām yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhaya ārcitum icchati /
tasya tasya acalāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmy aham //
sa tasya śraddhayā yuktas tasya-ārādhanam īhate /
labhate ca tataḥ kāmān maya aiva vihitān iha tān // iti /
yāṃ yāṃ tanum iti indra-ādi-devatā-viśeṣās tat-tad-antaryāmitaya āvasthitasya bhagavatas tanavaḥ śarīrāṇi ity-arthaḥ /
ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca /
ity-ādi / prabhur eva ca iti sarva-phalānāṃ pradātā ca ity-arthaḥ / yathā ca
yajñais tvam ijyase nityaṃ sarva-deva-maya acyuta /
yaiḥ sva-dharma-parair nātha narair ādādhito bhavān /
te taranty akhilām etāṃ mayām ātma-vimuktaye //
iti / sa ītihāsa-purāṇeṣu sarveṣv eva vedeṣu sarvāṇi karmāṇi sarva-īśvara-ārādhana-rūpāṇi, tais taiḥ karmabhir ārādhitaḥ puruṣa-uttamas tat-tad-iṣṭaṃ phalaṃ dadāti iti tatra tatra prapañcitam / evam hi sarva-śaktiṃ sarva-jñaṃ sarva-īśvaraṃ bhagavantam indra-ādi-devatā-antaryāmi-rūpeṇa yāga-dāna-homa-ādi-veda-udita-sarva-karmaṇāṃ bhoktāraṃ sarva-phalānāṃ pradātāraṃ ca sarvāḥ śrutayo vadanti / catur-hotāro yatra saṃpadaṃ gacchanti devair ity-ādyāḥ / catur-hotāro yajñāḥ, yatra parama-ātmani deveṣv antaryāmi-rūpeṇa avasthite, devaiḥ saṃpadaṃ gacchanti --- devaiḥ saṃbandhaṃ gacchanti yajñā ity-arthaḥ / antaryāmi-rūpeṇa avasthitasya parama-ātmanaḥ śarīrataya āvasthitānām indra-ādīnāṃ yāga-ādi-saṃbandha ity uktaṃ bhavati / yatha ūktaṃ bhagavatā ---
bhoktāraṃ yajña-tapasāṃ sarva-loka-mahā-īśvaram /
iti / tasmād agny-ādi-devatā-antara-ātma-bhūta-parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-rūpa-bhūtāni sarvāṇi karmāṇi, sa eva ca abhilaṣita-phala-pradāta īti kim atra apūrveṇa vyutpatti-patha-dūra-vartinā vācyataya ābhyupagatena kalpitena vā prayojanam / evaṃ ca sati liṅ-ādeḥ ko 'yam arthaḥ parigṛhīto bhavati / yaja deva-pūjāyām iti devatā-ārādhana-bhūta-yāga-ādeḥ prakṛty-arthasya kartṛ-vyāpāra-sādhyatāṃ vyutpatti-siddhāṃ liṅ-ādayo 'bhidadhati iti na kiṃcid anupapannam / kartṛ-vācināṃ pratyayānāṃ prakṛty-arthasya kartṛ-vyāpāra-saṃbandha-prakāro hi vācyaḥ / bhūta-vartamāna-ādikam anye vadanti / liṅ-ādayas tu kartṛ-vyāpāra-sādhyatāṃ vadanti /

body.text:
api ca kāminaḥ kartavyatā karma vidhāya karmaṇo devatārādhanarūpatāṃ taddvārā phalasaṃbhavaṃ ca tattatkarmavidhivākyāny eva vadanti / vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabhata bhūtikāmo vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā vāyum eva svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa evainaṃ bhūtiṃ gamayatītyādīni / nātra phalasiddhyanupapattiḥ kāpi dṛśyata iti phalasādhanatvāvagatir aupādānikīty api na saṃgacchati / vidhyapekṣitaṃ yāgādeḥ phalasādhanatvaprakāraṃ vākyaśeṣa eva bodhayatītyarthaḥ / tasmād brāhmaṇāya nāpaguretety atrāpagoraṇaniṣedhavidhiparavākyaśeṣe śrūyamāṇaṃ niṣedhyasyāpagoraṇasya śatayātanāsādhanatvaṃ niṣedhavidhyupayogīti hi svīkriyate / atra punaḥ kāminaḥ kartavyatayā vihitasya yāgādeḥ kāmyasvargādisādhanatvaprakāraṃ vākyaśeṣāvagatam
anādṛtya kim ity upādānena yāgādeḥ phalasādhanatvaṃ parikalpyate / hiraṇyanidhim apavarake nidhāya yācate kodravādilubdhaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ janam iti śrūyate tad etad yuṣmāsu dṛśyate / śatayātanāsādhanatvam api nādṛṣṭadvāreṇa / coditāny anutiṣṭho vihitaṃ karmākurvato ninditāni ca kurvataḥ sarvāṇi sukhāni duḥkhāni ca paramapuruṣānugrahanigrahābhyām eva bhavanti / eṣa hy evānandayati -- atho so 'bhayaṃ gato bhavati -- atha tasya bhayaṃ bhavati -- bhīṣāsmād vātaḥ pavate bhīṣodeti sūryo bhīṣāsmād agniś candraś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ -- iti / etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ -- etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi dadato manuṣyāḥ praśaṃsanti yajamānaṃ devā darvīṃ pitaro 'nvāyattā ityādyanekavidhāḥ
śrutayaḥ santi / yathoktaṃ dramiḍabhāṣye -- tasyājñayā dhāvati vāyur nadyaḥ sravanti tena ca kṛtasīmāno jalāśayāḥ samadā iva meṣavirsapitaṃ kurvantīti / tatsaṃkalpanibandhanā hīme loke na cyavante na sphuṭante / svaśāsanānuvartināṃ jñātvā kāruṇyāt sa bhagavān vardhayeta vidvān karmadakṣa iti ca /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, having enjoined the obligation for one who desires [a result], the very sentences that enjoin the respective <s>karmas</s> state both the nature of the <s>karma</s> as worship of the deity and the possibility of the fruit through that [worship]: 'He who desires prosperity should offer a white [animal] to <s>Vāyu</s>. <s>Vāyu</s> is the swiftest deity. He approaches <s>Vāyu</s> with his own share. That [<s>Vāyu</s>] leads him to prosperity.' And so forth. No impossibility of the accomplishment of the fruit is seen here, so the understanding that [the sacrifice] is a means to the fruit is not merely 'superimposed' (<s>aupādānikī</s>) — this too does not hold. The meaning is that the remainder of the sentence itself reveals the specific manner in which sacrifice and the like are means to the fruit, as required by the injunction. Therefore, in 'One should not revile a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — when in the remainder of the sentence of the injunction prohibiting reviling, the being-a-means-to-a-hundred-tortures of the prohibited act of reviling is heard — it is accepted as useful for the prohibitory injunction. But here, having disregarded the specific manner — understood from the remainder of the sentence — in which sacrifice and the like, enjoined as obligations for the desirous, are means to the desired result such as heaven, etc.,
why is the means-to-fruit character of sacrifice and the like fabricated through <s>apūrva</s>? It is heard [in a story]: 'Having hidden a treasure of gold in a closet, he begs from wretched people greedy for <s>kodrava</s> (inferior grain) and the like' — that is exactly what is seen among you. Even the being-a-means-to-a-hundred-tortures is not through an unseen [force]. For one who carries out what is enjoined and performs the prescribed <s>karma</s>, and for one who does not perform [it] and commits prohibited acts — all pleasures and pains come through the grace and disfavor of the Supreme Person alone. 'For He alone gives bliss' — 'then he becomes free from fear' — 'then there is fear for him' — 'From fear of Him the wind blows, from fear [of Him] the sun rises, from fear [of Him] <s>Agni</s>, <s>Candra</s> (the Moon), and Death, the fifth, run.' And: 'Under the governance of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon are held in their places' — 'Under the governance of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, people praise the giver, the gods [attend to] the sacrificer, the ancestors follow the ladle' — there are manifold <s>śrutis</s> of this kind. As stated in the <s>Dramiḍabhāṣya</s>: 'By His command the wind runs, the rivers flow, and the reservoirs of water made with fixed boundaries by Him do not transgress [their limits], like rams tethered to a post.' 'For these [things] in the world do not deviate or burst forth, because they are grounded in His will. Knowing those who follow His rule, that Blessed Lord, out of compassion, would increase [their welfare] — the wise one, skilled in action' — thus also.

paramapuruṣayāthātmyajñānapūrvakatadupāsanādivihitakarmānuṣṭhāyinas tatprasādāt tatprāptiparyantāni sukhāny abhayaṃ ca yathādhikāraṃ bhavanti / tajjñānapūrvakaṃ tadupāsanādivihitaṃ karmākurvato ninditāni ca kurvatas tannigrahād eva tadaprāptipūrvakāparimitaduḥkhāni bhayaṃ ca bhavanti / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā --
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ /
ityādinā kṛtsnaṃ karma jñānapūrvakam anuṣṭheyaṃ vidhāya --
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya
iti sarvasya karmaṇaḥ svārādhanatām ātmanāṃ svaniyāmyatāṃ ca pratipādya --
ye me matam idaṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ /
śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ //
ye tv etadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam /
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ //
iti svājñānuvartinaḥ praśasya viparītān vinindya punar api svājñānupālanam akurvatām āsur aprakṛtyantarbhāvam abhidhāyādhamā gatiś coktā --
tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu narādhamān /
kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu //
āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani /
mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim // iti /
sarvakarmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo madvypāśrayaḥ /
matprasādād avāpnoti śāśvataṃ padam avyayam //
iti ca svājñānuvartināṃ śāśvataṃ padaṃ coktam / aśrutavedāntānāṃ karmaṇy aśraddhā mā bhūd iti devatādhikaraṇe 'tivādāḥ kṛtāḥ karmamātre yathā śraddhā syād iti sarvam ekaśāstram iti vedavitsiddhāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: For those who perform the prescribed duties such as <s>upāsana</s> (meditation) preceded by knowledge of the true nature of the <s>Paramapuruṣa</s> (Supreme Person), by His grace there arise happiness leading up to the attainment of Him, and fearlessness, each according to one's qualification. For those who do not perform the duties prescribed through <s>upāsana</s> and other means preceded by knowledge of Him, and who commit prohibited acts, by His restraining power alone there arise immeasurable sufferings preceding the non-attainment of Him, and fear. As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> — "Perform your prescribed duty, for action is superior to inaction" (BG 3.8) — having thus enjoined that all <s>karma</s> (action) is to be performed preceded by knowledge — "Surrendering all actions unto Me" (BG 3.30) — having thus established that all actions are a form of worship of Him and that all selves are under His control — "Those persons who always follow this teaching of Mine with faith and without envy, they too are released from the bondage of <s>karma</s>; but those who, finding fault with this, do not follow My teaching — know them to be deluded in all knowledge, lost, and devoid of discrimination" (BG 3.31-32) — having thus praised those who follow His command and censured those who are opposed, and further, having declared that those who do not uphold His command fall within the <s>āsura</s> (demoniac) nature, the lowest destiny is also stated — "Those who are hateful, cruel, the lowest of men in the cycle of births, inauspicious — I hurl them perpetually into <s>āsurī</s> (demoniac) wombs. Having attained a demoniac birth, deluded in birth after birth, not attaining Me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, they then go to the lowest state" (BG 16.19-20). "Even while always performing all actions, one who depends on Me, by My grace attains the eternal, imperishable abode" (BG 18.56) — thus the eternal abode is also declared for those who follow His command. The excessive praises made in the <s>Devatādhikaraṇa</s> (the section on deities in Mīmāṃsā) are meant so that those who have not studied <s>Vedānta</s> should not lose faith in <s>karma</s> (ritual action); the established conclusion of those who know the <s>Veda</s> is that all of it constitutes a single <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), so that faith may arise in <s>karma</s> as such.

tasyaitasya parasya brahmaṇo nārāyaṇasyāparicchedyajñānānandāmalatvasvarūpavajjñānaśaktibalāiśvaryavīryatejaḥprabhṛtyanavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇavatsvasaṃkalpapravartyasvetarasamastacidacidvastujātavatsvābhimatasvānurūpaikarūpadivyarūpataducitaniratiśayakalyāṇavividhānaṃtabhūṣaṇasvaśaktisadṛśāparimitānantāścaryanānāvidhāyudhasvābhimatānurūpasvarūpaguṇavibhavāiśvaryaśīlādyanavadhikamahimamahisīsvānurūpakalyāṇajñānakriyādyaparimeyaguṇānantaparijanaparicchedasvocitanikhilabhogyabhogopakaraṇādyanantamahāvibhavāvāṅmanasagocarasvarūpasvabhāvadivyasthānādinityatāniravadyatāgocarāś ca sahasraśaḥ śrutayaḥ santi / vedāham etaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ
parastāt / ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ / tasya yathā kapyāsaṃ puṇḍarīkam evam akṣiṇī / ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśas tasminn ayaṃ puruṣo manomayo 'mṛto hiraṇmayaḥ -- manomaya iti manasaiva viśuddhena gṛhyata ityarthaḥ -- sarve nimeṣā jajñire vidyutaḥ puruṣād adhi -- vidyudvarṇāt puruṣād ityarthaḥ -- nīlatoyadamadhyasthā vidyullekheva bhāsvarā -- madhyasthanīlatoyadā vidyullekheva seyaṃ daharapuṇḍarīkamadhyasthākāśavartinī vahnirśikhā svāntarnihitanīlatoyadābhaparamātmasvarūpā avāntarnihitanīlatoyadā visyud ivābhātītyarthaḥ / manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ / satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ / ākāśātmā sarvakāmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyātto 'vākyānādaraḥ /
māhārajanaṃ vāsa ityādyāḥ / asyeśānā jagato viṣṇupatnī / hrīś ca te lakṣmīś ca patnyau /tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ / kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke / yad ekam avyaktam anantarūpaṃ viśvaṃ purāṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt / yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman / yo 'syādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman / tad eva tad u bhavyamā idaṃ tadakṣare parame vyoman nityādiśrutiśataniścito 'yam arthaḥ /
body.translated_text: There are hundreds of <s>śruti</s> (scriptural) passages that establish the following regarding this Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>: His essential nature is of unlimited <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), and purity; He possesses innumerable, unsurpassably excellent <s>kalyāṇa-guṇas</s> (auspicious qualities) such as <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>śakti</s> (power), <s>bala</s> (strength), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>vīrya</s> (valour), and <s>tejas</s> (splendour); all other entities, both sentient (<s>cit</s>) and insentient (<s>acit</s>), are directed by His will alone; He has a divine form that is singular, suited to and desired by His own nature; He bears infinitely varied, unsurpassably auspicious ornaments befitting that form; He wields weapons of unlimited, wondrous, and manifold kinds matching His own power; His consorts possess greatness of unsurpassable majesty in essential nature, qualities, glory, sovereignty, disposition, and other attributes, suited to and desired by Him; His infinite retinue possesses immeasurable auspicious qualities of knowledge, action, and the like, fitting His own nature; His divine abode — with all enjoyable objects, instruments of enjoyment, and other things of boundless great splendour appropriate to Him — is of a nature and character beyond the reach of speech and mind; and these passages concern the eternality and the freedom from all defects of all these. [The <s>śrutis</s> include:] "I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), of the colour of the sun, beyond darkness" (Puruṣa Sūkta); "The golden <s>Puruṣa</s> who is within the sun"; "His eyes are like lotuses blooming under the sun's rays"; "The space within the heart — in that is this <s>Puruṣa</s>, made of mind, immortal, golden" — 'made of mind' means He is grasped only by the purified mind; "All the twinkling stars were born from that <s>Puruṣa</s> who is of the colour of lightning" — meaning from the <s>Puruṣa</s> who has the hue of lightning; "Like a streak of lightning shining in the midst of a dark rain-cloud" — this flame abiding in the space within the small lotus of the heart, whose <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) nature resembles a dark rain-cloud placed within it, shines like lightning within an inner dark cloud — this is the meaning; "Made of mind, having <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath) as His body, of the form of light; of true desire, of true resolve" (Chāndogya Up. 3.14); "Whose nature is space, who contains all desires, all fragrances, all tastes, who pervades all this, who is beyond words and indifferent [to praise]" (Chāndogya Up. 3.14); "Whose garment is of golden colour" and similar passages; "She, <s>Viṣṇupatnī</s> (the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>), is the sovereign of this universe" (Ṛg Veda); "<s>Hrī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s> are Your consorts"; "The wise ones always see that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>" (Ṛg Veda 1.22.20); "[They see Him] shining far beyond this realm of <s>rajas</s>"; "That which is one, unmanifest, of infinite forms, the ancient one, beyond darkness"; "He who knows [<s>Brahman</s>] hidden in the cave, in the supreme heaven"; "He who is the overseer, in the supreme heaven"; "That very thing, which will be — this, in the imperishable, in the supreme heaven" — and so on, in hundreds of eternal <s>śrutis</s>, this meaning is established.

body.text:
tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam iti viṣṇoḥ parasya brahmaṇaḥ paraṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūraya iti vacanāt sarvakāladarśanavantaḥ paripūrṇajñānāḥ kecana santīti vijñāyate / ye sūrayas te sadā paśyantīti vacanavyaktiḥ, ye sadā paśyanti te sūraya iti vā / ubhayapakṣe 'py anekavidhānaṃ na saṃbhavatīti cet / na / aprāptatvāt sarvasya sarvaviśiṣṭaṃ paramasthānaṃ vidhīyate / yathoktaṃ -- tadguṇās te vidhīyerann avibhāgād vidhānārthe na ced anyena śiṣṭā iti / yathā yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapāla ityādikarmavidhau karmaṇo guṇānāṃ cāprāptatvena sarvaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ karma vidhīyate tathātrāpi sūribhiḥ sadā dṛśyatvena viṣṇoḥ paramasthānam aprāptaṃ pratipādayatīti na kaścid virodhaḥ / karaṇamantrāḥ kriyamāṇānuvādinaḥ stotraśastrarūpā
japādiṣu viniyuktāś ca prakaraṇapathitāś cāprakaraṇapathitāś ca svārthaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvasthitam evāprāptam aviruddhaṃ brāhmaṇavad bodhayantīti hi vaidikāḥ / pragītamantrasādhyaguṇaguṇiabhimānaṃ stotram / apragītamantrasādhyaguṇaguṇiniṣṭhaguṇābhidhānaṃ śastram / niyuktārthaprakāśanāṃ ca devatādiṣv aprāptāviruddhaguṇaviśeṣaprtipādanaṃ viniyogānuguṇam eva / neyaṃ śrutir muktajanaviṣayā / teśāṃ sadādarśanānupapatteḥ / na+pi muktapravāhaviṣayā / sadā paśyantīty ekaikakartṛkaviṣayatayā pratīteḥ śrutibhaṅgaprasaṅgāt / mantrārthavādagatā hy arthāḥ kāryaparatve 'pi siddhyantītyuktam / kiṃ punaḥ siddhavastuny eva tātparye vyutpattisiddha iti sarvam upapannam / nanu cātra tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam iti parasvarūpam
eva paramapadaśabdenābhidhīyate / samastaheyarahitaṃ viṣṇvākhyaṃ paraṃ padam ityādiṣv avyatirekadarśanāt / naivam / kṣayantam asya rajataḥ parāke, tadakṣare parame vyoman, yo asyādhyākṣaḥ parame vyoman, yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman nityādiṣu paramasthānasyaiva darśanam / tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam iti vyatirekanirdeśāc ca / viṣṇvākhyaṃ paramaṃ padam iti viśeṣaṇād anyad api paramaṃ padaṃ vidyata iti ca tenaiva jñāyate / tad idaṃ parasthānaṃ sūribhiḥ sadādṛśyatvena pratipādyate /
body.translated_text: From the statement "The wise ones always see that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>" (<s>tad Viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ</s>), it is known that there exist certain beings of complete knowledge who have vision at all times — namely, the <s>sūris</s> (eternally liberated souls). The sentence may be construed as: "Those who are <s>sūris</s>, they always see," or alternatively, "Those who always see, they are <s>sūris</s>." If one objects that on either interpretation a multiple injunction is impossible — no, because since it is unattained by all, the supreme abode qualified by all its special features is being enjoined. As stated: "Its attributes are enjoined because, due to non-difference [from the primary injunction], they serve the purpose of injunction, unless they are already taught by another [passage]." Just as in the injunction of a ritual such as "the eight-kapāla offering to <s>Agni</s>," the ritual together with all its subsidiary details is enjoined because both the ritual and its details are unattained, so too here, the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as that which is always seen by the <s>sūris</s>, is being presented as something unattained — hence there is no contradiction. The <s>Vaidikas</s> (Vedic scholars) hold that ritual-accompanying <s>mantras</s> — which describe the act being performed, which take the form of <s>stotra</s> (hymns of praise) and <s>śastra</s> (recitations), which are employed in <s>japa</s> (repetition) and the like, whether occurring within a particular context or outside it — all convey their own meaning as it actually is, presenting what is unattained and non-contradictory, just like the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (prose explanatory portions). A <s>stotra</s> (hymn of praise) is the attribution to a deity of qualities achievable through a previously chanted <s>mantra</s>. A <s>śastra</s> (recitation) is the statement of qualities belonging to the deity that are achievable through a <s>mantra</s> not previously chanted. And the illumination of the meaning to which they are applied — the presentation of unattained, non-contradictory, particular qualities of deities and the like — is in accordance with their liturgical application. This <s>śruti</s> does not refer to liberated souls (<s>muktas</s>), because perpetual vision is impossible for them [since they were not always liberated]. Nor does it refer to the ongoing stream of liberated souls [collectively], because the expression "they always see" is understood as referring to each individual agent, and [interpreting it otherwise] would amount to breaking the <s>śruti</s>. It has been said that meanings found in <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages) are established even when the overall purport is injunctive. How much more so when the purport is directed at an already established reality — this is proven through [ordinary] linguistic comprehension. Thus everything is consistent. Now, one might object: here the expression <s>paramaṃ padam</s> (supreme abode) in "that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>" denotes the supreme essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) itself, since in passages like "the supreme state called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from all that is to be rejected," there is no distinction seen [between <s>padam</s> as 'abode' and <s>padam</s> as 'nature']. This is not so. In passages such as "[they see Him] shining far beyond this realm of <s>rajas</s>," "in the imperishable, in the supreme heaven," "He who is the overseer, in the supreme heaven," "He who knows [<s>Brahman</s>] hidden in the cave, in the supreme heaven," and other eternal <s>śrutis</s>, it is the supreme abode that is being referred to. And the separate mention in "that supreme <s>padam</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>" [distinguishing <s>padam</s> from <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself] also [shows this]. Furthermore, from the qualifier in "the supreme <s>padam</s> called <s>Viṣṇu</s>," it is known by that very passage that there exists another <s>paramaṃ padam</s> as well. Thus, this supreme abode is being presented as that which is always seen by the <s>sūris</s>.

etaduktaṃ bhavati -- kvacitparasthānaṃ paramapadaśabdena pratipādyate, kvacitprakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpaṃ, kvacidbhagavatsvarūpam / tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūraya iti parasthānam /
sargasthityantakāleṣu trividhaiva pravartate /
guṇapravṛttyā paramaṃ padaṃ tasyāguṇaṃ mahat //
ityatra prakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpam /
samastaheyarahitaṃ viṣṇvākhyaṃ paramaṃ padam /
ityatra bhagavatsvarūpam / trīṇy apy etāni paramaprāptatvena paramapadaśabdena pratipādyante / kathaṃ trayāṇāṃ paramaprāpyatvam iti cet / bhagavatsvarūpaṃ paramaprāpyatvād eva paramaṃ padam / itarayor api bhagavatprāptigarbhatvād eva paramapadatvam / sarvakarmabandhavinirmuktātmasvarūpāvāptir bhagavatprāptigarbhā / ta ime satyāḥ kāmā anṛtāpidhānā iti bhagavato guṇagaṇasya tirodhāyakatvenānṛtaśabdena svakarmaṇaḥ pratipādanam /
body.translated_text: What is meant is this: in some places the word <s>paramapadam</s> (supreme abode/state) denotes the supreme abode (<s>parasthānam</s>), in some places it denotes the essential nature of the self freed from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial matter), and in some places it denotes the essential nature of <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Lord). "The wise ones always see that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>" — here it refers to the supreme abode. "At the times of creation, sustenance, and dissolution, [<s>Prakṛti</s>] operates in three ways through the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents); His supreme state, beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, is great" — here it refers to the essential nature of the self freed from <s>Prakṛti</s>. "The supreme state called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from all that is to be rejected" — here it refers to the essential nature of <s>Bhagavān</s>. All three of these are denoted by the word <s>paramapadam</s> because they are the supreme attainment. If one asks how all three can be the supreme attainment — the essential nature of <s>Bhagavān</s> is <s>paramapadam</s> precisely because it is the supreme object to be attained. The other two also have the status of <s>paramapadam</s> because the attainment of <s>Bhagavān</s> is inherent in them. The realization of the self's essential nature, freed from all bondage of <s>karma</s> (action), contains within it the attainment of <s>Bhagavān</s>. [As the <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> states:] "These desires are real, [but they have] a covering of untruth" (Chāndogya Up. 8.3.2) — here, by the word <s>anṛta</s> (untruth), one's own <s>karma</s> is denoted as that which conceals the host of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>guṇas</s> (auspicious qualities).

parasthānaprāptir api bhagavatprāptigarbhaiveti suvyaktam / kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāka iti rajataḥśabdena triguṇātmikā prakṛtir ucyate kevalasya rajaso 'navasthānāt / imāṃ triguṇātmikāṃ prakṛtim atikramya sthite sthāne kṣayantam -- vasantam ityarthaḥ / anena triguṇātmakāt kṣetrajñasya bhogyabhūtād vastunaḥ parastād viṣṇor vāsasthānam iti gamyate / vedāham etaṃ
puruṣaṃ mahāntam ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastād ityatrāpi tamaḥśabdena saiva prakṛtir ucyate / kevalasya tamaso 'navasthānād eva / rajasaḥ parāke kṣayantam ityanenaikavākyatvāt tamasaḥ parastād vasantaṃ mahāntam ādityavarṇaṃ puruṣam ahaṃ vedety ayam artho 'vagamyate / satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma / yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman / tadakṣare parame vyomann iti tatsthānam avikārarūpaṃ paramavyomaśabdābhidheyam iti ca gamyate / akṣare parame vyoman nityasya sthānasyākṣaratvaśravaṇāt kṣararūpādityamaṇḍalādayo na paramavyomaśabdābhidheyāḥ / yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ, yatra rṣayaḥ prathamajā ye purāṇā ityādiṣu ca ta eva sūraya ity avagamyate / tadviprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ samindhate viṣṇor yatparaṃ padam ityatrāpi viprāso
-- medhāvinaḥ, vipanyavaḥ -- stutiśīlāḥ, jāgṛvāṃsaḥ -- askhalitajñānās ta evāskhalitajñānās tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā stuvantaḥ samindhata ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: It is also clearly established that the attainment of the Supreme Abode is itself included within the attainment of the Lord. In '<s>kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke</s>' (dwelling beyond this <s>rajas</s>), the word '<s>rajas</s>' denotes <s>Prakṛti</s> consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, since <s>rajas</s> alone cannot subsist independently. Having transcended this <s>Prakṛti</s> consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, '[He is] dwelling (<s>kṣayantam</s> — meaning 'residing') in the abode that is established.' From this it is understood that <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s dwelling-place is beyond the entity consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s> that serves as the object of experience for the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). In the text 'I know this great Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), of the color of the sun, beyond the darkness (<s>tamas</s>),' the word '<s>tamas</s>' likewise denotes that very <s>Prakṛti</s>, since <s>tamas</s> alone cannot subsist independently. Since this is syntactically connected with '<s>kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke</s>,' the meaning understood is: 'I know the great Person, of the color of the sun, dwelling beyond the darkness [i.e., <s>Prakṛti</s>].' [From the texts:] '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite'; 'He who knows [<s>Brahman</s>] hidden in the cave, in the supreme space (<s>parame vyoman</s>)'; 'In that imperishable, supreme space' — it is understood that His abode, which is of an unchanging nature, is what is denoted by the word 'supreme space' (<s>paramavyoman</s>). Since in the text 'in the imperishable, supreme space,' the abode, being eternal, is heard as imperishable — therefore the solar orb and other perishable entities are not what is denoted by the term 'supreme space.' In the texts 'Where the ancient gods, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, abide' and 'Where the first-born sages, the ancient ones' — it is understood that those very ones are the 'wise seers' (<s>sūrayaḥ</s>). In the text 'Those wise ones (<s>viprāsaḥ</s>), those eloquent praisers (<s>vipanyavaḥ</s>), those ever-wakeful ones (<s>jāgṛvāṃsaḥ</s>) kindle [the light of] that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — '<s>viprāsaḥ</s>' means 'the intelligent ones,' '<s>vipanyavaḥ</s>' means 'those given to praise,' '<s>jāgṛvāṃsaḥ</s>' means 'those of unfailing knowledge' — those very ones of unfailing knowledge, constantly praising that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, are resplendent: this is the meaning.

children.text:
para-sthāna-prāptir api bhagavat-prāpti-garbha aiva iti suvyaktam / kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāka iti rajataḥ-śabdena tri-guṇa-ātmikā prakṛtir ucyate kevalasya rajaso 'navasthānāt / imāṃ tri-guṇa-ātmikāṃ prakṛtim atikramya sthite sthāne kṣayantam --- vasantam ity-arthaḥ / anena tri-guṇa-ātmakāt kṣetra-jñasya bhogya-bhūtād vastunaḥ parastād viṣṇor vāsa-sthānam iti gamyate / veda aham etaṃ
puruṣaṃ mahāntam āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastād ity-atra api tamaḥ-śabdena sa aiva prakṛtir ucyate / kevalasya tamaso 'navasthānād eva / rajasaḥ parāke kṣayantam ity-anena eka-vākyatvāt tamasaḥ parastād vasantaṃ mahāntam āditya-varṇaṃ puruṣam ahaṃ veda ity ayam artho 'vagamyate / satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma / yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman / tad-akṣare parame vyomann iti tat-sthānam avikāra-rūpaṃ parama-vyoma-śabda-abhidheyam iti ca gamyate / akṣare parame vyoman nityasya sthānasya akṣaratva-śravaṇāt kṣara-rūpa-āditya-maṇḍala-ādayo na parama-vyoma-śabda-abhidheyāḥ / yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ, yatra rṣayaḥ prathama-jā ye purāṇā ity-ādiṣu ca ta eva sūraya ity avagamyate / tad-viprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ samindhate viṣṇor yat-paraṃ padam ity-atra api viprāso
--- medhāvinaḥ, vipanyavaḥ --- stuti-śīlāḥ, jāgṛvāṃsaḥ --- askhalita-jñānās ta eva askhalita-jñānās tad-viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā stuvantaḥ samindhata ity-arthaḥ /

body.text:
eteṣāṃ parijanasthānādīnāṃ sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ityatra jñānabalāiśvaryādikalyāṇaguṇagaṇavatparabrahmasvarūpāntarbhūtatvāt sad evaikam evādvitīyam iti brahmāntarbhāvo 'vagamyate / eṣām api kalyāṇaguṇaikadeśatvād eva sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ity atredam iti śabdasya karmavaśyabhoktṛvargamiśratadbhogyabhūtaprapañcaviṣayatvāc ca sadā paśyanti sūraya iti sadādarśitvena ca teṣāṃ karmavaśyānantarbhāvāt / apahatapāpmetyādy apipāsa ityantena salīlopakaraṇabhūtatriguṇaprakṛtiprākṛtatatsaṃsṛṣṭapuruṣagataṃ heyasvabhāvaṃ sarvaṃ pratiṣidhya satyakāma ityanena svabhogyabhogopakaraṇajātasya sarvasya satyatā pratipāditā / asatyāḥ kāmā yasyāsau satyakāmaḥ / kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ / tena pareṇa brahmaṇā svabhogyatadupakaraṇādayaḥ
svābhimatā ye kāmyante te satyāḥ -- nityā ityarthaḥ / anyasya līlopakaraṇasyāpi vastunaḥ pramāṇasaṃbandhayogyatve saty api vikārāspadatvenāsthiratvād tadviparītaṃ sthiratvam eṣāṃ satyapadenocyate / satyasaṃkalpa ityeteṣu bhogyatadupakaraṇādiṣu nityeṣu niratiśayeṣv ananteṣu satsvapyapūrvāṇām aparimitānām arthānām api saṃkalpamātreṇa siddhiṃ vadati / eṣāṃ ca bhogopakaraṇānāṃ līlopakaraṇānāṃ cetanānām acetanānāṃ sthirāṇām asthirāṇām ca tatsaṃkalpāyattasvarūpasthitipravṛttibhedādi sarvaṃ vāti satyasaṃkalpa iti /
body.translated_text: The inclusion of these — the retinue, abode, and the rest — within [the statement] 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone, dear one, was this in the beginning' is understood because they are included within the nature of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which possesses hosts of auspicious qualities such as knowledge, strength, sovereignty, and the rest. And since these too are but a portion of the auspicious qualities, and since in 'Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning,' the word 'this' (<s>idam</s>) refers to the phenomenal world mixed with the class of experiencers subject to <s>karma</s> and the objects of their experience; and since in 'the wise seers always see' (<s>sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ</s>), they are described as always beholding — and hence are not included among those subject to <s>karma</s>. By the texts beginning with 'free from evil' (<s>apahatapāpmā</s>) and ending with 'desireless' (<s>apipāsa</s>), all the defective nature belonging to the three-<s>guṇa Prakṛti</s>, the material world, and the souls enmeshed therein — which together serve as the accessories of [the Lord's] play — is negated; and by '<s>satyakāma</s>' (one of true desires), the reality of everything belonging to the category of the Lord's own objects of enjoyment and instruments thereof is established. '<s>Satyakāma</s>' means 'one whose desires (<s>kāmāḥ</s>) are true (<s>satya</s>).' '<s>Kāmāḥ</s>' means 'things desired.' The objects desired by that Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — namely, His own objects of enjoyment and their instruments — are true, meaning eternal. Even though the other entities that serve as accessories of play, though eligible for being objects of valid knowledge, are unstable since they are the locus of transformation — the opposite of that, namely stability, is expressed of these [the Lord's own objects] by the term 'true' (<s>satya</s>). By '<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>' (one of true resolve), it is stated that even though these eternal, unsurpassable, and infinite objects of enjoyment and their instruments already exist, unprecedented and unlimited objects too are accomplished by mere resolve. And the differentiation of the nature, existence, and activity of all these — instruments of enjoyment, instruments of play, sentient and non-sentient, stable and unstable — depends entirely on His resolve: this is [the meaning of] 'He wills [and it is so], [He is] of true resolve.'

children.text:
eteṣāṃ parijana-sthāna-ādīnāṃ sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ity-atra jñāna-bala-aiśvarya-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇavat-para-brahma-sva-rūpa-antarbhūtatvāt sad eva ekam eva advitīyam iti brahma-antarbhāvo 'vagamyate / eṣām api kalyāṇa-guṇa-eka-deśatvād eva sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ity atra idam iti śabdasya karma-vaśya-bhoktṛ-varga-miśra-tad-bhogya-bhūta-prapañca-viṣayatvāc ca sadā paśyanti sūraya iti sadā-darśitvena ca teṣāṃ karma-vaśya-anantarbhāvāt / apahata-pāpma īty-ādy apipāsa ity-antena salīlā-upakaraṇa-bhūta-tri-guṇa-prakṛti-prākṛta-tat-saṃsṛṣṭa-puruṣa-gataṃ heya-sva-bhāvaṃ sarvaṃ pratiṣidhya satya-kāma ity-anena sva-bhogya-bhoga-upakaraṇa-jātasya sarvasya satyatā pratipāditā / asatyāḥ kāmā yasya asau satya-kāmaḥ / kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ / tena pareṇa brahmaṇā sva-bhogya-tad-upakaraṇa-ādayaḥ
sva-abhimatā ye kāmyante te satyāḥ --- nityā ity-arthaḥ / anyasya līlā-upakaraṇasya api vastunaḥ pramāṇa-saṃbandha-yogyatve saty api vikāra-āspadatvena asthiratvād tad-viparītaṃ sthiratvam eṣāṃ satya-padena ucyate / satya-saṃkalpa ity-eteṣu bhogya-tad-upakaraṇa-ādiṣu nityeṣu niratiśayeṣv ananteṣu sat-svapya-pūrvāṇām aparimitānām arthānām api saṃkalpa-mātreṇa siddhiṃ vadati / eṣāṃ ca bhoga-upakaraṇānāṃ līlā-upakaraṇānāṃ cetanānām acetanānāṃ sthirāṇām asthirāṇām ca tat-saṃkalpa-āyatta-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛtti-bheda-ādi sarvaṃ vāti satya-saṃkalpa iti /

body.text:
itihāsapurāṇayor vedopabṛṃhaṇayoś cāyam artha ucyate --
tau te medhāvinau dṛṣṭvā vedeṣu pariniṣṭhitau /
vedopabṛṃhaṇārthāya tāv agrāhayata prabhuḥ //
iti vedopabṛṃhaṇatayā prārabdhe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe --
vyaktam eṣa mahāyogī paramātmā sanātanaḥ /
anādimadhyanidhano mahataḥ paramo mahān //
tamasaḥ paramo dhātā śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
śrīvatsavakṣā nityaśrīr ajayyaḥ śāśvato dhruvaḥ //
śārā nānāvidhāś cāpi dhanur āyatavigraham /
anvagacchanta kākutsthaṃ sarve puruṣavigrahāḥ //
viveśa vaiṣṇavaṃ tejaḥ saśarīraḥ sahānugaḥ //
śrīmadvaiṣṇavapurāṇe --
samastāḥ śaktayaś caitā nṛpa yatra pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
tadviśvairūpyaṃ rūpam antyaddharer mahat //
mūrtaṃ brahma mahābhāga sarvabrahmamayo hariḥ //
nityaivaiṣā jaganmātā viṣṇoḥ śrīr anapāyinī /
yathā sarvagato viṣṇus tathaiveyaṃ dvijottama //
devatve devadeheyaṃ manuṣyatve ca mānuṣī /
viṣṇor dehānurūpāṃ vai karoty eṣātmanas tanum //
ekāntinaḥ sadā brahmadhyāyino yogino hi ye /
teṣāṃ tatparaṃ sthānaṃ yad vai paśyanti sūrayaḥ //
kalāmuhūrtādimayaś ca kālo na yadvibhūteḥ pariṇāmahetuḥ //
mahābhārate ca --
divyaṃ sthānam ajaraṃ cāprameyaṃ durvijñeya, cāgamair gamyamādyam /
gaccha prabho rakṣa cāsmān prapannān kalpe kalpe jāyamānaḥ svamūrtyā //
kālaḥ sa pacate tatra na kālas tatra vai prabhuḥ /
iti / parasya brahmaṇo rūpavattvaṃ sūtrakāraś ca vadati -- antas taddharmopadeśād iti
body.translated_text:
In the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>, which serve to supplement the <s>Veda</s>, this same meaning is stated —
'Seeing those two learned ones well-established in the <s>Vedas</s>, the Lord caused them to compose [texts] for the purpose of supplementing the <s>Veda</s>.'
In the blessed <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, which was begun as a supplement to the <s>Veda</s>:
'Clearly this one is a great <s>yogin</s>, the eternal Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>);
Without beginning, middle, or end, greater than the great;
Beyond darkness, the Creator, bearing conch, discus, and mace;
With the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark on His chest, eternally accompanied by <s>Śrī</s>, unconquerable, eternal, immovable' —
'Arrows of various kinds, and a bow of extended form,
followed <s>Kākutstha</s> [<s>Rāma</s>], all having taken human forms' —
'He entered the divine radiance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, together with his body and attendants.'
In the blessed <s>Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa</s>:
'O king, where all powers are established — that is the universal form of <s>Hari</s>, the great final form;
That is <s>Brahman</s> in embodied form, O greatly blessed one; <s>Hari</s> is made up of all <s>Brahman</s>' —
'Eternal indeed is <s>Śrī</s>, the mother of the world, inseparable from <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
just as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is omnipresent, so too is She, O best of the twice-born' —
'In His divine form She has a divine body, and in His human form a human one;
<s>Śrī</s> fashions Her own form to correspond to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s body' —
'Those who are exclusively devoted, who constantly meditate on <s>Brahman</s>, who are <s>yogins</s> —
for them is that supreme abode which the wise seers behold' —
'And time, consisting of moments, <s>muhūrtas</s>, and the like, is not the cause of transformation of His sovereignty.'
And in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:
'O Lord, go to that divine abode, ageless, immeasurable, hard to know, accessible through the scriptures, primordial; and protect us, who have taken refuge, being born in every <s>kalpa</s> in Your own form' —
'He cooks time there; time is not lord over Him.'
The <s>Sūtrakāra</s> also affirms that the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> possesses form: 'Within [the solar orb], because of the teaching of Its attributes' (<s>antas taddharmopadeśāt</s>).
